Facebook Help Compendium

Official Facebook consumer help for the web, Windows browsers, and the iPhone app

2026-07-27

Facebook Help Compendium

This compendium contains the main content of 1481 articles from Facebook’s official consumer Help Center; articles include per-platform instructions inline, including the iPhone and iPad apps and computer browsers, where they differ. Pages belonging to the separate Meta Business Help Center that the crawl encountered are excluded, as are navigation-only listing pages. Facebook’s served pages do not expose the Help Center’s topic organization, so articles are grouped under editorial categories assigned by title keywords, sorted alphabetically, with article titles alphabetized within each category (ignoring leading words such as How to). Site chrome, feedback prompts, and tracking parameters have been removed.

Add captions to your Page’s video on Facebook

Add captions to video

Upload .srt file

Edit existing video captions

My captions aren’t showing

You can add captions to your Page’s video to make it accessible to a broader audience. You can automatically generate captions and edit them, write them yourself or you can upload a SubRip (.srt) file.

Add captions to your Page’s video

  1. Click What’s on your mind, [Name]? at the top of your feed, then click Photo/Video.
  2. Click Add photos/videos and select a video from your computer.
  3. Once your video has uploaded, click Next.
  4. Click Closed captions on the left, then select whether you’d like to auto-generate captions or upload a SubRip (.srt) file.
  5. Click Next, then click Post.

If you choose to upload a .srt file, make sure that your caption files are correctly named and formatted before you upload them.

To add captions to an existing video on your Page, find the post on your Page’s timeline, click Options in the top-right corner, select Edit Post and follow the steps above.

Note: People who watch your Page’s video with sound turned off will automatically see captions. People who watch your video with sound turned on will need to turn on captions to see them. The language people see captions in is determined by their preferred language.

Add or remove captions on your video on Facebook

Add captions to my video

Add captions in another language

Remove captions from my video

This is about adding captions to a video you upload to your profile. You can also add captions to videos you upload to your Page.

You can add captions to a video to make it accessible to a broader audience using the SubRip (.srt) file format. If you’re just getting started, learn about naming conventions for .srt files and common .srt formatting issues.

Add captions to your video

  1. Click Photo/video at the top of your timeline or Feed.
  2. Click Add photos/videos and choose a video from your computer.
  3. Click Post.
  4. We’ll notify you when your video is ready to view.
  5. Search for the video on your timeline or Feed.
  6. Click Options in the top right, then click Edit post.
  7. Click Edit from composer, then click Add captions.
  8. Click Upload next to Upload captions and then select a Subrip (.srt) file from your computer.
  9. Click Save.

To add captions in other languages, repeat steps 4–6 for each additional language you want to add.

Remove captions from a video you’ve uploaded

  1. Click your video to expand it.
  2. Click Options in the top right, then click Edit post.
  3. Click Edit from composer, then click Add captions.
  4. Click Delete next to the file you want to remove.
  5. Click Save.

Can I use Facebook’s keyboard shortcuts with my screen reader?

What screen readers work?

JAWS keyboard shortcuts

Window-Eyes keyboard shortcuts

VoiceOver keyboard shortcuts

You can use Facebook’s keyboard shortcuts with the following screen readers:

  • JAWS (Version 16+): Go to Settings Center or Quick Settings, and turn on Allow Web Application Reserved Keystrokes.
  • Window-Eyes (Version 9.2+): Turn on Web Application Mode.
  • VoiceOver (Any Version): Facebook’s keyboard shortcuts will automatically work with VoiceOver.

There are many third-party screen readers available. Learn which screen readers you can use with Facebook.

How can I like, comment on or share a Feed post on Facebook using a screen reader?

Like a post

Comment on a post

Share a post

Screen reader not working

Like, comment on or share a post using a screen reader

Facebook for computer (Facebook)

  1. From your Feed, move your screen reader focus to the desired post’s Like, Comment or Share option.
  2. Press the enter (return) key to select an option.

Facebook for iOS using VoiceOver rotor

  1. From your Feed, swipe right or left (or tap) using 1 finger to move VoiceOver focus to the desired post.
  2. Double tap using 1 finger to select the post.
  3. Swipe up or down using 1 finger to until you hear the option that you want: “like”, “comment” or “share.” If you don’t hear these options, make sure your VoiceOver rotor is set to Actions. Rotate 2 fingers on your screen as if you’re turning a dial to access the VoiceOver rotor. Keep turning until you get to Actions, and then lift your fingers to choose this option.
  4. Double tap using 1 finger to select the option.

Facebook for iOS using VoiceOver

  1. From your Feed, swipe left or right (or tap) using 1 finger to move VoiceOver focus to the desired post.
  2. Double tap using 1 finger to select the post.
  3. Swipe left or right using 1 finger to move focus to Like, Comment or Share.
  4. Double tap using 1 finger to select an option.

Facebook for iOS using VoiceOver with action sheets

  1. From your Feed, swipe right or left (or tap) using 1 finger to move VoiceOver focus to the desired post.
  2. Double tap using 2 fingers to open the action menu.
  3. Swipe left or right using 1 finger to select one of the following options: Like, Comment or Share.
  4. Double tap an option using 1 finger to select it.

Facebook for Android using TalkBack or Voice Assistant

  1. From your Feed, swipe right or left (or tap) using 1 finger to move the focus to the desired post’s options: Like, Comment or Share.
  2. Double tap an option using 1 finger to select it.

How can I navigate Facebook with keyboard shortcuts?

Use keyboard shortcuts

Action shortcuts list

Keyboard shortcuts not working

Screen reader shortcuts

Log into Facebook on a computer to use keyboard shortcuts.

Facebook has shortcuts (access keys) for people who rely on their keyboards to navigate. Different web browsers (example: Firefox, Internet Explorer) may have different keyboard shortcuts.

Keyboard shortcuts only work if you aren’t in a text box. If you have an issue while using keyboard shortcuts, please log into Facebook and send us accessibility feedback.

Learn how to turn keyboard shortcuts on or off.

Action Shortcuts

Some shortcuts help you do things such as like, comment or share something on Facebook. These shortcuts only use one keyboard key.

  • J and K - Scroll between Feed stories.
  • enter/return - See more of the selected story.
  • P - Post a new status.
  • L - Like or unlike the selected story.
  • C - Comment on the selected story.
  • S - Share the selected story.
  • O - Open an attachment from the selected story.
  • / - Search.
  • Q - Search chat contacts.
  • ? - Open a list of these keyboard shortcuts while in Feed.

Keyboard shortcuts may not work in video calls or video players.

Using Keyboard Shortcuts with Screen Readers

Most common screen readers (example: VoiceOver, JAWS) support Facebook’s keyboard shortcuts automatically.

Turn on shortcuts for JAWS

  1. Use Insert/Caps Lock + 3.
  2. Press the shortcut key.

Mobile Phone

Adjust video captions

Change caption text size

Captions hard to see

I can’t read captions

Computer

You can adjust what video captions look like in your video settings.

  1. Click Edit next to Captions Display.
  2. Click next to each option to adjust your settings for:
    • Background Color: the color of the caption’s background.
    • Background Opacity: how transparent the caption’s background is.
    • Text Color: the color of the caption’s text.

You can adjust what video captions look like in your device settings.

  1. Go to your device’s home screen.
  2. Tap [Image: iphone settings]Settings.
  3. Tap Accessibility, then tap Subtitles & Captioning.
  4. Tap Style.
  5. Tap to select or create a new style.

Keep in mind that not all videos on Facebook have captions. Learn how to add captions to a video you’ve added.

How do I respond to a chat in messages on Facebook using a screen reader?

How do I respond to a message?

How do I type a message?

How do I review my message?

Respond to a chat in messages on Facebook using a screen reader

  1. Navigate to the conversations list on the left.
  2. Locate the conversation and activate its link, which will move focus to the Type a message field.
  3. Focus on the Type a message field at the bottom.
    • Your screen reader may announce the content of the last message in the conversation and who sent it.
    • Windows screen readers may announce the description with their commands for reading the field name and contents.
    • VoiceOver users can access the description by pressing ctrl-option-shift-h on the keyboard.
  4. Enter the text that you want to send and press the enter key to send it.
  5. To review your message, navigate to the appropriate heading structure.

How do I start a new conversation in messages on Facebook using a screen reader?

How do I start a new conversation?

How do I add recipients?

How do I send a message?

How do I review my message?

Start a new conversation in messages on Facebook using a screen reader

  1. Activate New Message button in the banner section.
  2. To add recipients, focus on Type the name of a person or group and enter a person or group. Use the arrow keys to select an option, and press the enter key to add the recipient.
  3. Focus on the Type a message field at the bottom and enter the text that you want to send.
  4. Press the enter key to begin your conversation.
  5. To review your message, navigate to the appropriate heading structure.

How does automatic alt text work on Facebook?

Edit automatic alt text

Hear automatic alt text

Detailed image description

Alternative text (alt text) is a text-based description added to an image that can benefit people who are blind and have low-vision. If the person who uploaded or posted the image doesn’t include alt text, Facebook’s Automatic Alt Text (AAT) technology uses computer vision and artificial intelligence to automatically create a description of the image. The automatic alt text may not always be complete, but you can edit the alt text for images you upload or post.

To hear the automatic alt text for an image, open Facebook using a screen reader and focus on the image. You’ll hear a description entered by the person who uploaded the image or a list of objects, concepts or locations the image may contain as recognized by Facebook’s AAT technology. If you think the alt text of an image violates our Community Standards, you can report the image.

Languages automatic alt text supports

Detailed descriptions for Android, iPhone and iPad

If you’d like to know more about an image, using a screen reader, focus on the image and open the action menu. From there, select Generate detailed image description.

The detailed image description can include:

  • [Name’s] description: Alt text entered by the person who uploaded or posted the image.
  • Facebook-generated description: Alt text that is automatically generated by Facebook.
  • Text in This Image: Any text in the image, read from top-left to bottom-right.
  • Position Information: Where objects in the image are located.
  • Size Information: The size of an object is used to determine the focus of an image.
  • Elements by Category: Objects are put into categories like people, plants and objects.

If you have any problems with automatic alt text, please send us accessibility feedback.

Update (September 2025): All videos on Facebook are now Reels. All videos posted to Facebook will be shared as reels, regardless of length or orientation. This unifies the video experience for creators and viewers. Learn more about this change.

Some reels on Facebook have automatically generated captions available, translated into different languages. If translated captions are available, you can:

  • Change the caption language.
  • Customize caption appearance.

Available languages

Automatically-generated translated captions support the following languages:

  • Arabic (Standard)
  • Brazilian Portuguese
  • English
  • Hindi
  • Indonesian Bahasa
  • Spanish (Latin America)
  • Tagalog
  • Tamil
  • Telugu
  • Urdu
  • Vietnamese

Turn on captions

To enable captions:

  1. While watching a reel, click Closed captions.
  2. Click the language you want to use for the subtitles.

Customize how the captions look

To edit captions:

  3. Click the option you would like to change. The available options are:
    • Background Color
    • Background Opacity

    • Text Color

Note:

  • Captions aren’t available on all reels. Captions may be only available in the video’s original language.
  • If captions aren’t available on a reel, you won’t see Closed captions.
  • A reel’s creator can decide if they want captions to be turned on by default. When you watch the reel, you can switch the captions on and off.

Why you may be having problems adding captions to your reel on Facebook

My SRT file is incorrect

SRT file format example

My captions aren’t showing

Update (September 2025): All videos on Facebook are now Reels. Any video you post to Facebook will be shared as a reel, regardless of length or orientation. This unifies the video experience for creators and viewers. Learn more about this change.

If you’re having problems trying to add captions to your reel, the SubRip (.srt) caption file you’re trying to upload may be formatted incorrectly.

A subtitle or closed caption file contains both the text of what is said in the reel and time codes for when each line of text should be displayed. Each subtitle in an .srt file is provided in a block. Each block should include a number, a start and end time for the subtitle, and the subtitle text. Blocks should be separated by a single line, and there shouldn’t be any spaces or lines after the last block in the file.

When creating your SubRip (.srt) file, make sure that:

  • Each subtitle has a unique sequence number. Start with 1 and continue to the last subtitle in the file.
  • The times include every digit in the format hh:mm:ss,fff. Be sure to add leading zeros (example: 01:09:05,050) as necessary and include only two colons and one comma.
  • The text file is encoded UTF-8. If it’s not encoded in UTF-8, try opening the file in any text editor and saving it again under a new file name.

Age requirements for managed Meta accounts

Age for Meta Horizon services

Age for Meta business tools

Age for Admin Center

All ages outlined below may vary, subject to applicable legal requirements and the age of legal majority where you reside.

Age requirement for Meta Horizon managed services

You have to be 18 years of age or older to be an admin for Meta Horizon managed services.

To use a device that’s managed by an organization:

  • You have to be 18 years of age or older to use an Individual Mode device.
  • You have to be 18 years of age or older to use a Shared Mode device that requires an account.
  • You have to be 13 years of age or older to use a Shared Mode device that does not require an account.

If you are a Meta Horizon managed services admin, then:

  • You must ensure that all apps on a Shared Mode device are appropriate for anyone who may use the device.
  • You must provide a parent or legal guardian of a person using a Shared Mode device who is under the age of 18 with parent information about user readiness as well as all applicable health and safety warnings before the person uses the device.

You must follow, and ensure all other users follow, all health, safety and other warnings and instructions provided by Meta before and during use of the managed devices, including without limitation the information located at L (l.facebook.com).

Age requirement for Meta business tools

You have to be 16 years of age or older to use a managed Meta account for business tools such as Business Manager and Ads Manager. You have to be 18 years of age or older to access Admin Center.

Age requirement for Admin Center

You have to be 18 years of age or older to have access to your organization’s Admin Center.

Archive or delete content on Facebook

Archive my content

Restore archived content

Move content to Trash

Restore content from Trash

Currently, this feature isn’t available to everyone.

You can archive or delete some of the content you share on Facebook, like posts, photos and videos, directly from your Feed or your timeline. From each post, you can choose to:

  • Move to Archive. When you move content to your Archive, it’ll only be visible to you. If you choose to restore your content, it’ll be visible to the audience that was selected before it was moved to Archive.
  • Move to Trash. When you move content to your Trash, it’ll stay there until it is automatically deleted 30 days later. While it’s in your Trash, it’ll only be visible to you.
    • During the 30 days, you can restore your content to where you originally posted it on Facebook, move it to your Archive or you can select content to delete before the 30 days are over. When you restore your content, it’ll be visible to the audience that was selected before it was moved to Trash.
    • After 30 days, the content will be automatically deleted and can’t be restored.

You can also manage some of your content from the Manage Activity section of your activity log. Learn more about managing Archive and Trash in your activity log.

Keep in mind, only certain types of content can be moved to Archive or Trash.

Archive your content

  1. Go to the post that you’d like to archive.
  2. Click Options in the top right of the post.
  3. Click Move to Archive.

Restore your archived content

You can restore your archived content in your Activity log.

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & Privacy.
  3. Click Activity Log.
  4. In the menu on the left, scroll down and click Archive, then click Post Archive. From here:
    • If you see the content you want to restore:
      1. Find the content you’d like to restore, then click Options.
      2. Click Restore to profile, then click Restore.
    • If you don’t see the content you’d like to restore:
      1. Click Filter at the top of your activity log, then filter your content by date.
      2. Add a start and end date, then click Save Changes.
      3. Find over the content you’d like to restore, then click Options.
      4. Click Restore to profile, then click Restore.

After you’ve moved an item to your Archive, it’ll only be visible to you. When you restore your content, it’ll be visible to the same audience you chose before you archived your content.

Move your content to Trash

  1. Go to the post that you’d like to trash.
  2. Click Options in the top right of the post.
  3. Click Move to Trash.

Keep in mind, when you move something to Trash it’ll be automatically deleted after 30 days, unless you choose to delete it sooner or restore it. Once the content is deleted after 30 days, it can’t be restored.

Restore content you’ve moved to Trash

You can restore content in your Trash in your activity log.

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & Privacy.
  3. Click Activity Log.
  4. In the menu on the left, scroll down and click Trash.
  5. From here, you can:
    • Restore your content to where it was when you posted it: Hover over the content you’d like to restore, then click Options. Click Restore to profile, then click Restore to confirm.
    • Move content to your Archive: Hover over the content, then click Options. Click Move to archive. Your content will move to your archive.

After you’ve moved your content to Trash, it’ll be deleted after 30 days. During the 30 days, you can restore your content to where you originally posted it on Facebook. When you restore your content, it’ll be visible to the same audience you chose before you deleted your content. If you move your content to Archive, it’ll only be visible to you.

Check if an email is really from Facebook

Is this email from Facebook?

Check email address

Confirm Meta email

What if email is suspicious?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Facebook will never ask you for your password in an email or send you a password as an attachment.

If you get an email that says it’s from Facebook, here are some ways to confirm it’s really from us.

Check the address

Any correspondence from Facebook or Meta will only come from one of these email domains, or any subdomains of the following (such as support.facebook.com or business.fb.com):

  • fb.com
  • facebook.com
  • facebookmail.com
  • instagram.com
  • meta.com
  • metamail.com

However, look out for a misspelled version of any of these, since it might be someone pretending to be Meta or Facebook.

Look for our logo

If you use Gmail, Yahoo Mail or Apple Mail, you can trust the email if the Facebook logo appears alongside our email address.

Confirm that we emailed you

Go to facebook.com/recent_emails/security, or:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then Settings.
  3. Select Accounts Center, then Password and security.
  4. Below Security checks, select Recent emails.
  5. View security emails (such as a request to change your password) from the last year in the main SECURITY tab. View any other emails sent in the last two days in the OTHER EMAILS tab. Note: If we send an email containing a special link or a security code, we may hide that information in your settings to help protect your Facebook account. You’ll need to be able to log into your email account in order to view it.

If you’re a business, go to Meta Business Support Home to review your account status and note any support issues.

More information

  • What to do if you still think the email is suspicious.
  • Choose what you get notified about.

Delete or cancel deletion of your Facebook Page

I can’t delete my Page

What happens if I delete?

To delete your Page, you’ll need to have Facebook access with full control of your Page.

If you don’t want to permanently delete your Page, but want to hide it publicly, you can also deactivate your Page or unpublish your Page instead of deleting it.

When you request that we delete your Facebook Page, we’ll deactivate your Page immediately, but it won’t be permanently deleted until 14 days have passed.

You can also learn more about how to delete your personal account.

Note: If your Page does not have at least one person with Facebook access with full control, it will be automatically deactivated and scheduled for deletion.

Delete your Page

If you have Facebook access with full control:

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page photo in the top right.
  4. Click Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  5. Click Access and control in the left menu.
  6. Select Delete Page, then click Continue and follow the steps. You may be asked to re-enter your password.

Note: If you don’t see the option to delete your Page, make sure you have Facebook access with full control of your Page. Learn how to see what your access is to a Page.

Cancel deletion of your Page

When you request that we delete your Facebook Page, we’ll deactivate your Page immediately, but it won’t be permanently deleted until 14 days have passed. If you decide you do not want to delete your Page within 14 days, you can reactivate your Page to cancel deletion.

Note: You cannot reactivate a Page from the Page’s business settings. It can only be reactivated from a personal Facebook profile.

To reactivate your Page:

  1. From your main profile click your profile photo in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Below Your activity, click Reactivate a Page. This feature only works if you have Pages that have been deactivated but not permanently deleted.
  4. Find the Page you want to reactivate and click Reactivate.

How Facebook’s Location Settings work

Turn off Location Services

What is Location Services?

What is my IP address?

Learn more about Facebook’s Location Settings

iOS Location Settings

Android Location Settings

Learn more about your Location information

When Location Services is turned off, we may still estimate your location using things like check-ins, events and information about your internet connection.

Specific location information like your device’s GPS signal and connection information like your Wi-Fi connection or IP address (internet protocol address) help us understand where you are. Your IP address is a unique number assigned to a device, like a phone or computer, that allows it to communicate over the internet. Numbers are assigned according to standard guidelines, or protocols. Just like you need a mailing address to receive a letter from a friend, your device needs a digital address to receive information on the internet.

We use this information to provide more relevant and personalized experiences, protect your account, and provide better ads. See our Privacy Policy and Privacy Center to learn more about how we use your location information.

How to find birthdays and change your birthday settings on Facebook

Find friends’ birthdays

Change my birthday

Who can see my birthday?

I can’t change my birthday

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Find your friends’ birthdays

You can find upcoming birthdays from the Friends section on Facebook:

  1. From your Feed, select Friends from the left menu.
  2. Click Birthdays from the left menu.

From here, you’ll see today’s birthdays, recent birthdays, and upcoming birthdays.

Update your birthday settings

You can update your birthday and who can see it on Facebook. Birthdays need to match across all accounts in an Accounts Center. If you have additional Facebook profiles, your birthday from your main profile will carry over to your additional profiles. You can’t change your birthday on your additional Facebook profiles, but you can change who can see your birthday on each of your profiles.

Change your birthday

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Click About and then click Contact and basic information.
  3. Below Basic info, click Edit next to your birthday.
  4. In Accounts Center, click Edit.
  5. Update your birthday and then click Save.

Note: There’s a limit to how many times you can change your birthday. If you’ve recently changed it, you may need to wait before you can change it again.

Change who can see your birthday on your profile

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Click About and then click Contact and basic information.
  3. Below Basic info, click Audience next to your birthday. You can choose who can see your birth date and your birth year.
  4. Select your audience and then click Save.

On Facebook, you can choose who can see the day and month of your birthday as well as who can see the year of your birthday. If you choose not to share the day and month of your birthday, your friends won’t get a notification about your upcoming birthday.

To change who can see your birthday on an additional Facebook profile, switch to the profile you want to use, and then follow the steps above.

How to find your Facebook settings

Where are my settings?

Where is Dark mode?

Where is Data Saver?

Where is delete my account?

We’ve recently made some changes to the way settings are organized on Facebook.

Note: You can use search in Settings to find what you’re looking for.

The new Settings experience is only available on mobile at this time. All mobile users will be moved to the new settings design unless you have Facebook access to a page in the new Pages. You will not be able to keep the old settings design.

What was updated

We’ve reduced the number of steps it takes to access some settings and updated the structure within the Settings menu. We haven’t changed any of our settings so you can still find the controls you need.

  • Settings
  • Privacy shortcuts

All settings and privacy shortcuts are now contained within those two options.

Updates to the Settings and Privacy menu structure

  • Your time on Facebook: Can now be found in Settings, below Preferences. You can use Your Time on Facebook to see how much time you spend on Facebook and manage your time.
  • Two-factor authentication: Can now be found in Settings and Privacy, below Security and Login. Two-factor authentication is a security feature that helps protect your Facebook account in addition to your password.
  • Dark mode: Can now be found in Settings and Privacy, below Preferences. You can switch to a dark background with Dark Mode.
  • Reaction preferences: Can now be found in Settings, below Preferences. You can choose to hide the number of reactions on posts from others and on your own posts.
  • Video: Can now be found in Settings as Media below Preferences. You can manage things like video quality and autoplay.
  • Language and region: Can now be found in Settings, below Preferences. Use Language to choose which language Facebook appears in.
    • Note: On FB Lite, you’ll still find Language directly below Settings and Privacy.
  • Data Usage: Can now be found in Settings and Privacy, below Media. You can use Data Saver to lower the resolution on videos.
    • Note: On FB Lite, you’ll still find Data Usage below Settings and Privacy.

Updates to the Settings menu structure

In Settings on your mobile app, you’ll now find these menu options:

  • Account: In this section, you can do things like manage your passwords and payment info.
  • Preferences: In this section, you can do things like manage the amount of time you spend on Facebook or manage how you see things on your Facebook Feed.
  • Audience and Visibility: In this section, you can manage things like your block list or who can see your posts or profile.
  • Permissions: In this section, you can manage the information Facebook uses from things like your games and devices.
  • Your information: In this section, you can do things like see a log of your Facebook activity and manage your Facebook info.
  • Your activity: In this section, you can review your activity and content you’ve been tagged in below Activity Log.
  • Community Standards and Legal Policies: In this section, you can find info on our standards and policies.

Updates to the Privacy menu structure

We have re-organized the Privacy section into other categories. Here is where you can now find those settings:

  • Privacy Settings: Setting options formerly listed below Privacy Settings can now be found below Account or Audience and Visibility.
    • Check a Few Important Settings can now be found in Privacy Checkup, below the Account section.
    • Manage your profile can now be found in the Audience and Visibility section below Profile Information.
    • Learn more with Privacy Basics can now be found by searching “privacy basics” using Facebook search.
    • Settings that control who can see your activity, posts, and profile can be found within the Audience and Visibility section.
    • Profile Locking can now be found below Permissions. Use Profile Locking to show a limited view of your profile’s content.
  • Privacy Center can now be found on the settings home page.
  • How you get message requests: Can now be found within “How people find and contact you” below the Audience and visibility section.
  • Timeline and Tagging: Has been re-named to Profile and Tagging and can now be found below Audience and Visibility. Use Profile and Tagging to manage settings such as who can see posts you’re tagged in on your profile.
  • Public Posts: Has been renamed to Followers and Public Content and can now be found below the Audience and Visibility section. Use Followers and Public Content to manage settings like who can follow you and who can comment on your public posts.
  • Blocking: Can now be found below Audience and Visibility. Use Blocking to manage who can see things like your profile or what you post.
  • Location: Can now be found below Permissions. Use Location to manage your location settings.
  • Active Status: Can now be found below Audience and Visibility. Use Active Status to manage who can see when you’re active.

Updates to the Deactivation and Deletion settings

You can deactivate or delete your account or update memorialization settings below Account Ownership and Control. Account Ownership and Control can now be found in “Personal and Account Information,” below “Account” within “Personal and Account Information.”

I have limited access to my Facebook account

Why is my account limited?

My account has a virus

My account is blocked

What can I do on Facebook?

Sometimes people get blocked from using features on Facebook for reasons other than malicious software.

Your account may have limited features right now because a computer you used to access Facebook may have a virus or malicious software. We did this to help prevent this problem from spreading to other accounts.

We’ll let you know if there are other steps you need to take. Otherwise, your account should return to normal once we fix the problem. Keep in mind, this can take a few days.

What to know about limited access

  • You can still browse Facebook, but can’t comment on posts or send friend requests.
  • Depending on the type of issue, you may be able to access Facebook as normal on another computer, phone or tablet.
  • You can stay updated about your account by checking your Support Inbox.

Learn more about how to keep your account secure, including tips for passwords and suspicious links.

If you don’t enable a connected experience across your accounts in an Accounts Center

What if I don’t enable connected experiences?

What happens if I don’t share posts?

What happens if I don’t log in?

What happens if I don’t sync profile info?

You can choose which connected experiences to enable for accounts added to the same Accounts Center. If you choose to not enable a connected experience you won’t be able to:

  • Share stories, posts and/or reels across your Instagram and Facebook profiles. Note:
    • Any Instagram posts that were already shared to Facebook will still be visible on Facebook, and any Facebook posts that were already shared to Instagram will still be visible on Instagram.
    • If you’ve shared a story across Instagram and Facebook, it will still be visible on Facebook and Instagram until its 24-hour period of time is complete. Learn more about how to delete photos or videos from your story on Facebook and Instagram.
  • Log in with accounts. This means that:
    • You’ll no longer be able to use Facebook to log into Instagram or Instagram to log into Facebook.
    • If you created an Instagram account with a Facebook account and you decide to remove that Instagram account from the same Accounts Center as your Facebook account, then you’ll be prompted to create a password for Instagram. This also applies to Facebook accounts created using an Instagram account.
    • We won’t log you out of any sessions or devices. To review and log out of any sessions, you can visit your Facebook settings or Instagram settings.
  • Sync your name, profile picture, username or avatar across Facebook, Instagram and Meta Horizon.
    • If you remove an account from an Accounts Center, your profile info for profiles in that account will no longer sync. Any future changes you make to your name, profile picture, username or avatar will only apply to the profile you’re updating.
    • Learn how to update your name, profile picture, username or avatar on Facebook.
    • Learn how to update your name, username or avatar on Instagram.
    • Learn how to update your name, profile picture,username or avatar on Meta Horizon.
  • Sync your shopping activity across accounts.
    • Your shopping activity, like items added to your wishlist, will only be visible in the account where they took place.
    • Note: Synced shopping activity isn’t available to everyone who has access to Accounts Center.
  • Follow people on Meta Horizon. You won’t be able to:
    • Automatically send follow requests to your Facebook friends or people you follow on Instagram who also have Meta Horizon profiles and have chosen to show their Facebook and/or Instagram profiles with their Meta Horizon profile.
  • Choose which of your profiles are shown together. You won’t be able to:
    • Choose which names or usernames are shown in each of your profiles. For example, you won’t be able to update your Instagram profile to show your Facebook name or Meta Horizon username.
    • Update your Meta Horizon profile to show your Facebook name or Instagram username, and who can see this information (for example, anyone or only your followers on Facebook and/or Instagram who are also on Meta Horizon).
    • Note: You can always see your Facebook name and Instagram profiles in your own Horizon profile. This setting controls how others can see your Facebook name and Instagram profiles.
  • View media captured in Meta Horizon Worlds in your Facebook or Instagram photo galleries through Meta Cloud Albums. You won’t be able to:
    • Choose which of your accounts in an Accounts Center can access media captured from Meta Horizon Worlds from your Meta Horizon profile.

What happens if I deactivate?

What happens to my Pages?

Deleting or deactivating your Facebook account also deletes or deactivates all profiles under your account. Learn how to delete or deactivate individual profiles.

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you deactivate your account:

  • You can reactivate whenever you want.
  • People can’t see your timeline or search for you.
  • Some information may remain visible to others (example: messages you sent).
  • You will not be able to use your Facebook account to access Meta Quest Products or your Meta Quest information.

If you delete your account:

  • You can’t regain access once it’s deleted.
  • We delay deletion a few days after it’s requested. A deletion request is cancelled if you log back into your Facebook account during this time.
  • Some information, such as messaging history, isn’t stored in your account. This means friends may still have access to messages you sent after your account has been deleted.
  • Copies of some material (example: log records) may remain in our database but are disassociated from personal identifiers.
  • If you use your Facebook account to log in to Meta Quest, deleting your Facebook account will also delete your Meta Quest information. This includes your app purchases and your achievements. You will no longer be able to return any apps and will lose any existing store credits.

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Notifications in the left menu.
  4. Scroll down to Where You Receive Notifications, then click Email.
  5. Select All, Suggested or Required notifications below Email Frequency.
    • If you select All or Suggested: Click the toggle next to Pages and profiles you manage to turn this setting on or off.

After turning email notifications on for Pages You Manage, you can also choose the types of email notifications you receive and for which Pages.

Manage email notifications for Pages from your main profile:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Notifications in the left menu.
  4. Below What Notifications You Receive, click Pages You Manage.
  5. Click on the Page you want to manage notifications for.
  6. Toggle email notifications on or off next to Page notifications on your profile.

If you turn email notifications on for your Page, below Emails about your Page you can toggle these email categories on or off:

  • Marketing & promotions: Discover Meta products and services that may help make your Page a success.
  • Help & guidance: Stay up to date with tips and educational resources for managing your Page.
  • Surveys & research: Learn how you can help improve the Pages experience.

If you turned on email notifications for your Page and no longer want to receive them, you can unsubscribe at the bottom of your email notification or adjust your notification settings at any time.

My personal Facebook account is suspended or disabled

My account was suspended

Appeal my account suspension

Why was my account disabled?

My account was disabled

The time-period you can appeal suspension of an account varies by region.

We may suspend your Facebook account if we find that the account or activity on it may not follow our Community Standards. You can appeal the suspension within 180 days. If you don’t appeal the suspension after 180 days or if your appeal isn’t successful, we’ll permanently disable your account.

When an account is suspended or disabled, it’s not visible to anyone and you can’t use it.

You’ll know if your account is suspended or disabled because you’ll be informed in an email, and when you log in you’ll see We suspended your account or We disabled your account.

Appeal a suspension

To appeal a suspension, log into Facebook. You’ll be prompted to appeal the suspension within 180 days.

If your account is disabled

If you don’t appeal within 180 days or if your appeal isn’t successful, your account will be permanently disabled. You won’t be able to request another review of the decision.

Note: We may disable your account without suspending it first, such as in cases of severe or time-sensitive violations. Learn more about how we define severe violations from the Community Standards.

Why your account might be suspended or disabled

Some examples of why your account might be suspended or disabled include:

  • Posting content that doesn’t follow our Community Standards
  • Misrepresenting your identity in order to to mislead or deceive others, evade enforcement or violate our Community Standards, including impersonating someone
  • Contacting other people for the purpose of harassment, advertising, promoting or other conduct that’s not allowed.

Note: In certain regions, we may suspend and disable accounts for people in a specific age range in accordance with local laws and regulations.

Why can’t I remove a strike?

You may be able to remove a strike from your Facebook account if it’s the first time we removed content for not following the Community Standards within the past year.

Remove a first-time strike

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Click Options and select Profile Status.
  3. Click the information about the content we removed.
  4. Click Fix it.
  5. Select Remove your warning.

What happens when you go through the process to remove a strike

To remove your strike, you’ll be prompted to read about our policies and what they mean to avoid issues on your account later. You’ll also have a chance to share what you think happened (example: “I didn’t know about the rules”) to help us continue to improve our products and policies.

What happens after you remove a first-time strike

After you go through the process to remove a strike:

  • The strike will be removed from your account.
  • Your content will not be restored. Learn how to request a review to restore your content.
  • You won’t have another chance to remove a strike for a year. You may still be able to request a review to restore your content.

Troubleshooting

If you don’t see the option to remove the strike, it might be because this isn’t your first time getting a strike within a year, or because the strike isn’t eligible to be removed.

If your friend or family member is irreversibly mentally or physically unable to maintain their Facebook account, we may be able to help you remove it.

  • For a child under 13: We require our members to be at least 13 years old. If you believe there is a child under the age of 13 using Facebook, please report the account to us.

Keep in mind this form should only be used to report medically incapacitated users. Learn what to do if you’ve lost access to your account, or how to report a hacked account or deceased user.

We don’t consider someone who is in rehab or prison to be incapacitated. If you’re a member of law enforcement and would like to report someone on Facebook who is currently imprisoned, please submit a request.

In some cases, when you submit an ID, you can choose to opt out of your ID being used for this purpose, and instead it will be deleted within 30 days in accordance with our standard policies. When this setting is turned on, encrypted photo(s) of your ID(s) will be kept for no longer than one year to help improve our automated systems for detecting fake IDs and related abuse.

When this setting is turned off, encrypted photo(s) of your ID(s) will be deleted within 30 days of submission or of turning this setting off.

Unfamiliar locations in the ‘Where you’re logged in’ section of your Facebook account

My account has unfamiliar locations

Someone else is logged in

What if I forgot to log off?

If you see a location that you don’t recognize, first check if it’s related to your mobile device. Often, when signing in through a mobile device, you’re routed through an IP address that doesn’t actually reflect your actual location.

If you don’t recognize a location and it’s not connected to a mobile device, it could be because:

  • We have inaccurate information: Sometimes we can only provide an approximate location that may appear inaccurate compared to your actual location.
  • You forgot to log off: You might be seeing the location of a mobile device you’re still logged in to. If you think you’ve left yourself logged in on someone else’s mobile device, you can log yourself out.
  • Someone else has access to your Facebook account: If you think someone else is logged in to your account, you should first log yourself out and then secure your account by changing your password.

Unlock your Facebook account

My account is locked

I can’t get codes

Recover my account

My account was locked for security

If we see unusual activity on your account, we might lock it for security. You’ll know that we locked your account if:

  • You get an email from Facebook saying that we locked your account.
  • You log into Facebook and see a message that your account has been locked.

We’ll take you through some steps to unlock your account the next time you log into Facebook or when you follow the link in the email.

Unlock your account if it was locked for security

  1. Open Facebook.
  2. Select Get started and follow the on-screen steps.

We may ask you to confirm your identity.

If you can’t access your account to unlock it

If your account is locked but you can’t log in to Facebook to unlock it, we can help recover your account.

Learn more about recovering your Facebook account.

If you don’t get a code to confirm your account

If you are experiencing issues receiving confirmation codes on your phone or email:

  • Sometimes the confirmation codes may take longer to arrive. If you’ve requested several codes already, wait a day before trying again.
  • Make sure that you’re checking the correct phone number or email address for the codes.
  • Check your spam folder.
  • If you requested to get a code on your phone and you don’t see it, check the blocked messages on your phone. Your phone may be screening or blocking confirmation code texts.
  • Check your phone’s network connection. A poor network connection may be the reason you’re not receiving a code.
  • Check to make sure your phone has enough space to receive an SMS confirmation text.
  • Try restarting your phone.
  • Contact your carrier to check your mobile plan. Sometimes your mobile plan may affect the type of messages you can receive. Ask your carrier what kind of message your current plan allows you to receive.

Updates to gray accounts on Facebook

What is a gray account?

Change Page ownership

Export my gray account data

Delete my gray account

If you continue managing your Pages or groups with a gray account, you risk losing access to them once the gray account is automatically disabled.

A gray account is an account used to log into Facebook that is not associated with a personal profile or account. People used to be able to manage their Pages with gray accounts before we required individuals to have a personal Profile in order to create, manage, or run ads on a Page.

Gray accounts don’t have access to the same security features as standard accounts. Because of this, we are disabling gray accounts and requiring gray account administrators to use their standard Facebook account for improved security and account safety on Facebook.

If you use a gray account, you have the following options:

  • Use your existing standard account that represents you as an individual to continue using Facebook. You can create a new account if you don’t have one already.
  • Change ownership of any Pages or groups you manage by granting your standard account full access to the Page or group. If your gray account is the sole admin of any Pages, those Pages will be removed.
    • Manage roles for a Page.
    • Make someone an admin or moderator of a Facebook group.
  • Export your information from your gray account.
  • Delete your gray account or wait for it to be automatically disabled.

Note:

  • If you’re trying to invite a user to be an admin of your Page, some users may not be discoverable when searching for them using an email address because of their privacy settings.
  • You can also search for a user on desktop using their Facebook profile URL.
  • If you send a page admin invite for a Page but the recipient doesn’t receive it, they can accept the invite from the Page or from their Page invites.

About Facebook Ads

Control my ad preferences

Why am I seeing this ad?

What information is used?

I can’t manage my ads

How Ads Work on Facebook

A business creates an ad. They choose the type of audience they’d like to reach. If you’re in that audience, Facebook shows you the ad.

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

When we ask people about our ads, one of the top things they tell us is that they want to see ads that relate to things they care about. We learn about this primarily from your activity on Facebook, such as Pages or posts you like and posts or comments you make. We may also learn about your interests from some of the websites and apps you use, depending on your settings. We call this online interest-based advertising, and many companies do this.

How does this work?

Let’s say that you’re thinking about buying a new TV, and you start researching TVs on the web and in mobile apps. Based on this activity, we may show you ads for deals on a TV to help you get the best price or other brands to consider. And because we think you’re interested in electronics, we may show you ads for other electronics in the future, like speakers or a game console to go with your new TV.

Meta adheres to the framework established by the Digital Advertising Alliance, Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada and the European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance, a coalition of organizations that develops privacy standards for online advertising, so if you don’t want us to use your activity information from websites and apps you use to show you ads that are more relevant to you, we won’t. If you don’t want Meta to use information based on your activity on websites or apps off Facebook for the purpose of showing you ads, you can opt out in your settings. You can also opt out from all participating companies through the Digital Advertising Alliance in the USA, the Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada in Canada or the European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance in Europe.

How do I manage the ads I see?

People also tell us they want more control over the ads they see. That’s why we have Ad preferences. Your Ad preferences page lets you manage your ad experience on Facebook. For example, if you’re not interested in electronics, you can choose to “see less” ads about electronics in the Ad topics setting in your ad preferences. You can also control whether we use information that other businesses or organizations send us about your activity on their apps or websites, or your offline interactions with them such as in-store purchases, to show you ads. You can do so in your Activity from other businesses setting, which is available from your Ad preferences.

You can also access your ad preferences from the “Why am I seeing this ad?” tool from every ad on Facebook. Learn more about why you are seeing an ad here.

To learn more, visit About Facebook Ads or read our Cookies Policy.

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

The ads you see depend on a number of factors.

Learn why you see specific ads

  1. Click Options in the top right of the ad.
  2. Click Why am I seeing this ad?. You’ll see factors that may have influenced why you saw this ad (for example, activity on Meta technologies or with the advertiser).
  3. If available, click Next to view more information about why you’re seeing an ad.

How machine learning helps us provide insight into why you saw an ad

We use machine learning models to help explain the insights you see in Why am I seeing this ad?. These models help surface how certain activity both on and off Meta technologies may have contributed to Facebook showing you a particular ad.

For example, liking a post, clicking on an ad, or activity on websites, apps, and products sent to us from advertisers contribute to these insights. Meta’s use of your activity off Meta technologies depends on your ad settings. While these insights don’t represent all the factors contributing to delivering an ad, we use them to provide you with an informative and understandable view into some of the factors that contributed to why you saw an ad.

How we decide which ads to show you

We want the ads you see on Facebook to be as interesting and useful to you as possible. These are examples of things we could use to decide which ads to show you:

  • Your activity on Facebook (such as liking a Page or clicking on ads you see). If you have linked your Facebook and Instagram accounts, your activity on Instagram may also affect the ads you see on Facebook. Depending on your region, your interactions with AI products may also affect the ads you see.

  • Content you create or interact with across Facebook and Instagram.

  • Other information about you from your Facebook account (example: your age, your gender, your location, the devices you use to access Facebook).

  • Information advertisers, their partners, and our marketing partners share with us that they already have, like your email address.

  • Additional policies are in place for ads shown to teens.

  • Your activity on websites and apps off of Facebook. Learn more about how to turn this off in your ad settings.

Your settings may not affect whether we use your information to avoid showing you certain ads. For example, we may not show you ads for something you’ve recently purchased.

Note:

  • Why am I seeing this ad? provides an explanation of some of the activity we think may have influenced why our ads delivery system showed you this ad.

  • Learn more about your activity by visiting Activity log or visit Export your information where you can export your information to a device or external service. Learn more about exporting your information.

  • We don’t share information that personally identifies you (information such as your name or email address that by itself can be used to contact you or identifies who you are) unless you give us permission. To learn more about the information Meta receives and how we use it, visit our Privacy Policy and Cookies Policy.

  • We use information you provide us, actions you’ve taken on our platforms and if applicable, actions you’ve taken on other websites, apps or in stores that those businesses or organizations have shared.

  • We do not use information with special protections, you choose to provide, to show you ads.

Learn more about how ads work on Facebook.

To adjust what ads you see

If you’re seeing ads that aren’t interesting to you, you can:

  • Adjust your ad preferences. Visit your Ad preferences page, where you can manage things like your interests and your profile information to get a more personalized experience. Learn more about your Ad preferences.
  • Update your ads based on activity from other businesses. You can choose whether we use information that other businesses or organizations send us about your activity on their apps or websites, or your offline interactions with them such as in-store purchases, to show you ads.
  • Hide ads from an advertiser. If you’re seeing an advertiser that isn’t interesting to you, you can hide an ad or hide an advertiser.

You can also manage your ad preferences in Accounts Center.

Your Information and Facebook Ads

Your ad preferences are based on information you’ve shared with Facebook, Pages you like or engage with, ads you click on, apps and websites you use, and information from our data providers and advertisers.

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Your profile picture or name may be paired with an ad to show your activity on Facebook (example: if you follow or like the Starbucks Page).

Change who can see your social actions with Facebook ads

  1. Click on your profile picture in the top right, then click Settings & privacy.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Ad preferences.
  4. Click the Manage info tab.
  5. Scroll down to the Other settings section and click Social interactions, then select your account.
  6. Below Who can see your social interactions alongside ads? you can select Friends or Only Me.

Keep in mind:

  • This setting applies to your likes, follows, comments, shares, app usage, check-ins, recommendations, and events you joined that appear with ads your friends see.
  • Your name and profile picture will only appear to the people who have permission to view your Page likes.
  • It’s against our advertising policies for advertisers to use your name directly in an ad. If you see an ad you think might be using your name in a different way, please report it.
  • If you’re under 18, your social actions are not shown alongside ads. Changing who can see your social actions will not have an effect until you’re 18 years old.

Learn more about ads and privacy and how advertising works on Facebook.

This page used to contain a list of the third-party data providers that Meta worked with to offer their targeting segments directly on Facebook, and a description of that program. After we last updated our Privacy Policy, we terminated this program. Meta no longer works with third-party data providers to offer their targeting segments directly on Facebook.

Businesses may continue, on their own, to work with data providers. Many businesses today work with third parties to help manage and understand their marketing efforts. For example, an auto dealer may want to customize an offer to people who are likely to be interested in buying a new car. The dealer also might want to send offers, like discounts for service, to customers that have purchased a car from them. To do this, the auto dealer works with a third-party company to identify and reach those customers with the right offer.

So businesses who advertise to you may be using a list of people that they’ve gotten, or gotten the ability to use, from third parties that they work with for their marketing efforts. Businesses that advertise on Facebook are required to have any necessary rights and permissions to use this information, as outlined in our Custom Audience Terms that businesses must agree to.

You can learn more about what influences the ads you see and control your ads experience by visiting Ad preferences. You can also learn more about why you are seeing an ad here.

Control the Ads You See

See more interesting and useful ads on Facebook by updating your ad preferences to reflect the things you care about. Managing your ad preferences is only possible in some areas right now.

This setting controls whether we can use information that other businesses or organizations send us about your activity on their websites, apps or in stores to show you more relevant content.

If you don’t allow us to use this activity to show you more relevant content, the content you see may still be based on other types of information, such as your activity on our platform. It may also be based on information from a specific business that has shared a list of individuals or devices with us, if we’ve matched your profile to information on that list. Additionally, if you connect information to Meta, the content you see may also be based on that information. This includes, for example, information from external accounts and apps you connect to Meta, like for shopping with certain retailers or to use with AI at Meta features.

The choice you make in your Activity from other businesses setting will apply to all of your accounts in the same Accounts Center. Regardless of your choice under this setting, businesses and organizations may send us your activity, and we may anonymize it or use it to improve our products as described in our Privacy Policy.

Your Ad preferences page lets you adjust the ads you see while on Facebook and gives you the ability to update your ad settings to control information we can use to show you ads.

View and adjust your Ad preferences

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Ad preferences.

Note: Not everyone will be able to access this setting in Meta Account or Accounts Center at this time. If these steps don’t work for you, try updating your app or go to accountscenter.facebook.com on your web browser.

From here, you can select Customize ads or Manage info.

In the Customize ads tab you can:

  • See your ad activity
  • Manage your ad topics
  • See the ads you’ve saved
  • Review advertisers you saw ads from

In the Manage info tab you can:

  • Manage information from your profile used to show you ads
  • Personalize ads based on your activity from other businesses
  • Choose if you get ads shown by Meta in other apps
  • Choose who can see your social interactions alongside ads

Note: Changing your ad preferences influences which ads you see, but it won’t change the total number of ads you see.

Advertisers you saw ads from

The Advertisers you saw ads from section of Ad preferences lets you see the advertisers we’ve shown you ads from most recently. These are advertisers we think will be most interesting and relevant to you based on your activity on and off Facebook. You can choose to hide ads from these advertisers and view which advertisers you’ve already hidden.

Hide ads from an advertiser

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Ad preferences.
  4. Click the Customize ads tab.
  5. Click See all next to Advertisers you saw ads from.
  6. Below Advertisers you saw ads from, you’ll see a list of advertisers. Click on any advertiser you want to hide ads from and then click Hide ads.

Note: Not everyone will be able to access this setting in Meta Account or Accounts Center at this time. If these steps don’t work for you, try updating your app or go to accountscenter.facebook.com on your web browser.

Learn more about why you see ads from certain advertisers.

Ad topics

Ad topics is a list of topics you can choose to see less of while on Facebook and Instagram. These include ad topics such as alcohol, parenting, pets and social issues, elections or politics. Please note, the social issues, elections or politics topic preference is not available in every country.

Adjust your Ad topic preferences

  1. Click on your profile picture in the top right, then click Settings & privacy.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Ad preferences.
  4. Click the Customize ads tab.
  5. Click See all next to Ad topics.
  6. Below Ad topics advertisers can use to reach you, you’ll see topics that represent interest categories advertisers can use to reach you. We add you to these categories based on your activity.
  7. To see less of an ad topic, click the topic you want to see less of and then select See less.

On the Ad topics page, you’ll now see this topic below Your ad topic choices. You can change your preference at any time by selecting a topic and choosing No preference.

You can also browse all ad topics and choose to see less of the ones you aren’t interested in by using the search bar at the top of the Ad topics page.

Note:

  • If you have linked your Facebook and Instagram accounts, your ad topic preference selections will apply across both accounts. If you have not linked your accounts, you can learn how to update your ad topic preferences for the ads you see on Instagram.
  • If you choose to see less of an ad topic, you won’t get as many ads about that topic, and advertisers can’t target you based on an interest in it. You may still see some ads related to these topics even if you chose to see less of them. If you do see an ad related to a topic that you chose to see fewer of, you can hide the ad, and we’ll use your feedback to improve the relevance of the ads you see.
  • If you add accounts to the same Accounts Center (for example, your Facebook and Instagram accounts), we’ll adjust this setting to match across your accounts. For ad topics you’ve selected to See less of, we’ve applied that preference to all accounts in the same Accounts Center.

Please note, all advertisers are subject to our ad policies. Ads that promote or reference restricted content categories must comply with all applicable local laws, required or established industry codes, guidelines, licenses and approvals, and include age and country targeting criteria consistent with Facebook’s targeting guidelines and applicable local laws.

Ad preferences

Your Ad preferences page also let you see how we’re using information to show ads we think will be most interesting for you and let you adjust how this information can be used to show you ads. In your Ad preferences page you can:

  • View common questions about how information is used to show you ads on Facebook.
  • Choose whether or not we can show you personalized ads based on your activity on other websites, apps or offline.
  • Review what information advertisers can use to reach you, such as certain Facebook Profile information and other categories, and choose whether this information can be used to show you ads.
  • View advertisers that can choose to show their ads to certain audiences you have been included in based on your activity or information and decide whether these audiences can be used to show you ads.
  • Choose how advertisers can reach you off of Meta Company Products.
  • Adjust who can see your social interactions alongside ads on Facebook.

Note: You can also visit the Accounts section in Accounts Center to control how your information is combined and used across your accounts, including for ads.

Learn more about how Facebook decides which ads to show you.

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

There are a few ways to give us feedback about the ads you see on Facebook. Giving us feedback may impact which ads we show you in the future. To give feedback:

  • Tell us more about what you like. Liking Pages and adding things you like to your profile (example: movies, bands, sports teams) will help us show you more relevant ads.
  • Hide ads you don’t like.
  • If you find an explanation confusing when using Why am I seeing this ad?, answer Was this information useful? to share feedback.
  • Adjust your ad preferences. To learn more about how Facebook uses information to show you ads, and to help influence the ads you see, adjust your ad preferences.
  • Update your Activity from other businesses setting in your ad preferences. Learn more about how to adjust how ads are shown to you based on your activity on and off Meta technologies.
  • Report an ad. When you report an ad, it is subjected to our ad review system. That process relies on automated tools, and in some cases manual review, to check ads against our Advertising Policies. When we detect a violation of our policies, we will remove the ad. We continuously review ads on our platform based on many signals, including user feedback, to improve the integrity and relevance of advertising on Facebook.

How Facebook ads use machine learning

How do ads use machine learning?

What determines which ads I see?

How does the ad auction work?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

[Embedded video omitted]

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

To decide which ads to show you, we use Advertiser audience selections and the results of our Ad auction to determine the best ad to show you at a given point in time.

Our machine learning models are part of our ads delivery system that learns as it receives new information, without being explicitly programmed.

This allows the machine learning models to carry out tasks quickly and efficiently, like delivering ads that might be relevant to you.

What determines which ads you see

The two main factors we use to determine which ads to show you are:

  • Advertiser audience selection
  • Results of our ad auction

During the ad auction our machine learning models calculate a “total value score” from three major factors: the advertiser bid, the estimated action rate and the ad quality score.

The ad with the highest total ad value is the one that is delivered to you.

Advertiser audience selection

When creating an ad campaign, advertisers first choose their desired audience through our business tools.

Advertisers can create audiences based on age, location, interests and categories. For example, some information you provide us, combined with actions you take, might suggest to us you’re interested in something, like cooking or fitness, or that you might be part of a larger group (called a category), like a mobile user.

Advertisers can also use information they have about their audiences, like a list of emails or people who’ve visited their website, to build a custom audience or a lookalike audience.

Note:

  • Advertisers can include teens in their audience based only on age and location.
  • When advertisers show ads about credit, employment or housing opportunities, we limit the categories they can choose to create an audience.

Ad auction

The second step we use is an ad auction to determine the best ads to show you at a given point in time. Our system gathers ads for which you were included in the advertiser’s selected audience and moves them to the auction stage.

For ads that enter the auction, our system selects the top ads to show to you based on which ads have the highest total value score.

To make sure the winning ad maximizes value for both people and businesses, the winner of the ad auction (which is the ad that is shown to you) is the ad with the highest total value score.

The total value score is a calculation that takes into account three major factors: the “advertiser bid”, the “estimated action rate” and the “ad quality.”

  • Advertiser bid. This is the bid placed by an advertiser for an ad. Because we use the total value score to determine the winner of the ad auction, an advertiser with the highest bid doesn’t always win the auction.
  • Estimated action rate. The estimated action rate is an estimate of how likely it is that you’ll take the advertiser’s desired action, like visiting the advertiser’s website or installing their app. To do this, our machine learning models may consider your activity on and off Meta technologies, as well as other factors.
  • Ad quality. The ad quality score is a measure of the quality of an ad. The ad quality score is determined by machine learning models and uses many sources including feedback of people viewing or hiding the ad, as well as assessments of low-quality attributes (like too much text in the ad’s image, sensationalized language or engagement bait).

The estimated action rates and ad quality help make sure that you see ads that are more relevant to you, even if that ad did not have the highest advertiser bid.

Note:

  • If an advertiser engages in clickbait and engagement bait, it does not improve the performance of their ad.
  • We may make adjustments that could affect auction outcomes and prices. Learn more about ad auctions adjustments.

How machine learning improves ad delivery

As more people view an ad, share feedback, or click through to make a purchase on an advertiser’s website, our models get better at predicting the estimated action rate and ad quality of an ad.

Ways to review and manage how you see ads

  • Customize your Ad preferences in Accounts Center to influence the ads you see. You can also update your Activity from other businesses settings to choose whether we use information that other businesses or organizations send us about your activity on their apps or websites, or your offline interactions with them such as in-store purchases, to show you ads. Note: you must be logged in to change your ad preferences and Information and permissions settings.
  • Hide an ad that isn’t interesting or useful to you or review why you’re seeing a particular ad.
  • Update your profile settings and walk through Privacy Checkup to make sure you’re sharing your information with who you want.
  • Visit Access your information in Accounts Center to see your Activity log, Facebook settings and Privacy Center for your Facebook profile.
  • Visit Export your information where you can export your information to a device or external service. Learn more about exporting your information.
  • Learn more about why you’re seeing an ad with the “Why am I seeing this ad?” tool that uses advertiser selections and machine learning models to show you more information about the ads you see.“Why am I seeing this ad?” allows you to tap on ads in your Facebook Feed, get context on why they’re appearing and take action to further personalize what you see. Learn more about why you may be seeing an ad.

Common misunderstandings about ads on Facebook

  • Meta does not sell your data to advertisers or anyone else.
  • We don’t share information that personally identifies you with advertisers unless you’ve given us permission.
  • Meta does not use the content of people’s text messages or phones’ microphone to inform ads or change what you see in your Facebook Feed.

To learn more about the information we receive and how we use it, visit our Privacy Policy and Cookies Policy.
