How ads work on Facebook

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

The ads you see depend on a number of factors.

Learn why you see specific ads

  1. Click Options in the top right of the ad.
  2. Click Why am I seeing this ad?. You’ll see factors that may have influenced why you saw this ad (for example, activity on Meta technologies or with the advertiser).
  3. If available, click Next to view more information about why you’re seeing an ad.

How machine learning helps us provide insight into why you saw an ad

We use machine learning models to help explain the insights you see in Why am I seeing this ad?. These models help surface how certain activity both on and off Meta technologies may have contributed to Facebook showing you a particular ad.

For example, liking a post, clicking on an ad, or activity on websites, apps, and products sent to us from advertisers contribute to these insights. Meta’s use of your activity off Meta technologies depends on your ad settings. While these insights don’t represent all the factors contributing to delivering an ad, we use them to provide you with an informative and understandable view into some of the factors that contributed to why you saw an ad.

How we decide which ads to show you

We want the ads you see on Facebook to be as interesting and useful to you as possible. These are examples of things we could use to decide which ads to show you:

  • Your activity on Facebook (such as liking a Page or clicking on ads you see). If you have linked your Facebook and Instagram accounts, your activity on Instagram may also affect the ads you see on Facebook. Depending on your region, your interactions with AI products may also affect the ads you see.

  • Content you create or interact with across Facebook and Instagram.

  • Other information about you from your Facebook account (example: your age, your gender, your location, the devices you use to access Facebook).

  • Information advertisers, their partners, and our marketing partners share with us that they already have, like your email address.

  • Additional policies are in place for ads shown to teens.

  • Your activity on websites and apps off of Facebook. Learn more about how to turn this off in your ad settings.

Your settings may not affect whether we use your information to avoid showing you certain ads. For example, we may not show you ads for something you’ve recently purchased.

Note:

  • Why am I seeing this ad? provides an explanation of some of the activity we think may have influenced why our ads delivery system showed you this ad.

  • Learn more about your activity by visiting Activity log or visit Export your information where you can export your information to a device or external service. Learn more about exporting your information.

  • We don’t share information that personally identifies you (information such as your name or email address that by itself can be used to contact you or identifies who you are) unless you give us permission. To learn more about the information Meta receives and how we use it, visit our Privacy Policy and Cookies Policy.

  • We use information you provide us, actions you’ve taken on our platforms and if applicable, actions you’ve taken on other websites, apps or in stores that those businesses or organizations have shared.

  • We do not use information with special protections, you choose to provide, to show you ads.

Learn more about how ads work on Facebook.

To adjust what ads you see

If you’re seeing ads that aren’t interesting to you, you can:

  • Adjust your ad preferences. Visit your Ad preferences page, where you can manage things like your interests and your profile information to get a more personalized experience. Learn more about your Ad preferences.
  • Update your ads based on activity from other businesses. You can choose whether we use information that other businesses or organizations send us about your activity on their apps or websites, or your offline interactions with them such as in-store purchases, to show you ads.
  • Hide ads from an advertiser. If you’re seeing an advertiser that isn’t interesting to you, you can hide an ad or hide an advertiser.

You can also manage your ad preferences in Accounts Center.

To give you transparency about the ads you see, advertisers may choose or be required to disclose information about themselves and their ads. Meta may also provide additional details about an ad or advertiser.

Here is some of the information you can learn about the ads you’re seeing on Facebook:

What is Audience Network?

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

If an advertiser is part of Meta’s Audience Network, you may see their ads outside of Meta platforms. This may include apps and websites on your mobile phone or computer. Meta uses data to determine the most relevant ads for you, and to help the advertiser reach the types of people they want to reach. Learn more about how Meta shows you ads.

Meta Audience Network connects advertisers with third-party app publishers who work with apps to show advertising. These apps offer ad space to multiple advertisers, or ad networks like Meta Audience Network, through real-time bidding auctions. This means that apps (or third parties on their behalf) send out real-time requests to advertisers or ad networks such as Meta Audience Network who may wish to bid on the right to show an ad in the app. The bid request may include information like the app you’re using and your device information, such as your advertising device ID.

If you have not provided permission for us to personalize the ads we show you based on your activity information from businesses and organizations that send us your activity, we’ll only use this activity information to do so after we’ve removed or combined information so we no longer know it’s yours.

You can learn what influences the ads you see and how to manage your ad experience on the About Ads page. Learn more about the information Meta receives and how we use it in our Privacy Policy and Cookies Policy.

You can opt out of ads shown by Meta’s Audience Network by updating your Ads in other apps setting in your Ad preferences.

Making ads better and giving you more control on Facebook

Manage my ad preferences

Control ads I see

Opt out of interest-based ads

Why am I seeing this ad?

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

When we ask people about our ads, one of the top things they tell us is that they want to see ads that relate to things they care about. We learn about this primarily from your activity on Facebook, such as Pages or posts you like and posts or comments you make. We may also learn about your interests from some of the websites and apps you use, depending on your settings. We call this online interest-based advertising, and many companies do this.

How does this work?

Let’s say that you’re thinking about buying a new TV, and you start researching TVs on the web and in mobile apps. Based on this activity, we may show you ads for deals on a TV to help you get the best price or other brands to consider. And because we think you’re interested in electronics, we may show you ads for other electronics in the future, like speakers or a game console to go with your new TV.

Meta adheres to the framework established by the Digital Advertising Alliance, Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada and the European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance, a coalition of organizations that develops privacy standards for online advertising, so if you don’t want us to use your activity information from websites and apps you use to show you ads that are more relevant to you, we won’t. If you don’t want Meta to use information based on your activity on websites or apps off Facebook for the purpose of showing you ads, you can opt out in your settings. You can also opt out from all participating companies through the Digital Advertising Alliance in the USA, the Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada in Canada or the European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance in Europe.

How do I manage the ads I see?

People also tell us they want more control over the ads they see. That’s why we have Ad preferences. Your Ad preferences page lets you manage your ad experience on Facebook. For example, if you’re not interested in electronics, you can choose to “see less” ads about electronics in the Ad topics setting in your ad preferences. You can also control whether we use information that other businesses or organizations send us about your activity on their apps or websites, or your offline interactions with them such as in-store purchases, to show you ads. You can do so in your Activity from other businesses setting, which is available from your Ad preferences.

You can also access your ad preferences from the “Why am I seeing this ad?” tool from every ad on Facebook. Learn more about why you are seeing an ad here.

To learn more, visit About Facebook Ads or read our Cookies Policy.

Personalized ads

If you choose personalized ads, you can discover products and brands that relate to your interests and activity on Meta Company Products.

We’ll use your information for ads, including the following:

  • Your activity on our products, such as if you like Pages or comment on posts.
  • How you engage with ads, such as clicking or liking them.
  • Content you view or interact with on our products.
  • Topics we think you may be interested in.
  • Your profile information, such as your age, gender you provide, location, work and education

We’ll also use your interactions with ads you see to personalize features and experiences for you. Learn more about the information we use for ads in the Privacy Policy.

Less-personalized ads

If you choose less-personalized ads, you’ll have a different ad experience. You’ll see a variety of products and brands through ads that are less related to your interests. Your browsing may be paused by ad breaks. Your ability to advertise and monetize with ads will be limited. Learn more about these limitations.

We’ll use some of your information for ads:

  • How you engage with ads, such as clicking or liking them
  • Your age, the gender you provide and your location
  • Your device information, like the device or browser you’re using
  • Information about the content you’re viewing while you browse on our products.
  • For example, Bente opens Instagram in the morning and scrolls her Feed. She sees ads based on the content she’s viewing while she browses. This information is used to show her ads only while she’s browsing this time. When she opens Instagram again in the afternoon, she sees ads related to the content she’s viewing while she browses this time. Her ads are not based on the content she viewed while browsing last time.

You’ll also no longer have access to some Ad preferences that aren’t relevant to you, because we won’t use that information to show you less-personalized ads.

Use Meta Company Products free of charge with ads

What to expect with ads?

Manage my ad preferences

Why am I seeing this ad?

This subscription is only available in the European Region and the United Kingdom.

By choosing to use our products free of charge, you can discover new products and brands through ads.

Here’s what to expect when you use our products free of charge with ads:

  • You will see ads when you use Meta Company Products.
  • We’ll process your information from your accounts in the same Accounts Center to show you ads.
  • We’ll use cookies on our products to personalize your ads and measure how they perform.
  • We’ll process your information for ads, including information you provide, your activity on Meta Company Products, your connections, app, browser and device information, depending on the ad experience you choose. Learn more about this info and how we show personalized ads.

If you’re already using our products free of charge with ads, your experience will stay the same, and your previous ad preferences and choices will continue to apply. For example, if you allow us to, we will continue to use your activity information from ad partners to show you ads, and use cookies on other apps and websites to personalize your ads and measure how they perform. You can change these choices at any time.

Once you choose to use our products free of charge, your choice will apply to all your accounts in the same Accounts Center. Learn more about how we process information across your accounts in Accounts Center.

Why does Meta ask for my consent?

If you choose to use our products free of charge with ads, you will be asked to allow Meta to process your information for ads. Laws require that you should be able to freely choose if you opt-in to the processing of your information involving combining and cross-using your information and certain use of cookies. Meta relies on your consent as our legal basis for this information processing. You can withdraw your consent at any time.

Other ways to manage your ads

  • Manage whether you see personalized or less personalized ads. Learn more about this choice.
  • Adjust other Ad preferences. Visit your Ad preferences page, where you can manage things like your ad topics and recent ad activity.
  • Learn more about why you’re seeing an ad. “Why am I seeing this ad?” provides an explanation of some of the activity that may have influenced why our ads delivery system showed you this ad.
  • Hide ads from an advertiser. If you’re seeing an ad or advertiser that isn’t interesting to you, you can hide an ad or hide ads from an advertiser.
  • Opt out from all participating companies. If you don’t want us to use the websites and apps you use to show you more relevant ads, we won’t. You can opt out through the European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance. Or opt out using your mobile device settings.

If you prefer to use our products without ads, you can choose to subscribe. If you subscribe, you won’t see ads when you use your Facebook, Instagram, Threads or WhatsApp accounts that are in the same Accounts Center.

We are committed to your privacy and keeping your information secure. Learn more in the Privacy Policy and Cookies Policy.

Why am I seeing ads from an advertiser on Facebook?

Manage my ad preferences

Why am I seeing this ad?

Control activity off Meta

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

[Embedded video omitted]

We want the ads you see on Facebook to be personalized to your interests and to introduce you to new things. Here are some of the factors we might consider to show you ads.

Your activity on Meta technologies

Some of your activity across the Meta Products may help us show you ads that we think you might be interested in. Your activity on Meta technologies might include:

  • Pages on Facebook you’ve liked.
  • Ads you’ve clicked on.
  • Content you create or interact with across Facebook and Instagram.
  • Places you’ve checked in to using Facebook.
  • Liking a post.
  • Depending on your region, your interactions with AI products.

Your activity off Meta technologies

Your activity off Meta technologies is activity that other businesses and organizations share with us about your interactions with them, such as visiting their apps or websites or in-store purchases. These businesses and organizations may send us this information via our Business Tools. We then use this information to do things like give you a more personalized experience on Facebook.

You can choose whether we use this activity information to show you ads and other content, in your Activity from other businesses setting.

Advertiser choices

Advertisers want to connect with people they think will enjoy their products, so they make choices about who to show their ads to. You can find information about these choices in the Advertiser choices section of Why am I seeing this ad?

A few things advertisers could use that help them show you more personalized ads:

Profile information. Your age, location or other information you provide on your profile. If you haven’t selected a gender, we may show you ads associated with a gender. Gender may be based on inferences from your profile and activity. We limit the options advertisers can use to show ads to teens.

Interests and categories. Some information you provide us, combined with your activity on or off Meta technologies, may help us think you’re interested in something, like cooking or fitness, or that you might be part of a larger group (called a category), like a mobile user. We can use your interests and categories to connect you with businesses who we think you might be interested in and advertisers can choose to include people with specific interests or who belong to certain categories of people in their audiences.

Lookalike audiences. A lookalike audience is a way for advertisers to use Facebook to reach people that may be similar to people that have already shown an interest in their business. We use some of the things you do or information you give us to help create lookalike audiences.

For example, an advertiser might tell us they’d like to show ads to people who may be similar to people who are already interested in their business (such as people who’ve liked their Page or visited their website). We match things like the interests or demographics (example: your city) of the people who are already interested in the business to help show ads to other people that we think might be interested in the advertiser’s business or products.

Custom audiences. Custom audiences are a way for advertisers to show their ads to a group of people who may have already interacted with their business. A few ways we help advertisers make Custom audiences:

  • Your activity on a business’s website or app. Advertisers can choose to add our Business Tools, like the Meta Pixel or Facebook SDK, to their website or app. These tools allow the advertiser to send information about people’s interactions on their website or app to Facebook, such as when someone makes a purchase or opens their app. This helps us show you ads that we think may be interesting to you.

  • Lists from a business. Advertisers may get information from you (like your email address) when you interact with them outside of Facebook, like if you make a purchase in their store or create an account for a rewards program. They can create a hashed list with that information and upload it to Facebook. We can match users using the list to help the advertiser reach people who may be interested in their business and without Facebook learning any new identifying information about you. If you see another company using a list for an advertiser, it’s likely because the advertiser is working with an advertising agency. For example, if Company X hires Agency Y to run its ads, Agency Y would upload its own list to Facebook and Company X would use that list to show you ads.

  • Offline activity. Offline activity is activity you may do in a store, like make a purchase. If a business gives us this information, we can use it to help show their ads to people who may be interested in their business. We can also help businesses reach the right people by letting them know if their customers have engaged with their ads on Facebook or other Meta technologies.

Location information: We may use your location information to show you ads from advertisers trying to reach people in or near a specific place. We get this information from things such as:

  • Where you connect to the internet.
  • Where you use your phone.
  • Your location from your Facebook and Instagram profile.

How machine learning helps us provide insight into why you saw an ad

We use machine learning models that mirror our ads delivery models to provide the insights found in Why am I seeing this ad? These models help surface how certain activity both on and off Meta technologies may have contributed to Facebook showing you a particular ad.

For example, activities such as liking a post, clicking on an ad, or activity on websites, apps and products sent to us from advertisers can all contribute to why you’re seeing an ad. Meta’s use of your activity off Meta technologies depends on your ad settings. While these insights don’t represent all the factors contributing to delivering an ad, we use them to provide you with an informative and understandable view into some of the factors that contributed to why you saw an ad.

Ways to review and manage your information:

  • Customize your Ad preferences to see ads that are more relevant to you. From there, you can update your ad settings to control things like if we show you ads based on your use of apps and websites off Meta technologies. You can also update your ad preferences from Accounts Center.
  • Tell us you don’t want to see an ad that isn’t interesting or useful to you, or review why you’re seeing a particular ad.
  • Update your profile settings and walk through Privacy Checkup to make sure you’re sharing your information with who you want.
  • Visit Access your information in Accounts Center to see your Activity log, Facebook settings and Privacy Center for your Facebook profile.
  • Visit Export your information where you can export your information to a device or external service. Learn more about exporting your information.

To learn more about the information we receive and how we use it, visit our Privacy Policy and Cookies Policy.

Adjust my ad preferences

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Your Ad preferences page lets you adjust the ads you see while on Facebook and gives you the ability to update your ad settings to control information we can use to show you ads.

View and adjust your Ad preferences

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Ad preferences.

Note: Not everyone will be able to access this setting in Meta Account or Accounts Center at this time. If these steps don’t work for you, try updating your app or go to accountscenter.facebook.com on your web browser.

From here, you can select Customize ads or Manage info.

In the Customize ads tab you can:

  • See your ad activity
  • Manage your ad topics
  • See the ads you’ve saved
  • Review advertisers you saw ads from

In the Manage info tab you can:

  • Manage information from your profile used to show you ads
  • Personalize ads based on your activity from other businesses
  • Choose if you get ads shown by Meta in other apps
  • Choose who can see your social interactions alongside ads

Note: Changing your ad preferences influences which ads you see, but it won’t change the total number of ads you see.

Advertisers you saw ads from

The Advertisers you saw ads from section of Ad preferences lets you see the advertisers we’ve shown you ads from most recently. These are advertisers we think will be most interesting and relevant to you based on your activity on and off Facebook. You can choose to hide ads from these advertisers and view which advertisers you’ve already hidden.

Hide ads from an advertiser

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Ad preferences.
  4. Click the Customize ads tab.
  5. Click See all next to Advertisers you saw ads from.
  6. Below Advertisers you saw ads from, you’ll see a list of advertisers. Click on any advertiser you want to hide ads from and then click Hide ads.

Note: Not everyone will be able to access this setting in Meta Account or Accounts Center at this time. If these steps don’t work for you, try updating your app or go to accountscenter.facebook.com on your web browser.

Learn more about why you see ads from certain advertisers.

Ad topics

Ad topics is a list of topics you can choose to see less of while on Facebook and Instagram. These include ad topics such as alcohol, parenting, pets and social issues, elections or politics. Please note, the social issues, elections or politics topic preference is not available in every country.

Adjust your Ad topic preferences

  1. Click on your profile picture in the top right, then click Settings & privacy.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Ad preferences.
  4. Click the Customize ads tab.
  5. Click See all next to Ad topics.
  6. Below Ad topics advertisers can use to reach you, you’ll see topics that represent interest categories advertisers can use to reach you. We add you to these categories based on your activity.
  7. To see less of an ad topic, click the topic you want to see less of and then select See less.

On the Ad topics page, you’ll now see this topic below Your ad topic choices. You can change your preference at any time by selecting a topic and choosing No preference.

You can also browse all ad topics and choose to see less of the ones you aren’t interested in by using the search bar at the top of the Ad topics page.

Note:

  • If you have linked your Facebook and Instagram accounts, your ad topic preference selections will apply across both accounts. If you have not linked your accounts, you can learn how to update your ad topic preferences for the ads you see on Instagram.
  • If you choose to see less of an ad topic, you won’t get as many ads about that topic, and advertisers can’t target you based on an interest in it. You may still see some ads related to these topics even if you chose to see less of them. If you do see an ad related to a topic that you chose to see fewer of, you can hide the ad, and we’ll use your feedback to improve the relevance of the ads you see.
  • If you add accounts to the same Accounts Center (for example, your Facebook and Instagram accounts), we’ll adjust this setting to match across your accounts. For ad topics you’ve selected to See less of, we’ve applied that preference to all accounts in the same Accounts Center.

Please note, all advertisers are subject to our ad policies. Ads that promote or reference restricted content categories must comply with all applicable local laws, required or established industry codes, guidelines, licenses and approvals, and include age and country targeting criteria consistent with Facebook’s targeting guidelines and applicable local laws.

Ad preferences

Your Ad preferences page also let you see how we’re using information to show ads we think will be most interesting for you and let you adjust how this information can be used to show you ads. In your Ad preferences page you can:

  • View common questions about how information is used to show you ads on Facebook.
  • Choose whether or not we can show you personalized ads based on your activity on other websites, apps or offline.
  • Review what information advertisers can use to reach you, such as certain Facebook Profile information and other categories, and choose whether this information can be used to show you ads.
  • View advertisers that can choose to show their ads to certain audiences you have been included in based on your activity or information and decide whether these audiences can be used to show you ads.
  • Choose how advertisers can reach you off of Meta Company Products.
  • Adjust who can see your social interactions alongside ads on Facebook.

Note: You can also visit the Accounts section in Accounts Center to control how your information is combined and used across your accounts, including for ads.

Add a trusted email domain in Admin Center

Why trust a domain?

Domain verification approval

My domain is automatically trusted

If you are an admin with permissions to add and remove email domains for your organization’s managed Meta accounts, then you can add a trusted domain in Admin Center.

You may want to trust a domain in Admin Center if you are unable to verify the domain or if you don’t own the domain. For example, if your organization uses managed Meta accounts for business tools such as Meta Business Suite, then you may want to trust an email domain that’s owned by an organization you work with (example: an external agency) to help make it easier for people who work there to join your business portfolio.

Note: All admins in Admin Center and Device Manager (if relevant) as well as anyone using a managed Meta account for business tools (example: Meta Business Suite) must use an email domain that’s been verified or trusted in Admin Center. If your organization has a subscription to Meta Horizon managed services, then you can choose to restrict access to only people using a verified or trusted domain.

Trust a domain in Admin Center

To trust an email domain in Admin Center:

  1. Click Security in the left menu of Admin Center.
    • To do this, you need the right permissions and you need to be logged into Admin Center.
  2. Click Domain verification.
  3. Click Verify a new domain in the top right.
  4. Enter the domain name, select No, trust this domain, then click Continue.

If there are multiple admins in your organization, then an approval request will be sent to them by email to approve trusting this domain.

If you are the only admin in your organization and you’ve been using Admin Center for under 90 days, then you will receive an email asking you to confirm that this is a trusted domain. If your organization has been using Admin Center for 90 days or more, then you will need to add another admin and they will need to approve trusting this domain.

Note: The domain of the person’s account who set up Admin Center automatically becomes a trusted domain.

Add or edit membership/participation questions for a Facebook group you admin, and view answers

Add membership questions

Edit membership questions

View member answers

If you’re a group admin, you can ask people who request to join or participate in your group to answer up to 3 questions to help you decide whether or not to approve them. In public groups, these are called participation questions. In private groups, these are called membership questions, unless limited membership is turned on.

If limited membership is turned on, people can automatically join your private group without admin approval as limited members. Limited members can see your group’s content and react, but won’t be able to post, comment, or chat until they’ve been approved by an admin to participate. Instead of membership questions, you can add participation questions to help you decide whether or not to approve a limited member to participate in your group. When you turn on limited membership, any membership questions you previously set up for your private group will become participation questions.

Questions are limited to 200 characters.

Responding to membership and participation questions isn’t mandatory. However, admins can use Admin Assist to automatically approve or decline people based on whether or not they answered the questions.

Add or edit questions

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Manage in the left menu.
  3. For private groups, click Membership questions (or Participation questions if limited membership is turned on). For public groups, click Participation questions.
  4. Click Create or Edit.
  5. Add or edit the question.
  6. Choose a question type: Checkboxes, Multiple choice or Written answer.

View someone’s answers after you’ve approved them

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Members or People at the top of the group. If you don’t see Members or People, click More.
  3. Find the person whose answers you want to view and click their name.
  4. Scroll down to Membership questions or Participation questions and click View answers.

Admins can’t view someone’s responses if they answered the questions before July 2021.

Note:

  • If a prospective member exits without answering the questions, their request to join or participate will still go through.
  • If they did not answer the questions, prospective members and participants will receive 4 automatic notifications (after 3 hours and after 1, 2 and 3 days). Notifications will stop after 3 days.
  • Members and participants can edit their answers.

Only system admins can assign admin roles to people in Admin Center.

An admin role can be assigned or removed from Directory or Admin roles in Admin Center. You may want to manage roles from Directory if you want to change 1 person’s permissions, or from Admin roles if you want to change permissions for many individuals or a group.

By default, people have no admin permissions when they’re given a managed Meta account. Learn about age requirements for Admin Center access.

For customers with a subscription to Meta Horizon managed services, assigning admin roles in Admin Center is different to assigning roles in Device Manager.

Note: The way you assign admin roles to people from an external organization is different than the below instructions.

Change someone’s permissions in Directory

You may want to manage roles in Directory if you want to change 1 person’s permissions. To do this:

  1. Click Account management in the left menu of Admin Center.
  2. Click the name of the person whose role you want to change.
    • You can filter the directory by name or email to find the person’s account more quickly.
  3. Click the Access tab.
  4. Click Manage admin roles.
  5. To assign someone an admin role:
    • In the Available tab, click the checkboxes next to the roles you want to assign. Then, click Confirm.
  6. To remove someone’s admin role:
    • If you want to remove all roles, then you need to click Remove as admin, then Confirm. If you want to remove some but not all roles then, in the Assigned tab, click the checkboxes next to the roles you want to remove, then click Confirm.

Change people’s permissions in Admin roles

You may want to manage roles in Admin roles if you’re making changes for many people at once, or a group. To do this:

  1. Click Account management in the left menu of Admin Center.
  2. Click Admin roles in the menu.
  3. Click the name of the admin role.
  4. In the Individuals tab you can:
    • Assign this role to someone by clicking Assign role to individuals, selecting the people you want to assign the role to, then clicking Assign role.
    • Remove this role from someone by clicking Options to the right of their name, selecting Remove admin role then confirming by clicking Remove role.
  5. In the Groups tab, you can:
    • Assign this role to a group by clicking Assign role to groups, selecting the groups you want to assign the role to, then clicking Assign role.
    • Remove this role from a group by clicking Options to the right of the group’s name, selecting Remove admin role, then confirming by clicking Remove role.

Blocked from sending friend requests on Facebook

Why am I blocked?

How to avoid future blocks?

My requests were unwelcome

How long is the block?

If you’re currently not able to send friend requests, this is usually because:

  • You recently sent a lot of friend requests.
  • Your past friend requests have gone unanswered.
  • Your past friend requests were marked as unwelcome. Though we can’t lift the block early, it’s temporary and will end automatically within a few days.

It’s important to us that people only receive friend requests from people they know or have a real-life connection to. We understand that this can be frustrating, and that you might not have known about our friending policies. To help keep Facebook an open and welcoming experience for everyone, we try to prevent people from unintentionally sending unwanted friend requests.

To avoid being blocked in the future, consider the following when sending friend requests:

  • Try to only send friend requests to people you already know (example: family, friends, coworkers, classmates).
  • To connect with people you don’t know (like celebrities), follow them instead of sending them a friend request.
  • Make sure you’re using the name you go by in everyday life. People you know may accidentally miss your friend requests if they don’t recognize you.

Browsers that support video calling on Facebook

Create managed Meta accounts for people in your organization in Admin Center

Create managed accounts

Connect identity provider

Create multiple accounts

If you’re an admin with relevant permissions, then you can create managed Meta accounts for people in your organization. You can create accounts directly in Admin Center or by connecting a third-party identity provider (IdP) including Google Workspace, Okta and Microsoft Azure AD.

Managed Meta accounts can be used for products connected in Admin Center. You can also assign admin permissions to a managed Meta account.

Learn about age requirements for managed Meta accounts.

Connect an identity provider to set up automated provisioning of managed accounts

If you have Admin Center permissions to connect identity providers, then you can connect Google Workspace Directory, Microsoft Entra ID or Okta in Admin Center. If you want to connect a different IdP, or you want to connect multiple identity providers, then you need to set up a custom integration.

Connecting an IdP is a good option if you’re creating many accounts and/or you want account changes (such as deactivation) to be managed automatically through the IdP.

To connect Google Workspace Directory, Microsoft Entra ID or Okta in Admin Center:

  1. Click Account management in the left menu of Admin Center.
    • To do this, you need the right permissions and you need to be logged into Admin Center.
  2. Click Automated provisioning in the menu.
  3. Click Set up automated provisioning. Alternatively, click Add integration in the top right.
  4. Select one of the listed identity providers then follow instructions in Admin Center for your choice.

Create accounts directly in Admin Center

If you have admin permissions to manage your organization’s directory, then you can create managed accounts directly in Admin Center. These accounts need to be manually managed.

To create accounts directly in Admin Center:

  1. Click Account management in the left menu of Admin Center.
    • To do this, you need the right permissions and you need to be logged into Admin Center.
  2. Click Create accounts, then select Create an account or Create multiple accounts.
    • Alternatively, you can click Import a CSV or XLSX. Follow instructions in Admin Center to complete this.
  3. Enter the name(s) and email address(es) of the accounts you want to create, then click Confirm or Add people.

After accounts have been created

When a managed account has been created for someone, you can see it in Directory in Admin Center. You may need to wait a few minutes and refresh the page to see the accounts after you have added them.

People need to activate their account after it has been created for them.

Learn how to create a group of managed accounts. Groups help you manage who has access to different products connected in Admin Center.

How to request a review of a fact-check rating

Request review of content

Appeal misinformation violation

Guidelines for review

What happens after review?

This Request review feature is available to users to request a review of a specific fact-check on your content. In cases where the feature is unavailable, you can send review requests to fact-checkers through email. If your content was matched by Meta’s technology to a fact-checker rating, Meta processes those review requests. Read more about how to request a review below.

We’re committed to fighting the spread of false information on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads. In certain countries, we work with independent fact-checkers who are certified through the non-partisan International Fact-Checking Network to help identify and review false information. Fact checkers check and rate the accuracy of information in the content that you share.

Meta may take a number of different actions on content or accounts that go against our policies – both policies about actions we take when a fact-checker rates content as false and separate policies like those about what is and isn’t allowed on our platforms. Fact-checkers are not responsible for these actions, which include but are not limited to:

  • Processing review requests on Community Standards violations. You can request a review of Community Standards violations on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads.
  • Removing content from Facebook, Instagram, and Threads.
  • Removing or blocking Pages and accounts.
  • Reducing the distribution of false information on Facebook, Instagram, and Threads.

Fact-checkers may rate a piece of content shared from:

  • Your profile
  • A Page you have Facebook access with full control of
  • A group your an admin of

They can process review requests for content or ads they directly rated. When Meta enforces on content or ads that are identical to what fact-checking partners have debunked, Meta processes those review requests.

You can request a review if you corrected the rated content or ad. You can also dispute a fact-check rating for content or ad you created if you believe that the rating is inaccurate. To request a review of fact-checked content or ad that fact-checkers directly rated, or Meta’s technology matched to fact-checker ratings, follow these instructions.

How to request a review

  • To request a review of fact-checked content from your profile, go to Profile Status.
  • To request a review of fact-checked content from a Page you’re the owner of, go to Page Status.
  • To request a review of fact-checked content from a group you’re the admin of, go to Group Status.
  • To request a review of fact-checked content for your ad, go to Business Support Home.

Each one of those locations will show the fact-checks that have been applied and any restrictions Meta placed on the profile, Page, group or advertising account as a result.

Note:

  • You can’t request a review of decisions about content your group or Page shared but didn’t create.
  • You can request a review of a fact-check rating once.

Guidelines for requesting a review

  • Submit your review within 7 days.
  • Deleting a post or ad will make it impossible for your review to be processed. Don’t delete the post if you would like to request a review.
  • Make sure you include all relevant information in your requested review. Fact checkers or Meta may experience delays or be unable to process your review without that information. Meta will auto-reject requests for a review after 14 days if they have not yet been processed.

Additional information on review requests fact-checkers process:

  • Fact checkers are not required to respond to requested reviews that include harassment, hateful conduct or other threatening language.
  • Fact checkers try to process requested reviews within 3 business days and will notify you of their decision on your appeal.
  • If your content is rated by multiple fact checkers, your review request will automatically be sent to every fact checker that rated your post. Every fact checker must update their ratings in order for the enforcement to be lifted entirely.

What happens once a requested review has been processed

If a fact checker or Meta decides to change a rating based on a correction or dispute:

  • Meta will no longer add an informational label or move the content lower in Feed.
  • Disapproved ads associated with the post may be allowed to run.
  • We will no longer count the fact check rating against our policies where people who repeatedly share content rated False or Altered will be put under some restrictions for a given time period.

It may take a few days for these updates to happen. Page owners can go to Page Status, Group admin can go to Group Status, and users can go to Profile Status to see their current status, including whether any fact checks continue to be applied to their content. Advertisers can go to Business Support Home to see the current status of their ad.

Identity provider custom integrations in Admin Center (Allow custom integration to manage accounts)

Create custom integration

Allow custom integration to manage accounts

Generate new bearer token

SCIM integration with JumpCloud

Admins with permissions to connect identity providers can create an identity provider custom integration in Admin Center. You may need to do this if your organization wants to connect an identity provider that you can’t connect directly in Admin Center, or if you want to connect multiple identity providers.

Identity providers that are connected in Admin Center, either directly or via a custom integration, can be used to automatically create and manage accounts in your organization.

Create a custom integration

Learn how to set up custom integrations in our API documentation.

Allow the identity provider added by custom integration to add and manage accounts

After you’ve created the custom integration, you can allow it to add and manage accounts for your organization. To do this:

  1. Click Account management in the left menu of Admin Center.
    • To do this, you need the right permissions and you need to be logged into Admin Center.
  2. Click Automated provisioning in the menu.
  3. Click the name of your integration.
  4. Click the API access tab.
  5. Click the checkbox next to Manage accounts, then click Save.

Generate a new bearer token

When you reset the access token for your custom integration, any API calls that depend on the existing token and app secret will stop working.

If you need to reset your integration’s access token, then:

  1. Click Account management in the left menu of Admin Center.
    • To do this, you need the right permissions and you need to be logged into Admin Center.
  2. Click Automated provisioning in the menu.
  3. Click the name of your integration.
  4. In the Details tab, click Reset and copy token.
  5. Make sure Long lived token is selected for the access token type, then click Reset token.

It may be worth securely storing this token for further use. Delete any copies after the integration setup is complete. Only share the token with app developers you trust – anyone with access to the token will be able to access information about your organization.

How Identity Provider data works with Admin Center

In order for an Identity Provider to work correctly when integrated via Admin Center, the data from the integration must follow these rules:

  • Meta requires the username to be a valid email address within your organization.
  • Meta requires email addresses to be unique across all users in an organization.
  • Meta will automatically add an email entry matching the username and set it as the primary email if required.
  • Meta will only contact users via their primary email address and will only display the primary email address for the managed Meta account.
  • Meta allows SSO login to be configured against any of a user’s email addresses.

Using third-party SCIM integrations

You can use JumpCloud or PingFederate when configured for SCIM 2.0 using Bearer Tokens, to set up accounts in Admin Center.

Overview of Meta Admin Center

Get access to Admin Center

Set up Admin Center

Create managed accounts

I can’t access Admin Center

Admin Center allows organization admins to create and manage Meta accounts for people in their organization, as well as manage security settings and connected products.

Getting access to Admin Center

Your organization can get access to Admin Center through Meta Horizon managed services or by migrating to managed accounts for business tools such as Meta Business Suite.

People can only access your organization’s Admin Center if they are given admin permissions. If people have a managed account without admin permissions, then they will only be able to view their own account details in the Accounts Center for their managed account.

The URL for the Admin Center homepage is L (l.facebook.com). If you cannot access this link, then you do not have admin permissions for your organization.

Setting up Admin Center

The first tasks for setting up Admin Center include ensuring your organization receives emails from work.meta.com and verifying your organization’s email domain(s).

Creating managed accounts

Admins can create managed accounts for other people in their organization, to be used to access products connected in Admin Center, such as business tools (example: Meta Business Suite) or Meta Horizon managed services. Accounts can be created by connecting a third-party identity provider or by creating accounts directly in Admin Center.

People need to activate their account after it has been created for them.

Logging in with a managed account

People log into their managed account either with a password or using single-sign on (SSO).

Removing browser add-ons or extensions

Remove a browser add-on

Malicious add-ons

Stop Facebook working

Add-on permissions

Most web browsers support useful third party add-ons (example: plugins, extensions) that can add new features and functionality. However, if an add-on or extension is malicious, it may cause you to experience spam, cause your Facebook account to send unwanted messages by itself or allow third parties to view and copy your Facebook information, also known as scraping. Certain extensions, such as ad blockers, can stop Facebook from working properly.

If you think your web browser add-ons may be malicious, you can remove them:

Mozilla Firefox

Internet Explorer

Google Chrome

Safari

Microsoft Edge

Opera

Note: Extensions can request certain permissions when added to your browser, including permission to read or edit data on websites you visit. If a malicious browser extension is granted permission to read or change information while you’re logged into Facebook, it can potentially view or change your Facebook information.

Facebook can’t control how a browser extension uses its permissions or prevent it from viewing your information if you give it permission to view your information on Facebook, so we recommend only using extensions that don’t request these permissions and only using extensions from developers you know and trust.

Request a verified badge on Facebook

Request a verified badge

Requirements for verification

I can’t get verified

What is Meta Verified?

Some verified accounts are owned by a notable person, brand, or entity, while others are subscribed to Meta Verified.

  • Verified badges mean an account has been verified based on their activity across our products and information or documents they provide.
  • Meta Verified is a paid subscription that comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

If you already have an existing verified badge based on prior requirements, you can still subscribe to Meta Verified.

We encourage admins of verified Pages and profiles to use two-factor authentication.

We verify an account based on its activity across our products and the information or documents provided.

A Facebook Page or profile with a verified badge next to it now indicates that Facebook has confirmed that it is the authentic presence for that person or brand. The verified badge used to require notability and uniqueness. You may still see users with a verified badge that represents our previous eligibility requirements.

Verify your profile or Page

Subscribe to Meta Verified to get a verified badge for your profile. Check the eligibility criteria for Meta Verified.

You can also apply for the verified badge for a profile or Page if you are a public figure, celebrity or brand and meet certain account and eligibility requirements outlined below.

Note: Meta Verified is available to verify profiles only, not Pages. Notable Pages can still apply for a verified badge. As we test and learn, there will be no immediate changes to accounts on Instagram or Facebook that are already verified based on prior requirements.

Requirements to apply for a verified badge

We evaluate Facebook Pages and profiles based on several factors to determine if they meet our verification criteria.

Pages and profiles must follow our terms and Community Standards, and be:

  • Authentic: Represent a real person, registered business or entity.
  • Unique: Be the only presence of this person or business. Only one Page or profile per person or business may be verified, with exceptions for language-specific Pages and profiles. We don’t verify general interest Pages and profiles (example: Puppy Memes).
  • Complete: Have an about section, Page or profile photo and recent activity, including at least one post.
  • Notable: Represent a well-known, often searched person, brand or entity. We review Pages and profiles that are featured in multiple news sources, and we don’t consider paid or promotional content as sources for review.

If you don’t meet the criteria, you can still show your Page or profile is authentic in other ways.

For example, you can link to it from an official website, Instagram profile or Twitter account. You can also subscribe to Meta Verified to get a verified badge for your profile.

Once an account is memorialized, the content the person shared (example: photos, posts) remains on Facebook and is visible to the audience with whom it was shared. If the account holder chose a legacy contact, the legacy contact can control who can post tributes on the memorialized account and who can see those tributes.

In rare cases, we consider requests for additional account information or content. You’ll be required to provide proof that you’re an authorized representative (example: family member) and a court order. Please keep in mind that sending a request or filing the required documentation doesn’t guarantee that we’ll be able to provide you with the content of the deceased person’s account. In addition, we’ll memorialize the deceased person’s account once we receive your request.

If you’d like to send us a request, please contact us.

Requesting release of your Page’s ownership from a Business Account

Request Page ownership release

Page release pending

Page linked to Instagram

I can’t request release

Business Manager Admins can only approve and reject requests in Meta Business Suite.

You can request release of Page ownership on Business Accounts if you have full Facebook access to a Page. The request has 30 days pending period to be approved or declined before expiration. All admins of the Page cannot send another request if the request is pending.

After the request has been submitted, the current Business Manager admin of the Page will receive an email notification that can guide them through the process.   5. Click Page setup in the left menu, then click Page access.
  6. Below Business Account access, tap Request release next to the Page you want released. You’ll only see this if your Page has a Business Account owner.

Send message requests from your Page

How do I send a message request?

How do I send a message to a Page?

How do I send a message to a profile?

How do I turn on messaging for my Page?

This feature is gradually rolling out and may not be available for all Pages yet.

A Page can send up to 10 new message requests per day to start conversations with people and Pages (followers or non-followers).

Note: This does not change your Page’s ability to send a direct message to reply to a person who has commented on your Page’s Post or on a post in a Facebook Group that you manage.

Eligibility for message recipients

In order for your Page to start a conversation with someone, the person or Page you are trying to reach must:

  • Depending on whether the person follows your Page or not, they must have message delivery settings turned on to receive messages from Pages they follow or Pages they don’t follow.
  • Be an adult based on the laws in your country.
  • Be based in a country where this feature is available.

In order for your Page to send a message request to another Page, the Page you are trying to reach must:

  • Have messaging turned on.
  • Not have blocked the sending Page.
  • Depending on whether you are following the receiving Page or if they follow your Page, the receiving Page must allow messages from you in their messaging audience controls. If they don’t, their settings will prevent you from messaging them.

Eligibility for Pages

At this time, Pages with a large number of followers are eligible to send messages to followers. Additionally, a Page must:

  • Have messaging turned on for your Page.
  • Have at least one adult (non-minor) admin.
  • Be based in a country where this feature is available. (Note: Even if available in your country, this feature may not be rolled out to all Pages yet.)

Depending on the laws in your country, before sending a message request to a follower, you may need to ensure that your Page has first obtained the follower’s consent or opt-in.

Send a message to Page or profile

Make sure that you’re switched into your Page before sending a message.

To send a message by going to their Facebook profile or Page:

  1. Switch to the Page you want to send a message from.
  2. Go to a follower’s profile or Page
  3. Tap Message under their profile picture. On some pages, you might find this option after you tap .
  4. Type your message in the text box at the bottom.
  5. Tap .

To send a message via the Messenger app:

  1. Switch to the Page you want to send a message from.
  2. Tap to open the Messenger app.
  3. Tap .
  4. Type in the name of a user or Page.
  5. Type your message in the text box at the bottom.
  6. Tap .

Set up single sign-on in Admin Center for your organization’s managed Meta accounts

Enable SSO for my organization

Add an identity provider

What are break-glass accounts?

Set up reauthentication settings

If you’re an admin with permissions to set up and manage single sign-on (SSO) for your organization’s managed Meta accounts, then you can add an identity provider (IdP) that manages user authentication to Admin Center. This enables people to be able to log into their managed account using the same SSO credentials they use with other systems in your organization.

We recommend you verify your organization’s email domain(s) before enabling SSO.

Note: Setting up SSO is required for organizations migrating to managed Meta accounts for business tools (example: Meta Business Suite).

Enable SSO for your organization’s managed accounts

To enable SSO for your organization’s managed Meta accounts:

  1. Click Security in the left menu of Admin Center.
    • To do this, you need the right permissions and you need to be logged into Admin Center.
  2. Click Single sign-on in the Security menu.
  3. Click Add IdP.
  4. Copy our SSO metadata (including audience URL, recipient URL and ACS URL) and provide it to the IdP you’re connecting. It may take up to 24 hours for your IdP to process our SSO metadata. When you’ve done this, return to Admin Center then click I’ve added the metadata.
  5. Add your IdP’s SSO metadata. This includes:
    • The name of your SSO setup.
    • The SAML URL.
    • The SAML issuer URL.
    • The SAML certificate.
    • The option to enable SAML single logout if your IdP supports this. By enabling SAML single logout, when people using SSO log out of their IdP they will also be logged out of their managed Meta account – and if they log out of their managed Meta account, a request will be sent to the IdP to log out the user from their IdP session. If you want to enable SAML single logout, you will need to:
      • Add your ACS (Assertion Consumer Service) URL from the section above to your IdP’s SAML configuration as the Logout URL.
      • Find your SAML Single Logout URL in your IdP settings, then add this to the SAML Single Logout URL box in Admin Center.
  6. Click Validate IdP metadata.
  7. Enter a test email address, then click Test SSO.
    • Make sure this email address can be used for SSO via the IdP you are adding. You will also need to make sure you are already logged into the IdP with this email address (or that you are able to log in during the test).
  8. A new tab will open with your IdP login page. Return to Admin Center, then click Check result.
  9. In the Assign email domains section, click Review assignment to assign an IdP to your verified domains so that people with email addresses belonging to these domains can log in with SSO. Use the dropdown menu to the right of each verified domain to assign your chosen IdP. If you leave domains unassigned, then people using those domains will still need to log in using a password.
  10. You can choose to select a default IdP for any new verified or all unverified domains that are added to your Admin Center.
  11. Click Confirm assignment.
  12. Add break-glass accounts, which can provide you with emergency access when SSO is down. Even when they are on an SSO-assigned domain, break-glass accounts are logged into with a password. Two-factor authentication must be set up for break-glass accounts.
    • Your break-glass accounts should be different from your existing admin accounts. Store them securely and only use them when SSO is unavailable.
  13. Click Activate SSO to turn it on. Clicking Save changes does not activate SSO.

Learn how to edit domain assignment, default IdPs and break-glass accounts in your organization’s SSO setup in Admin Center.

SSO reauthentication settings

In Admin Center, you can prompt a SAML check on managed accounts every day, every 3 days, every week, every 2 weeks, or never.

You can also force a SAML reset for everyone by clicking Require now next to Require everyone to re-authenticate now.

Unlock someone’s managed Meta account in Admin Center

Unlock a managed account

My account is locked

Account locked due to unusual activity

What is a suspended account?

Admins with permissions to view account-related security alerts and logs can unlock managed Meta accounts if needed.

Managed Meta accounts are locked if unusual activity is detected.

If the person whose account is locked usually logs in with a password and uses a verified domain, or logs in via SSO (example: their Google account), then in some cases they will receive an email with a link to unlock their account. In other cases, we will ask an admin to investigate the issue first.

If the person whose account is locked usually logs in with a password and doesn’t use a verified domain, then we will send an email to an admin for them to investigate the issue. The account will then need to be unlocked by an admin.

Admins will also receive alerts telling them when an account is locked and when the person has regained access.

Note: Locked accounts are different than suspended accounts.

Unlock someone’s managed Meta account

To unlock someone’s managed Meta accounts in Admin Center:

  1. Click Security in the left menu of Admin Center.
  2. Click Security alerts.
    • If we lock someone’s managed Meta account, we will email you about it and also notify you in Admin Center. You can also click View alert in the email we send you or click on the notification in Admin Center to reach Security alerts.
  3. Click View detail next to the alert.
  4. Review the information.
  5. Click Unlock account. This sends a link to the person’s email address that lets them unlock their account.
    • You can also choose to review the security logs, contact the account owner or send a question in Admin Center if you need to investigate further before unlocking the account.
    • If the account had permissions to access Meta business tools, such as Meta Business Suite, you can click Go to business log to ensure there was no malicious activity by this account.

Verify your organization’s email domain in Admin Center (Add a trusted domain)

Verify my email domain

Add a trusted domain

Remove a domain

Admins with permissions to add and remove email domains can verify email domains in Admin Center.

Verifying your organization’s email domain in Admin Center proves that your organization owns it and prevents any other organizations from verifying it. There are other admin actions that you can only take on accounts using verified domains, such as editing an account’s name, email or phone number, the ability to generate account activation links, and more granular control of how single sign-on (SSO) works. People using a verified domain may also be able to troubleshoot being locked out of their managed account.

If you are unable to verify a domain (example: you don’t own the domain or it’s been verified in another Admin Center), then you can add it as a trusted domain.

All admins in Admin Center and Device Manager (if relevant) as well as anyone using a managed Meta account for business tools (example: Meta Business Suite) must use an email domain that’s been verified or trusted in Admin Center. If your organization has a subscription to Meta Horizon managed services, then you can choose to restrict access to only people using a verified or trusted domain.

Note: Ensure you are allowing emails from work.meta.com.

Verify domains in Admin Center

To verify your organization’s email domain in Admin Center:

  1. Click Security in the left menu of Admin Center.
    • To do this, you need the right permissions and you need to be logged into Admin Center.
  2. Click [Image: Domain verification] Domain verification.
  3. Click Verify a new domain in the top right.
  4. Enter your domain name, select Yes, verify this domain, then click Continue.
  5. Select one of the three available options to verify your domain:
    • Email verification (immediate): You’ll need access to an admin email. Click this option to see a list of email addresses that the verification code can be sent to.
    • HTML file upload (immediate): You’ll need admin access to your website’s root folder.
    • DNS TXT record (up to 72 hours): You’ll need to sign into your domain name provider.
  6. Complete the on-screen instructions for your chosen option.

If you need to verify multiple domains, you will need to follow the instructions above for each individual domain.

Verifying your domain by DNS TXT record

Remove domains

Click Remove domain next to the domain in Domain verification in Admin Center, then click Confirm.

All admins must use a verified or trusted domain. If you want to remove a domain currently used by admins then you will need to remove admin access for those accounts.

Why is the Facebook app requesting permission to access features on my Android?

Why does Facebook need permissions?

What permissions does Facebook use?

What is ‘Download files’ permission?

What is ‘Read/write contacts’?

If you install the Facebook app on your Android, your phone or tablet should let you know that the app is asking for your permission to access information or use features from your Android. Almost all apps need certain permissions to run on Android, and we use these permissions to run features in the app. Keep in mind that Android controls the way the permissions are named, and the way they’re named doesn’t necessarily reflect the way the Facebook app uses them.

We realize that some of these permissions sound scary, so we’d like to provide more info about how we use them. Below, you’ll find a list of some of the permissions we request for the Facebook app, as well as an example of how we use each one. Keep in mind that this list doesn’t include all of the Android permissions we request or all of our uses of those permissions.

  • Android permission (what you’ll see on your Android): Download files without notification; Examples of what we use this permission for: This allows us to improve the app experience by pre-loading News Feed content.
  • Android permission (what you’ll see on your Android): Read/write your contacts; Examples of what we use this permission for: These permissions allow you to import your phone’s contacts to Facebook and sync your Facebook contacts to your phone.
  • Android permission (what you’ll see on your Android): Add or modify calendar events and send email to guests without owners’ knowledge; Examples of what we use this permission for: This allows you to see your Facebook events in your phone’s calendar.
  • Android permission (what you’ll see on your Android): Read calendar events plus confidential information; Examples of what we use this permission for: This allows the app to show your calendar availability (based on your phone’s calendar) when you’re viewing an event on Facebook.

We may update this, so check back here to learn more about Android permissions and how we use them. To learn more about how we collect and use data, review our Data Policy.

About Political Content Control on Facebook

Adjust political content

See less political content

See more political content

I can’t find the setting

We’ve spent the last few years refining our approach to political content on Facebook, making it easier for people to adjust the amount of political content they see on Facebook.

Political content includes content that mentions:

  • Governments
  • Elections
  • Social topics

You can use the political content control to adjust whether Facebook recommends or does not recommend political content in your Feed.

You can further personalize your Facebook experience using the customization tools available in your Content Preferences through Settings, or in just a few clicks directly within your Feed.

Manage political content setting in Content Preferences through Settings

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & privacy, then click Content Preferences.
  3. Click Political content.
  4. Select your preferred political content control setting.
    • The Default setting suggests political content from profiles you don’t follow.
    • If you toggle the control to “off”, we won’t suggest political content when we recognize it.

Manage political content setting in Feed directly from your posts

  1. Go to any post in Feed.
  2. Click in the top right of the post.
  3. Click Hide post.
  4. Click Content Preferences.
  5. Click Political content.
  6. Select your preferred political content control setting.
    • The Default setting suggests political content from profiles you don’t follow.
    • If you toggle the control to “off”, we won’t suggest political content when we recognize it.

You can also learn how to see fewer ads about social issues, elections or politics while on Facebook. Learn more about how Meta addresses political content.

If you’d like to see fewer ads about social issues, elections or politics while on Facebook, you can adjust your ad topic preferences in Accounts Center.

Adjust your ad topic preferences

  4. Click See all next to Ad topics under the Customize ads tab.

On the Ad topics page, you’ll now see this topic under Topics you see less of. You can change your preference at any time by selecting a topic and choosing No preference.

These types of ads can be identified on Facebook by the Paid for by disclaimer, followed by information about the organization or individual responsible for the ad. Learn more about what we consider to be ads about social issues, elections or politics.

  • If you have linked your Facebook and Instagram accounts, your ad topic preference selections will apply across both accounts. If you have not linked your accounts, you can learn how to update your ad topic preferences for the ads you see on Instagram.

How ads about social issues, elections and politics are identified on Facebook

Report an unauthorized ad

What is a political ad?

Find ads in Ad Library

See fewer political ads

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

To increase transparency around the ads we show you about social issues, elections or politics, we have measures to help ensure the authenticity of these types of ads on Facebook and all Meta Products. A social issue, electoral or political ad in feeds or stories can be identified on Facebook by the Paid for by disclaimer.

We consider ads to be about social issues, elections or politics if:

  • They’re made by (or on behalf of), or about a candidate running for public office, a political figure, a political party or advocates for the outcome of an election to public office.
  • They’re about any election, referendum, or ballot initiative, including “go out and vote” or election campaigns.
  • They’re about social issues in the location where the ad is placed. Learn more about what we consider to be ads about social issues.
  • They’re regulated as political advertising.

Learn more about what’s considered an ad about social issues, elections or politics in our Business Help Center.

Report an ad about social issues, elections or politics

  1. Click Options in the top right of the ad.
  2. Click Report ad.
  3. Click Unauthorized political ad.
  4. Click Submit.

Learn more about how to see fewer ads about social issues, elections or politics. Please note, the social issues, elections or politics topic preference is only available in certain countries.

How Facebook uses data to show voting and election information

What data does Facebook use?

How does Facebook use my location?

Turn off election reminders

Learn how to turn on or off Facebook notifications about voting and elections.

We use your primary location data to show you reminders about election-related information in your state or voting district. These reminders include information like how and when to participate in an upcoming election.

Facebook’s parent company, Meta, relies on its legitimate interests as the legal basis to provide these election reminders and related features, as described in the Privacy Policy. You can turn these reminders on or off at any time.

You may see the option to enter your street address and state to receive more specific information about voting. Entering your address is optional, and we don’t display it to other people on Facebook. If you choose not to provide your street address and state, you may still receive voting and election reminders based on your primary location.

We may also use the location information you provide in other Facebook features about government, voting and elections.

Learn more about location privacy on Facebook from the Privacy Center.

Facebook sends notifications about voting and elections to people in many countries. You can manage these notifications in the Voting reminders section of your notification settings.

If you turn off these reminders, you won’t see notifications from Facebook about things like registering to vote or information on how to vote, unless you turn them back on.

Turn on or turn off Facebook notifications about voting and elections

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Notifications in the left menu.
  4. Scroll down and click Voting reminders.
  5. Select On or Off from the dropdown menu next to Voting reminders and, where available, Local voting alerts.

Below Voting reminders, you may see the option to enter your street address to receive more specific information about voting. Entering your address is optional, and we don’t display it to other people on Facebook. Learn more about how Facebook uses location data to show election information.

Facebook sends voting reminders to help people stay informed about important election deadlines and voting resources. These reminders are sent to everyone who is old enough to vote, regardless of which candidate or party they support.

Facebook’s parent company, Meta, relies on its legitimate interests as the legal basis to provide these election reminders and related features, as described in the Privacy Policy.

Reminders about voting and elections on Facebook

Basic Mobile Browser Help

Basic Mobile Browser Help

Manage voting reminders

Change my primary location

What information is used?

I can’t vote

You may see reminders and posts about elections and voting. Facebook sends these reminders to help people make their voice heard during an election. These reminders are sent to everyone who is old enough to vote, regardless of which candidate or party they support.

Reminders

On Facebook, we use your age (18+) and primary location to show you reminders about election-related information such as registration, vote-by-mail and Election Day reminders in your state or voting district. These reminders may include things like:

  • How to register to vote
  • Information about voting by mail
  • Notifications about local elections

To receive more specific voting reminders, you can provide additional information about where you live. Learn more about what information we use to determine your location.

Information for voting and election reminders comes from state and local governments as well as our partners Ballotpedia and DemocracyWorks. These partners work with state and local governments to gather authoritative data about voting and elections.

Learn how to manage notifications about voting and elections.

Posts

During elections, you may see your friends post about voting. You can also use Facebook to share your own election experiences. The voting reminders that appear in Feed provide an opportunity to share.

What if I can’t vote?

Information about elections may be shown to anyone on Facebook of voting age in countries where election reminders are available. We don’t try to determine who can vote, so you may still see election reminders even if you’re unable to vote. Countries and states have varying rules about eligibility to vote that can depend on age, nationality, criminal history and other factors. You can learn more about voter eligibility on your local or national government website.
