Meta Verified for creators is a paid subscription that provides tools to help you build more confidence with new audiences and protect your brand. This subscription comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

Automatic renewal

Meta Verified subscriptions are billed on a recurring basis and renew automatically, unless canceled. You will be charged on the same date as your original purchase, until you cancel.

Learn more about payments for Meta Verified creator subscriptions.

Subscription plans & benefits

We offer several subscription plans for creators. Plans, benefits, and availability may vary by region, by app, and by account. To see the specific features available to your account, please start the subscription process.

  • Plans: Meta Verified Standard; Benefits: - Verified badge - Impersonation protection - Enhanced support (chat and email support) - Search optimization - Add images to links - Exclusive stickers
  • Plans: Meta Verified Plus; Benefits: - Verified badge - Impersonation protection - Enhanced support (chat and email support) - Search optimization - Add images to links - Exclusive stickers - Featured profile - Links in Reels (2 per month)
  • Plans: Meta Verified Premium; Benefits: - Verified badge - Impersonation protection - Enhanced support (chat and email support) - Search optimization - Add images to links - Exclusive stickers - Featured profile - Links in Reels (4 per month) - Custom chat themes
  • Plans: Meta Verified Max; Benefits: - Verified badge - Impersonation protection - Enhanced support (chat and email support) - Search optimization - Add images to links - Exclusive stickers - Featured profile - Links in Reels (4 per month) - Custom chat themes - Personalized content strategy advice

Learn more about Meta Verified subscription benefits.

Note: Meta Verified creator subscriptions are only available for eligible subscribers. Subscription plans and benefits listed may not be available to all regions or creators.

Learn how to subscribe to Meta Verified.

Eligibility

To purchase a Meta Verified subscription, you need to meet the eligibility requirements.

The following accounts are eligible for Meta Verified:

  • Instagram professional creator account
  • Instagram personal account
  • Facebook professional creator account
  • Facebook personal account

You can verify up to two eligible profiles that are added to the same Accounts Center:

  • One Instagram account and one Facebook account

Verification process

When you subscribe to Meta Verified, you’ll follow a verification process and submit an application for review.

You’ll choose a subscription plan, select the profile(s) you want to verify, set up your recurring subscription payment, and confirm your identity.

Step 1. Choose your profile

You’ll choose the profile(s) you want to verify and set up your recurring subscription payment.

You can verify up to two eligible profiles that are added to the same Accounts Center.

When you bundle your subscription and verify two profiles instead of one (example: one Instagram account and one Facebook account), you may receive a discounted price. Both profiles may need to have similar names and pictures.

Note: Advanced Protection needs to be enabled on the profile(s) you’re verifying. This security feature can’t be disabled once your subscription is active.

Step 2. Confirm your identity

You’ll confirm your identity.

To confirm your identity, you’ll need to upload photos of a government-issued photo ID.

Note: If eligible, you may be verified using your activity across Meta products, such as name tenure and profile completeness including name and picture.

Step 3. Get reviewed

You’ll submit your information for review.

Once you complete the application process and submit your information, it’ll go into review. After review, you’ll get a notification with an update on your verification status. This process can take up to 3 business days.

Learn how to troubleshoot issues when subscribing to Meta Verified.

After you’re verified

If your application is approved, your subscription will become active and your selected profile(s) will be verified. You’ll get access to the Meta Verified benefits associated with your subscription plan.

Learn how to manage and make changes to your subscription:

  • View subscription details
  • Update subscription payment method
  • View subscription payment history
  • Change subscription plan
  • Contact Meta Verified support
  • Cancel subscription

Important information

  • Subscribers must agree to the Meta Verified Terms of Service and follow our Instagram Terms of Use, Facebook Terms of Service, and Community Standards.
  • If you provide false or misleading information during the verification process, Meta may prevent your profile from being verified, remove your verified status, or take additional action on the account.
  • After successfully subscribing to Meta Verified, certain activity may result in Meta’s revocation of your subscription due to integrity concerns and potential fraud risk.

About Stars visibility on Facebook

Can people see my Stars?

Delete a Stars comment

What are Stars badges?

The Stars you send to a creator are visible to others viewing the comments and the creator. If you take a specific action related to a video or a page (example: liking a video), that action may be visible to people on Facebook.

You can always delete the comment after your Stars are sent:

  1. Click
  2. Click Delete on the comment.

Your activity

For streaming live videos, the following actions may be seen by others depending on your privacy settings:

  • Liking or following a Page: When you like or follow a Page, your friends may see your name when they come across that Page (example: “[Name] and 4 other friends like this”).
  • Liking a video: When you like a video, your name may be visible when your friends come across that specific video (example: “[Name] also liked this”).
  • Commenting and sending Stars on a video: This badge can be seen by anyone viewing the comment thread each time you reply to a comment on that thread.
  • Stars badges: Viewers who have sent Stars will also earn badges that are visible by their name. The Stars badge will appear on comments sent to the creator on any of their lives for a week before disappearing. There is no way to delete or remove this badge until it expires.
  • Sharing a video: You can choose to share a video to your timeline or in a direct message to a person or group. When you do this, it will be visible to your selected audience.
  • Sending Stars to a creator: Creators will be able to see your name, the amount of Stars you sent and your customized message when you send Stars to that creator.

About subscription for no ads

How much does a subscription cost?

Cancel my subscription

What happens if I don’t subscribe?

I can’t change my subscription

This subscription is only available in the European Region and the United Kingdom.

We’ve introduced a choice for how you see ads and use Meta Company Products. You can choose to subscribe to use Meta Company Products without ads or you can use them free of charge with ads. You are required to make this choice to continue to use Meta Company Products. This choice will apply to all your accounts in the same Accounts Center.

Here’s what to expect with your subscription:

  • When you subscribe, you won’t see ads when you use your Facebook, Instagram, Threads or WhatsApp accounts that are in the same Accounts Center. If you have any accounts that have not been added to this Accounts Center, you will also need to make a choice for those accounts to either use Meta Company Products free of charge with ads or subscribe for each separate account or Accounts Center. You can also add all your accounts to the same Accounts Center. Learn how to add or remove accounts in Accounts Center.
  • Your subscription applies to both our websites and our apps, regardless of where you originally purchased your subscription.
  • While you are subscribed, your information will not be used for ads. Learn more about how we process your information for other purposes.
  • Because you won’t see ads with your subscription, some ad settings will no longer be relevant to you, and you won’t have access to those settings.
  • You may still see posts, messages and other branded content from businesses and creators, like if you follow a brand or creator.
  • You’ll still have access to our usual features, like Feed, Stories and Reels on Facebook and Instagram and chats and calls on WhatsApp.
  • Subscription payments are charged on a monthly basis, unless you cancel at least 24 hours before your next payment date through your Ad preferences.
  • Your ability to advertise and monetize with ads will be limited. Learn more about how your subscription may affect your ability to advertise or monetize with ads.

After you subscribe, you’ll stop seeing ads within 24 hours or after restarting your app.

Note: Facebook Lite users should close the app for at least 10 minutes to ensure you stop seeing ads once you subscribe.

Pricing of a subscription for no ads

The price you pay for a subscription for no ads on Meta Company Products depends on how many Facebook, Instagram and Threads accounts are in the Accounts Center where you have subscribed. It also depends on whether you subscribe through our websites or the Apple App Store or Google Play store, after taxes.

Note: You will only be charged for accounts on surfaces where we currently show ads, but your choice applies to all accounts added to the same Accounts Center. This means your information across those accounts will not be used for ads and you won’t see ads on any of our Meta Company Products when using those accounts. Additionally, prices may vary slightly from what’s listed below depending on the location you purchase your subscription due to currency exchange rate differences, local taxes and ordinances, and inconsistencies in the pricing tiers of in-app purchases using Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

  • Subscribe on Facebook.com or Instagram.com; Price: €5.99 per month for one account, plus €4 per month (or price in applicable local currency) for each additional account in the same Accounts Center
  • Subscribe in app using Apple App Store or Google Play Store; Price: €7.99 per month for one account, plus €5 per month (or price in applicable local currency) for each additional account in the same Accounts Center

If you don’t want to subscribe, you can choose to continue using Meta Company Products free of charge with ads. If you choose to use Meta Company Products free of charge with ads, you can also adjust your ad experience setting to manage whether you see personalized or less-personalized ads.

We are committed to your privacy and keeping your information secure whether you choose to use Meta Company Products free of charge with ads or subscribe. Learn more in the Privacy Policy and Cookies Policy.

Learn how to subscribe to use Meta Company Products without ads.

Changing your subscription in the Apple App Store or Google Play Store

If you subscribed in app while signed into the Apple App Store or Google Play Store and want to cancel or make changes to your subscription for no ads, you must be signed into the same Apple ID or Google account you used when making the purchase. You won’t be able to cancel your subscription or add or remove accounts to your subscription unless you are signed into the correct Apple ID or Google account.

Learn about billing and payments for Meta Verified creator subscriptions.

Automatic renewal

Meta Verified creator subscriptions are billed on a recurring basis and renew automatically, unless canceled.

You will be charged on the same date as your original purchase, until you cancel. (Example: If you purchased your subscription on January 24th, you’ll be charged again on February 24th, March 24th, and so on.)

Note: If your billing date falls on a day that doesn’t occur in a given month (example: the 31st), you’ll be charged on the last day of the following month instead.

Subscription price

The price of your subscription depends on the subscription plan you choose.

Accepted payment methods

Where you purchase Meta Verified determines which payment methods you can use. This is because your subscription is tied to the platform, device type, and account you use to sign up.

If you purchase directly through Meta, you can use:

  • Credit Cards: Visa, Mastercard, American Express
  • Debit Cards: Visa, Mastercard, American Express

If you purchase through the Apple App Store or Google Play Store, payment methods may differ:

  • Apple payment methods
  • Google payment methods

Manage payments

Keeping your payment information up to date is important for maintaining your Meta Verified subscription and ensuring your business stays verified.

Where you purchase Meta Verified determines where you can manage your payment information:

  • If you purchase directly through Meta, you can update your subscription payment on Instagram or Facebook using a computer.
  • If you purchase through Apple, you need to manage your subscription payment through the Apple App Store.
  • If you purchase through Google, you need to manage your subscription payment through the Google Play Store.

Note: If you signed up through Apple or Google, make sure you’re signed into the same Apple or Google account you used for your purchase. If you use a different account, you won’t see your Meta Verified subscription or be able to update your payment.

Update payment method

Any changes to your payment method take effect at the end of your current billing cycle. You need to have at least one valid payment method on file to keep your subscription active.

Note: We recommend adding a backup payment method to your account. If your default payment fails, your backup will be charged to keep your subscription active. If you don’t have a backup and your payment fails, you may receive a short grace period to resolve any payment issues before your subscription is canceled.

Learn how to update your payment method for Meta Verified.

View payment history

You can view your Meta Verified subscription payment history, including payment amount, date, and status.

Learn how to view your payment history for Meta Verified.

Refunds

Refunds for Meta Verified subscriptions are only available if you meet the eligibility requirements.

Refunds are returned to the original payment method used to purchase your subscription. Refunds may take several business days, and in some cases up to 60 days, depending on your bank or payment provider.

Learn more about refunds for Meta Verified subscriptions.

Note: Meta does not offer any credits or partial refunds for canceled Meta Verified subscriptions.

Offers and discounts

We currently offer the following discount for Meta Verified creator subscriptions:

  • Bundle discount: When you bundle your subscription and verify two profiles instead of one (example: one Instagram account and one Facebook account), you may receive a discounted price.

Note: Offers and discounts may not be available to all regions or creators. Eligibility and availability may change.

Cancel subscription

If you cancel your Meta Verified subscription, it’ll stay active until the end of your current billing cycle. After that, your subscription will end and you’ll lose access to all Meta Verified benefits.

To avoid being charged for another billing cycle, you need to cancel your subscription at least 24 hours before your next payment date.

Creators with active Meta Verified subscriptions can change their subscription plan.

When you change your plan, your subscription payment amount will change to the new plan price. Your subscribed profiles will stay the same.

Note: This feature is slowly rolling out and may not be available to all regions or creators. Plans, benefits, and availability may vary by region and app.

What to know before you change your plan

  • Active subscription: To change your plan, you need to have an active monthly Meta Verified subscription.
  • Eligible profiles: Your subscription needs to contain eligible Instagram or Facebook profiles.
  • Purchase method: You can only change your plan on the platform and device where you originally purchased your subscription. For example, if you purchased Meta Verified on Instagram, you can only change your plan on Instagram (not Facebook). Similarly, if you purchased your subscription on an iOS device, you need to be on an iOS device to change your plan (not Android).

Changing to a higher-priced plan typically takes effect within 24 hours of payment and doesn’t require an additional review process. You should receive access to the benefits for that plan after the 24-hour period. Your monthly payment amount will automatically update to the new plan price for future billing cycles.

Changing to a lower-priced plan takes effect at the beginning of your next billing cycle and doesn’t require an additional review process. You’ll continue having access to the benefits in your higher-priced plan until then.

Note: Changing plans is only available on mobile devices. This feature is not supported on computers.

Having trouble?

If you have trouble changing your subscription plan, we recommend that you make sure:

  • You have an active monthly Meta Verified subscription.
  • There isn’t a pending plan change already in review. This process typically takes effect within 24 hours.
  • You’re changing your plan on the platform and device where you originally purchased your subscription. (Example: If you purchased Meta Verified on Instagram while on an iOS device, you need to be on Instagram using an iOS device to change your plan.)
  • You’re using a mobile device. This feature isn’t available on desktop computers.
  • Your subscription payment method hasn’t failed or been declined.
  • You haven’t already changed to a lower-priced plan during this billing cycle. You’ll need to wait until the next billing cycle to make further changes.
  • To report a problem if you experience a technical issue while changing plans.

Note: This feature is slowly rolling out and may not be available in your location yet.

If you still have trouble changing your subscription plan, please contact Meta Verified Support.

Creators with active Meta Verified subscriptions get access to a variety of benefits, including enhanced support.

Enhanced support

Meta Verified enhanced support is a customer service benefit for subscribers. It offers direct help from human agents through chat and email.

Support requests from Meta Verified subscribers are prioritized, resulting in faster response times and quicker resolutions. Higher subscription plans unlock additional benefits, such as active case monitoring and phone support.

The enhanced support benefits are only available for active Meta Verified subscriptions.

Types of support

The following types of support are available with Meta Verified subscriptions, depending on your subscription plan:

  • Chat agent support – Get access to chat support (All plans)
  • Email support – Get 24/7 access to email support (All plans)
  • Prioritized support – Get help resolving your issues more quickly (Plus, Premium, Max)
  • Phone support – Request a call from an agent (Premium, Max)
  • Dedicated monitoring – Get active monitoring of support cases to expedite resolution (Max)

Note: Email support is available 24/7, while chat and phone support hours may vary. When you select a support channel, you’ll see the available hours for your language and region.

Chat support is only available on the Instagram and Facebook mobile apps (not available on computers).

Note: Support may not be available on mobile browsers.

Types of issues supported

You can request help with common account issues, including:

  • Meta Verified subscription management
  • Payments, billing, and refunds for your subscription
  • Questions about your verification status
  • General account access or security issues
  • Profile editing, review, and management

Languages available for support

Meta Verified support is offered in multiple languages, depending on the support channel and issue type:

  • Chat and email support: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Portuguese, Spanish, Thai, Turkish
  • Phone support: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Portuguese, Spanish, Thai, Turkish

Contact Meta Verified support

Instagram mobile app (iPhone)

Instagram mobile app (Android)

Facebook mobile app (iPhone)

Facebook mobile app (Android)

To help our support team resolve your issue more quickly, please provide as much detail as possible when submitting your support case. We recommend attaching screenshots or videos that show the issue, especially if you’re reporting a technical issue.

Tracking your support case

When you contact Meta Verified support, you’ll receive a case ID number for your support case (example: 12345678912345). Use this number to reference your case in any follow-up communications.

You can check the status of your support case on your Meta Verified support screen. Make sure you’re logged into the correct verified account to view your cases.

Your case will show one of several statuses, such as “Received”, “In Progress”, or “Completed”. If you have any questions or need more information, you can reply to your case while it’s still open.

If you don’t respond to the support agent within 7 days, your case will be automatically closed. Closed cases can’t be re-opened. If you still need help, you’ll need to submit a new case.

Note: You can only have one active chat with support at a time. To start a new chat, you’ll need to close your current chat first.

Troubleshooting tips

If you have trouble with Meta Verified support, try the following steps:

  • Check your subscription status. Make sure you’ve completed the verification process and have an active Meta Verified subscription.
  • Check your account login. Make sure you’re logged into the correct verified account.
  • Review your subscription plan. Check that your subscription plan includes the type of support you need.
  • Use a supported platform. Make sure you’re using a platform that supports the type of help you’re looking for (platforms are listed in this article). Support may not be available on mobile browsers.
  • Update your app. Make sure you’re using the latest version of the Instagram or Facebook app.
  • Clear your app data. Try clearing your app data, then restart the app.
  • Report technical issues. If you experience a technical problem, report a bug for further assistance.

Meta Verified for creators is a paid subscription that provides tools to help you build more confidence with new audiences and protect your brand. This subscription comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

Learn about Meta Verified eligibility requirements for creators below.

You need to meet the eligibility requirements in order to qualify for Meta Verified.

Subscriber eligibility

To purchase a Meta Verified subscription, you need to meet the following requirements:

  • Be at least 18 years old, or the age of majority in your country of residence.
  • Be located in a country where Meta Verified is available.
  • Have an eligible Instagram or Facebook account.
  • Have a government-issued photo ID.
  • Not exceed the number of times you can make changes to your account within a certain time period prior to applying for verification (examples: changes to profile name, profile picture, username, location, or account type).
  • Agree to the Meta Verified Terms of Service and follow the Instagram Terms of Use, Facebook Terms of Service, and Community Standards.

Account eligibility

The following accounts are eligible for Meta Verified:

  • Instagram professional creator account
  • Instagram personal account
  • Facebook professional creator account
  • Facebook personal account

You can verify up to two eligible profiles that are added to the same Accounts Center (one Instagram and one Facebook). When you verify two profiles, both may need to have similar names and pictures.

Note: Account eligibility requirements differ between Instagram and Facebook.

Instagram account eligibility

Your selected Instagram account needs to:

  • Be an Instagram personal or creator account. This account may need to have a profile picture and name that meets Meta Verified naming standards.
  • Have Advanced Protection turned on.
  • Meet minimum activity requirements.
  • Be located in a country where Meta Verified is available.
  • Follow the Instagram Terms of Use and Community Standards.

Facebook account eligibility

Your selected Facebook account needs to:

  • Be a Facebook personal or creator account. This account may need to have a profile picture and name that meets Meta Verified naming standards.
  • Have Advanced Protection turned on.
  • Meet minimum activity requirements.
  • Be located in a country where Meta Verified is available.
  • Follow the Facebook Terms of Service and Community Standards.

Note: Eligibility requirements are subject to change as we improve the product experience for subscribers.

How does Meta Pay protect me?

We value the trust you place in us. We take precautions to prevent unauthorized access to information you’ve saved on Facebook.

When you spend money on Facebook, we may share your contact or shipping info with sellers and their service providers according to our privacy policy. However, we don’t share your payment card info or third-party payment login info with sellers, with the recipients of a donation, or any other merchant when you make a payment on Facebook.

Facebook may also store your info so you don’t have to enter it again when you make a future purchase. If you don’t want us to store your payment info for future use, you can remove the payment methods you’ve added to your account.

ID requirements for Meta Verified creator subscriptions

What ID do I need?

My ID was rejected

Video selfie verification

Covering ID information

This article is about Meta Verified for creators on Facebook and Instagram.

Looking for business information? Please visit the Meta Verified for businesses Help Center.

When you subscribe to Meta Verified, you may need to upload photos of a government-issued photo ID to confirm your identity.

Learn about the ID requirements for Meta Verified creator subscriptions below.

ID requirements

Your ID needs to:

  • Be a valid, unexpired government-issued photo ID.
  • Include your name, photo, and date of birth.
  • Have a photo that shows your full face clearly.
  • Have a name that matches your profile name or meets Meta Verified naming standards.

Taking ID photos

When you take photos of your ID, make sure you:

  • Take a photo of the ID head-on, avoiding angles.
  • Use a well-lit area.
  • Place your ID on a flat surface with a contrasting background.
  • Include the entire ID with all four corners visible, avoiding any cutoffs.
  • Don’t use camera flash to minimize glare.
  • Remove any other objects from the photo.

Uploading ID photos

When you upload photos of your ID, make sure:

  • The ID meets the requirements listed above.
  • The ID hasn’t expired.
  • The ID is fully visible with all four corners in the frame.
  • The ID information is readable and clear.

Note: We won’t accept your ID photos if they don’t meet the requirements.

Video selfie verification

As part of the verification process, you may be asked to upload a video selfie to confirm your identity. You’ll see instructions on your screen for how to take a video selfie of your full face.

Our technology analyzes the video to estimate the location of parts of your face (like your eyes), but doesn’t allow us to individually identify you or any other person. The information helps us distinguish videos of live people from videos of photographs used to impersonate live people.

A snapshot of the video is sent to human reviewers to compare it with the profile picture on your account. The information is processed to confirm you’re a real person. This takes a few seconds before getting deleted. This video will never be visible on Facebook.

My name is one word

I reached my edit limit

This article is about Meta Verified for creators on Facebook and Instagram.

Looking for business information? Please visit the Meta Verified for businesses Help Center.

Meta Verified creators can update their profile name, but there are important eligibility rules and restrictions.

Note: This feature may not be available to all regions or creators.

Profile name eligibility

Your verified profile name must match the legal name on your government-issued ID. If eligible, you may be able to use a different name that meets our naming standards (this feature isn’t available to everyone).

If your legal name is just one word (a mononym), you may not be able to use it as Meta requires both a first and last name.

Note: When updating your verified name, the new name needs to be similar to the name originally used when you signed up with. If you have a bundled subscription with more than one verified profile, each profile may need to have similar names.

Accepted profile name formats

  • Abbreviations (example: Sid for Siddharth)
  • Spelling variations (example: Maria vs Marya)
  • First initials (example: LM for Lisa Marie)
  • Compound names (example: Mary vs Mary-Lou)

Not accepted:

  • Symbols, numbers, unusual capitalization, repeating characters, or punctuation
  • Characters from multiple languages
  • Certain titles (example: religious titles)
  • Offensive or suggestive words of any kind

Edit restrictions

When you subscribe to Meta Verified, there are important rules about editing your profile name.

Locked fields

When you first apply for Meta Verified and your application is under review, you may not be able to update certain profile information – including your profile name.

Edit limits

You can only change your verified profile name a limited number of times.

  • Instagram: You can update your profile name twice every 14 days.
  • Facebook: You can update your profile name once every 60 days.

If you reach the editing limit, you’ll need to wait before making another change.

Review and approval

Profile changes need to be reviewed and approved before they can display on your verified profile. Your new name won’t appear until it passes review.

While your update is in review and pending approval, you may not be able to make additional edits to your profile name.

Note: Profile name changes may get rejected if they don’t meet our policies or the eligibility requirements in this article.

Troubleshooting tips

If you’re having trouble changing your verified profile name, make sure:

  • Your new name matches your ID. Your profile name should match your ID, unless you’re eligible to use a different name.
  • Your name is an accepted format. Formats that aren’t accepted (including single-name structures) may be rejected.
  • Your new name is similar to your original account name. New names that aren’t similar to the name you signed up with may be rejected.
  • Your verified profiles have similar names. If you have a bundled subscription with more than one verified profile, each profile may need to have similar names.
  • You haven’t reached your edit limit. If you’ve already reached the maximum number of times you can edit your profile name, you’ll need to wait before trying again.
  • You don’t have any pending profile updates. If you already have a profile change in review, you may not be able to submit another update until it’s approved. Reviews can take up to 3 days.
  • Your Meta Verified application isn’t still being reviewed. You can’t update your profile name while your verification application is pending.
  • You’re on a supported platform. Editing your profile name is only available on certain platforms (see supported platforms).
  • Your profile updates follow our policies. Your profile updates need to follow the Meta Verified Terms of Service, Instagram Terms of Use, Facebook Terms of Service, and Community Standards.

Reasons why you might not be able to use the Stars button

I can’t use Stars button

My account was recently created

My payments account is disabled

Stars are turned off for creator

If you’re unable to purchase Stars because the Stars button is disabled, it may be because:

  • Your account was recently created. If your Facebook account was created within the past 30 days, Stars will be available to you when your account is over 30 days old.
  • Your payments account is disabled. If you are unable to purchase Stars, check to see if your Facebook payment account has been disabled, or view your Stars balance.
  • Stars are turned off for the creator. If you can access Stars on one creator’s video, but not on another creator’s video, Stars may be turned off for that creator.
  • Your version of the Facebook app is outdated. If you haven’t updated your app in a while, check the App or Play Store to download the latest version of the app.
  • You’re not currently logged in. If you’re not logged into your Facebook account, you need to log in to access Stars.
  • You’re logged in to an additional profile. Additional Facebook profiles are different from your main profile, and aren’t eligible to send Stars. If you’re logged into an additional profile, you’ll need to switch to your main profile to send Stars.
  • You’re logged in as a Page. Facebook Pages aren’t eligible to send Stars. If you’re logged into your Page, you’ll need to switch into your profile to send Stars.
  • You’re in an ineligible country. If you’re still unable to use Stars, make sure that both you and the creator are located in a country eligible for Stars.

Revoked Meta Verified creator subscriptions

My subscription was revoked

Why was my subscription canceled?

Re-apply for Meta Verified

I can’t update my payment

This article is about Meta Verified for creators on Facebook and Instagram.

Looking for business information? Please visit the Meta Verified for businesses Help Center.

When your Meta Verified subscription gets revoked, you immediately lose all subscription benefits. This is different from canceling your subscription, where you typically have access to benefits until the end of your current billing cycle.

There are several reasons why Meta Verified subscriptions may get revoked or unexpectedly canceled.

Common reasons for revocation

Payment issues

Your subscription will be canceled if your payment method fails and there is no backup payment method on file. We recommend adding a backup payment method so that if your default payment fails for any reason, your backup payment will be charged to keep your subscription active.

Learn how to update your payment method for Meta Verified.

Verification failure

If your verification doesn’t pass the review process after submitting your first payment, your subscription will be canceled and you’ll be eligible for a refund.

Learn about refunds for Meta Verified creator subscriptions.

Profile updates

If you update your verified profile information and your changes aren’t approved because they violate our policies, your subscription may be revoked.

Policy violations

If your verified account violates our policies, your subscription will be revoked. Subscribers must agree to the Meta Verified Terms of Service and follow our Instagram Terms of Use, Facebook Terms of Service, and Community Standards.

Account deletion

If you delete your verified account, your subscription will be canceled.

Account removed from bundle

If you remove one of your verified accounts from an existing subscription bundle, your subscription will be revoked after 7 days or at the end of your current billing cycle – whichever comes first. If you re-subscribe that account to the same bundle within this period, your subscription will stay active.

Change in eligibility

If you no longer meet the eligibility requirements (example: moving to a location where Meta Verified is not available), your subscription will be canceled.

Learn more about Meta Verified eligibility requirements for creators.

App store changes

If you make changes to your subscription directly through the Apple App Store or Google Play Store (example: changing your plan), your subscription may be revoked.

Learn how to manage your Meta Verified subscription.

What happens if your subscription is revoked

If your subscription gets revoked, we will attempt to notify you via email and in-app notification.

You’ll immediately lose access to all Meta Verified subscription benefits (this includes support and any open cases with the support team). Revocation is different from canceling your subscription, where you typically have access to benefits until the end of your current billing cycle.

If you want to re-apply for Meta Verified, we recommend making sure your account meets the eligibility requirements and follows our policies. You may need to make updates to your account or payments before signing up again.

Learn how to subscribe to Meta Verified.

Meta Verified for creators is a paid subscription that provides tools to help you build more confidence with new audiences and protect your brand. This subscription comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

Learn how to subscribe to Meta Verified below.

When you subscribe to Meta Verified, you’ll follow a verification process and submit an application for review.

You’ll choose the profile(s) you want to verify, set up your subscription payment, and confirm your identity.

You can verify up to two eligible profiles (one Instagram and one Facebook) that are added to the same Accounts Center. When you bundle your subscription and verify two profiles instead of one, you get a discounted price.

What to know before subscribing

  • To qualify for Meta Verified, you need to meet the eligibility requirements.
  • If you subscribe two profiles, they need to be added to the same Accounts Center. Advanced Protection needs to be enabled on the profile(s).
  • If you don’t complete the verification process within 3 days, your subscription will be canceled and you’ll be eligible for a refund.
  • When your application is in review and pending verification, you may not be able to update certain profile information. This can include your profile name, username, category, location, and date of birth.

Note: If you provide false or misleading information during the verification process, Meta may prevent your profile from being verified, remove your verified status, or take additional action on the account.

Subscription for no ads pricing when you move between the EU and UK

Change my subscription price

Cancel my subscription

Re-subscribe in new region

My subscription was canceled

If you move between the European Region (EU) and the United Kingdom (UK), the price of your subscription for no ads may be different in your new region.

What happens to your subscription

Your subscription for no ads stays active when you move between the EU and UK. You’ll continue to be charged at your current subscription price until you cancel and re-subscribe at the new price. The subscription for no ads is only available in the EU and UK. If you move from the EU or UK to another region, your subscription will be canceled automatically if you purchased your subscription through the web or on an Android device. If you subscribed on an iPhone or iPad, you’ll need to cancel your subscription. Learn more about how to cancel your subscription for no ads.

How to access pricing in your new region

If you’d like to subscribe at the price available in your new region, you’ll need to cancel your current subscription and then re-subscribe. The steps to do this depend on how you originally subscribed.

If you subscribed on the web

  1. Go to your subscription settings.
  2. Cancel your current subscription.
  3. After your subscription expires, re-subscribe at the updated price for your new region.

If you subscribed on Android

To access the new regional price on Android, you’ll need to cancel your subscription and update your Google Play Store country.

  1. Cancel your subscription in the Google Play Store.
  2. Change your Google Play Store country or region to match your new location. You’ll need a payment method from your new country.
  3. After your subscription ends and your store country is updated, re-subscribe at the price available in your new region.

Note: If you only change your Play Store country without canceling, Google will continue to charge you at your original subscription price.

If you subscribed on iPhone or iPad

To access the new regional price on iOS, you’ll need to cancel your subscription and update your App Store country.

  1. Cancel your subscription in your Apple ID settings. Apple requires you to cancel all active subscriptions before you can change your App Store country.
  2. Change your App Store country or region to match your new location. You’ll need a payment method from your new country.
  3. After your subscription ends and your store country is updated, re-subscribe at the price available in your new region.

Note:

  • Your current subscription stays active until the end of your billing cycle, even after you cancel.
  • You won’t be charged again after you cancel unless you re-subscribe.
  • Once you re-subscribe in your new region, you’ll be charged the price for that region.

Troubleshoot sign-up issues for Meta Verified creator subscriptions

I can’t subscribe to Meta Verified

My ID upload failed

My verification failed

This article is about Meta Verified for creators on Facebook and Instagram.

Looking for business information? Please visit the Meta Verified for businesses Help Center.

Learn how to troubleshoot verification issues when subscribing to Meta Verified.

Find the issue you’re experiencing below.

Unable to subscribe

If you’re not able to subscribe to Meta Verified, we recommend that you:

  • Make sure you meet the eligibility requirements to subscribe.
  • Make sure you have an eligible account.
  • Make sure you have Advanced Protection enabled on the profile(s) you’re verifying. This is required to subscribe.

Issues uploading ID

When you upload photos of your ID for verification, make sure it’s a valid, unexpired government-issued photo ID that meets the Meta Verified ID requirements.

When you take photos of your ID, make sure you:

  • Take a photo of the ID head-on, avoiding angles.
  • Use a well-lit area.
  • Place your ID on a flat surface with a contrasting background.
  • Include the entire ID with all four corners visible, avoiding any cutoffs.
  • Don’t use camera flash to minimize glare.
  • Remove any other objects from the photo.

When you upload photos of your ID, make sure:

  • The ID meets the requirements listed above.
  • The ID hasn’t expired.
  • The ID is fully visible with all four corners in the frame.
  • The ID information is readable and clear.

Note: We won’t accept your ID photos if they don’t meet the requirements.

Verification failed

There are a few reasons verification may have failed:

  • You didn’t successfully complete the verification process within 3 days. If this happens, your subscription will be canceled and you will be eligible for a refund.
  • We weren’t able to verify your identity. If this happens, you can try subscribing again after the refund process is complete.

Payment issues

Learn how to troubleshoot payment issues for Meta Verified.

Technical issues

If you notice a broken feature or technical problem when subscribing to Meta Verified, you can report it. This can help us identify and fix problems when something’s not working correctly.

Learn how to report technical problems.

Note: Meta Verified Support is only available after you have successfully completed the verification process.

I want to leave Meta

This subscription is only available in the European Region and the United Kingdom.

To comply with regulatory requirements in the European Region, we’ve introduced a choice about how you see ads and use our products. You can subscribe to use our products without ads, or you can use them free of charge with ads. We’ve updated our Terms and Privacy Policies to reflect these options. You can review the updated terms and policies here:

  • Meta Terms of Service

  • Instagram Terms of Use

  • Threads Terms of Use

  • Meta Privacy Policy

  • If you use our products free of charge with personalized ads: You will see ads that are related to your interests and activity.; If you use our products free of charge with less-personalized ads: You will see ads that are less related to your interests and activity. You may see ad breaks, which means you’ll sometimes have to view an ad for a short period of time before you can continue browsing.; If you subscribe to use our products without ads: You won’t see ads on our products. You’ll still see posts, messages, or other branded content from businesses and creators, like if you follow a brand or creator.

  • If you use our products free of charge with personalized ads: You won’t pay a fee to use our products.; If you use our products free of charge with less-personalized ads: You won’t pay a fee to use our products.; If you subscribe to use our products without ads: You’ll be charged a monthly fee. You can learn more about pricing.

  • If you use our products free of charge with personalized ads: Your information will be processed for ads. You can review the Meta Privacy Policy to learn more about how we process your information for ads or other purposes.; If you use our products free of charge with less-personalized ads: Less of your information will be processed for ads. Learn more about the types of information that will be processed for ads if you choose less-personalised ads.; If you subscribe to use our products without ads: Your information won’t be processed for ads. You can review the Meta Privacy Policy to learn more about how we process your information for other purposes.

You can change your choice at any time. If you choose to use our products free of charge with ads, you’ll have access to Ad preferences, including your Ad settings. You’ll be able to adjust your ad experience setting at any time to manage whether you see personalized or less-personalized ads. Learn more about this choice.

We hope that you’ll continue to use Meta Company Products. If you don’t want to accept the changes, you can choose to leave our services, and we would be sorry to see you go.

The conversation starts when the other person responds to your message or sends a like back to you. You receive a notification on your Facebook app that someone liked or messaged you in Dating. You may only message a suggested match further once they reply or send you a like back.

Conversations you have in Dating will appear in the Matches tab within Dating. These conversations won’t show up in Facebook Messenger.

How Facebook Dating is different from Facebook

Facebook Dating is different from your Facebook profile in several ways:

  • Although you access Dating from your Facebook account, your Dating profile is different from your Facebook profile. Your current Facebook friends and anyone outside of Dating can’t see your Dating profile. For example, your Dating activities don’t appear on your Facebook Feed.
  • All conversations you have in Dating are separate from your conversations on Facebook Messenger.
  • You can delete your Dating profile without deleting your Facebook account. However, deleting your Facebook account also deletes your Dating profile.

Note that if you become friends on Facebook with someone you’ve matched with, your matches or suggested matches in Dating will still be able to see your Dating profile.

How location services work with Facebook Dating

Change my dating location

My dating location is wrong

Turn off location services

Turn on Location Services for your Facebook account when creating your Facebook Dating profile or when asked by Facebook. Dating uses Location Services to suggest matches based on your distance preferences, so you won’t be able to see or match with people unless Location Services can confirm your Primary Dating location.

Your Primary Dating location is where you initially signed up for Facebook Dating, updated only when you choose to change it. Moving locations does not update your Primary Dating location, which may result in a location mismatch message.

Change or check your primary dating location

  1. From your Facebook app, tap Menu in the top left, then tapDating.
  2. Tap Profile in the top right.
  3. Tap Dating preferences, then tap Dating location.
  4. Tap Update to update your location.

Additional locations added through Match Anywhere do not use Location Services. Learn more about Match Anywhere.

Turning off location services

After creating your Dating profile, you may turn off Facebook Location Services and continue to use Dating. You’ll see matches based on your most recently confirmed dating location. Your dating location is visible on your Dating profile.

Keep in mind that turning off Location Services will affect your overall Facebook experience, not just Dating. Facebook uses your location to provide more relevant and personalized experiences, like helping you to check-in, find events and get better ads. Learn more about location data use in our Privacy Policy.

How video selfie age verification works on Facebook Dating

How video selfie works

How to take video selfie

My video selfie failed

How long does verification take?

This feature is only available in some states.

When you use Facebook Dating, you may be asked to give us additional information to verify your age. You can upload your ID or take a video selfie to verify your age.

How your age is verified with a video selfie

After you’ve taken a video selfie, we’ll share an image from the selfie with the vendor. Our vendors’ technology only estimates age. It can’t identify specific people. Once your age has been estimated and shared with us, we will delete the image within 30 days. We don’t share any other information about you with the vendor.

How to take the selfie

If you choose to take a video selfie to verify your age, you’ll see instructions on your screen for how to take the selfie. If you haven’t used the camera on Facebook before, we’ll ask you for permission to use the camera so you can take the selfie.

When you take the selfie, make sure your whole face is visible and that you have enough light for the camera. Avoid wearing anything that blocks your face, like a mask or hat. You’ll be asked to move your face in different directions, such as to the right and left and up and down.

Once you’ve taken the selfie, you’ll see a screen to submit your selfie. You can continue to use other parts of Facebook or exit the app after you’ve submitted your selfie.

It can take up to 20 minutes to verify your age. You will get a notification with the outcome of the verification.

Keeping Facebook Dating Safe

Is Facebook Dating safe?

Keep my community safe

Report someone on Dating

Facebook Dating guidelines

When you use Facebook Dating, you must follow our Community Standards. To help keep yourself and the community safe while using Dating, there are some important things to keep in mind:

  • Do not misrepresent your identity by claiming or implying to be someone you are not.
  • Do not mislead others regarding who you are or what you’re doing, including but not limited to misrepresenting biographical details about yourself such as name, age, or location.
  • Do not sell, advertise or solicit goods or services.
  • Do not post or share a photo that depicts an unaccompanied minor. An adult must be clearly visible in any photos that include a minor.
  • Do not post or share a photo of an unclothed minor.

Learn more about Facebook Dating Safety Guidelines.

Photo tips for Facebook Dating

Increase my profile views

My photos are blurry

What photos should I use?

We may remove or ask you to verify your Dating profile if we think you might be misrepresenting yourself. Learn more about authentic identity in our Community Standards.

Others only get one first impression of you, so make it great!

Follow these photo tips to help increase your Dating profile views:

  • Select a photo of just you for your primary photo. Make sure your face is clearly shown.
  • Select clear photos taken in well-lit areas.
  • Incorporate photos of you doing things you love, so people can learn about your hobbies and interests.
  • Select photos someone else took of you, not just selfies!
  • DO NOT post a photo that depicts an unaccompanied minor.
  • DO NOT post a photo of an unclothed minor.

Note: You should post a photo of yourself before you post photos of other people.

If you’re still stuck on what photos to use, ask yourself these questions:

  • Am I the main focus of the photo?
  • Can people clearly see my face?
  • Do I have more than just selfies?
  • Do my photos have good lighting?
  • Is my photo blurry?
  • Do I have a few photos of me doing things I love, like my interests and hobbies?
  • Does this photo reflect who I am and what I love to do?
  • Does this photo help start a conversation?

If you delete your Dating profile, you lose your profile, including your Dating answers, likes, matches and conversations. This information is not recoverable. Even if you delete your profile, your matches can still see conversations they had with you.

California Cyberbullying Prevention Act on Facebook

Report bullying or harassment

Contact form for reporting

What are Community Standards?

Bullying and harassment happen in many places and come in many different forms from making threats and releasing personally identifiable information to sending threatening messages and making unwanted malicious contact. We do not tolerate this kind of behavior, as described in Meta’s Community Standards, because it prevents people from feeling safe and respected.

We include a link on nearly every piece of content for reporting bullying, harassment, and other issues, as described on the Safety Center. Our global teams work to quickly review content you report. If you have a Facebook account, you can report bullying and harassment content to us in this way at any time. If you don’t have a Facebook account, you can report bullying and harassment to us using the contact form. We remove anything that violates our policies.

Change event privacy

When you create an event, you can choose its privacy setting. You can’t change the privacy setting after the event has been created. Example: You can’t change a public event to a private event.

Privacy settings

  • Private: Visible only to the people who are invited. You can choose to allow guests to invite their friends. People who are invited can see the event description, photos, posts and videos.
  • Public: Visible to anyone on or off Facebook. Anyone can see things like the event description, photos, posts and videos. All events hosted by a Facebook Page are public.
  • Friends: Visible only to your Facebook friends. Your friends can see the event description, photos, posts and videos.
  • Group: The group privacy setting determines who can see the event.
    • Public group: Visible to anyone on or off Facebook. Anyone can see things like the event description, photos, event discussion and videos.
    • Private group: Visible only to members of the group. Group members can see the event description, photos, posts and videos.

Event settings

Event name rules

Event name character limit

Event names must accurately reflect the event. Only the host of the event can manage event details.

Event names can’t include:

  • Terms or phrases that may be abusive or violate someone’s rights.
  • Improper capitalization. Event names must use grammatically correct capitalization and may not include all capital letters, except for acronyms. The first letter of the event name must be capitalized.
  • Symbols (example: ®) or unnecessary punctuation.
  • Long descriptions, such as a slogan. Event names are limited to 64 characters.

How event invitations work for people who are off of Facebook

Opt out of event invitations

What information is collected?

Delete my contact information

Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”, “we”,“our” or “us”) processes your mobile phone number and/or your email address if you’re invited to a Facebook event through an email or text message (SMS). We process this information even if you aren’t a user of Facebook and/or don’t have an account with us (a “Non-user”).

About off-Facebook invitations and how they work

The host of a Facebook event can send invitations to guests even if they’re a Non-user, by contacting them through their email address or phone number.

If you don’t have a Facebook account, we’ll send a link to the event invitation to your email or phone number. You can use that link to respond to the event or opt out.

  • If you respond that you’re going or may be going, we’ll use the same contact information to send you event updates (example: time or location change).
  • There are different ways you can opt out:
    • Unsubscribe from the event: We will stop sending you updates about the event.
    • Block the host: The host will not be able to invite you to any of their future events.
    • Block Facebook events: We will not send any event invitations to that email address or phone number.

You can also create a Facebook account and log in to respond to the event. The name you use for your account is how you’ll show up to other guests. With an account, you’ll have full access to the event which means you’ll be able to see who is going, see and participate in event discussions and post and view photos or videos of the event.

What information is collected about Non-users

Event hosts can provide the mobile phone number and/or email address of Non-users. If you choose to attend an event as a Non-user, we will also save your RSVP status.

How we use a Non-user’s information

If a Non-user responds as “Going” or “Maybe” to a Facebook event, we use their information to communicate changes about the event and to inform the host about RSVPs. Hosts may also use the guest lists of events to extend invitations to other events. This information will not be shared outside of this use case, and a Non-user can delete their information or block the inviter at any time.

We will retain Non-users’ contact information until 180 days after the end of the event, or until a Non-user requests us to delete their information, as described below.

How we transfer information

We may share the information we collect globally, both internally across our offices and data centers, and externally with our partners, service providers and vendors. As Meta is global, with users, partners and employees around the world, transfers are necessary for a variety of reasons, including so we can operate and provide the services described here.

Non-user information will be transferred or transmitted to, or stored and processed in:

  • Places we have infrastructure or data centers, including the United States, Ireland, Denmark and Sweden, amongst others
  • Countries where Meta Products are available
  • Other countries where our partners, service providers and vendors are located outside the country where you live, for purposes as described here.

We rely on appropriate mechanisms for international data transfers. For example, for information we collect:

  • We utilize standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission and by other relevant authorities.
  • We rely on determinations from the European Commission, and from other relevant authorities, about whether other countries have adequate levels of data protection.
  • We use equivalent mechanisms under applicable laws that apply to data transfers to the United States and other relevant countries.

How Non-users can exercise their rights

We provide Non-users with the ability to exercise their rights under applicable laws. To exercise your rights, contact us using the contact information below.

You can also see if we have your contact information and request that we delete it from our address database.

We hope that we can satisfy any queries a Non-user may have about the way in which we process their personal information. In some countries, you may also be able to contact the Data Protection Officer for Meta Platforms, Inc. or Meta Platforms Ireland Limited if you are in the European Union. Depending on your jurisdiction, you may also contact your local Data Protection Authority (“DPA”) directly.

Learn more about how privacy works on Facebook, Instagram and in the Facebook Help Center.

Privacy notice for United States residents

You can learn more about the consumer privacy rights that may be available to you by reviewing the United States Regional Privacy Notice.

Contact us

If you have questions about this notice, or have questions, complaints or requests regarding your information, please use this form.

Alternatively, if you don’t have access to the form, you can also write to us at the following address:

Meta Platforms, Inc.

FAO: Privacy operations

1601 Willow Road

Menlo Park, CA 94025, US

How is Facebook preventing platform abuse?

What is platform abuse?

What is Cambridge Analytica?

How is my data protected?

We’re investigating all apps on our platform and conducting a full audit of any apps with suspicious activity. If we find developers that misused personally identifiable information, we’ll ban them from Facebook. You can also edit the privacy and settings for your apps and games.

Protecting your privacy is at the heart of everything we do at Facebook. We need to do more to safeguard your privacy, so we’re taking action on potential past abuse and putting stronger protections in place to prevent future abuse of our platform.

  1. Notifying you if an app misused your data. Moving forward, if we remove an app for misusing data, we’ll tell everyone who used that app. We’re also building a way for you to see if your data might have been accessed through “thisisyourdigitallife,” the app that sent data to Cambridge Analytica and violated our platform policies.
  2. Making it easier to manage the apps you use. We already show you what apps your account is connected to and what data you’ve permitted those apps to use. Going forward, we’re making these choices easier to find and manage by showing you a tool at the top of your Feed.
  3. Turning off access for unused apps. If you haven’t used an app within the last 3 months, we’ll remove the app’s access to your information.
  4. Restricting Facebook Login data. We’re changing the way login works to reduce the data that an app can request without app review. Apps can only request name, profile photo and email address. Requesting any other data will require our approval. We have a responsibility to protect your data and are committed to protecting your information and making our platform safer.

Signs and prevention methods for radicalization

Signs of radicalization

Help a loved one

What to do next

Get support

Violent and extremist groups are dangerous for both members of the group and the people they target. People join these groups for many reasons, but people who are lonely, isolated or excluded may be more likely to feel connected to these groups’ messages.

Once someone joins a group, they might finally feel like they have a place to belong. It might also feel good to blame their problems on someone else or feel like they are part of a cause. People may get pulled into violence and hate with false promises of status, power and protection. The attraction can be even greater for anyone struggling with their personal and professional lives.

Signs that someone is at risk

It can be hard to know for sure if someone is a part of these groups if they don’t openly talk about it. We have worked with experts at the Rahber Programme to identify the common signs of extremism, so you can be more confident in supporting someone.

Below are some of the common signs of radicalization:

  • Show unusual amounts of anger or aggression; and saying intolerant or discriminatory things that disrespect another person’s physical appearance, character, or identity (ethnic, racial, color, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, education background, language, etc.).
  • Discussing violence or conspiracy theories; becoming obsessive over particular political or religious grievances, identities, groups, or ideologies of violence; and supporting violence towards other cultures, nationalities, or religions.
  • Spending unhealthy amounts of time online, being secretive about which groups of people they are talking to online, and appearing to talk from the script of an extremist organization might indicate they’re being influenced or controlled.
  • Idolizing historical extremists or violent groups; sharing memes or videos with extremist symbols and signs, or terms that indicate harmful or violent intent.
  • Creating, viewing, liking, or sharing extremist content, including relating to weaponry, extremist literature, or with the intention to incite violence.

Keep in mind that these behaviors don’t always mean someone is part of an extremist or violent group. Your friend could be struggling with something else, like depression, suicidal thoughts or stress.

What to do next

It can be upsetting or confusing if you think someone you know is involved in an extremist group. You might not know how to bring it up to them or what to do. But helping them is the kindest thing you can do.

Former extremists often explain that violence and hate ruined their lives and broke apart their families. They also saw that violence didn’t change the things that the radical group was mad about.

Extremist groups are harmful to the people in the group. Group leaders may lie or brainwash their followers with false information. The leaders may also take advantage of group members by having the members do violent or illegal things.

Group members may also face harsh consequences for their actions within the group. They may go to jail, lose their jobs, hurt their family and friends or lose their good reputations.

The good news is there is hope if someone you know wants to leave an extremist group. You can help them by having an open talk with them about what is going on in their life.

Use the following tips when having a conversation about this with your loved one:

  1. Avoid arguing and telling them they’re wrong
    • No one likes being told they’re wrong or feeling that their emotions are being dismissed. Focus on the common ground between you.
    • Avoid words like extremist, racist or radicalized, which could make them feel like you don’t understand them.
    • Don’t reduce their identity to their involvement in a radicalized group.
  2. Listen, empathize and be patient
    • Find a time that is good for you both and try to avoid interruptions to help your friend feel more heard.
    • Focus on a two-way conversation and shared understanding.
    • Reassure them that your concern is genuine. Think about how best to express your love and support.
    • Think about the things extremism is giving them (for example, community or belonging), and think of healthier ways your friend can get those needs met.
  3. Ask open-ended questions
    • Try to get them talking about how they’re feeling.
    • You may learn they are facing a different problem. Take the opportunity to support them with any struggle they are having.

You may need to get help from an expert or a counselor. If the conversation goes well, you can also encourage your friend to get the help they need from our trusted partner Life After Hate. You can also reach out directly to Life After Hate for help.

Get support

You may need to get help from an expert or a counselor. If the conversation goes well, you can also encourage your friend to get the help they need from our trusted partners at the Rahber Programme. You can also reach out directly to Rahber for support.

How can Rahber help you or your loved one?

  • Rahber believes that we all essentially yearn for peace and with the right support can work together towards harmonious and peaceful societies. They inspire people to seek help and help others if they find themselves troubled by hate or violence in society.
  • They help people identify positive narratives embedded in our society and religion that people can use to bring peace, inclusivity, and tolerance within themselves and their community.
  • They help people identify resources that can help people report and prevent hateful conduct, violence and harassment.
  • They inspire forgiveness, empathy, and peace, and motivate people to practise non-violent communication, dialogue and conflict resolution in their daily lives.
  • They build people’s trust in the institutions protecting citizens; and encourage people to seek help for mental health problems.
  • They recognize and identify ways hateful conduct and disinformation can instigate violence and how to prevent it.

How Facebook responds

Nonviolent politics are allowed on Facebook. However, we don’t allow people to limit the freedoms of others, discriminate against anyone else based on protected characteristics, glorify violence, or praise or support known hate or terrorist organizations on our platform.

To keep others safe, serious threats of violence as well as hate and terrorist groups aren’t allowed on Facebook. We look carefully at content, pages, profiles, and groups and also work with law enforcement if we think there might be a real risk of harm. You can read more about this in our Community Standards.

If you see content like this on Facebook, report it to us so we can review it. Learn more about how to report something on Facebook.

About recommendations on Facebook

What content is recommended?

What content is not recommended?

Why was my content not recommended?

What are recommendation guidelines?

We make personalized recommendations to the people who use our services to help them discover new communities and content. Both Facebook and Instagram may recommend content, accounts, and entities (such as Pages, Groups, or Events) that people do not already follow. Some examples of our recommendation experiences include Pages You May Like, “Suggested For You” posts in Feed, People You May Know, or Groups You Should Join.

Our goal is to make recommendations that are relevant and valuable to each person who sees them. We work towards our goal by personalizing recommendations, which means making unique recommendations for each person. For example, if you and another person have Facebook Friends in common, we may suggest that person as a potential new Friend for you.

Facebook’s baseline standards for recommendations

At Facebook, we have guidelines that govern what content we will recommend to people. Through our Recommendations Guidelines, we work to avoid making recommendations that could be low-quality, objectionable, or particularly sensitive. For users under 18, Facebook has additional age-appropriate content guidelines. Our Recommendations Guidelines are designed to maintain a higher standard than our Community Standards, because recommended content and connections are from accounts or entities you haven’t chosen to follow. Therefore, not all content allowed on our platform will be eligible for recommendation. We use technology to detect content, accounts, and entities that don’t meet these Recommendations Guidelines and to help us avoid recommending them. As always, more severe violations of our Community Standards will be removed from Facebook.

In developing these guidelines, we sought input from 50 leading experts specializing in recommender systems, expression, safety, and digital rights. Those consultations are part of our constant efforts to improve these guidelines and provide people with a safe and positive experience when they receive recommendations on our platform. We’ve worked with youth experts around the world to understand what types of content may be appropriate for adults, but too mature for teens. Our guidelines are designed to ensure recommendations are appropriate for our global community while providing enhanced protections for teen users.

We want to provide you with more information about the types of content, accounts, and entities that we try to avoid recommending, both to keep our community more informed and to provide guidance for content creators about recommendations.

Content recommendations

There are three categories of content that are allowed on our platforms, but that may not be eligible for recommendations. These categories are listed below, as are some illustrative examples of content within each category.

Content that impedes our ability to foster a safe community, such as:

  1. Content that discusses self-harm, suicide, or eating disorders, as well as content that depicts or trivialises themes around death or depression. (We remove content that encourages suicide or self-injury, or any graphic imagery.) We hide certain suicide and self-injury related content to protect teens from potentially distressing or sensitive material. For example, we would age restrict:
    • A post where someone is describing their own personal experiences with suicide, self-injury or eating disorders, except in the context of recovery.
    • A photo or video showing people in a hospital engaging in euthanasia or assisted suicide.
    • A Story where someone is talking about their own extreme weight loss behavior.
  2. Content that may depict violence, such as people fighting. (We remove graphically violent content.) We hide most graphic and disturbing imagery from teens, even if we’d allow it behind a warning screen for adults. For example, we would age restrict:
    • A photo of a severely burned person, which we’d cover with a warning screen for adults.
    • A photo or video of shootings, brutality, or deadly car crashes.
  3. Content that may be sexually explicit or suggestive, such as pictures of people in see-through clothing. (We remove content that contains adult nudity or sexual activity.) We hide additional content from teens that doesn’t contain explicit nudity or sexual activity but could be considered sexually suggestive. For example, we would age restrict:
    • A post with near nudity such as nudity covered by digital overlay.
    • A photo zoomed in on someone’s buttocks.
    • A Story with sexually suggestive language describing sexual encounters, including the use of sexual metaphors.
  4. Content that promotes the use of certain regulated products, such as tobacco or vaping products, adult products and services, or pharmaceutical drugs. (We remove content that attempts to sell or trade most regulated goods.) We hide content from teens that could influence them to engage in activities that are potentially harmful. For example, we would age restrict:
    • A post offering to sell tobacco, nicotine products, alcohol, or firearms when shared by a legitimate brick-and-mortar business.
    • A Story encouraging people to take psychedelic drugs (also known as entheogens) or cannabis products.
    • Images with recipes for alcoholic drinks.
    • A post selling weight loss products or services.
  5. Content that promotes or favorably depicts the use of weight loss products or services and cosmetic surgeries.
  6. Content shared by any non-recommendable account or entity (e.g., Groups or Pages, as outlined below).

Content that is associated with low-quality publishing, such as:

  1. Unoriginal content that is largely repurposed from another source without adding material value.
  2. Long captions unrelated to the underlying content and coordinated comment networks intended to artificially drive engagement and distribution.

False or Misleading Content, such as: In countries where Meta supports third-party fact-checking, content including claims that have been found false by independent fact-checkers. (We remove misinformation that could cause physical harm or suppress voting.)

Account and entity recommendations

We generally do not recommend accounts (including Profiles and Page admins) or entities (such as Pages, Groups, or Events) that:

  1. Recently violated our Community Standards. This does not include accounts or entities that we otherwise remove from our platforms for violating our Community Standards.
  2. Repeatedly and/or recently shared content (including the names or cover photos associated with groups or Pages) we try not to recommend across the categories described in the Content Recommendations section above.
  3. Repeatedly engaged in misleading practices to build followings, such as purchasing ‘likes’.
  4. In countries where Meta supports third-party fact-checking, recently and repeatedly posted “False” and “Altered” information as determined by independent third-party fact-checkers.
  5. Are associated with offline movements or organizations that are tied to violence.
  6. Teens will not be recommended accounts that we’ve found regularly share age-inappropriate content, or if their name or bio suggests the account is inappropriate for teens.

We may let people know when they’re about to engage with an entity that meets any of the above criteria to help them make informed decisions.

A similar set of these guidelines applies to recommendations on Instagram. Those guidelines can be found in the Instagram Help Center.

When you save something on Facebook, you can add it to a collection. It’s also possible to add items to a collection later.

You can save something to a collection from:

  • Marketplace
  • Your Feed

Save a post or video and add it to a collection

  1. Click Options in the top right of the item.
  2. Click Save, Save post or Save video.
