If you’d like to save an Event, click Options then Save. You can then add the Event to a collection like a previously saved item.

Save an Event

Save an item on Marketplace and add it to a collection

  1. Go to the Facebook app.
  2. Tap Menu in the top left of Facebook.
  3. Tap Marketplace. If you don’t see Marketplace, tap See more.
  4. Tap a listing you want to save, then tap Save.
  5. Below Add to a collection, tap the collection you’d like to save it to or create a new collection.

Add a previously saved item to a collection

  1. Click See more on the left menu.
  2. Click Saved.
  3. Find the item, then click Add to collection.

You can add items to more than one collection. If you unsave an item, it’s removed from any collections you’ve added it to. Only you can see the items you’ve saved, unless the privacy settings of the collection are Public, Friends or Contributors only.

Block certain words from appearing in comments on your Facebook Page

If you help manage a Facebook Page, you may block certain words from appearing in comments on your Page. When people include a word you’ve blocked in a comment, we’ll hide the comment so that it doesn’t appear on your Page.

You can also block comments with profanity. Learn how to turn the profanity filter on and off for your Page.

If you have Facebook access to a Page, you can choose up to 1,000 keywords in any language (example: words, phrases or emoji) to block from comments on your Page.

We’ll also automatically hide variations of the keywords that you want to block so that the variations don’t contribute to the 1,000 keyword limit. Variations include common misspellings, plurals, abbreviations and words that use numbers or symbols. For example:

  • If you block the word “tree,” we’ll automatically block variations of that word such as: TREE, t.r.e.e., tr33, treee and #tree. This means that you don’t have to include these variations in your keyword list.
  • If we find keyword variations in your list, you can choose to remove them so that they aren’t included in your keyword limit.

Keep in mind: If you have task access to a Page, you can choose keywords to block in Meta Business Suite. We’ll automatically hide variations for keywords that you add, but you won’t be able to review or remove variations.

Block keywords from your Page

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page photo at the top right, then click Settings & privacy.
  4. Click Settings, then in the left menu, click Followers and public content.
  5. Click Hide comments containing certain words from your Page.
  6. Add keywords that you want to block:
    • To add words or phrases: Type words or phrases separated by commas.
    • To add an emoji: Click Emoji, then select the emoji you want to block.
    • To add a list of keywords:
      • You can copy a list of keywords, paste it in the text box, then press Enter on your keyboard.
      • If you manage multiple Pages, you can copy your keyword list from one Page to another. To copy the list from your Page, click Options. Switch to the Page that you want to add your list to, then follow the instructions above to add your list to that Page.
      • If you’d like to upload a list of keywords, click Options, then select Upload from .CSV and follow the instructions to upload your file.
  7. Review your keyword list.
    • If you included variations in your list, click Show Variations to see them. The variations will appear in gray. You can remove them by clicking Remove [number] Variations.
    • If you want to remove an individual keyword from the list, click X next to it. You can also click Clear list to remove all of your keywords.
  8. Click Save.

Keep in mind

You can only hide comments containing certain words from appearing in content you created. This setting does not affect the comments on other people’s posts or posts you’re added to as a collaborator.

The profiles and Pages that created the comment and their friends will still be able to see the hidden comments.

You can unhide comments that contain blocked words by going to the comment and clicking Unhide.

Change the privacy settings on your collection

Keep in mind

  • When creating a collection on your computer, the collection will be set to Only me. If you invite someone to your collection, it will change to Contributors only. If you remove all contributors, it’ll change back to Only me.

  • When you change the privacy of a collection, the collection will be hidden from any followers who aren’t part of the new audience. If you change the privacy back to include them, it’ll be unhidden for them.

    For example, changing the privacy from Public to Friends hides the collection from any followers who aren’t your friend on Facebook. If you set it back to Public, followers who aren’t your friend will be able to see the collection again.

  • If you want to change the privacy of a collection set to Contributors only, first you’ll need to remove all the contributors. Once you remove the contributors, you can change the privacy setting.

Limit past posts

What happens to tagged posts?

When you share something on your profile, you can use the audience selector to choose who it’s shared with. If you want to change who can see things you’ve already posted, you can:

  • Choose a new audience for one of your past posts.
  • Change who can see all of your past posts to Friends at one time with Limit Past Posts.

Choose a new audience for one of your past posts

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook, then click your name to go to your profile.
  2. Scroll down to the post you want to edit.
  3. Click the audience selector next to the date or time on the post. The icon will be different depending on its current audience settings.
  4. Select who can see the post from the options that appear (example: Public, Friends, Only Me).

Change who can see all your past posts at one time

If you’d like to limit who can see all of your past posts at one time, you can Limit Past Posts in your account settings. This will change all your past posts visible to more people than just your friends (example: posts shared with Public) to be visible to only your Friends.

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. In the left, click Posts.
  4. Next to Limit who can see past posts, click Limit Past Posts.
  5. Click Limit Past Posts to confirm.

When you use Limit Past Posts to change the audience of all your past posts

  • When you Limit Past Posts, you’ll change the audience of all your past posts to Friends. If you want to change the audience of your posts back to what they were, you’ll need to change the audience of each individual post. Limiting the audience of your previous posts cannot be reversed in one click.
  • If you have shared a previous post with a custom audience, such as Friends except Acquaintances or Close Friends, Limit Past Posts won’t change the audience for those past posts.
  • If you tagged someone in the post, the audience of the post will still include the person you tagged and people they include in posts they’re tagged in. Learn more about how to change the audience of a post to just your friends when you tag someone. You can also remove the tag.
  • Limit Past Posts only controls the audience for posts you’ve shared. If you’ve been tagged in someone else’s post, they control the audience for their posts.
  • When you share something on someone else’s profile, that person controls the audience for the post.

Control what you see in Feed on Facebook

Customize my Feed

Hide a story

Stop seeing false news

Reduce clickbait and spam

We care about your experience on Facebook, and we want to make sure that you see the stories that matter to you most. Learn more about what kinds of posts you may see, and here are some ways you can control what you see in Feed.

Fight the Spread of False News

We know that you don’t want to see false news, and we don’t want it on Facebook either. If you feel like you’re still seeing false news, here’s what you can do:

  • Learn how to spot false news. Knowing what to look out for may help you make informed decisions on what to read and share.
  • Mark a news story as false. Learn how to take action on stories that you think are false.
  • Unfollow a person or Page. When you unfollow a person or a Page, you won’t see their posts in your Feed anymore.

Customize Your Feed

We want to show you the stories that are most meaningful to you, but sometimes we might get it wrong. Here’s what you can do to customize your Feed and make sure that you only see the stories that you want to see, when you want to see them.

  • View and adjust your Feed preferences. These preferences help you control what you see on your Feed.
  • Hide a story that appears in your Feed. You can hide a single post, or opt to see fewer posts from a specific person, Page or group.
  • Report something. If you see something on Facebook that you think violates our Community Standards, you can report it to us.
  • Use Interested or Not interested to see more of what you want and less of what you don’t in Feed.

Reduce Clickbait and Spam in Feed

Clickbait and spam are often posts or ads with misleading headlines that may lure you to click on them in your Feed. We’ve made updates so that you’ll see less of these kinds of posts and ads, but if you click on something that you think is spam, learn about what you can do.

Create posts and save drafts for your Facebook Page

Create a Page post

Save a post as draft

The instructions below are for managing your Facebook Page’s posts using Facebook on a computer, the Facebook app for iOS or Android, or Meta Business Suite on a computer. You can also manage your posts from the Meta Business Suite mobile app.

If you have a Facebook profile or additional profile, you can learn more about how to share and manage your posts.

Only people with Facebook access can create a Page post on Facebook. Users who have task access and have been given permission to manage content can only create posts from Meta Business Suite.

You can create Page posts from either Facebook or Meta Business Suite. If you’re using a computer, you can only save multiple posts as drafts in Meta Business Suite. If you’re using the Facebook app, you can only save one post as a draft at a time.

When you create a post from your Page on Facebook, your audience will always be set to public. If you want to adjust your post’s privacy settings, you can create your post in Meta Business Suite.

Create a post from Facebook

To create a post for your Page from Facebook:

  1. Switch to the Page you want to use.
  2. From the top of your Feed, click What’s on your mind, [Page name]?.
  3. Create your post, then click Next. (Note: The audience for your Page’s post will be set to public. If you want to adjust your post’s privacy settings, you can create your post in Meta Business Suite.)
  4. Review your post settings.
  5. Click Post.

Create a post from Meta Business Suite

To create a post for your Page from Meta Business Suite:

  1. Switch to the Page you want to use.
  2. From your Page, click Meta Business Suite in the left menu.
  3. Click Create post underneath your Page’s profile picture.
  4. Add content for your post.
  5. You can add a collaborator for your post.
  6. You can set a specific date and time you want your post to publish.
  7. Adjust your post’s privacy settings.

Save a post as a draft

If you’re using a computer, you can only save posts as drafts in Meta Business Suite. If you’re using the Facebook app, you can only save one post as a draft at a time.

To save a post as a draft:

  1. Switch to the Page you want to use.
  2. From your Page, click Meta Business Suite in the left menu.
  3. Click Create post underneath your Page’s profile picture.
  4. Add content for your post.
  5. Click Finish later to save your post as a draft.

To go back to your drafts:

  1. Switch to the Page you want to use.
  2. From your Page, click Meta Business Suite in the left menu.
  3. Click Content in the left menu.
  4. Click Drafts at the top of the page and then select a draft.
  5. If you want to save the draft again, click Finish later. If you want to publish the draft, click Publish.

Deactivate or reactivate your Facebook Page

Deactivate my Page

Reactivate my Page

What happens if I deactivate?

Deactivating your Page hides it from the public, including people who follow it.

Your Page won’t be visible to the public until it’s reactivated again and you will not be able to make any edits to your Page. You can deactivate your Page at any time if you have Facebook access with full control of a Page. Pages are automatically deactivated if they no longer have at least one person with Facebook access with full control.

You can also unpublish your Page instead of deactivating it. Your Page will no longer be visible publicly while it’s unpublished, but you can still make edits to your Page. However, those edits won’t become visible publicly until you publish your Page

Deactivating or unpublishing a Page does not delete it. Learn more about how to delete a Page.

Note: When a parent Page is deactivated, any child Pages associated with it will also be deactivated. This includes store location Pages or other child Pages linked to the parent Page.

Deactivate your Page

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page’s profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  4. Click Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  5. In the left menu, click Access and control.
  6. Select Deactivate Page and click Continue, then follow the steps to deactivate your page. You may be asked to enter your password.

Reactivate your Page

You cannot reactivate a Page from the Page’s business settings. It can only be reactivated from a personal Facebook profile.

  1. Log into your main Facebook profile.
  2. Click Options or your profile picture at the top right of Facebook.
  3. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  4. Below Your activity, click Reactivate a Page.
  5. Find the page you want to reactivate and click Reactivate.

When you reactivate a parent Page, any child Pages associated with it will also be reactivated. But if the child Page was deactivated separately, an admin has to reactivate it separately from the parent Page.

Note: Child pages can’t be reactivated until the parent Page is reactivated.

What to do if your Facebook account has been deactivated

If you deactivated your Facebook account, Pages that only you controlled were also deactivated. If you’d like to reactivate your Pages, you must first reactivate your account by logging back into Facebook or using your Facebook account to log in somewhere else.

Remember, you’ll need to have access to the email or mobile number you used to log in to complete the reactivation. After you reactivate your account, you can follow the instructions below to reactivate your Pages.

If you deleted your Facebook account, you can cancel your account deletion within 30 days of initiating the deletion and reactivate your Pages.

To cancel your Facebook account deletion:

  1. Log into your Facebook account within 30 days of deleting your account.
  2. Click Cancel Deletion.

If your Page has been deactivated because the last person with Facebook access with full control no longer has an active Facebook account, you can submit a Page admin dispute.

What is identity confirmation?

What happens if I miss the deadline?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

In an effort to increase accountability of Pages, Facebook is requiring people who manage high potential reach Pages to get authorized to publish as their Page. You’ll know if you need to get authorized if you receive a notification from Facebook.

If you receive a notification from Facebook, you must get authorized by the deadline posted in the notification to continue to be able to publish posts as your Page. If you don’t complete the authorizations process before the deadline, your ability to switch into and post as your Page will be limited. You can still post on the Page from your personal profile.

Get authorized

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center in the left menu.
  4. Click on Personal details.
  5. Click on Identity confirmation.
  6. Click on Get started and then follow the on-screen instructions.

Note: If your Page has a System User, you will need to verify all Business Manager accounts in order to let your System User publish on your Page.

You can revisit your authorization status at any point by going to Identity Confirmation in General Account Settings. When you complete this process, it applies to all the Pages you manage and your status will show as “Identity Confirmed.”

Keep in mind that if you turn off two-factor authentication or Location Services, you may be asked to complete the authorization process again.

For more information, please see the Page Publishing Authorizations Guide in the Facebook Business Center.

How is my feedback used?

We welcome your suggestions and ideas. With over a billion people on Facebook, feedback from community members like you helps us as we constantly improve our features and services. Though we can’t respond to everyone who submits feedback, we review many of the ideas people send us to improve the Facebook experience for everyone. We may use feedback or suggestions submitted by the community without any restriction or obligation to provide compensation for them or keep them confidential.

If you’re not looking to give feedback but you need help with a specific issue, you can find answers to common questions in the Help Center.

How We Collect Your Feedback

At some point while you’re using Facebook or the Help Center, you may be asked to fill out a survey. This is one of the ways we ask people to let us know what we can do to improve their experience.

How We Use Your Feedback

Feedback from the people who use Facebook has helped us redesign our products, improve our policies and fix technical problems. We always appreciate your feedback or other suggestions about Facebook. As noted above, we may use feedback or suggestions submitted by the community without any restriction or obligation to provide compensation for them or keep them confidential.

  • The comment will be hidden for everyone else.

Hide comments

To hide a comment and its replies from a post on your Page:

To unhide a comment and its replies from a post on your Page:

  1. From your Page, go to the post that has a comment you want to unhide.
  2. At the top of the comments section, click Most Relevant, then select Hidden by This Page.
  3. Go to the comment you want to unhide, then follow one of these options:
    • Below the comment, click Unhide.
    • Hover over Options, then click Unhide comment.

Sort hidden comments

To sort comments on a post, you can use the dropdown menu in the comments section of a post. When you select Hidden by This Page from the dropdown menu, you’ll see all hidden comments of that post.

The comment ranking setting must be turned on in order to sort hidden comments. Comment ranking is turned on for Pages by default, but you can turn it off at any time.

To sort hidden comments on a post on your Page:

  1. From your Page, go to the post that has hidden comments.
  2. At the top of the comment section, click Most Relevant.
  3. Select Hidden by This Page. From here, you can:
    • See the comments and replies that you chose to hide. If you only chose to hide replies to a comment, you’ll also see the original comment. You’ll also see comments that are automatically hidden by the profanity filter and comments that have words that you chose to block from your Page.
    • Unhide a comment by clicking Unhide below the comment.
    • Block or report a profile. Go to the comment from a profile that you want to block or report, then hover over the profile name. Click Options, then select Block or Report profile.

After you hide a comment, you can report it from the comments section if it doesn’t follow our Community Standards. Next to the comment, click Options, then select Report comment.

You can ban the profile or Page that made the comment by going directly to the profile or Page.

What are ad policies?

There are a few ways to give us feedback about the ads you see on Facebook. Giving us feedback may impact which ads we show you in the future. To give feedback:

How can I navigate Feed using a screenreader on Facebook?

Navigate Feed with screenreader

Feed heading structure

Feed ARIA landmarks

Feed Heading Structure

Your Feed has headings that you can navigate with screen readers:

  • Home is an h1 heading.
  • Feed is an h2 heading and marks the beginning of your Feed stories.
  • Friend requests, messages and notifications are h3 headings that appear when you click one of the icons.
  • The chat sidebar is an h4 heading, as are the subheadings for favorites, groups, friends, apps and other popular features.
  • Individual stories in Feed have h5 headings.
  • Ads have h6 headings.

Feed ARIA Landmarks

ARIA document landmarks are used to represent the major parts of Feed. Besides the main, banner, search and content info landmarks, other navigational landmarks have appropriate labels. For example, the bookmarks menu in the left column is marked as a navigational landmark with an appropriate heading.

You can change your account settings, privacy settings and visit the Help Center from menu options in the banner landmark region.

Check your messages, friend requests and notifications by using the buttons in the banner landmark region on any page.

How do I use hashtags on Facebook?

Who can see my hashtag posts?

Hashtags turn topics and phrases into clickable links in your posts on your personal timeline, Page or groups. This helps people find posts about topics they’re interested in. To make a hashtag, write # (the number sign) along with a topic or phrase and add it to your post. For example:

I just saw the cutest puppy! #dogs.

When you click a hashtag, you’ll see a feed of posts that include that hashtag. You may also see some related hashtags at the top of the page.

Please keep in mind:

  • A hashtag must be written as a single word, without any spaces.
  • You can include numbers in a hashtag, but punctuation and special characters (like $ and %) won’t work.
  • You can search for a hashtag using the search bar at the top of any page.
  • You’ll only see posts that were shared with you.

Learn more about who can see your posts when you use hashtags.

How Page review count and recommendation score are determined

My Page rating changed

Turn on Page recommendations

Remove spam reviews

A Page’s rating is based on the reviews and recommendations people share about the business Page on Facebook. Only Pages that turn on recommendations may show a rating, and a Page may not have a rating if it hasn’t received at least 5 reviews.

Keep in mind that when someone recommends a business, they can select an audience to share it with. For example, if they post a recommendation and select Friends as the audience, only their friends can see their recommendation. Only recommendations that are shared publicly are included in a Page’s overall rating.

Depending on who is viewing the Page, the review count on a Page may fluctuate because some reviews left on a Page are only visible to custom audiences by the reviewer. If a user is within a review’s custom audience (such as a reviewer’s friends), then it will show in their review count.

When the Page admin switches into the Page, the review count that they see is of the number of public reviews, which are the only reviews that help calculate the recommendation score. Public reviews have a globe icon next to the date the review was posted.

We do not verify that users purchased the product or used the service they are reviewing or recommending on Pages on Facebook.

See a Page’s rating

  1. Go to the Page by clicking its name in your Feed or searching for it.
  2. Click Reviews below the cover photo. You may need to click More to see it.

You can learn how to see insights about your Page’s recommendations.

You can also learn how to turn recommendations for your business on or off.

Spam reviews

Any Page reviews that violate our spam policies will be removed to improve the quality and trustworthiness of Page ratings. As a result, when spam reviews are removed, the rating of a Page may change.

If you didn’t post the comment marked as spam, you can click I didn’t post this and we’ll help you secure your account.

How to find eligible posts for Community Notes on Facebook

Why can’t I write a note?

Community Notes on Facebook is currently in beta and some features might be unavailable.

If you find a bug while Community Notes is still in beta, you can report it by shaking your phone.

Community notes are designed to provide helpful context and additional information on posts that may be misleading or could benefit from more context. It’s up to the community to decide which posts get notes and what context is most helpful.

To find posts eligible for community notes, you can either look for posts on your Facebook Feed or select a post from the Community Notes tab.

Find posts from Community Notes

You can quickly find eligible posts from your Facebook menu:

  1. Open Facebook on your device.
  2. Click Menu in the top right of Facebook.
  3. Select Community Notes.
  4. Click Write notes or Rate notes to find eligible posts.

Find posts from your feed

Most public content is eligible for a note, including posts by politicians, Meta, or Meta executives. The following posts most likely are not eligible currently for notes:

  • Private posts
  • Ads

To determine if a post is eligible, open the three-dot menu on the post. If it’s eligible for a note, you’ll see a “Write community note” or “Community Notes” option in the menu.

If you see a post that breaks our rules

If you come across a post that you believe goes against our Community Standards, please report it directly instead of writing a note. This helps our team address or remove the content as quickly as possible. To report a post, go to the three-dot menu and select Report.

Learn more about how to report on Facebook.

Requesting a note

If you find an eligible post that could benefit from additional context, but you’re unable to write a note or are unsure how to proceed, you can request a note. Community Notes contributors can view posts that have been requested and decide whether to add a note.

I don’t think Facebook should have taken down my post

Request a review

My post was removed

Appeal a decision

If Facebook removed your content but you don’t think it went against our Community Standards, we usually offer the chance to request a review on decisions you disagree with. During busy periods, we may not be able to review all requests, but we’ll keep you updated about the status of your request. Even if we are not able to review your request, your feedback still helps us do better in the future.

Facebook removes content like photos, comments, or posts if they violate our Community Standards. Our Community Standards define what is and isn’t allowed on Facebook, and they apply all over the world. They’re designed to encourage expression and create a safe environment on Facebook.

We know we don’t always get it right when we decide to take something down. If your content was taken down and you think it doesn’t go against our Community Standards, you may be able to request a review of the content and we’ll take another look at the decision we made if we can. If we find we’ve made a mistake, we’ll let you know, and your content will be restored. For some types of content, you won’t have the option to request a review but we’re working on adding more options so you’re able to give feedback.

Let us know when you disagree with a decision to remove your content

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click your profile name.
  3. Click Options, then click Profile Status.
  4. Open the message we sent you about taking down this content.
  5. If you see the option, click Request review.

After we review your content, you’ll receive a notification that will let you know if your content is back on Facebook or if we confirmed it didn’t follow the Community Standards.

If we reviewed your content and you still don’t agree with our decision, you may be able to appeal to the Oversight Board. Keep in mind that not all decisions are eligible for appeal to the Oversight Board and the board only selects a certain number of eligible appeals, so they may not choose yours to review. You can read more about the board’s bylaws and structure or learn about them on their website.

Visit our Transparency Center to learn more about how Facebook uses technology and review teams to detect, review and take action on content.

If someone you know is in danger, please contact local emergency services immediately for help.

After you’ve called emergency services, connect with your friend or call someone who can. Showing that you care matters. Make sure they know that you’re there for them and that they aren’t alone.

If the threat of physical danger isn’t immediate, use the resources below.

Resources you can use to help someone

  • Provide support to this person or contact a family member, friend, counselor or teacher who may be able to provide support.
  • Find a local helpline in your country and share resources and contact information that this person may find helpful.
  • Report the content to us so we can reach out to this person with information that may be helpful to them.

Learn about and manage suggested content in your Facebook Feed

Manage suggested content

What influences suggestions?

Hide suggested posts

Turn off suggested content

To help you discover new things on Facebook, we suggest certain content in your Feed. Content suggested for you is personalized based on what may be relevant to you and are influenced by things such as your previous Facebook activity. Content that is suggested for you can be videos, photos, or articles from Pages and groups that you don’t already follow. These suggestions are not paid for.

What influences suggested content

Many factors influence which suggested content you see, and some factors have more influence than others. Some of the most important factors include:

  • Who interacted with the content: Content may be suggested for you if other people who interacted with it also previously interacted with the same group, Page, or content as you.
  • Related topics: If you’ve recently engaged with a certain topic on Facebook, we may suggest other content that are related to that topic. For example, if you recently liked or commented on a post from a basketball Page, we could suggest other posts about basketball.
  • Location: You may see suggested content based on where you are and what people near you are interacting with on Facebook.

Facebook’s standards for suggested content in Feed

Our goal is to make recommendations that are relevant to each person who sees them. Through our Recommendations Guidelines, we work to avoid making recommendations that could be low-quality, objectionable, or particularly sensitive. We also avoid making recommendations that may be inappropriate for younger users.

Manage what you see

You have control over which content is suggested for you in the Facebook app for Android or iOS.

To manage suggested content:

  1. On the Facebook app, go to the suggested content that you want to manage, then tap Options.
  2. Select how you want to manage this content:
    • Hide post to see less content like this.
    • Snooze the Page for 30 days to temporarily stop seeing content from them.
    • Hide all from the Page to stop seeing content from them.
    • Report post if the content concerns you.

Learn the difference between organic, paid and post reach

What is organic reach?

What is paid reach?

Why did my reach drop?

What is post reach?

Post reach is the number of people who saw any of your posts at least once. This metric is estimated.

Paid reach is the number of people who had a paid post from your Page enter their screen. Organic reach is the number of people who had an unpaid post from your Page enter their screen. Organic reach can be broken down into viral and nonviral:

  • Viral: The number of people who had any content from your Page or about your Page enter their screen because their friend likes or follows your Page, engages with a post, shares a photo of your Page and checks into your Page.
  • Nonviral: The number of people who had any content from your Page enter their screen. This doesn’t include when someone’s friend likes or follows your Page, engages with a post, shares a photo of your Page and checks into your Page.

If your post reaches someone through both paid and organic distribution, they’re counted toward each. Keep in mind that the sum of organic and paid reach won’t always equal post reach. For example, if one person sees your post through both organic and paid distribution, they’ll be counted as 1 in organic reach, 1 in paid reach, and 1 in post reach.

Why has my Page’s organic reach dropped?

There are many factors that affect reach, including how people are engaging with your Page’s content, how people have engaged with similar types of content in the past, the quality of the content and other factors such as time of day and whether people are on Facebook on their mobile phone or computer. It’s normal for reach to change based on these factors.

Limit who can see your Facebook posts

Limit who sees my posts

Edit who sees past posts

Change privacy for old posts

You can edit who can see past posts from you when you take a break from someone.

Limit which posts someone can see

  1. Go to facebook.com/take_a_break.
  2. Select the person you’d like to see less of.
  3. Below Edit Who Can See Past Posts, choose the option that best fits your preferences.

Limiting posts

You can choose to keep all posts as they are, edit individual posts, or edit all your posts and posts you’re tagged in.

  • Keep all posts as they are: No posts will be changed. You’ll still see the person you want to see less of in your past posts.
  • Edit individual posts: Edit your posts one by one from your friendship page. You’ll be able to untag yourself in other people’s posts and change the privacy settings for your posts.
  • Edit all my posts and posts that I’m tagged in. Choosing to edit all posts will automatically:
    1. Change the privacy setting for any of your posts that the person you’re taking a break from is tagged in.
    2. Remove tags of you from any posts the person you’re taking a break from has tagged you in.
    3. Remove tags of you from all posts by other people that both you and the person you’re taking a break from are tagged in.

Keep in mind that if you choose to edit all posts and posts you’re tagged in, it may be difficult to find those posts in the future.

Manage AI-generated titles for your public posts

Turn off AI titles

Turn on AI titles

Give feedback on AI title

We may use AI to generate a title for your public posts on your Page or profile in pro mode. We do this because post titles can help others who are searching for content or questions similar to your post.

An AI-generated title may appear at the top of your post and will be attributed to AI, such as through the label Title generated by AI from Meta. It may also appear in search engine result pages.

If you don’t see an AI-generated title when you view your post on Facebook, a title may still have been generated for your post. The title may only appear when someone views your post from search engine results.

AI generates titles based on the content in your post. If you include personal or sensitive information in your post, that information may appear in an AI-generated title and could appear in search engine results.

Note: Some post titles generated by AI may be inaccurate or inappropriate.

Turn AI-generated titles on or off for posts on your Page or profile in pro mode

You can choose whether AI-generated titles appear on your public posts on your Page or profile in pro mode. AI-generated post titles are turned on by default, but you can turn them off for your Page or profile in pro mode at any time.

If you turn this setting off:

  • AI-generated titles won’t appear on your past posts.
  • Meta won’t generate titles for your future public posts.

If you turn this setting on:

  • AI-generated titles may appear on your past posts.
  • Meta may generate titles for future public posts.

Note: This setting doesn’t apply to posts you make in Facebook groups, so titles may still appear on your group posts even if you have this setting off.

To change this setting on Facebook:

  1. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  2. Select Posts.
  3. Turn Allow AI-generated titles on your public posts on or off.

If you don’t see this setting, it may not be available to you.

Give feedback on an AI-generated title

To give feedback on an AI-generated title, log into Facebook.

  1. Go to the post.
  2. Select More options (three dots).
  3. Select the option to give feedback on the title.

Learn more about AI at Meta.

Remove or hide posts from your Facebook Page

Delete a post

Hide a post

Restore a deleted post

I can’t delete a post

These steps are for people with Facebook access to a Page. If you have task access, you can delete or manage Page posts from Meta Business Suite.

You can delete posts shared from your Facebook Page by moving them to the trash. When you move content to your trash, it’ll stay there until it is automatically deleted 30 days later. While it’s in your trash, it will not be publicly visible.

During this 30-day period, you can restore your post to where you originally posted it on Facebook, or you can select content to delete before the 30 days are over. When you restore content, it’ll be visible to the audience that was selected before it was moved to trash.

After 30 days, your post will be permanently removed from your Page and your Page’s activity log. It cannot be restored.

Delete a post from your Page with Facebook access

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page’s profile picture in the top right, then click your Page’s name.
  4. Go to the post on your Page, then click Options in the top right.
  5. Click Move to trash, then click Move.

Keep in mind, when you move something to trash it’ll be automatically deleted after 30 days, unless you choose to delete it sooner or restore it. Once the content is deleted after 30 days, it can’t be restored.

Hide a post from your Page

You may be able to hide some posts (example: cover photo updates, profile picture) from your Page.

When you hide a post, it will be removed from your Page, but not from your Page’s activity log. Hidden posts on your activity log are still discoverable and visible to anyone who has Facebook access to your Page.

If a post you’ve hidden was shared, it may still be visible to the audience it was shared with in other places on Facebook, such as in Feed and search. Any photos in posts you hide from your Page will still be visible when people visit your Page’s Photos section.

To hide a post from your Page with Facebook access:

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page’s profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  4. Go to the post on your Page, then click Options in the top right.
  5. Click Hide post.

To unhide a post from your Page:

If you previously hid posts from your Feed, you can still find and manage them in your Activity Log:

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Go to your Activity Log.
  4. Search for or filter by Hidden posts.
  5. Click Unhide (or Add to Page) next to any post you want to restore.

Note: The ‘Hide post’ option has been replaced by ‘Not Interested’ in the post menu. Posts you mark as Not Interested help personalize your Feed but are not stored as hidden posts in your Activity Log.

Note: This option is only available for some posts.

What does it mean to “Like” something on Facebook?

What does Like mean?

What are reactions?

Can I dislike something?

Clicking Like below a post on Facebook is a way to let people know that you enjoy it without leaving a comment. Just like a comment, anyone who can see the post can see that you liked it.

For example, if you click Like below a friend’s video:

  • People who can see the video will be able to see that you liked it.
  • The person who posted the video will get a notification that you liked it.

When you like something, this lets us know to show you other content that we think you’d also like to see.

Is there a way to dislike something?

You can react to a post or comment (example: ) to express a specific response to something. Reactions include Like, Love, Haha, Wow, Sad and Angry.

Posts that receive a lot of Angry reactions tend to be a factor in negative experiences on Facebook. We use Angry reactions to evaluate and rank content in Feed and reduce those negative experiences. For example, if we see that a post has a lot of Angry reactions, this may affect whether the post will be shown to other people.

Other ways to dislike something

You can hide, snooze or unfollow a post or report something that you dislike. This lets us know that you don’t want to see similar posts in the future.

What it means to save your mobile number or email address for faster login on Facebook

Save my mobile number

Turn off saved login

What is a unique code?

Remove saved login info

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

This feature is only available on some Android devices.

When Facebook asks you to confirm your mobile number or email address, you may be prompted to save your mobile number or email address in order to make it easier to log into Facebook, Instagram or WhatsApp on the same device in the future. You can turn off your saved mobile number or email address any time.

Save your mobile number or email for faster login

The next time you need to confirm your mobile number or email address, follow the prompts to save your mobile number or email address.

Turn off your saved mobile number or email

  1. Tap Menu in the top left of Facebook.
  2. Scroll down and tap Settings & privacy.
  3. Tap Accounts Center. If you don’t see Accounts Center, you may have to tap Settings first.
  4. Tap Password and security
  5. Tap Save login info.
  6. If you have multiple accounts, choose the account for which you want to remove saved login info.
  7. Tap Saved mobile number or Saved email.
  8. Tap Turn off.

What happens when you save your mobile number or email for faster logins

A unique code that is stored on your device will be used to create verification info for your account. The unique code is a randomly generated string of numbers that is encrypted and stored on your device and used to authenticate the device and mobile number or email address of the account you are trying to access. This unique code stays on your device. The verification information is an encrypted token, based on the unique code and the time when it was created. Facebook will use this unique code to confirm that you are on the same device and use the verification info to automatically confirm your account on Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. This process is faster and easier than confirming your account via SMS.

If you register on WhatsApp, your WhatsApp number will then be shared with Meta to see if there is verification info that matches that number. When this happens, Meta will not save your WhatsApp number or use it for any other purpose. Meta will then share the verification info with WhatsApp to pair with the unique code saved on your device and automatically verify your number.

Why are comments ranked?

When you see Most relevant above the comments on a post, it means that comments you see are ranked, and you’re more likely to see high-quality comments that are relevant to you. Learn more about Facebook Feed Ranked Comments.

This means that you’re more likely to see the following at the top:

  • Comments or reactions from your friends.
  • Comments from verified profiles and Pages.
  • Comments with the most likes and replies.

This personalized order is only available for comments on Page posts and profiles with a large number of followers. If a Page manager or profile owner has turned off comment ranking, the Page or profile will display post comments chronologically by default. Learn more about how Facebook ranks comments and posts.

Change the order of comments on a post

You can change the order that you see comments on a Page post as a Page manager or visitor, or on a profile as the creator of the Profile. This only affects how you see comments, not other people. Keep in mind that Pages and some profiles may have different comment ordering options, and changing the order of comments isn’t permanent.

To change the order of comments, click the current comment ordering option in the bottom right of the post (example: Newest comments, All comments, Most relevant). You may need to click View more comments first. From here, select a new option:

  • Newest comments to show all comments, with the newest comments first.
  • All comments to show all comments, including potential spam. The most relevant comments will appear first.
  • Most relevant to show friends’ comments and the most engaging comments first.

What is proactive feedback?

When you have certain experiences on Facebook, like viewing something that you think goes against our Community Standards, you may be asked to give feedback. Hearing from you helps us understand how to make your experience on Facebook better in the future.

Keep in mind that you may not always be asked to give feedback, and providing it is always optional. Some experiences will also allow you to send us a report after you provide feedback so that someone on our Community Operations team can review it.

You can also give us proactive feedback about a product or feature.

Sharing your thoughts and input helps us keep Facebook a safe and welcoming place for everyone.

Why does Facebook cover offensive comments in posts?

Unhide offensive comments

Why are comments covered?

What is comment ranking?

We only cover offensive comments on Feed posts in the Facebook app for Android right now.

When you select the comment section of someone’s Facebook post in your Feed, you may notice that some comments are covered because they might be offensive.

We’ll cover an offensive comment with a message that says, “This comment is hidden because it might be offensive.” The comment will still be visible to the person who wrote it but will be hidden for everyone else.

How does Facebook determine if a comment is offensive?

We may label a comment as being offensive (example: hate speech or violence inciting content) if it appears to go against Facebook’s Community Standards and is unranked. A post’s comments are unranked if the comment ranking setting is turned off for the profile. This means that comments on a post will appear in most recent order by default. Learn more about comment ranking.

Unhide covered comments

To help you engage with things that matter most to you, we’ll let you decide if you want to see comments that might be offensive. If you want to see a covered comment and its replies, select Unhide below the comment. At that time, it will only be visible to you and the person who wrote it. We’ll automatically cover the comment again when you refresh the post.

Why does only a link appear when some news articles are shared on Facebook?

Instructions for news publishers

What is Article 15?

Why are links only headlines?

What happens in Czechia?

The European Union Copyright Directive (EUCD) causes EU member states to create rules for how platforms can display previews of certain news articles. When someone other than the press publisher shares an article from a news site, it may display as a link without images or text from the article. Please note that EU member state countries have different rules which impact how people see news content or links.

While Article 15 of EUCD does not apply to private or non-commercial uses of press publications by individual users or in respect of the use of individual words or very short extracts of a press publication, in order to respect the Article 15 principle of publisher control, Facebook has decided to voluntarily change the way some news links are shared in selected jurisdictions - for example as a headline and hyperlink only - unless the press publisher grants us a licence to display them as we do now, which may include rich rendering based on meta tag designations.

Instructions for news publishers

By default, links to press publisher domains shared by someone other than the press publisher on Facebook or without their permission will be shown with only the hyperlink and the headline of the page linked to.

What happens when a press publisher posts its own publications?

Where a press publisher posts links to its own press publications on Facebook or permits their use, no changes are currently being made to how those links will be shown to users - which may include rich rendering based on meta tag designations. If you are a press publisher and your own posts are showing up in limited form, it might be because you need to verify ownership of your domain and assign it to the page. You can find more information on the Developer Help Center on how to verify your domain and assign it to the appropriate Page. Please note that if your links lead to a subdomain such as “news.example.com,” it is the root domain “example.com” that you need to verify ownership of and assign.

Why Facebook displays country locations on Page posts

My Page location is wrong

Hide my Page location

Why is my location shown?

What is business verification?

In an effort to increase accountability and transparency of Pages, posts in your News Feed from certain pages will show the country or region where the person or business that manages that Page is based.

Only posts from Pages that are based in one country and reach large audiences in another country will show the location of the page manager. Facebook includes this information because, in rare cases, the person posting may try to mislead people about where they’re based.

Will Facebook display country location on my Page posts?

If you are an admin for a Page that reaches a large number of people in a country or region other than the one you’re based in, you may be notified that your primary location will be shown on posts you create.

Your primary location is determined by your information and activity on Facebook, including the stated location on your Facebook profile and device and connection information. If we’re not able to confirm your primary location, you’ll be prompted to complete the Page publishing authorization process in order to continue publishing posts in the Page’s voice.

If you spend several weeks in a country, your primary location might update. If this happens, the primary location shown on Page posts will also update.

If you have completed business verification and show a Confirmed Page Owner country in Page Transparency, we will not show individual posting admins’ country locations but may show your Confirmed Page Owner’s country if it is different from where most of your audience is based.

Note:You can submit a request for Facebook to hide your primary country location for special circumstances including risks to personal safety. Businesses can complete business verification to show their Confirmed Page Owner’s country instead of admins’ country locations.

Why you might see posts from Facebook about registering to vote

Can I register to vote on Facebook?

You may see a post from Facebook asking you to register to vote. This post may also ask you to remind your friends to register to vote. We’ve created these posts because we want to help people who are eligible to vote by reminding them to register before the deadline. If you see one of these posts, it’s likely that the registration deadline to vote in the next election in your area is approaching.

Keep in mind that you can’t register to vote on Facebook. We work with non-partisan organizations, such as TurboVote, to help people register to vote.

Facebook’s parent company, Meta, relies on its legitimate interests as the legal basis to provide these election reminders and related features, as described in the Privacy Policy.

Do not use apps or websites that offer free Facebook likes and followers

I shared my login details

Change my Facebook password

What are access tokens?

My account was limited

If you’ve shared your login information with one of these apps or sites, you should change your Facebook password to protect your account.

Some apps and websites offer free likes or followers in exchange for your Facebook login details. None of these services are affiliated with or endorsed by Facebook, and you should never let anyone else access your Facebook account.

If you give these apps or websites your login information, whether with an access token or by giving them your username and password, they can gain complete access to your account. They can see your personal messages, find information about your friends, and potentially post spam or other harmful content on your profile. This puts your security, and the security of your friends, at risk.

If it looks like you’ve shared your login details with one of these apps or websites, we may limit some features on your Facebook account for a period of time. We may also remove any likes or other engagement you got from using these apps or websites.

You can learn more about how to keep your account secure here.

You can use lists to organize your friends on Facebook. Using a list, you can post an update for specific people, like your coworkers or friends who live near you. You can also see updates from specific groups of people (example: close friends, family).

You can add or remove friends from these lists at any time.

Your friend lists on Facebook

To help you get started, you have friend lists for:

  • Close Friends: Friends you may want to share exclusively with.
  • Acquaintances: People you might want to share less with. You can choose to exclude these people when you post something, by choosing Friends except Acquaintances in the audience selector.
  • Restricted: This list is for people you’ve added as a friend but just don’t want to share with, like your boss. When you add someone to your Restricted list, they will only be able to see your Public content or posts of yours that you tag them in.

You can also create custom lists to organize friends as you like. You choose who goes into these lists and what (if any) privacy restrictions apply.

How does Facebook use my information to show suggestions in People You May Know?

Hide People You May Know

Stop friend suggestions

Why am I seeing suggestions?

People You May Know can help you and your friends connect with other people on Facebook. People You May Know suggestions may show you people you might want to add as a friend who you haven’t seen on Facebook yet or who may be new to Facebook.

People You May Know suggestions can be friends of friends, people in your network or people you may have something in common with.

What information does Facebook use to show suggestions in People You May Know?

People You May Know suggests people you might be likely to add as a friend on Facebook. Friend suggestions come from things like:

  • Having friends in common.
  • Your profile information and networks (example: your current city, school or work).
  • Your Facebook activity (example: joining groups or being tagged in the same photo or post).
  • Contacts you or someone you may know uploaded to Facebook or Messenger.

If you upload your contacts through the Facebook app, learn how to manage contact uploading. If someone has uploaded their contacts and it includes your mobile phone number or email address, you may show up as friend suggestions for each other.

For more information, please see our notice on contact uploading for Non-Users.

I’m seeing people I don’t know suggested as People You May Know on Facebook.

Remove a suggestion

Stop seeing suggestions

Why am I seeing this?

People You May Know suggestions come from things like having mutual friends or being a part of the same network. We regularly update People You May Know to improve suggestions. However, sometimes we might get it wrong and show someone you don’t know or want to add as a friend.

How do I remove a friend suggestion?

If you think a suggestion is unhelpful, you can remove it. Removing unhelpful suggestions helps improve People You May Know so that you see fewer suggestions like them.

To remove a suggested friend:

  • From Friends, click Remove next to their name.
  • From your News Feed, click on the picture of the person you want to remove.

Blocking someone stops them from showing up as a friend suggestion, and you also don’t show as a suggestion for them. Learn more about what happens when you block someone on Facebook.

You can also temporarily hide People You May Know from your News Feed.

Manage follower settings on Facebook

When someone follows you, your posts may appear in their Feed. When you become friends with someone on Facebook, they automatically start following you. If you turn on pro mode for your profile, people who aren’t your friends can follow you.

Your profile type determines who can follow you

The Public follower setting option will be removed from default profiles. These changes will happen to profiles gradually, so you might see some profiles with public followers but not pro mode for now. If you currently have a default profile and allow friends and the public to follow you, you have two options:

  • Keep letting anyone follow you on pro mode, or
  • Use a regular profile and only let friends follow you.

Note: You can regain your previous followers and the ability to have followers by turning on pro mode.

If you don’t choose an option, pro mode will be turned on automatically to keep your followers. To access additional features in pro mode, you must first enable ads.

To enable ads:

  1. Click Boost post on your Facebook post.
  2. Click Enable. When you do, you’ll be agreeing to Meta’s Commercial Terms and acknowledging that Facebook will show more information about profiles in pro mode.

You can turn pro mode off anytime.

Additional settings

  • Public Post Comments: Allows you to select who can comment on your public posts. Learn how to adjust who can like or comment on your public posts.
  • Public Post Notifications: Allows you to select if you want to get notifications when people who aren’t your friends start following you and share, like or comment on your public posts.
  • Public Profile Info: Allows you to select who can like or comment on changes to your Intro section that is part of your public profile. This includes changes to profile photos, profile videos, cover photos, featured photos and Feed updates. Learn how to adjust who can like or comment on your public profile information.

About changes to Meta’s fundraising tools in the European Economic Area

Why are fundraising tools changing?

What happens to my existing fundraiser?

Can I still donate to charities?

What are the new fundraising options?

As of 1 July 2024, current fundraising tools are no longer available on our platforms to any charities in the European Economic Area. You can learn more information in this article about these changes and check what fundraising tools are available for your nonprofit. Specifically, these changes impacted charities in Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Republic of Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden.

Send people to your website to donate

We want to point you to helpful tools so people can donate to your charity directly. In an effort to support charities, we have built the option to update the Donate button at the top of your Page to send people directly to your website to donate by following these steps:

  1. Go to your Page settings.
  2. Select Action button.
  3. Choose Donate.
  4. Add the link to your website.

What to know if your organization was enrolled to receive donations from Facebook Payments

  • Donation services and e-money accounts: As of 1 July 2024, your e-money account agreement with Facebook Payments ended and your Facebook e-money account was closed. You should’ve received your final payout from Facebook Payments on or before 15 July 2024. Charities that still have outstanding funds can contact us for support. Please note that we may be required to refund undistributed balances to the donors.

  • Outstanding funds: You should’ve received your final payout from Facebook Payments on or before 15 July 2024. Charities that still have outstanding funds can reach out through the Payouts contact form for support on required account actions to receive their payouts. Separately, we may contact you to resolve any issues with the outstanding payments. Already approved financial admins can find their current payout method in the Payouts section under settings. Please note, if we cannot process the payment to you, we may be required to refund the donor(s).

  • Fundraising tools: As of 1 July 2024, fundraising tools are no longer available to charities in the European Economic Area. These main features were affected:

  • Feature: On-Facebook Donate Ads; Starting 1 July 2024: No longer supported in the European Economic Area.

  • Feature: Fundraisers, Donate buttons on posts and pages; Starting 1 July 2024: No longer supported in the European Economic Area and all active fundraisers ended automatically and donate buttons are disabled.

  • Feature: Fundraiser API; Starting 1 July 2024: No longer supported in the European Economic Area. This means our API can no longer be used to create fundraisers.

  • Feature: Charity Manager; Starting 1 July 2024: Insights, supporter lists, automated thanking and bulk messaging are no longer available. This means charities don’t have access to past data from these features.

  • Feature: Donation receipts; Starting 1 July 2024: Receipts will only be provided to process refunds or chargeback requests.

What to know if your organization was enrolled to receive donations from PayPal Giving Fund Ireland

  • Fundraising tools: As of 1 July 2024, fundraising tools are no longer available to charities in the European Economic Area. These main features were affected:

  • Feature: On-Facebook Donate Ads; Starting 1 July 2024: No longer supported in the European Economic Area.

  • Feature: Fundraisers, Donate buttons on posts and pages; Starting 1 July 2024: No longer supported in the European Economic Area and all active fundraisers and donate buttons ended automatically.

  • Feature: Charity Manager; Starting 1 July 2024: Insights, supporter lists, automated thanking and bulk messaging are no longer available. This means charities don’t have access to past data from these features.

  • Feature: Transaction reports and Donation activity reports; Starting 1 July 2024: Meta provides a limited transaction report in Charity Manager for informational purposes for donations made to support your charity on Facebook prior to 1 July 2024. For enrolled charities, PPGF Ireland will provide donation activity reports for donations made prior to 1 July 2024 to support your charity on Facebook.

  • Feature: Donation receipts; Starting 1 July 2024: Receipts will only be provided to process refunds or chargeback requests.

Meta requires that nonprofits in the United States using key fundraising tools are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

PayPal Giving Fund will provide donation and fundraising activity reports to nonprofits that are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund. Meta will continue to provide limited transaction and fundraising reports in Nonprofit Manager but will no longer issue tax documentation.

Meta cannot guarantee the accuracy of these limited reports. They will not reflect donation payment processing details, including fees which are charged by a third-party payment processing partner, and should be used for informational purposes only.

About nonprofit registries

Find my nonprofit registry

My nonprofit isn’t registered

My nonprofit lost fundraising tools

Contact Goodstack

As of October 31, 2023, we partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund for nonprofits in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

To qualify for Meta’s fundraising tools, your organization must be actively registered with an eligible registry for your country or region. There may be more than one registry in your country or region. Check that your registry is on the list of acceptable registries.

About nonprofit registries

A nonprofit registry is an official list of nonprofit or charitable organizations. Each country manages its own registries and maintains its own requirements for how an organization is registered.

Registries are managed by your respective country or region. We rely on your country’s government to update each registry with legitimate nonprofits.

To find out if your organization has an active registration or how to get registered, you must contact the registry for your country.

Note: Nevertheless, we only accept certain organization types from a country’s registry.

US-based nonprofits

Meta verifies US-based nonprofits directly with the Internal Revenue Service. Your organization must be a registered 501(c)(3) and must not appear on either the California Attorney General blocklist or the Franchise Tax Board tax-exempt status blocklist.

Nonprofits outside of the US

For nonprofits outside of the US, Meta uses information from our third-party partner, Goodstack, who checks government registries directly and shares details with us. Goodstack is a nonprofit verification service that confirms whether your organization is actively registered with an eligible government registry in your country or region.

If your nonprofit is unable to register or has lost access to Meta’s fundraising tools because of a government-registry issue, please first confirm that you’re on your country’s registry. If your organization is a registered charity but isn’t yet listed with Goodstack, you can register for verification.

Further questions about your nonprofit’s status

If you believe what we have determined about your status is incorrect, you can contact us to resolve the issue.

About offsite donations

Submit a website link

Why was my link not approved?

My donation didn’t go through

In some cases, people may see a “Donate” button on a nonprofit’s Page or on posts directing them to a third-party website to make a donation. Meta doesn’t have any role in processing or paying out these donations made on third-party websites. In these cases, donations to a nonprofit are processed by the payment processor chosen by the nonprofit and/or the third-party website provider, and are subject to the payment processor’s terms and policies, including any applicable refund or fee policies.

Meta has no visibility into or control over these terms or policies, including any terms agreed upon between the nonprofit and its payment processor. Meta also doesn’t issue receipts for these donations. Any receipt you receive will come from the nonprofit or its payment processor.

Why nonprofits may not receive donated funds

If a nonprofit doesn’t receive donated funds, the nonprofit’s payment processor may also have terms or policies governing the nonprofit’s eligibility to receive funds. If the payment processor concludes that its terms or policies are not met, the payment processor may decline to send the funds to the nonprofit. There may also be other instances where the payment processor is unable to deliver the funds to the nonprofit, such as a technical error.

Meta has no control over payment eligibility decisions by the payment processor or other payment processing activities, and isn’t able to view the payout status of any donations to nonprofits made on third-party websites. If you have questions about the status of your donation or eligibility for a refund, please contact the nonprofit or its payment processor.

How website donation links work

If you want to direct people to donate on your website, you must submit a website link for review. You can submit a website link for review at any time by going to Nonprofit Manager on Facebook. Then, in the Website links section, click Submit link.

We’ll review your link, and if it’s approved, any time a link is shared to Facebook or Instagram from that domain, it may include features that may help you get more donations.

Note: You don’t need to submit individual campaign links or pages from your site for approval once your domain is approved.

Why website donation links may not be approved

In some cases, your submitted website link may not be approved. This may be because:

  • The nonprofit organization represented in the link you submitted doesn’t match the nonprofit name we have for you in our records
  • Location data on the link you submitted doesn’t match what we have in our records
  • The link you submitted is a commercial link asking people to buy or shop for items
  • The link you submitted is political or government affiliated
  • The link you submitted contains controversial content, including but not limited to: pornography, misinformation, hate speech, etc.

As of October 31, 2023, we partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund for nonprofits in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

If a donor wants to support an eligible nonprofit automatically each month, they can choose to set up a recurring payment to PayPal Giving Fund (PPGF). This payment will be sent to PPGF at regular intervals, which grants your donated funds to your selected nonprofit in accordance with its policies.

NOTE: Currently, only monthly recurring donations are supported.

How recurring donations work

Donors can set up recurring donations whenever they donate to fundraisers, to posts, or whenever they donate on a nonprofit’s Facebook Page. Learn more about how to donate to a fundraiser or support a nonprofit on Facebook.

If a donor wants to cancel their recurring donation, they need to cancel at least 24 hours before the next billing or renewal date. If the transaction is already processed, PPGF can’t refund the donation. Learn more about requesting a refund for donations on Facebook.

What is PayPal Giving Fund?

As of October 31, 2023, we partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund for nonprofits in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

A donation made to PayPal Giving Fund to support a nonprofit through its Facebook Page or a fundraiser on Facebook may be tax-deductible. Since tax laws vary by country and region, you should consult a tax professional or review the laws for your area to determine whether a donation is tax-deductible.

After you make a donation, you will receive an official donation receipt from PayPal Giving Fund directly to your email. This receipt shows that you’ve made this donation as a charitable contribution and that you’re not receiving any goods or services in return.

Note: Meta will only provide a confirmation for donations which does not act as an official donation receipt that can be used for tax purposes. Donors can find donation confirmations by going to Orders and Payments in the Settings menu.

You can get added as a financial account administrator for your nonprofit’s Facebook Page.

Nonprofits outside of the US must go through Meta’s support team to add finanical administrators to a Page. The steps below will automatically open a support ticket for you if your nonprofit is outside of the US.

Financial account admin abilities

Even if you’re already another type of admin for your Page, you’ll still need to get added to the Page as a financial account admin to have access to these abilities.

  • Change financial info
  • Access donor reports
  • Submit inquires about payments

Add a financial admin

Note: New financial admins have to be added by a current financial admin.

Step 1: Go to Payouts

  1. Login to Facebook.
  2. Click your profile picture at the top right.
  3. Click Settings & Privacy.
  4. Click Settings.
  5. Click Account Settings.
  6. Click Payouts.

Step 2: Add financial admin

Note: Only people who are friends with your nonprofit’s account can be added as finanical admins.

  1. On Payout, click Settings at the bottom left.
  2. Scroll to bottom.
  3. Under “Payout accounts admin,” click Update.
  4. Enter the name of the user account you want to add.

If the current financial admin is no longer with the organization and you can’t contact them, you’ll need to contact the support team to be added as the financial admin. In order to get the financial admin changed you’ll need to reach out from the account of the person you want to be listed as the new financial admin.

For us to make this change, you’ll need a written letter with the organization’s letterhead granting permission for you to be added as the new financial admin. This letter should include:

  • A signature from someone in the organization that has permission to grant this change.
  • The email address associated with your Facebook profile and/or link to your Facebook profile.
  • A copy of your photo ID for verification.

Note: The letter should be scanned and uploaded as a pdf file, and must be clear enough to read for us to accept it.

You can apply to Facebook fundraising tools by completing an online application. Before you begin, make sure you’re the admin of the Page and that your charity is enrolled in PayPal Giving Fund.

Note: You cannot save partially completed applications. If you have to stop working on the application before you’ve submitted, then you’ll have to start over when you return.

Complete application

Note: You’ll need to use a computer to apply.

Step 1: Go to the application

  1. On your computer, login to Facebook.
  2. Complete and submit the application for Facebook fundraising tools.

Step 2: Enter your organization’s info

  1. On the application page, click Start application.
  2. Select your country.
  3. Select Country registry.
  4. Click Next.
  5. Read “Before you start.” Check that you have everything you need.
  6. Click Next.
  7. Enter the details for your organization:
  • Country
  • Business type
  • Registered legal name of organization
  • Nonprofit category. Example: The World Wildlife Fund would be in the “Environmental” category.
  • Address info
  • Organization phone number
  • Organization email address
  • Tax ID type
  • Tax ID number. Note: The ID must be an exact match to the ID that PayPal Giving Fund and the IRS has for your organization. This includes all characters, numbers, spaces, and hyphens.
  1. Certify that the info is true and click Next.
  2. Select your organization in the PayPal Giving Fund Organization Name dropdown.
  3. Click Next.
  4. Enter CEO or highest ranking official information
  • First name
  • Middle name (optional)
  • Last name
  • Date of birth
  1. Click Next.
  2. Click Submit.
  3. Click Done.

After you submit your application, you’ll see a screen that thanks you for applying. Your organization’s Facebook Page will be reviewed as part of the application process. We make sure that what your organization posts follows our Community Standards.

Check your application status

Note: You may receive requests from Facebook after you’ve submitted your application for further or clarifying information. If we reach out to you, we’ll send the request to the Support Inbox of your organization’s Facebook Page.

  • How long review takes: If all information is complete, reviews can take up to 3 weeks from the date you submitted your application. Reviews can take longer if more information is needed.
  • Where to check status: You can check the status of your application in the Support Inbox of your organization’s Page.
  • How we’ll contact you: When a decision has been made about your application, a message will be sent to the Support Inbox of your organization’s Page.
