Saving application and who can submit

You cannot save partially completed applications. If you have to stop working on the application before you’ve submitted, then you’ll have to start over when you return.

Note: Only the admin for your organization’s Facebook Page can complete and submit the application.

Complete application

Note: You’ll need to use a computer to apply.

Step 1: Go to the application

  1. On your computer, login to Facebook.
  2. In the top right, click .
  3. Scroll down to Community Resources, then click Fundraisers.
  4. On the left, under “Sign up for Charitable Giving Tools,” click Sign up. You will automatically go to the application.

Step 2: Enter your organization’s info

  1. On the application page, click Start application.
  2. Select your country.
  3. Select Country registry.
  4. Click Next.
  5. Choose “Network for Good - by check.”
  6. Click Next.
  7. Read “Before you start.” Check that you have everything you need.
  8. Click Next.
  9. Enter the details for your organization:
    • Country
    • Business type
    • Registered legal name of organization
    • Nonprofit category. Example: The World Wildlife Fund would be in the “Environmental” category.
    • Address info
    • Organization phone number
    • Organization email address
    • Tax ID type
    • Tax ID number
  10. Certify that the info is true and click Next.

You’ll automatically go to a screen where you upload documents to verify the info you entered about your organization.

Step 3: Upload verification document, enter CEO info, and submit

  1. To add your document, click Upload. Acceptable documents include:
    • Utility or phone bill: Must be from the last 6 months.
    • Business license: Must be current and government issued.
    • Business tax filing: Must be from previous tax year. Example: If you apply in 2021, then your document must be from 2020.
    • Certificate of formation: Must be from last 50 years.
    • Articles of incorporation: Must be from last 50 years.
  2. You’ll see the file name when it’s uploaded successfully. Click Next.
  3. Enter the info for your CEO or highest ranking official:
    • First name
    • Middle name (optional)
    • Last name
    • Date of birth
  4. Click Next.
  5. Click Submit.
  6. Click Done.

After you submit your application, you’ll see a screen that thanks you for applying. Your organization’s Facebook Page will be reviewed as part of the application process. We make sure that what your organization posts follows our Community Standards.

My Page is not eligible

Meta requires that nonprofits in the United States using key fundraising tools are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

As of October 31, 2023, we partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund for nonprofits in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

Eligibility for Meta’s Fundraising Tools depends on which country/region your organization is based in. Nonprofits that apply and are approved may receive donated funds from PayPal Giving Fund. You will have access to all of the fundraising tools.

Facebook can deny any organization access to Fundraising Tools. Learn more about why an organization might be denied access to fundraising tools.

Apply for Meta’s Fundraising Tools.

Accessing the application for Meta’s Fundraising Tools

To access the application, make sure that you are a Page admin for your nonprofit’s Page, and your nonprofit Page meets the following requirements:

  • The address of the organization is included in the “About” section of the Facebook Page, with the map set to public visibility.
  • The Page’s category is “Nonprofit Organization” or “Charity Organization” as the first option.
  • Page is published (and at least 2 days old).
  • Page has at least 1 post.
  • Has both a cover photo and a profile picture.
  • Follows our Community Standards

To be eligible, your nonprofit must

  • Be registered with an acceptable registry for your country or region. Find a registry.
  • Be in a country or region where donation payouts through our partners is available:
    • United States
    • United Kingdom
    • Canada
    • Australia
  • Be successfully enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund and confirm that the PayPal Giving Fund profile matches your EIN or tax ID on record.

Required info and material

Note: Only the admin for your nonprofit’s Facebook Page can complete and submit the applications. Incomplete applications can’t be saved. If you have to stop before you finish, then you’ll need to start over when you come back.

Category, standing, and Page

  • Good standing with IRS: Before you start the application, check that you are in good standing with the IRS.
  • Know your category: The type of work your organization does or supports. Example: The World Wildlife Federation would be in the “Environmental” category.
  • Have a Facebook Page: Your organization must have an active Page on Facebook.

Info about your organization

You’ll have to provide your organization’s:

  • Name
  • Address
  • Contact info, like a telephone number
  • Tax ID, Charity Number, Registration Number, or Revenue Number based on your location

Info about your CEO or highest ranking official

You’ll need to provide some info about your organization’s CEO or highest ranking official:

  • Name
  • Date of birth
  • Address

All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

PayPal Giving Fund will provide donors with official donation receipts that can be used for tax purposes.

Donation receipts

After you make a donation, you will receive an official donation receipt from PayPal Giving Fund directly to your email. This receipt shows that you’ve made this donation as a charitable contribution and that you’re not receiving any goods or services in return.

Meta will only provide a confirmation for your donation which you can find by going to Orders and Payments in the Settings menu. This is for informational purposes only and not to be used for tax purposes. As the tax laws vary by state and by country, please consult a tax professional regarding the deductibility of this donation.

You can contact PayPal Giving Fund for any concerns regarding missing or lost receipts.

For more support with donations to nonprofit fundraisers, call 1-888-851-6382. A phone agent may open a case for you.

These agents can only open cases for problems with nonprofit fundraisers and donations, or sending or receiving money on Messenger.

You can join others on Facebook in fun activities, like running or doing push-ups, and raise money for nonprofits.

How fundraiser challenges on Facebook work

Nonprofits will create a fundraiser challenge. Users will see an ad in their Feed for the challenge and they can join from there.

When they join, they’ll be prompted to start their own fundraiser to join the challenge. Donors will donate to the fundraiser just as they would any other fundraiser on Facebook.

As they complete the activities in the challenge, they can post about them in the fundraiser they created and the challenge group. Other participants of the fundraiser will post about their activities too.

Join a challenge

When you see an ad for a fundraiser challenge for a nonprofit that you support, you can join the challenge and raise money for the organization.

  1. On your computer, login to Facebook.
  2. From the ad for the challenge you want to join, click the button that lets you join or get started.
  3. At the bottom of the challenge page, click Get started. You’ll be prompted to create your own fundraiser for the challenge.
  4. Follow the prompts on screen to create your fundraiser.
  5. After you’ve entered all the info for your fundraiser, click Create.

After your fundraiser is created, you can invite your friends to donate, or share the challenge to encourage other to participate.

Invite friends to donate

  1. From the “Congratulations” screen, tap Get started. You’ll automatically be moved to a screen where you can invite friends.
  2. Tap Invite next to the names of the people you want to invite.
  3. When you’re done, tap X at the top. You’ll automatically be moved through sharing your fundraiser and donating to it.
    • Note: If you’re not ready to share your fundraiser or donate to it, tap X at the top of the pop up window.

The people you invite to will be notified about your invitation. You can share your fundraiser or donate to it at any time after it’s created.

Share the challenge with your friends

  1. On your computer, login to Facebook.
  2. Click Fundraisers on the left.
    • Note: If you don’t see Fundraisers, then click See more on the left and scroll down to find it.
  3. Click your fundraiser on the left.
  4. Click the name of the challenge to go to the challenge page.
  5. From the challenge page, click Share at the top right.

Share your progress and activity

You can post videos and updates on the progress of your activity to your fundraiser page. You can also share them in the challenge group. You can find the group on the nonprofit’s challenge page.

Giving Funds are a collection of nonprofits related to a similar cause. You can discover Giving Funds in your Feed and choose to make a one-time donation or a recurring monthly donation to the causes you care about. We cover all of the payment processing fees for donations made to nonprofits on Facebook.

How are nonprofits chosen?

We’re working with select community leaders to choose nonprofits that are featured in Giving Funds. The organizations featured in Giving Funds are not chosen by Facebook.

Note: Nonprofits must be enrolled with Meta Pay to be eligible to be in a Giving Fund.

How are funds distributed to nonprofits?

  • Your donation is divided evenly between all the nonprofits in the fund.
  • The minimum donation amount depends on how many nonprofits are featured in the fund. There’s a minimum donation of $1 to each nonprofit, so for example if there are 5 nonprofits, then the minimum donation is $5.
  • Each organization will receive funds according to our payout schedule for nonprofits enrolled with Meta Pay. Organizations receive money bi-weekly if they’ve raised at least $100 USD since their last payment.

What happens after removal?

Meta requires that nonprofits in the United States using key fundraising tools are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

As of October 31, 2023, we partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund for nonprofits in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

You may be able to have your nonprofit removed from Meta’s platforms.

Eligibility for removal support

Due to legal regulations, we are only able to support those nonprofits asking to be removed from Meta’s platforms which are:

  • US-based
  • 501(c)(3)

Request removal

Note: Requests for removal from Meta’s platforms must be made by an authorized representative of that organization.

You can request that your organization be removed from Meta’s Facebook and Instagram platforms, through this contact form. You can also request to have your organization removed through PayPal Giving Fund.

Removal process

After you send us your request to be removed from Meta’s platforms, one of our agents will respond to your request and ask you to verify your organization’s identity.

Provide verification documentation

To verify your nonprofit, you’ll be asked to provide us with a minimum of one of the following types of documentation:

  • Utility Bill (must be a bill within the last 6 months)
  • Business license
  • Company Letter authorizing your role on company letterhead
  • Government Documentation. Example: Tax documentation
    • Note: Tax documents must be from the previous year’s filing
  • Certificate of Formation (within the last 50 years)
  • Article of Filing (within the last 50 years)

Your organization’s name and EIN number must match what Meta has on file for the organization. If the information doesn’t match, then we won’t be able to remove the organization from our platforms.

Be sure that your documentation:

  • Is clear, not blurry or creased
  • Is within acceptable timeframes
  • Provides all the relevant information
  • Blacks out any personal information

Our agents review

After we’ve received your documentation, our agents will review. They will be verifying that:

  • The requester is an authorized representative of the organization
  • All of the provided information matches our files
  • The organization is US-based
  • The organization is a 510(C)(3)

You’re notified with decision

When all of the provided documentation has been reviewed and a decision has been made, we will email you with that decision. If we are unable to remove the organization from our platforms, we’ll let you know what next steps are for continuing your request.

Requests are commonly denied because the:

  • Provided documentation was out of date
  • Information, like name or EIN number, provided didn’t match our records
  • Images of the documentation were unclear or blurry

You’ll be able to respond to the email with supplemental documentation.

After an organization is removed from Meta’s platforms by their own request:

  • All fundraisers for that organization will be ended.
  • All processed donations will be paid out from PayPal Giving Fund.
  • All unprocessed donations will be refunded to donors.
  • The organization will no longer have access to Meta’s fundraising tools.
  • The organization will be able to access tools again if it’s in good standing with the IRS and all governing agencies.

To regain access to Meta’s fundraising tools, reach out to us using this form.

You can create a fundraiser to support nonprofits and causes you care about.

Receiving the Donation

Birthday donations from Facebook are sent to nonprofits in a monthly payment at the beginning of the month, separate from other payouts. Donations are distributed based on how the nonprofit is set up to receive donations:

  • Nonprofits connected to Meta Pay receive the donation via electronic transfer from Facebook.
  • Nonprofits that receive Facebook donations through Network for Good’s Donor Advised Fund will be mailed a check of Facebook donations from this pilot program to the address listed in GuideStar.
  • Nonprofits that have registered for a free account with Network for Good and have signed up for electronic funds transfer will receive their Facebook donations via electronic payment.

Enroll with PayPal Giving Fund

Funds not granted to nonprofit

Meta requires that nonprofits in the United States using key fundraising tools are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

As of October 31, 2023, we partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund for nonprofits in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

We partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund to benefit nonprofits in the Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. PayPal Giving Fund receives donations and grants donated funds to benefiting nonprofits, based on their policies and terms in eligible countries.

How funds are distributed

Note: You are responsible for complying with any applicable local fundraising laws.

When people donate to charitable causes, the money goes directly to PayPal Giving Fund. PayPal Giving Fund distributes donated funds to benefit nonprofits. All donated funds may be used by the benefiting charity on an unrestricted basis, regardless of any designations made by the donor or fundraiser creator.

Enrollment eligibility and country policy

As of December 16, 2024, nonprofits in the United States that are enrolled to use Meta’s fundraising tools are required to be enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

Enrollment is free and eligibility is based on policies in each country. Learn more about enrollment eligibility. Nonprofits do not have to be enrolled with Meta or with PayPal Giving Fund to receive donations, however, nonprofits enrolled with Meta and PayPal Giving Fund will receive donated funds more quickly and have access to all of Meta’s fundraising tools.

When funds are granted to nonprofits

  • Nonprofits enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund: PayPal Giving Fund will distribute donated funds within 45 days. Payouts are issued at the end of the month. You can learn more about how to enroll with PPGF.
  • Nonprofits not enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund: PayPal Giving Fund will distribute donated funds via check within 45 days in the US, and 90 days in Canada, the UK, and Australia.
  • Emergency response: When there’s a natural disaster, humanitarian crisis, or other event that needs urgent action, PayPal Giving Fund may try to accelerate grants to nonprofits working on relief and recovery for those events.

When funds cannot be granted to nonprofits through PayPal Giving Fund

  • No response: The organization didn’t respond to PayPal Giving Fund’s attempts to arrange delivery of the funds, or the check was returned or refused.
  • Nonprofit closed: The nonprofit closed after the original donation or is no longer accepting donations.
  • Does not meet requirements: The nonprofit does not meet the requirements of the Charity Certification Policy.

When PayPal Giving Fund cannot deliver funds to the nominated nonprofit, they will (whenever possible) ask donors to recommend another nonprofit. If the donor doesn’t respond, PayPal Giving Fund will reassign the funds to a similar nonprofit, as per the Donation Delivery Policy.

When will I get my payout?

What is a similar nonprofit?

Meta requires that nonprofits in the United States using key fundraising tools are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

Donations are made to PayPal Giving Fund, which grants donated funds to nonprofits according to PayPal Giving Fund’s timelines.

For PayPal Giving Fund-enrolled nonprofits, PayPal Giving Fund will distribute donated funds within 45 days. Payouts are issued at the end of the month. For PayPal Giving Fund-unenrolled nonprofits, PayPal Giving Fund will distribute grants with a check within 45 days in the US, and 90 days in Canada, the UK, and Australia. However, there are a few reasons why grants might not be paid out.

Reasons nonprofits may not receive donated funds

  • No response: The nonprofit didn’t respond to PayPal Giving Fund’s attempts to arrange delivery of the funds, or the check was returned or refused.
  • Nonprofit closed: The nonprofit closed after the original donation or is no longer accepting donations.
  • Does not meet requirements: The nonprofit does not meet the requirements of PayPal Giving Fund’s Charity Certification Policy.

When PayPal Giving Fund cannot deliver grants to the chosen nonprofit, they will, whenever possible, ask you to recommend another nonprofit. If you don’t respond, they will reassign the funds to a similar nonprofit, as per their Donation Delivery policy.

You can track and view the status of your donation by clicking the link within the official donation receipt sent to you by PayPal or through the PayPal Giving Fund donation tracker using the transaction ID.

Learn more about PayPal Giving Fund’s Nonprofit Certification and Donation Delivery policies.

You can also learn more about charitable giving with PayPal Giving Fund.

Why fundraising on Facebook isn’t available in India

Why can’t I fundraise?

When will fundraising return?

My fundraiser was before April 1

What was paused?

Fundraising in India is regulated by the Government of India and Indian charities on Facebook must be registered with GiveIndia.

Why fundraisers in India aren’t working

Facebook has paused all nonprofit fundraising and donations in India as of April 1, 2021. New laws announced by the Government of India require charities to file donor statements. The donor statements have to include donor IDs and user information that confirms the donor’s identity.

When fundraising tools will be available in India

As of now, all nonprofit fundraising tools and donations will be turned off indefinitely. We’re working to align our tools with the new regulations.

What’s been paused

The creation of any nonprofit fundraiser has been paused. All donations to nonprofit fundraisers or made directly to charities has been paused.

Fundraisers started before April 1, 2021 in India

  • If you started a fundraiser before April 1, then any funds raised up to March 31 will be paid out to the charity.
  • If your charity received donations before April 1, then those donations will be paid out to your organization.

Find out about donation refunds.

We’re required by European anti-money laundering laws to verify the identity of people making donations in certain amounts.

Why we ask for ID

European anti-money laundering laws require us to ask for ID from anyone that:

  • Makes a single donation that’s more than 50 euro
  • Donated more than 150 euros over a 31 day period

Types of ID you can provide

The ID you provide:

  • Must be government issued.
  • Must clearly show:
    • Name
    • Date of birth
    • Expiration date
    • Photo
  • Must be in color.
  • Must be a jpeg or .png
  • Cannot be damaged.
  • Cannot be a screenshot

How often you’ll be asked for ID

After we verify your identity, you can then make donations up to 500 euro. We cannot accept donations more than 500 euro.

About game privacy settings for games that do not require Facebook Login for Games

Change game sharing preferences

Update individual game settings

What is a game?

Certain games on Facebook can now be played without Facebook Login for Games and offer updated data-sharing options when you play. You can recognize these games by the icon in their game titles. These games can still offer personalized and social play experiences, but without asking you to share your Facebook profile data, email address, and friends list data with third-party game developers.

To help third-party apps comply with applicable laws and regulations concerning teens, we may share information about your age category (example: whether you are under 18) with third-party app and game developers on our platform.

Managing your sharing preferences for games

The first time you play any game, you can select which profile you want to use for your in-game identity — either your real Facebook profile name and profile picture, or a gaming-specific profile. You can also select your game visibility setting, which controls who on Facebook can see your gaming activity and enables third-party game developers to support social gameplay. Both of these selections will be applied to future games and allow you to start playing these games faster in the future.

You can always change your default sharing preferences within the Game Privacy settings in the Games tab on Facebook. Within these settings, simply tap Sharing preferences to update your default sharing preferences.

To change your default sharing preferences:

  1. From your Feed, click Play Games in the left side menu. (Note: If you don’t see Play Games, click See More.)
  2. Click , then click Game Privacy.
  3. Click Sharing preferences.
  4. Select your sharing preferences.
  5. Click Save.

You can update the individual game visibility preferences for each game you play. You can also update the individual profile selection preferences for each game you play (this option is only available to certain users).

To update your individual game preferences:

  1. From your Feed, click Play Games in the left side menu. (Note: If you don’t see Play Games, click See More.)
  2. Click , then click Game Privacy.
  3. Under Games you play, select a game.
  4. Select your sharing preferences for that game.
  5. Click Save.

You can also learn more about game privacy settings for games that require Facebook Login for Games.

What happens if I turn off?

Remove connected apps

Turning off Facebook’s integration with apps, games and websites removes apps or games you’ve connected to your Facebook account. You may have connected them to your account either by logging into them with Facebook or linking an account you have with them to Facebook (example: loyalty program or news subscription).

If you turn off Facebook’s integration with apps, games and websites, you won’t be able to log into apps, games and websites using Facebook or connect accounts you have with other apps and websites to Facebook. You may also lose information (example: favorite places, high scores) that can’t be recovered, and posts by apps or games to your timeline may be removed.

Turn off Facebook’s integration with apps, games and websites

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Apps and Websites in the left side menu.
  4. Scroll down to Preferences, then next to Apps, websites and games, click Turn Off.

Check your internet connection

Update your browser

Restart your computer

  • Close your internet browser and restart your computer.

How Ask on Forum works?

Ask questions on Forum

Forum is currently available for some people in the US, so it may not be available to you yet.

Find advice, recommendations, and insights on Forum from real people across Facebook groups using Ask.

You can find answers with Ask:

  • In the Ask tab in the bottom menu of the Forum app.

How Ask works

When you ask a question, Ask uses AI to:

  • Gather helpful insights from real people’s group posts and comments.
  • Summarize the most relevant posts and comments to answer your question.

Ask responses include information from public Facebook groups and groups you’re in. From the Ask response, tap to read the original posts and comments in the groups where the conversations happened.

What you can do with Ask

  • Ask questions: Type your question into the search bar to get answers and advice.
  • Explore topics: Tap on related questions to learn about connected topics.
  • Find groups: Discover new groups to explore and join related to your question.

Notes

  • Ask focuses on showing you high-quality answers and advice from real people. The answers you see may be personalized based on the groups you’re already in.
  • The AI that powers Ask summarizes existing group posts and comments.
  • Because Ask uses AI, the summaries might not be complete or may be inaccurate or inappropriate. Always read the original posts and comments for the complete context.
  • Keep in mind, your group’s posts and comments may show up in Ask.
  • Meta’s AI Terms apply to Ask on Forum.

Learn more about AI at Meta.

About Batch Mentions on Facebook

Who can see batch mentions?

Who can use batch mentions?

Turn off batch mentions

Batch mentions limits

Batch mentions is an alert feature on Facebook that allows you to mention multiple people in a post, comment, video, story or reel. This can be useful if you want to get the attention of a group of people at once. The batch mentions available to use are:

  • @followers helps creators keep their followers informed on their latest updates.
  • @attendees helps the event host share updates with attendees.
  • @everyone helps group admins update group members.
  • @highlight helps users share moments and highlights to friends.

Who can see content with batch mentions

Only people who can already see your content will be able to see batch mentions. For example, if you make a post and only some of your friends can see it based on your audience selection, then those friends will be the only ones who can see a batch mention.

Batch mentions notifications

Facebook has rules to prevent spam and make sure that batch mentions aren’t overused.

Here are some reasons why someone won’t get a batch mention notification:

  • They are not in the audience for the batch mention.
  • They can’t see the original content.
  • They have turned off your batch mentions settings.
  • If they blocked you.
  • If they already received too many batch mentions notifications in one day, they won’t receive any more.

Note: Facebook’s Notifications AI system will also decide whether or not to send a notification. By predicting what’s most likely to be relevant and interesting, the AI system will automatically determine the order in which new notifications are displayed.

Who can use batch mentions

Not everyone can use batch mentions. Here are some reasons why you might not be able to use the feature:

  • You are not the owner of an event and can’t use @attendees.
  • You are not an admin or moderator of a group and can’t use @everyone.
  • You don’t have any followers and can’t use @followers.

Note: If a group is too large, it may not support batch mentions.

Batch mentions use limits

To prevent people from using batch mentions too much, there are limits on the feature. For example, you might only be able to use @followers once per day. If you reach this limit, you won’t be able to use the feature again until the next day.

Turn off batch mentions

You can turn off all batch mentions notifications in your tag settings page. This means you won’t receive any notifications when someone mentions you in a post or comment. You can also turn off batch mentions from a specific group.

About customer lists on Facebook

What is a customer list?

How is my data protected?

Manage my ad preferences

Why am I seeing this ad?

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

A customer list is a file that contains information which is used by businesses to show you relevant ads on Facebook. Contact information in these lists is encrypted so your information is protected.

About customer lists

When you interact with a business, you may give them some information, like your name or phone number, to get business updates. That business, or an associated business, may want to reach you on Facebook. To reach you, they can upload a customer list on Facebook that may include your information.

A customer list consists of “identifiers”, which typically include a name, phone number or email address. The purpose of using this information is to help reach you, including by matching the identifiers with Facebook profiles.

How Facebook uses customer lists to show you ads

When the business uploads its customer list, user contact information from the list is encrypted using a cryptographic security method known as hashing. This turns the identifiers into randomized code to make sure your information is protected. This security feature also ensures that Facebook doesn’t receive your actual contact information from the customer list.

Once your information is turned into randomized code, the matching process can begin.

Facebook’s system takes the contact information it already has and turns it into a randomized code. Then this code is compared to the code uploaded by the business. If the code matches, Facebook may show a relevant ad.

After the match process is completed, Facebook will delete the hashed contact information.

Manage your ad preferences

You can go to your Ad preferences page and view advertisers that can choose to show their ads to certain audiences you have been included in based on your activity or information and decide whether these audiences can be used to show you ads.

Learn more about the ads you see on Facebook.

About Dashboard

Access my Dashboard

What is Dashboard?

Dashboard vs Professional Dashboard

This feature is gradually being released and not yet available to all users.

Dashboard is a feature in the Facebook app where you can get insights into your activity and inspiration for creating engaging content.

Tools and features in Dashboard

  • Challenges: Gain new skills when you produce original posts and engage with your connections.
  • Performance: See a summary of your profile’s performance over the last 28 days including content published, content engagement and reels/video plays. You can also find more detailed insights on your reels, videos and posts as further described below.
  • Reels: Turn your most popular videos into reels, find music from trending reels and explore different reels templates.

How to access Dashboard

You can access your dashboard from the Facebook app on iPhone or Android.

Differences between Dashboard and Professional Dashboard

While Dashboard is available to users on their main profile, Professional Dashboard is only available to users who have turned on pro mode or manage a Page. Professional Dashboard gives users access to advanced insights and professional tools that are geared more towards creators or businesses. (Note: If you have pro mode turned on, you will have access to Professional Dashboard instead of Dashboard.)

A few examples of insights and tools that are available in Professional Dashboard, but not on Dashboard, include reach, clicks, audience insights and monetization.

How we provide insights in Dashboard

If you access Dashboard, you can see aggregated insights to help you understand how people are engaging with your content, including posts, reels and videos. To provide these insights, we use aggregated information about how other people engage with your content on Facebook.

Even if you do not use Dashboard, your activity on Facebook (such as viewing another user’s post or reel or liking another user’s post) may be included in aggregate reports made available to other Facebook users who are using Dashboard. The type of information we collect and may display in aggregated form in Dashboard includes user activity such as the number of views, plays, replays, reactions, comments and shares. These insights are available on a range of content types, including posts, reels and videos. Where content is public, we may also show the breakdown of friend vs non-friend engagement.

About E-Invoicing for Taiwan

Basic Mobile Browser Help

Basic Mobile Browser Help

View my eGUI

What is an eGUI?

Beginning January 1, 2020, Facebook will enable the creation of electronic Government Uniform Invoices (eGUIs) via the Taiwanese E-Invoice Platform. To do this, Facebook will send transaction data to the Taiwanese E-Invoice Platform for Digital Goods and Services deemed in scope. This is in accordance with Taiwanese local laws as directed by the Ministry of Finance, which came into effect January 1, 2020.You may log into the Taiwanese E-Invoice Platform, approximately 48 hours after a transaction is made, to view your eGUI. Note that Facebook will associate your eGUI with your email address. If you already had an email address at the point of purchase, Facebook will use this. If you don’t have an email address at the point of purchase, they will be prompted to enter one and this will be used.Keep in mind that Facebook is not able to give tax advice. If you have any questions about your eGUI we suggest you contact your local tax advisors or the Taiwanese E-Invoice Platform administrators.

How to claim your lottery award

  1. Download the official Taiwan Ministry of Finance mobile app for iOS or Android.
  2. Open the Ministry of Finance mobile app.
  3. Select Carrier Pairing Settings.
  4. Select Add Carrier to pair your email to your mobile device.
  5. Tap Award Settings to pair your bank account information with your mobile device. You’ll receive an email from the Ministry of Finance if you win the lottery award. Winning numbers will be announced on the 25th day of the following month (example: Jan. to Feb. winning numbers will be announced on the March 25).The award will be wired into your bank account after you claim it in the Ministry of Finance app after the 5th day of the following month. Please contact the Ministry of Finance directly if you have any questions about the lottery.

About Facebook Page access

Basic Mobile Browser Help

Basic Mobile Browser Help

Give someone Page access

What is Facebook access?

What is task access?

Remove someone’s Page access

You can give trusted people Facebook access or task access to help manage your Page.

Facebook access

Facebook access comes with full control or partial control. People can switch into the Page and manage it on Facebook or through other Facebook tools. With Facebook access, people can manage the following with full or partial control:

  • Content: Create, manage or delete any content on your Page like posts, Stories, and more. Apply for rights management and monetization of original content.
  • Messages: Respond to direct messages as the Page in Inbox.
  • Comments: Respond to comments on the Page and edit or delete existing comments made by the Page.
  • Linked Accounts: Add, manage or remove linked accounts, such as Instagram.
  • Ads: Create, manage and delete ads.
  • Insights: Use Page, post and ad insights to analyze the performance of the Page.
  • Events: Create, edit and delete events by the Page.
  • Removal and Bans: Remove or ban people from the Page.

People with full control can also manage:

  • Settings: Manage and edit all settings, such as Page information and deleting the Page.
  • Access: Give or remove people’s Facebook or task access to the Page or linked Instagram account, including people with Facebook access with full control.

Giving Facebook access with full control to others gives them the same access as you. This means that they can give other people access to manage the Page, remove anyone from the Page (including you), or delete the Page. For your Page to remain active, it must have at least one person with Facebook access with full control. If there is no longer anyone with full control over the Page, it will be automatically deactivated and scheduled for deletion.

Task access

People with task access can manage the Page from other management tools such as Meta Business Suite, Creator Studio, Ads Manager, or Business Manager. This means they can’t switch into the Page or manage it on Facebook. People with task access can manage the following:

  • Content: Create, manage or delete any content on your Page like posts, Stories, and more. Apply for and access ways to manage rights to and potentially monetize your original content.
  • Messages and Community Activity: Respond to direct messages, comment, manage unwanted content, and report Page activity.
  • Ads: Create, manage and delete ads, and other ads-related tasks.
  • Insights: View Page, content, ad, and metric performance.

Community Manager access

Community Managers have access to moderate the chat of the Page’s live streams. They can’t switch into the Page or manage it on Facebook. Community managers can moderate live chats through the following actions:

  • Deleting, or reporting comments.
  • Suspending users from live stream chat for 15 minutes.
  • Ban users from current live stream, or from all live streams on the Page.
  • Pin comments to the top of the live chat. Note: If your Page is part of a business portfolio, your access levels are different.

About Facebook’s Network of Support

What is Network of Support?

What is anti-LGBTQ bullying?

The Facebook Network of Support (NOS) is comprised of six leading LGBTQ (lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, and queer) advocacy organizations. These organizations serve in a consultative capacity to Facebook on issues like anti-LGBTQ bullying. Learn more about these organizations:

  • GLAAD rewrites the script for LGBTQ acceptance. As a dynamic media force, GLAAD tackles tough issues to shape the narrative and provoke dialogue that leads to cultural change. GLAAD protects all that has been accomplished and creates a world where everyone can live the life they love.
  • GLSEN champions safe and affirming schools for all students. We envision a world in which every child learns to respect and accept all people, regardless of sexual orientation or gender identity/expression.
  • The Human Rights Campaign (HRC) is America’s largest civil rights organization working to achieve lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender equality.
  • The National Center for Transgender Equality (NCTE) is the nation’s leading social justice advocacy organization winning life-saving change for transgender people.
  • PFLAG promotes the health and well-being of lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender persons, their families and friends.
  • The Trevor Project is the leading national organization focused on crisis and suicide prevention efforts among lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and questioning (LGBTQ) youth.

Forum, a Facebook app, brings all your Facebook Groups and group conversations into one place. On Forum you can:

Forum and Facebook work together

Jobs eligibility

If you want to find or create a job on Facebook, you can use Marketplace to browse or create jobs. You can also create a job on your Page or in a group.

Jobs are public and can be seen by anyone on or off Facebook, including on Pages, Marketplace and Feed or other Meta platforms such as Instagram. Jobs are meant for people 18 years old or older and will be visible to adults on Facebook.

Some jobs that are shared on Marketplace may be listed by a third-party partner. If you want to apply to a job shared by a third-party partner, you’ll be redirected to the partner’s website. Any information you enter onto the partner website will be shared with the third-party partner and the employer.

When you message an employer from a job listing, the employer can view your Jobs Profile. You can choose whether your Jobs Profile is discoverable, but an employer you message can still see your Jobs Profile.

Who’s currently eligible

Learn our rules for jobs

  • Jobs that fall into these categories are prohibited on Marketplace:
    • Adult entertainment
    • In-person childcare, including nannies, babysitters, teachers and teacher assistants
    • Modeling, including underage modeling
    • Personal training
    • Physical therapy
    • Travel, including flight attendants, cabin crew, travel agents and tour guides
  • Jobs are meant for people aged 18 years or older. Any job postings targeting minors will be removed.
  • Jobs that are detected as fraudulent, including but not limited to – get-rich-quick, multi-level marketing or personally-identifying information harvesting schemes – will be removed.
  • Jobs found to be misleading, violent, hateful or containing discriminatory language will be removed.

About music in your content on Facebook

Add music to my video

Music in live videos

My video was muted

Dispute a music claim

We want to encourage musical expression on Facebook, while making sure we uphold our agreements with music rights holders. These agreements protect artists, songwriters, and other music rights holders by setting limitations around the amount of recorded music that can be included in Live broadcasts, videos, or your text posts.

You can add music to:

  • Live broadcasts
  • Reels
  • Stories
  • Text posts

About guidelines for using music in your content

Please keep the following general guidelines in mind when using music in your content:

  • There are no limits on music in Stories, or traditional musical performances (example: filming a live artist or band performing their own music).
  • The more full-length recorded tracks in your video, the more likely the video may be limited (example: muted or blocked).
  • Shorter clips of music are recommended in your videos.
  • There should always be a visual component to your video; recorded audio should not be the primary purpose of the video.

If we detect that your live video broadcast includes music in a way that doesn’t adhere to our music licensing agreements, you may receive a notification from us while filming. This notification is intended to alert you so you can make changes to your stream and avoid interruptions. If your video is muted or blocked, we’ll make it clear what actions you can take to stop the interruption. These actions may include an option to dispute a rights holder’s claim if you believe it was made in error.

If music rights change on Facebook, and you’ve added a song to your post, your story, or reel that Meta no longer has the rights to, your video will be blocked from being viewed by other people or will be muted.

For music in Stories:

  • Your story will be muted or blocked from being viewed by other people. Other photos and videos that don’t have the music won’t be muted or blocked.

For music in Reels:

  • Your reel will be blocked from being viewed by other people. You can download your reel and republish it with new music

For music in text posts:

  • Your post will be muted or blocked from being viewed by other people. Other photos and videos that don’t have the music won’t be muted or blocked.

Learn more about our Music Guidelines in our Terms of Service or how to replace muted audio on the Meta Business Help Center.

Accept or remove a fan badge on Facebook

How do fan badges work?

We are gradually enabling creators to set a custom top fan badge name for their most engaged fans. If a creator you engage with has set a custom top fan badge name and you are eligible to accept this badge by being one of their most engaged fans, you’ll receive a notification to accept the badge.

Any information in this article about the top fan badge also applies to a custom top fan badge name.

You can become eligible to display a rising fan or top fan badge for a creator’s Page or profile by being one of their most engaged fans.

  • Rising fans have earned a badge by starting to frequently engage with a creator by reacting to their content and commenting on or sharing their posts. They can be on their way to earning a top fan badge with continued engagement.
  • Top fans have earned a badge by continuously engaging with a creator by reacting to their content and commenting on or sharing their posts.

Accept a fan badge

Once notified of your rising fan or top fan status, select Accept badge from the notification to accept it. You can only qualify for one badge type at a time for every creator you earn a badge for.

If you accept a rising fan or top fan badge for a creator, or if you selected Turn on badges to earn badges for multiple creators at once, the badge(s) will appear next to your name when you comment on their posts. The creator may recognize rising fans or top fans in a public appreciation post that also displays your profile photo and name.

The badge is public, but it will only appear next to your name on the creator’s Page or profile you’re a rising fan or top fan of, not in your other interactions on Facebook.

Remove a fan badge

You can remove a top fan or rising fan badge at any time.

To stop displaying the badge, find a comment you’ve made on the creator’s Page or profile. Click the badge next to your name, select Manage Badge and toggle the badge on or off.

It may take some time for the changes to take effect.

How rising fan and top fan badges work

If you’ve accepted the rising fan or top fan badge:

  • The badge will appear next to your name in any comments you make on the creator’s Page or profile you’re a rising fan or top fan of, including your past comments. The badge will not appear in your other interactions on Facebook.
  • If you accept a rising fan or top fan badge, you automatically follow the Page or profile that the badge is for.
  • Rising fans and top fans are regularly updated, so it’s possible to lose your fan badge, but you can earn it back if you become a top engager again.
  • Rising fans and top fans may gain access to exclusive perks. If you lose your rising fan or top fan badge, you’ll no longer have access to these perks.
  • Creators can choose to remove individual rising fan or top fan badges, or turn off these badges for their Page or profile. If this happens, you will lose your badge.

Learn how to manage rising fan and top fan badges if you manage a Page or profile.

Appeal a Facebook content decision to the Oversight Board

Appeal my content decision

Appeal content I reported

Check my appeal eligibility

What is an Oversight Board Reference Number?

There are two types of content decisions you can appeal to the Oversight Board: a decision about your content or a decision about content by others that you’ve reported.

If you disagree that your content should’ve been taken down and you want to appeal to the Oversight Board, you must first go through the request a review process.

If you reported content from others that wasn’t taken down and you want to appeal to the Oversight Board to have the content removed, you must first go through the request another review process.

Before you can appeal Facebook’s content decision to the Oversight Board, you must first go through the request a review process on your content or on the content you reported.

If we’ve reviewed your content or the content you reported twice and you still disagree with our decision, you may be eligible to appeal that decision to the Oversight Board. Keep in mind that not all content and content decisions will be eligible for appeal but we’re adding more options.

Appeal a decision Facebook made about your content

Appeal a decision Facebook made about content you reported

Once you submit the appeal, the Oversight Board will decide whether or not to review it. The board only selects a certain number of eligible appeals to review, so they may not choose yours.

At any point following the submission of your appeal, you’ll be able to check the appeal status by logging on to the Oversight Board’s website using your reference number. Remember, you have 15 days from when the decision was made to appeal to the Oversight Board. After 15 days, the appeal window will expire.

Read more about the board’s bylaws and structure or learn about the Oversight Board in the Newsroom.

Are firearm sales allowed on Facebook?

The purchase, sale or trade of firearms, ammunition and explosives between private individuals isn’t allowed on Facebook. Please refer to this Help Center article for a list of items covered by this policy.

Firearm shops and online retailers are allowed to engage in commercial activity involving firearms and ammunition on Facebook (example: offering a gun for sale) as long as all applicable laws and regulations are followed.

Keep in mind that posts about firearms in general are allowed on Facebook. This includes discussions about sales in stores or by online retailers, posts advocating for changes to firearm regulation or anything else that follows our Community Standards and Terms.

Please note that updating your name in some places on Facebook may require you to submit one or more documents with your authentic name.

Gender identity and personal pronouns aren’t required on Facebook, but if you add them to your account, note that:

  • When Facebook contacts you, we’ll only refer to you by the name on your Facebook account. This will appear as the name listed in your General Account Settings.
  • Pronouns are not an option made available to advertisers in ads tools.
  • You can, but aren’t required to, add or update your gender identity in your About settings.
  • If you connect your Facebook account to a third-party app or website, the app or website may ask if you want to share your name.

For more information about changing your name and gender on government IDs in a US state, visit the National Center for Transgender Equality.

Verifying your identity

You may be asked to upload documents with your name to start or continue using features like Marketplace or Dating on Facebook. You can upload a government ID or something else from our ID list (example: mail, membership card) that shows your legal or authentic name.

What services can I book?

You can book appointments for services (example: haircuts) on a Facebook business Page. Keep in mind that not all business Pages have set up appointments on Facebook.

Book an appointment on a Facebook Page

  1. Go to the Page by clicking its name in your Feed or searching for it.
  2. Below the Page’s cover photo or in the top right of the Page, click Book Now.
  3. Depending on the Page’s settings, you’ll either be prompted to request an appointment or you’ll be able to select an available time.

When you book an appointment on a Page, you’ll get appointment reminders. If you want to cancel your appointment, open your Messenger conversation with the business, click View Details on the appointment confirmation and then click Cancel Appointment.

Businesses and organizations that send us your activity

What activity do businesses send?

How do businesses get my activity?

What are ad partners?

If you’re in the European Region or the United Kingdom, your ad choices are different. Learn more about your ad choices.

Businesses or organizations may send us your activity about what you do on their apps, websites or in stores. Depending on your choice using the Activity from other businesses setting, we may use this activity to show you relevant content.

Why businesses and organizations send us information about your activity with them

We receive information that businesses and organizations send us about your activity on their websites and apps, as well as some of your offline interactions, such as in-store purchases.

For example, if you interact with a business or organization outside of Facebook, Instagram, and other Meta products, like visiting their website, using their apps, or shopping with them online or in person, they can let us know about that activity.

You can decide if we use this activity to show you relevant content by adjusting your Activity from other businesses setting. If you allow us to use this activity, we may show you an ad or a reel for a shirt based on your visit to a clothing website, or we might provide a more relevant AI response based on this activity.

Here are some examples of businesses and organizations that send us your activity:

  • Retailers, including online shops and local stores you may have visited
  • News and information sites
  • Financial services, like banks or credit card providers
  • Insurance companies
  • Creators of the apps, games or content that you use
  • Other businesses or nonprofits you may have interacted with

Regardless of your choice under this setting, businesses and organizations may send us your activity, and we may anonymize it or use it to improve our products as described in our Privacy Policy.

If you don’t allow us to use this activity to show you relevant content, the content we show you will be based on other types of information we collect, such as your activity on our products (for example, liking a reel or post).

Other information businesses and organizations send us

Activity isn’t the only kind of information businesses and organizations send to us that can be used to show you ads. Businesses and organizations can also share customer or user lists with us.

For example, you may have signed up to receive emails from a business. That business may then send us a list of customers who signed up, which can be used to show you ads. You can review and control how these specific advertisers use your information in your audience-based advertising setting. You must be logged into your account to see and adjust these ad settings.

We also use information you connect to Meta regardless of the choice you make about whether we use activity sent from other businesses to show you relevant content. Examples include information from external accounts and apps you connect to Meta, like for shopping with certain retailers or to use with AI at Meta features. If you connect information to Meta, the content you see may also be based on that information.

Note: We don’t share any information with advertisers that by itself can be used to contact or identify you, such as your name or email address, unless you give us permission. To learn more about the information Meta receives from businesses and organizations and how we use it, visit our Privacy Policy.

Video or audio call someone on Facebook

Note: In audio or video calls between only two people, your IP address will be shared with the other person’s device to establish a peer-to-peer connection. A peer-to-peer connection uses your IP address to connect directly with the person you’re calling to help improve the audio and video quality of your call. While this happens in the background, it may be possible for the other person to discover your IP address.

Business reviews are only available on the Facebook app for iPhone and Android.

When you view an ad on Facebook, you may be asked to review your purchasing experience with that business. Keep in mind, Facebook doesn’t know if you made a purchase or not, so you may see review requests for businesses you didn’t purchase from.

If you’re asked to review your purchasing experience with a business, you’ll see that request in your Feed. Reviewing a business is optional.

If you made a purchase and would like to review:

  1. In your Feed, go to the review request.
  2. Tap the star rating you want to give the business.
  3. If you’d like to leave a written review, tap Tell others what you liked or didn’t like and type in your review.
  4. Once you’re done, tap Finish.

If you didn’t make a purchase:

  1. In your Feed, go to the review request.
  2. Tap Didn’t make a purchase.

If you leave a review, other people on Facebook will be able to see it. Your name and profile picture will be shown next to your review. You can edit or delete your review at any time.

Businesses can’t edit or remove your review, but like other people on Facebook, they can report it if they believe your review goes against our Community Standards. A business may reply to your review. If they reply, you’ll receive a notification.

What is branded content?

Channels, formerly called broadcast channels, are currently available to:

  • Pages with more than 10,000 followers
  • Profiles with pro mode turned on with more than 10,000 followers

Channels is a public messaging tool that allows you to share one-way messages like announcements and exclusive content directly to your followers in a chat format.

Only someone with full or partial control of a Page or someone who has a profile in pro mode can send content in Channels. People who join a channel can read and react to messages in the channel, as well as vote in polls, but they cannot send messages. Channels also allows for posting branded content to your followers. Learn more.

Since channels are designed for public messaging, they can be found and joined by anyone on Facebook or Messenger. Anyone can preview a channel when they receive a link or notification to join. Check if a link you are viewing on Facebook is secure

Basic Mobile Browser Help

Basic Mobile Browser Help

What is a secure link?

What is a suspicious link?

Report a suspicious link

What is Google Safe Browsing?

When you view a link from the Facebook Mobile Browser, Facebook checks links with security systems to inform you if they are secure.

If the link is secure

  • You’ll see the name or URL at the top of the page next to a green lock.
  • You’ll have a secure connection between your device and the website you’re visiting. This means Secure Socket Layer (SSL) technology is encrypting your connection to protect any sensitive information you may enter on the screen, such as your password and credit card numbers.

If the link is not secure

  • You’ll see the name or URL at the top of the page in gray with no symbol.
  • You’ll be able to view the link, but you won’t have a secure connection between your device and the website you’re visiting. This means any sensitive information you enter on the screen, such as your password or credit card numbers, won’t be encrypted.

If the link is suspicious

  • You’ll see the name or URL at the top of the page next to a red triangle.
  • You may also see a red or gray warning screen telling you the website appears suspicious, has a configuration problem or is spreading malicious software and may be unsafe to visit. We recommend not visiting pages with a red warning screen and being cautious when visiting pages with a gray warning screen.
  • If you’re blocked and still want to visit the website, tap View Details then select Proceed Anyways.
  • If you want to return to Facebook or the previous page you were viewing, tap Back to Safety.

If you come across a suspicious or spam link on Facebook, you can report it to us.

We use the Google Safe Browsing database and our own security systems to check for these threats.

Code Verify for Facebook

Use Code Verify

Code Verify orange circle

Code Verify red exclamation

The Code Verify web browser extension can add security to end-to-end encryption when you use Facebook on the web.

Code Verify automatically checks that you’re using an authentic version of Facebook Web to ensure that your messages are between you and your intended recipients. If Code Verify detects that the code you’re using to run Facebook Web doesn’t match the code everyone else is using, the extension notifies you to take action.

Use Code Verify

  1. Download the Code Verify web browser extension from the Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox or Microsoft Edge browser extension stores.
  2. Pin Code Verify to your toolbar.
  3. Use Facebook Web (facebook.com) to automatically run Code Verify. When the code is fully validated, you’ll see a checkmark in a green circle on the toolbar.

In your toolbar, click the green, orange or red Code Verify icon to see its status. Click Learn More for how to resolve certain issues or download the source code to investigate further.

Note:

  • The extension won’t read or access the messages you send or receive, and we won’t know if you’ve downloaded the extension.
  • The extension doesn’t log any data, metadata or user data, and it doesn’t share any information with Facebook. It also doesn’t read or access the messages you send or receive.
  • The extension verifies code for Facebook Web and doesn’t impact Facebook Desktop.
  • Performance might depend on pausing or disabling other browser extensions.

Error messages and how to fix them

If Code Verify can’t validate the code, you’ll see one of these messages:

Network timed out

Possible risk detected

Validation failure

Connect to Facebook without data charges

Conversion rate ranking

  • Mobile Helpadditional tabs menu

shareShare Article

A ranking of your ad’s expected conversion rate. Your ad is ranked against ads with your performance goal that competed for the same audience.

This metric is an ad relevance diagnostic and does not apply to campaigns or ad sets, only ads.

This metric is estimated.

About this metric

This ranking reflects your ad’s relative performance in the ad auction for the date range you’ve selected. Your ad can receive the following rankings, where average represents the 35th to 55th percentile:

  • Above average
  • Average
  • Below average (Bottom 35% of ads)
  • Below average (Bottom 20% of ads)
  • Below average (Bottom 10% of ads)

A conversion rate ranking of Below Average (Bottom 20% of ads) means that your ad had an expected conversion rate among the bottom 20% of ads with the same optimization goal competing for the same audience. At least 80% of ads with the same optimization goal competing for the same audience had a higher expected conversion rate.

How to use this metric

If your ads are not meeting your advertising objectives, use conversion rate ranking with quality ranking and engagement rate ranking to identify how you could improve results. See recommendations on how to improve your ad’s performance for each combination of rankings.

Note that some products and services naturally have lower conversion rates than others competing for the same audience.

How it’s calculated

This metric estimates the probability your optimization goal will be completed after your ad was on screen and ranks this probability against ads with the same optimization goal competing for the same audience in the ad auction. We base our estimates on the previous actions of the audience you’re trying to reach and your ad’s performance in the ad auction.

Conversion rate ranking is not available for ads with fewer than 500 impressions or ads with the following optimization goals: ad recall lift, impressions, reach, custom conversions or value.

Related metrics

  • Quality ranking
  • Engagement rate ranking

Further reading

  • About ad relevance diagnostics
  • How to use ad relevance diagnostics

Cookies on the Meta Products

Control my cookie preferences

How Meta uses cookies

Cookies from other companies

How to delete cookies

Cookies are small blocks of data used to store information on web browsers. They’re used to store and receive identifiers and other information on the devices you use.

Example: Cookies let websites know if you’ve visited that site before, which can help with things like saving an item to your shopping cart or remembering your display settings.

Other technologies, including identifiers associated with your device, and other software, are used for similar purposes. We refer to all of these technologies as cookies.

Ways we use cookies

Cookies help us provide, protect and improve the Meta Products, such as by personalizing content, tailoring and measuring ads, providing a safer experience, and analyzing use of our systems.

Note: The cookies that we use include session cookies, which are deleted when you close your browser, and persistent cookies, which stay on your browser until they expire or you delete them.

What we use cookies for

Authentication

Security, site and product integrity

Advertising, recommendations, insights and measurement

Site features and services

Performance

Analytics and research

Third-party websites and apps

Other ways you can control your information on Facebook

  • Use your ad preferences to learn why you’re seeing a particular ad and control how we use information that we collect to show you ads.
    • Learn more about how to adjust your ad preferences.
  • To show you better ads, we use information that businesses and organizations provide us with about your activity off Meta Company Products, including websites and apps.
    • You can control whether we use this information to show you ads in your ad settings.
    • Learn more about how to adjust how ads on Facebook are shown to you based on your activity from other businesses and organizations.
  • The Meta Audience Network is a way for advertisers to show you ads in apps and websites off the Meta Company Products.
    • One of the ways Meta Audience Network shows relevant ads is by using your ad preferences to determine which ads you may be interested in seeing. You can control this in your ad settings.
    • Learn more about Meta Audience Network in the Meta Business Help Center.
  • You can access the activity information we receive from other businesses and organizations about your interactions with them by visiting our Export your information tool.

Other ways you can control your information

The advertising companies we work with generally use cookies and similar technologies as part of their services.

  • You can opt out of seeing online interest-based ads from Meta and other participating companies, and learn more about how advertisers generally use cookies and the choices they offer through the:
    • Digital Advertising Alliance in the US
    • Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada in Canada
    • European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance in Europe
  • You can also opt out through your mobile device settings (where available) using Android, iOS 13 or an earlier version of iOS. Please note that ad blockers and tools that restrict our cookie use may interfere with these controls.
  • Your browser or device may also offer settings that allow you to choose whether browser cookies are set and to delete them.
    • These controls vary by browser, and manufacturers may change both the settings they make available and how they work at any time.
    • Learn more about how to control your browser cookies on each browser’s help center:
      • Google Chrome
      • Internet Explorer
      • Firefox
      • Safari
      • Safari Mobile
      • Opera

Note: Certain parts of the Meta Products may not work properly if you have disabled browser cookie use. Please be aware these controls are distinct from the controls that we offer you.

For more information on cookies, visit our Cookies Policy.

What operating systems are supported?

It’s important to use the latest version of the Facebook app to help fix problems when something isn’t working.

Note: If you’re unable to use the Facebook app, remember that you can use Facebook on a computer at facebook.com, and you can chat with others by visiting facebook.com/messages.

Download or update the Facebook app

  1. Go to your device’s app store.
  2. Search for and tap the Facebook app, then follow the on-screen instructions.

Troubleshooting tips

You can try the following options if you’re having trouble downloading or updating your Facebook app.

Make sure you have a strong Wi-Fi or mobile data connection

Check your internet connectivity. For best results, connect to Wi-Fi and retry the download.

Check your device storage space

Check your device’s storage space to make sure you have enough space to install the app.

Check for system updates in your device settings

Check for system updates in your device settings to make sure that the Facebook app is operating on the latest version of your device’s operating system.

Check if your device’s operating system is supported

If your operating system is supported, you’ll be able to receive regular updates to the Facebook app and you’ll be able to access new features as they become available. Learn more about what operating systems are supported by the Facebook app.

Delete the app, then reinstall it

Uninstall your Facebook app, restart your device and then re-install the Facebook app from your device’s app center.

Engagement rate ranking

  • Mobile Helpadditional tabs menu

shareShare Article

A ranking of your ad’s expected engagement rate. Engagement includes all clicks, likes, comments and shares. Your ad is ranked against ads that competed for the same audience.

This metric is an ad relevance diagnostic and does not apply to campaigns or ad sets, only ads.

This metric is estimated.

About this metric

This ranking reflects your ad’s relative performance in the ad auction for the date range you’ve selected. Your ad can receive the following rankings, where average represents the 35th to 55th percentile:

  • above average
  • average
  • below average (bottom 35% of ads)
  • below average (bottom 20% of ads)
  • below average (bottom 10% of ads)

An engagement rate ranking of below average (bottom 20% of ads) means that your ad had an expected engagement rate among the bottom 20% of ads competing for the same audience. At least 80% of ads competing for the same audience had a higher expected engagement rate.

How to use this metric

If your ads are not meeting your advertising objectives, use engagement rate ranking with quality ranking and conversion rate ranking to identify how you could improve results. See recommendations on how to improve your ad’s performance for each combination of rankings.

Note that engagement-baiting, such as asking for likes and comments, does not improve your ad’s performance.

How it’s calculated

This metric estimates the probability of engagement with your ad when it’s on screen and ranks this probability against ads competing for the same audience in the ad auction. Engagement includes post reactions, comments, shares, clicks and interactions associated with your ad such as expanding a photo to full screen or Page likes. We base our estimates on the previous actions of the audience you’re trying to reach and your ad’s performance in the ad auction.

Engagement rate ranking is not available for ads with fewer than 500 impressions or ads with the following optimization goals: ad recall lift, impressions, reach, custom conversions or value.

Related metrics

  • Quality ranking
  • Conversion rate ranking

Export my Facebook information
