About AI-generated titles for your posts in a public Facebook group

What is an AI-generated title?

Why does AI generate titles?

My own title disappeared

I don’t want an AI title

We may use AI to generate a title for your post in a public group. We do this because post titles can help others who are searching for content or questions similar to your post.

Generated titles may appear at the top of your post and will be attributed to AI. They may also appear in search engine result pages.

If you don’t see an AI-generated title when you view your post in the group, this does not mean a title has not been generated for your post. The generated title may only appear when someone views your post from search engine results.

AI will generate the title based on the content you include in your post, and any content included in your post may appear in the title.

If you added your own title to your group post, an AI-generated title may still be created for your post. However, the generated title won’t replace your title. Both titles will appear on the post, but the generated title will be attributed to AI.

If you don’t want an AI-generated title to appear on your post, you can delete your post.

We won’t add an AI-generated post title to all public group posts. Currently, we may add an AI-generated title to your post if it is shared in a public group and meets our Community Standards.

Note: Some post titles generated by AI may be inaccurate or inappropriate.

Learn more about AI at Meta.

About group highlights for private Facebook groups

Approve group highlights

What are group highlights?

Remove my approved highlights

I can’t manage highlights

Only certain private groups have group highlights available to them.

Group highlights enable members of certain private Facebook groups to approve some of their posts and comments to be shown publicly to non-group members.

If you’re a member of a private Facebook group with this feature, we may select certain of your post(s) or comment(s) to be included in group highlights, and may use AI at Meta to make such selections. We aim to select content for group highlights that helps give people a sense of what the group is about.

Selected content will only appear in group highlights if you consent to it, and it may appear in a section at the top of the group page for non-members, in Facebook search results, in search engine results, or elsewhere, for the public to see. If you approve your post or comment to be included in group highlights, anyone on or off Facebook can see the content you approved. If you don’t approve your post or comment to be shown publicly, it won’t be included in group highlights and will remain visible to members of the private group only.

Group highlights may include:

  • Text and photos from your post or comment
  • The number of comments on your post
  • The number and types of reactions
  • When the post was made

Group highlights currently don’t include the following information, but this may change in the future:

  • Your name or profile photo
    • Even though group highlights won’t include your name or profile photo, keep in mind that the content of your post or comment may reveal that you’re the author. This means that non-members could learn that you’re a member of the group.
  • The names of people you’ve tagged in your post or comment

As noted in Meta’s Privacy Policy, search engines and other third parties who access your publicly visible content can use it for their own purposes and at their discretion, and their use of this information is subject to their own terms and privacy policies.

No one can comment on or react to group highlights.

Manage your posts and comments selected for group highlights

As a group member, you’ll receive a notification if your post or comment is selected to be shown publicly as part of group highlights. Tap the notification to review the selected content and approve it if you want it to be included in highlights. If you decline or take no action, your content won’t be shown publicly in group highlights. You can also remove your approved posts or comments from group highlights at any time.

Before approving your content for group highlights, check that your content doesn’t include sensitive or identifying information about you or other people.

To manage your selected content or remove your approved content:

  1. Tap Menu in the top left of Facebook.
  2. Tap Groups. If you don’t see Groups, tap See more.
  3. Select the group where your post or comment was selected, then tap You.
  4. Below Group highlights, tap Manage.
    • If none of your posts or comments have been selected for Group highlights, you won’t see this section.
  5. At the top, select whether you want to view pending content or view content you’ve previously approved:
    • Pending: Below a selected post or comment, tap Approve to approve the content to be shown publicly as part of group highlights. You can also tap Decline to decline the content from being shown publicly.
      • If you want to see an example of what’s included in group highlights, tap See example below Add to highlights.
    • Approved: Below a previously approved post or comment, tap Remove highlight to remove the content from group highlights. This means that the content will go back to being visible to members of the group only.

If you’re no longer a member of the group where you approved your content for group highlights, you can remove your approved content by deleting your post or comment through your Activity Log. Learn how to delete content using your Activity Log.

If you’re an admin of a private group with this feature, learn how to manage group highlights.

About limited membership in a Facebook group

Turn on limited membership

Approve participation requests

Set up participation questions

This feature may not be available to you right now. Only certain large private visible groups can turn on limited membership. This feature is not available to private hidden groups.

If you’re an admin of a private group, you can turn on limited membership to allow people to automatically join your group without admin approval as limited members. Limited members can see all group content and members, react to group content, and invite others to join the group, but they won’t be able to post, comment, or chat until they’ve been approved to participate by an admin. They will be listed as “limited members” in your group.

People don’t need to complete a membership questionnaire to join as limited members, but a limited member may need to complete participation questions (if set up by an admin) when requesting to participate in the group. When you turn on limited membership, any membership questions you previously set up for your private group will become participation questions to help you decide whether or not to approve a limited member to participate in the group.

You can turn off limited membership at any time.

Turn on or off limited membership

  1. Open the Facebook app on your mobile device.
  2. Find the private group you want to turn on or off limited membership for.
  3. Tap Manage.
  4. Below Settings, tap Group settings.
  5. Below Membership, tap Limited membership.
  6. Next to On or Off, tap to turn limited membership on or off.
    • If you turn off limited membership, the joining experience for members returns to the default joining experience for private groups. Learn more about how private groups work.
    • If you turn off limited membership, existing limited members will become people with pending membership requests. These requests need to be approved before they can become a member of the group, see group content, and participate in the group.

If a limited member wants to post, comment, or chat in the group, they must submit a request to participate. A request to participate will be submitted to admins for review and approval or decline either when a limited member joins the group or when they create a post or comment in the group. The limited member’s posts and comments will only be published in the group if an admin approves their request to participate. Admins can set up participation questions for limited members to answer when requesting to participate in the group.

Limited members will be notified when their request to participate has been approved.

Limited members who are approved by an admin to participate become members who can then post, comment, and chat in the group. Limited members who haven’t been approved by an admin to participate in the group remain limited members who are unable to post, comment, or chat and any posts or comments they have created will not be published in the group.

Approve or decline participation requests from limited members

Instead of a membership request queue, a private group with limited membership turned on has a participation request queue. Participation requests may include pending posts and comments created by a limited member, and if an admin approves the limited member’s participation request, this approves the pending posts and comments for publishing in the group.

To review participation requests from limited members:

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Participation requests below Admin tools in the left menu.
  3. If you’d like, you can filter requests at the top of the page by clicking Questions, Request Age, Rules, Location, Profile Type, Gender or Friends.
  4. You can then:
    • Approve or Decline each request.
    • Approve all or Decline all.

Set up participation questions

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Participation questions in the left menu.
  3. Click Create questions to add your first question, or Create to add a new question.
  4. Click Toggle next to Group rules to ask first-time participants to agree.

How certain Admin Assist rules and group settings will apply when limited membership is turned on

  • Rules/Setting: Admin Assist rules; How Rules/Setting will apply: Any Admin Assist rules you’ve set up to automatically approve or decline membership requests will apply to approve or decline participation requests instead when you turn on limited membership. - If someone’s request to join as a member would be declined by an existing rule, their participation request will be declined. - If someone’s request to join as a member would be approved by an existing rule, such as the rule related to the age of the person’s Facebook account, their participation request will be approved.
  • Rules/Setting: Pre-approved members (Who is preapproved to join setting); How Rules/Setting will apply: If someone who is listed as a preapproved member joins a private group with limited membership turned on, their request to participate will be automatically approved.
  • Rules/Setting: Who can approve members setting; How Rules/Setting will apply: If your private group’s setting for Who Can Approve Member Requests has been set to allow Anyone in the group to approve member requests from friends, this will apply to participation requests when limited membership is turned on so that members can approve participation requests from their friends. Learn more about managing membership for your Facebook group.

Automatically manage participation requests when limited membership is turned on

You can use Admin Assist to automatically manage participation requests from limited members based on criteria that make sense for your group.

To automatically approve participation requests based on certain criteria:

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist below Admin Tools in the left menu.
  3. Below Manage requests, click Add next to Approve participant if.
  4. Choose Select Account Age, Participation questions, Friends in group, or Location..
  5. Click Update.

Note: Admin Assist will only automatically approve a participation request if all criteria are met.

What to know about limited membership

  • Limited membership isn’t available for private groups that are hidden.
  • Limited members are included in the member count for a private group.
  • Limited members are listed as such in the membership list for the group.
  • If someone has a pending request to join your private group when you turn on limited membership, they will automatically become a limited member of your group and their request will turn into a request to participate.
  • If you don’t want a particular limited member in your group, you can remove or ban the member from your group.
  • Before turning on limited membership, consider if this setting is a good fit for your private group. If you manage a sensitive group where you want to review and approve people before they can join and view group content and members, turning on limited membership may not be the right choice for your community.

About Meta AI comment summaries on your posts in a public Facebook group

What are comment summaries?

Where do summaries appear?

Can I turn off summaries?

Meta AI may generate a summary of the comments on your posts in public Facebook groups. Comment summaries help people catch up on the conversation.

Comment summaries may appear at the bottom of your post and will be attributed to Meta AI. They may also appear in search engine results.

A comment summary may only appear when someone opens your post from a search engine results page.

Meta AI generates the summary from your post and some of the comments on the post. Any content included in your post or the comments may appear in the summary.

Summaries are based on a selection of top comments, so they may not reflect every comment.

You can’t turn off Meta AI comment summaries for posts in Facebook groups.

If you delete your post, a summary won’t be available for that post.

If someone deletes a comment used in the summary, Meta AI may generate a new summary.

Note: Some Meta AI comment summaries may be inaccurate or inappropriate.

Learn more about AI at Meta.

Appeal Facebook’s decision to disable your group or remove content, and more about Group Quality

Appeal content removal

Appeal group disabled

Check my group status

What are Community Standards?

Group Quality shows you actions Facebook has taken to enforce our Community Standards in a group you admin. Based on activity in a group, Facebook may do any of the following:

  • Take down violating content.
  • Show a group’s content lower in Feed if a group repeatedly violates Community Standards. Facebook may also stop recommending that people join the group.
  • Turn on temporary post approval for individual members or for the entire group.
  • Disable the group if there are multiple admin and moderator violations, which includes:
    • If an admin or moderator creates content (example: posts, comments) that violates our Community Standards.
    • If an admin or moderator approves violating content from a group member.

Check your group status

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Group Status in the left menu.
  3. From here you can see content that was removed from your group for violating our Community Standards and/or false information in the group.

Appeal Facebook’s decision to take down content in your group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Group Status in the left menu.
  3. Click See Details next to the content.
  4. Select Request Review, then click Continue.

Admins can appeal both member violations (when members post violating content) and admin violations (when admins post or approve violating content). You can appeal your own admin violations and violations by another admin.

Once you ask us to take another look, the content will be reviewed again by Facebook. If we find we’ve made a mistake, we’ll let you and the content author know. Content must be appealed within 30 days.

If you don’t see the option to appeal, it could be because either another admin of your group has already requested to appeal the decision, or because certain violations of our Community Standards can’t be appealed. After you’ve appealed a violation, you can check the status of your appeal by selecting See Details next to the violation you’re appealing.

Learn how to review content before Facebook counts it as a violation of our Community Standards.

Appeal Facebook’s decision to disable your group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click See Details next to the message about your group being disabled, then follow the prompts.
  3. Select Request Review, then click Continue.

Once you ask us to take another look, your group will be reviewed again by Facebook. If we find we’ve made a mistake, we’ll let you know, and your group will be restored. Admins have 30 days to appeal Facebook’s decision to disable a group.

If you don’t see the option to appeal, it could be because either another admin of your group has already requested to appeal the decision, or because certain violations of our Community Standards can’t be appealed. After you’ve appealed a violation, you can check the status of your appeal by selecting See Details next to the violation you’re appealing.

Note:

  • Only admins can access Group Quality.
  • All items for sale also need to follow our Commerce Policies.

Community Standards Notification

When you go to a group that has Community Standards violations, you may see the notification “This Group may share content that violates our Community Standards.” We show this message so you know that you may see posts in the group that aren’t allowed on Facebook but that haven’t been marked as removed for Community Standards violations yet.

You may also see the notification “This Group has allowed posts that violate our Community Standards.”

If you see the notification, you can choose:

  • Review Group: Go to the group and review the content to make sure that you’re ok with the content that is shared in the group before you decide to join.
  • Join Group: Join the group without reviewing it.

You can also read our Community Standards to get a better idea of what kind of things are allowed on Facebook.

Change a Facebook group from private to public

Change group to public

Cancel public group change

Content visibility in public group

Private groups can now be changed to public.

A Facebook group can be either:

  • Public: Anyone on or off Facebook can see who’s in the group and what they post.
  • Private: Only members can see who’s in the group and what they post.
    • Note: Members can approve some of their private group posts and comments to be shown publicly to anyone on or off Facebook if group highlights are available in the group.

Learn more about differences between public and private groups.

What to know about changing a group’s privacy setting from private to public

  • Only a group admin can change the privacy setting of a group.
  • If an admin schedules a group to go from private to public, all admins have 3 days to cancel the change if they’d like to.
  • When an admin schedules the change from private to public:
    • All admins will get a notification when the privacy change is scheduled.
    • Everyone in the group will get a notification when the privacy change happens.
    • If the change is canceled, the group will stay private and admins will be notified that the change was canceled.
  • All new content, including posts and comments and reactions on those posts, in the now-public group will be visible to anyone on or off Facebook.
  • Content from when the group was private, such as posts, comments and reactions on those posts will only be visible to people who were members when the group became public, as well as admins and moderators. This includes new comments and reactions on content from when the group was private.
    • If an admin changes the group back to private, approved members will be able to see this content too, as discussed in the next section.
    • Keep in mind that if someone becomes a new admin or moderator of the now-public group, they’ll also be able to see content from when the group was private.
  • Only admins and moderators will be able to see the member list in the now-public group.
    • Keep in mind that anyone will be able to see if you post, comment, and react to or engage with group content, which means that others may infer that you were a member of the private group.
  • If a private group is set to hidden, making the group public will also make it visible, or discoverable to anyone in search and other places on and off Facebook.
  • When the group is changed to public, participation approval will be turned on for the group. Learn more about participation approval in public groups.
  • Anyone who had a pending membership request to the private group will automatically be added as a member of the now-public group, and their pending membership request will be converted to a pending participant request.

What to know about changing a group’s privacy setting from public back to private

  • If a group previously changed from private to public, the group can change back to private at any time regardless of its size or age. Learn how to change a Facebook group from public to private.
    • If an admin changes the group’s privacy setting back to private, all people who joined the group or were approved to participate when it was public will require membership approval to join the group now that it is private. Learn how to manage membership for your Facebook group.
  • If the group is changed back to private, admins will once again be able to control who joins the group and sees the group content and membership by approving or declining membership requests.
    • People who joined the group or were approved to participate while it was public will be removed from the group and membership requests will automatically be submitted for them for admin review.
    • When someone is removed from the group, they won’t be able to see the content and membership of the now-private group until they’re approved to join.
    • If approved to join the now-private group, those members will be able to see all group content, including the content from when the group was previously private.
    • The member list will also be visible to group members.

Change the privacy setting of a private group you admin

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Group settings in the left menu. If you don’t see Group settings, click Manage.
  3. Below Set up group, click next to Privacy.
  4. Select Public, then click Next.
  5. Click Change to public.

Once you select Change to public, you and the other group admins will have 3 days to cancel if you’d like. To cancel changing your group to public:

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Group settings in the left menu. If you don’t see Group settings, click Manage.
  3. Below Set up group, click next to Privacy.
  4. Click Cancel change.

Difference between public and private

Public groups can be changed to private if they are less than 30 days old or have fewer than 10,000 members. If your group was created 30 days ago or more and has 10,000 or more members and you want to switch from public to private, you can request an exception.

If you change a group to private, it can now be changed back to public.

A Facebook group can be either:

  • Public: Anyone on or off Facebook can see who’s in the group and what they post.
  • Private: Only members can see who’s in the group and what they post.- Note: Members can approve some of their private group posts and comments to be shown publicly on or off Facebook if group highlights are available in the group.

Learn about more differences between public and private groups.

What to know about changing a group’s privacy setting from public to private

  • Public groups can become private unless they have 10,000 or more members and were created at least 30 days ago.
  • If a group previously changed from private to public, the group can change back to private at any time regardless of its size or age.
  • Only a group admin can change the privacy setting of a group.
  • If an admin schedules a group to go from public to private, all admins have 3 days to cancel the change if they’d like to.
  • When an admin schedules the change from public to private:
    • All admins will get a notification when the privacy change is scheduled.
    • Everyone in the group will get a notification when the privacy change happens.
    • If the change is canceled, the group will stay public and admins will be notified that the change was canceled.
  • If you change a group to private, it can now be changed back to public.

Change the privacy setting of an eligible public group you admin

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Group settings in the left menu. You might have to click Manage first.
  3. Below Set up group, click Edit next to Privacy.
  4. Select Private.
  5. Follow the prompts.
  6. Click Change privacy to confirm.

Once you select Change privacy, you and the other admins will have 3 days to cancel if you’d like. When the group changes from public to private, it can be changed back to public by the admin.

Note: You can only change a public group’s privacy to private if the group was created fewer than 30 days ago or has fewer than 10,000 members.

If your group was created 30 days ago or more and has 10,000 or more members and you want to switch from public to private, you can request an exception.

What is a public group?

Delete a Facebook group you admin

What happens if I delete?

What happens to group members?

I can’t delete my group

You can delete a Facebook group only when it has no members.

Note: Deleting a group is permanent and can’t be reversed, so consider pausing the group instead.

Learn about the differences between pausing and deleting a group.

If you’re a group admin, you can delete your Facebook group by:

  • Private groups: Removing all members and then leaving the group, as long as the group creator has left the group or you are the group creator.
  • Public groups: Banning all members and then leaving the group, as long as the group creator has left the group or you are the group creator.

When no members remain in the group, it will automatically be paused.

Delete a group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Members (for private groups) or People (for public groups) at the top of the group. You might need to select More first.
  3. Click Options next to each member’s name and select Remove member (for private groups) or Ban from group (for public groups).
  4. Click Next, then click Confirm to proceed.
  5. Once you’ve removed the other members, and when you’re the last group member, then click Options next to your name and select Leave group. Click Delete group to confirm.

Keep in mind

  • Group members aren’t notified when you delete a group.
  • If the only admin of a Facebook group leaves the group, deactivates their account, or deletes their account, they’ll be prompted to invite a new admin(s). The group will automatically be paused if they don’t select a new admin or if no one accepts the admin invitation within 7 days.

Delete your posts and comments in a Facebook group

Delete my individual posts

Delete all my content

I can’t delete posts

If you’d like to delete posts and comments from a Facebook group, you can choose to delete:

  • Your individual posts from the group.
  • All the posts, comments, photos and other content you’ve shared in the group, all at once.

If you’ve been blocked from the group or were in a hidden group, you can delete all your posts, comments, photos and other content all at once, but you won’t be able to delete individual posts.

Delete individual posts, comments or reactions in the group

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook, then click your name to go to your profile.
  2. On your profile, click Options below your name and select Activity Log.
  3. In the left menu, click Your Facebook activity, then click Groups.
  4. Select Group posts and comments or Your reactions to posts in groups in the left menu.
  5. Scroll to what you want to delete, then click Options and select Delete, Unlike or Remove Reaction.

Delete all your posts, comments, photos and other content you’ve shared in the group

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook, then click your name to go to your profile.
  2. On your profile, click Options below your name and select Activity Log.
  3. In the left menu, click Your Facebook activity, then click Groups.
  4. Click Your Group membership activity .
  5. Scroll to the group you want to delete your content from, then click Options and select Delete your activity.
  6. Click Delete to confirm.

This doesn’t include activity like your invites and activity in group events and get-togethers, reactions, the names of albums you’ve created or documents you’ve created that other people have edited.

Note: Pages that have joined groups can’t delete posts and other activity from a Facebook group they’re no longer a member of.

Difference between a member, participant and visitor in a public Facebook group

What is a group member?

What is a group visitor?

What is a group participant?

In public groups, you can interact with a group as a member or as a visitor. Once a member or visitor posts or comments in the group, they become a participant.

Member: someone who has joined the group

  • No admin approval required
  • Can post and comment
    • Possible exception: if admins turn on participant approval, then members will need to be approved as participants before they can post or comment for the first time. Once someone is approved as a participant, their future posts might still require admin approval.
  • Sees group content in their Feed and other places on Facebook, and can be made an admin or moderator

Visitor: someone who isn’t a member of the group

  • No admin approval required
  • Can post and comment
    • Possible exception: if admins turn on participant approval, then visitors will need to be approved as participants before they can post or comment for the first time. Once someone is approved as a participant, their future posts might still require admin approval.

Participant: a member or visitor who has posted or commented in the group

  • Admin approval required if admin has turned on participant approval
  • Can post and comment
    • Note: once someone is approved as a participant, their future posts might still require admin approval if the admin has set up post approval.

Learn how to manage posts if you’re an admin of a public group.

Difference between pausing and deleting a Facebook group you admin

Basic Mobile Browser Help

Basic Mobile Browser Help

Pause my group

Delete my group

Difference between pausing and deleting

Who can delete a group?

If you’re an admin of a group, you can pause your group if you need a break from maintaining it. If you want to permanently remove your group from Facebook, you can delete it.

The table below outlines the differences between pausing and deleting a Facebook group:

  • Will the group appear in search?; If a group is paused…: Yes; If a group is deleted…: No
  • Is this action reversible?; If a group is paused…: Yes; If a group is deleted…: No
  • Can any group admin perform this action?; If a group is paused…: Yes; If a group is deleted…: No. Only the group’s creator (who is also an admin) can delete the group. If the creator admin is no longer a group member, any admin of the group can delete it.
  • Can new members join the group?; If a group is paused…: No, but admins can approve members who requested to join before the pause.; If a group is deleted…: No
  • Can admins or group members post, comment or add photos and videos?; If a group is paused…: No, but admins can manage posts written before the pause.; If a group is deleted…: No
  • Can admins remove posts, comments, photos and videos?; If a group is paused…: Yes; If a group is deleted…: No
  • Can admins remove and ban people from the group?; If a group is paused…: Yes; If a group is deleted…: No
  • Can admins edit group details including description or photo?; If a group is paused…: No, except they can change the group cover photo.; If a group is deleted…: No
  • Can group members or admins access their information?; If a group is paused…: Yes; If a group is deleted…: No

Differences between public and private Facebook groups

Change group to public

Change group to private

Who can see my group?

I can’t change group privacy

Private groups can now be changed to public.

[Embedded video omitted]

Summary

  • Who can see what people post, comment and share in the group?; Public: Anyone on or off Facebook; Private: Current members Note: Members can approve some of their private group posts and comments to be shown publicly on or off Facebook if group highlights are available in the group.
  • Who can see who’s in the group?; Public: Anyone on Facebook; Private: Current members
  • Who can see who the admins and moderators are?; Public: Anyone on Facebook; Private: Visible: Anyone on Facebook Hidden: Members and invited individuals
  • Can admins change the privacy setting after creating the group?; Public: Yes, public groups can change to private, unless the group has 10,000 or more members and was created 30 days or more ago. If the group previously changed from private to public, the group can change back to private at any time regardless of its size or age.; Private: Yes, private groups can change to public, but content from when the group was private will only be visible to people who were members when the group became public, admins, and moderators.
  • Can you become a member without admin approval?; Public: Yes; Private: With admin approval
  • Can you post without admin approval?; Public: With admin approval; Private: With admin approval
  • Can you post, comment and participate in the group without being a member?; Public: Yes, although admins can choose whether approval of posts and participants is required; Private: No
  • Can you share content from the group?; Public: Yes; Private: No Note: Members can approve some of their private group posts and comments to be shown publicly on or off Facebook if group highlights are available in the group.

Who can join and participate in the group

Public groups

  • Anyone on Facebook can join automatically (there’s no approval process).

  • Both members and non-members can post and participate, although admins can choose whether approval of posts and participants is required. Private groups

  • Requests to join require approval, unless the group has limited membership turned on.

  • Only members can post and participate, although admins can choose whether approval of posts is required.

    • In groups with limited membership turned on, limited members can react to group content but won’t be able to post, comment, or chat until they’ve been approved to participate by an admin.

Who can see and find the group

Public groups

  • Anyone on or off Facebook can see what’s shared in the group.

  • Anyone on Facebook can see who’s in the group.

  • Anyone on or off Facebook can find the group. Private groups

  • Only current members can see what’s shared in the group and who the members are.- Note: Members can approve some of their private group posts and comments to be shown publicly on or off Facebook if group highlights are available in the group.

  • Admins can choose whether it’s visible (anyone on Facebook can find it and request to join (or automatically join if limited membership is turned on)) or hidden (can only find it if invited or a member).

Examples of each group type

Public groups: Someone might choose to create a public group for something like fans of a television show, or travel tips for their city.

Private groups: Someone might choose to create a private group to discuss something more sensitive, like a health concern, or for a group of people who know each other, like a neighborhood.

View and manage group privacy settings

  • Check if a group is public or private.
  • Check if a private group is hidden or visible in search and other places on Facebook.
  • Change your group from public to private if you’re an admin of an eligible public group (a group that is less than 30 days old or has fewer than 10,000 members or previously converted from private).
  • Change your group from private to public.
  • Hide or unhide your group from search and other places on Facebook if you’re an admin of a private group.

Important considerations

  • Invited members are members of a group who can see the group in preview mode.
  • When a Page joins a group there could be several admins of that Page. All of them can see and interact with posts and members of the group.
  • In some private groups, admins can turn on limited membership, where people can automatically join without admin approval as limited members who can see all group content and react, but can’t post, comment, or chat until they are approved by an admin to participate.
    • A request to participate will be submitted to admins for review and approval or decline either when a limited member joins the group or when they create a post or comment in the group. Once a limited member has been approved by an admin to participate, they can then post, comment, and chat in the group.
  • Select rights owners may be able to search sale group posts, including sale posts listed in private groups, to prevent the misuse of intellectual property on Facebook.
  • We may review group content, including content in private groups, to maintain the integrity of our products, promote safety and security on and off our products, and improve our products and services as otherwise described in the Privacy Policy.

Earn a contributor badge in a Facebook group

Earn a contributor badge

How to get a contributor badge

My contributor badge disappeared

Turn off contributor badge

Earn a contributor badge – rising contributor, top contributor or all-star contributor – in a Facebook group by being one of the most active participants in the group. Participate and receive replies and reactions to earn points. Members, admins, and moderators can earn badges.

Your contributor badge appears by your name on posts, comments, and your group member profile.

How to earn a contributor badge

You can earn points and increase your chances of earning a contributor badge in a group by:

  • Receiving replies and/or reactions on your posts
  • Receiving replies and/or reactions on your comments
  • Being an admin or moderator (If you want to become an admin or moderator, you can send a message to a current admin and ask them to invite you to become an admin or moderator.)
  • Being a group expert (If you want to become a group expert, you can send a message to a current admin and ask them to invite you to become a group expert.)

Troubleshooting

  • If you had a contributor badge but no longer see it, the group admins might have turned off the Contributions feature.
  • If you know you’re a rising, top or all-star contributor but haven’t earned the badge, it might be because:
    • The group admins turned off the Contributions feature.
    • It’s a public group and you aren’t a member or admin/moderator of the group.

More information

  • If you earn a contributor badge but don’t want to display it, learn how to manage which badges appear by your name.
  • If you’re a group admin, you can turn contributor badges on or off by turning the Contributions feature on or off.
  • Learn more about group badges.

Note

  • Similar to other chats, interactions with AI are subject to our Community Standards and Terms of Service.

  • An AI’s response may be inaccurate or inappropriate and should not be used to make important decisions.

  • Meta AI uses your location information to give you more relevant responses. Your location information is based on things like the settings you’ve chosen on your device, or your activity across our products. Learn more about how to manage your location in the Privacy Center.

  • Other information from your profile such as your age and gender, and interests based on your activity across our products, such as the types of content, including ads, you view or interact with and how you interact with it, will be used to help personalize your interactions with AI. Learn more about how Meta uses this information in the Privacy Center. You can also see how information is used across your accounts in the same Accounts Center and export your information. Learn how to Export a copy of your information.

  • Depending on your prompt, the content generated may go against our Community Standards or Terms of Service of Meta’s platforms. Sharing AI-generated content on our platforms that go against these standards will be treated the same as sharing other content that go against our standards. If you share generated content that goes against our standards, your content may be removed and your account may be restricted or disabled. Learn more about the Community Standards and Terms of Service on:

    • Facebook, Messenger and Instagram
    • WhatsApp

  • Depending on your region, your interactions with AI products can be used to personalize content and ads.

  • Edits to a group’s AI (for example, editing the name, description or tagline) are reviewed by Meta to ensure they comply with the Meta AI Studio Policy.

  • AI responses may be generated from group content, like posts and comments, and include links to posts, consistent with Meta’s Privacy Policy.

  • Meta’s AI Terms apply to the feature and its use.

How additional profiles work in Facebook groups

Limits on additional profiles

Approve additional profiles

What happens if a profile is banned?

You are no longer able to create additional Facebook profiles. Existing additional profiles have not been affected.

Each additional profile has its own @username, Feed, friends list, Pages it follows, and groups it participates in. You can switch between profiles without logging in and out of Facebook.

Limits on additional profiles in groups

  • Up to two profiles from the same account can join/participate in the same group. For example, someone with two additional profiles has three profiles total (their main profile and two additional profiles), but only two of their profiles can join/participate in the same group.
  • Only one profile can interact with a single group post. For example, if you post in a group, you can’t comment or reply on that post with a different profile.

Membership/participation approvals for additional profiles

  • In groups where approvals are required (private groups and any public group that requires participant approval), each profile has to be approved. For example, if a member of a private group has an additional profile in order to post in the group with a different name, that additional profile will have to request to join/participate.
  • Additional profiles are considered to have joined Facebook at the same time as the account. For example, if someone joined Facebook five years ago then later created an additional profile and requests to join a group, Admin Assist will consider the profile to have joined Facebook five years ago.
  • To see if someone is using an additional profile, go to their profile and look for an @username.

Effects of suspending, banning and removing a profile

  • Admin/moderator action on a member’s profile: Suspend; Effect on that profile: Cannot participate in the group until the suspension ends; Effect on any of their profiles NOT in the group (main profile or additional profile): Cannot see, join or participate in the group until the suspension ends; Effect on any of their other profiles already in the group (main profile or additional profile): No effect. Can still see and participate in the group.
  • Admin/moderator action on a member’s profile: Ban; Effect on that profile: Cannot find the group in search, see any of its content, or be invited to the group again; Effect on any of their profiles NOT in the group (main profile or additional profile): Cannot find the group in search, see any of its content, or join/participate; Effect on any of their other profiles already in the group (main profile or additional profile): No effect. Can still find the group in search, see its content, and participate in the group. Note that up to two profiles from the same account can join/participate in the same group.
  • Admin/moderator action on a member’s profile: Remove; Effect on that profile: Can find the group in search, re-join and then participate; Effect on any of their profiles NOT in the group (main profile or additional profile): No effect. Can find the group in search, join and participate. Note that up to two profiles from the same account can join/participate in the same group.; Effect on any of their other profiles already in the group (main profile or additional profile): No effect

Admins can also prevent someone they banned from joining again under a different account.

Misuse of additional profiles

Keeping Facebook safe is a top priority. We have policies for additional profiles, and our Community Standards apply to all profiles. If someone goes against our standards from any of their profiles, it will affect their Facebook account. If someone repeatedly or egregiously violates our policies while using their additional profiles, one or more of their profiles (including their main profile) may be disabled.

If you’re concerned about additional profiles in a group you manage, consider:

  • Allowing anonymous posts in your group. People concerned about privacy might choose to post anonymously instead of creating an additional profile
  • Options for managing membership (for private groups)
  • Options for managing posts/participation
  • Setting up Admin Assist to make approvals easier
  • Tools that can catch spam in your group

More information

  • Switch between your profiles
  • Delete, deactivate or reactivate an additional Facebook profile
  • About additional Facebook profiles (Can people see my other profiles?)
  • The difference between your Facebook account and profile

  1. Type “@” and then the Page’s or group’s name.
  2. Select a name from the list that appears.

Keep in mind that depending on a Page’s settings, you may not be able to mention it.

When you mention a person, Page or group in a post or comment, a link is created. The audience for the link that’s created depends on the privacy settings of the person, Page or group you mention. For example, if you mention a secret group, only that group’s members can see the link. The person, Page or group you mention may get a notification, and the post or comment may appear on their timeline.

How Facebook suggests groups to join

How does Facebook suggest groups?

What info does Facebook use?

See fewer group suggestions

I can’t find suggested groups

What are suggested groups on Facebook?

Facebook makes personalized recommendations to help people discover groups and build community. Facebook may recommend groups that are similar to the groups you’re currently a member of, that your friends have joined, that are popular in your area or related to a topic you’ve demonstrated interest in on Facebook. Facebook doesn’t suggest private hidden groups.

You can learn more about the group by selecting the suggestion to preview the group, or you can join the group by selecting Join. If you think a suggestion is unhelpful, you can remove it and see fewer suggestions like it (see below).

How does Facebook suggest groups for me to join?

Facebook uses artificial intelligence (AI) technology to make personalized recommendations about the types of groups someone might be interested in joining or participating in. The technology suggests groups based on the information someone has shared on Facebook and what groups people who share things in common with them have joined and participated in. For example, if someone sets their current city to New York City, the AI technology may suggest a group about sightseeing in New York City.

Where might I see suggested groups on Facebook?

You might see suggested groups in your Feed, in your notifications, when you visit a group that you’re a member of, when selecting Groups from the left menu of your Feed, or when watching a video or viewing an event on Facebook.

What information does Facebook use for suggested groups?

Facebook takes into account a variety of factors when suggesting groups, including:

  1. Geographic information, like the current city listed in the About section of your Facebook profile, to suggest groups with members nearby
  2. Demographic information, like language and age, to suggest groups with similar members
  3. Groups someone you’re friends with has already joined or participated in and Pages they’ve followed
  4. Your activity in a group or Page, like if you’ve posted or interacted with posts about cars
  5. Your recent activity on other Facebook features like Marketplace, Search, Video and Events, like items you’ve sold, videos you’ve watched and events you’ve attended
  6. Trending or popular topics in groups
  7. Information you’ve added to your profile, like your interests

How can I influence what groups Facebook suggests to me?

We regularly update our AI technology to improve suggestions. However, sometimes we might get it wrong and show groups you aren’t interested in joining. Here are some things you can do to see more relevant suggestions:

  • Leave groups you no longer find relevant
  • Update your current city if it’s out of date
  • Remove friends you’re not interested in keeping up with
  • Hide a suggested group you’re not interested in by clicking Exit in the top right of the suggestion.

Invite group members to a Facebook event

Invite group members

I can’t invite members

Invite to a group event

Members of a group can create group events and invite other group members to join. When a group event is created, it appears in the group’s discussion and members can choose to join.

If someone removes themselves from a group event, they can’t be added again.

Invite group members to a Facebook event

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Events below the cover photo.
  3. Go to the event you want to invite people to, then click Invite below event’s name.
  4. Select the group members you want to invite and click Send invites.

Learn more about the number of people you can invite to an event.

Invite someone to join a Facebook group

Invite friends to group

Invite with email

Invite with link

There are a few ways new members can be invited to join a Facebook group:

  • Invite from the group: Admins and members can invite their Facebook friends to join a group by selecting Invite from the group.
  • Invite with email: Admins can use email to invite anyone to join their group, whether or not they’re Facebook friends.
  • Invite with link (only available for private hidden groups): If the group is a private hidden group, admins and members can use a link to invite anyone to join their group, whether or not they’re Facebook friends, if the admins allow.

Once someone is invited to join a group, they’ll be able to preview the group before deciding if they’d like to join the group, unless they were invited to the group by email or invited to a private hidden group with a link. If someone is previewing the group, they won’t be included in the total member count.

Note: If you invite people to a group, a group admin may need to approve the request before they can join. Pages can’t be invited to join groups as group members.

Admins and members can only invite a limited number of people to join each day.

Invite from the group

Admins and members can invite their Facebook friends to join a group.

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click + Invite below the cover photo.
  3. Select Invite Facebook friends.
  4. Select the names of the friends you want to invite. You can also type a friend’s name in the search bar.
  5. Click Send invites.

Invite with email

Admins can invite new members to a group by email.

The email will include a link to the Facebook group, where the person can confirm that they want to join. In public groups and private visible groups, they’ll be automatically approved. In private hidden groups, they’ll have to be approved by a group admin. Only the person who received the email can join the group with that link. The link will expire after 28 days.

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click + Invite below the cover photo.
  3. Select Invite with email.
  4. Add email addresses.
  5. Click Send invite.

Invite with link (only available for private hidden groups)

Admins and members can use a link to invite others to a private hidden group if the admins allow. The link can be shared on or off Facebook.

Once someone receives the invite to join the group, they’ll then have to request to join and be approved by a group admin. Any Facebook user with the link can see the group’s About info and request to join.

The link will expire after either 48 hours or 20 people click on it, whichever comes first. After the link expires, you can create a new link.

Keep in mind that people who receive the link from you might understand you’re a member of this group.

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click + Invite below the cover photo.
  3. Select Invite with link.
  4. Click the link to copy it, then share it. If you want to share the link through Facebook, click Done, +Invite, then Invite with link, and select a method for sharing it on Facebook.

Invite your Page followers to join your Facebook group

Invite Page followers to group

Automatic invites to group

Invite more than 1,000 people

I can’t invite followers

You can invite followers of your Page to join a group that the Page is an admin of.

Invite Page followers to your group

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  4. Click Invite, then click Invite Facebook followers.
  5. Type the names of the Page followers you want to invite to your group, click their names, and click Send Invites. You can manually invite up to 1,000 contacts per week.
  6. To enable group invites to automatically be sent to recently engaged Page followers, click Toggle next to Automatic Invites then click Confirm.

You can only enable automatic invites for one group at a time. Once you confirm which group you want to enable automatic invites for, you can’t change your decision for 7 days. People will receive an automatic invite if they:

  • Follow the Page
  • And recently engaged with the Page
  • And haven’t been previously invited to join the group

Note: If you’ve invited a person before, you won’t be able to invite them again.

Join a Facebook group

Join a Facebook group

Join group as Page

Can’t join a private group

I reached group limit

If you can’t join a group as your Facebook Page, it might be because the group admins don’t allow Pages to join their groups.

Join a group

  1. Click Groups in the left menu of your Feed.
  2. In the search bar at the top, enter the group name.
  3. Select the group and then click + Join Group below the cover photo.

You can join up to 6,000 groups. Once you reach this limit, you’ll need to leave some groups before you can join new ones.

To join a private group, you need to be approved by an admin, unless the group has limited membership turned on. Limited membership allows you to automatically join a private group without admin approval and to see and react to all group content, but you won’t be able to post, comment, or chat until you are approved by an admin to participate.

Learn more about the differences between public and private Facebook groups.

What happens next

You may have to wait for a group admin to approve your request, depending on the group settings. Hidden groups you’re not a member of won’t appear in search results. When you join a group, group members will see that you’re a member. Non-members may also see that you’re a member, depending on the group’s privacy level.

What to know about Pages joining groups

  • Multiple people may manage that Page. Page managers can see and interact with group posts and members, depending on the settings.
  • Group admins might not allow Pages to join their groups.
  • Groups can’t invite Pages to join. Pages can only request to join groups.
  • To join a group as a Page after joining as a profile, change your interaction settings.

Leave a Facebook group

Leave a group

What happens when I leave?

I can’t leave a group

Leave a group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Joined in the top right, then select Leave group.
  3. Click Leave Group to confirm.

When you leave a group:

  • Members won’t be notified if you leave.
  • You’re removed from the member list and the group will be removed from your list of groups.
  • You’ll no longer get group notifications or see group posts in Feed.
  • People will no longer know when you’ve seen a group post, even if you saw it before you left the group.
  • If you’re the only admin and you leave the group, you’ll be prompted to invite a new admin(s). The group will be automatically paused if you don’t select a new admin or if no one accepts the admin invitation within seven days.

This feature isn’t available to all groups right now.

If you’re a group admin, you can temporarily limit how frequently a member can post and/or comment in your group.

Temporarily limit how frequently a member can post and/or comment

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Members at the top. If you don’t see Members, click More.
  3. Find the person you want to limit and click Options, then select Limit Activity.

To remove limitations, click Toggle next to each limitation you want to remove. 4. To change limitations, click the limitation you want to change and select the new number of daily posts, hourly comments and/or expirations. 5. Click Save.

Manage anonymous participation and nicknames in a Facebook group you admin

Turn on anonymous posts

Turn off anonymous posts

Require post approval

If you don’t see the option to allow anonymous participation or nicknames in your group, it could be because one or both features are not available in your group for now.

If some members can’t post, comment or react anonymously or with a nickname, it could be because the feature(s) aren’t available to them for now.

If you’re a group admin, you can choose whether or not to allow anonymous participation (including nicknames) if the option is available in your group. People will be able to participate anonymously in the group unless an admin turns off anonymous participation for the group.

You can also choose to require anonymous and nickname posts and post edits to be approved by admins or moderators, even if you don’t have post approval turned on in your group.

Admins and moderators can see who posted, commented or reacted anonymously or with a nickname by going to their post, comment or reaction and tapping on the user’s profile photo (e.g., Anonymous).

Note:

  • If you allow anonymous participation (including nicknames) in your group, that means users can do all of the following: post, comment and react anonymously or with a nickname. You can’t allow anonymous posts but not anonymous comments, or allow anonymous posts but not nickname posts or comments, for example.
  • In larger groups, the nickname feature may be automatically enabled for the group and available to group members; admins can still turn on or off anonymous participation (which includes anonymous posting, commenting, and reacting) in these groups. For larger groups, the anonymous participation setting does not control nicknames; this means that turning off anonymous participation will not disable nicknames in these groups.
    • Nicknames help protect members’ privacy by keeping their main profile name hidden from other members in connection with posts, comments, and reactions made with a nickname. Admins and moderators can still see this information and take action to effectively moderate their group.
    • To see the main profile name associated with a nickname, an admin or moderator can tap the nickname’s profile photo and then, once viewing the member’s group profile, click the tab at the top for the member’s main profile.

Turn anonymous participation on or off

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. In the left menu, click Group settings. You might have to click Manage first.
  3. Below Manage discussion, click Edit next to Anonymous participation.
  4. Select your preferred option (on or off).
  5. Click Save.

Note:

  • In larger groups:
    • Turning off anonymous participation does not disable nicknames.
    • Nicknames remain enabled and cannot be turned off.
  • In all other groups:
    • Turning off anonymous participation will also turn off nicknames.
  • Admins should review the setting’s language to confirm whether it covers both anonymous participation and nicknames, or only anonymous participation.

Require approval of anonymous posts, nickname posts, and post edits

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. In the left menu, click Group settings. You might have to click Manage first.
  3. Below Manage discussion, click Edit next to Post approval.
  4. Select your preferred option.
  5. Click Save.

More information

  • If you remove or ban someone who is participating anonymously or with a nickname in your group, the user’s profile will also be removed or banned from the group.
  • As an admin or moderator, you can also block a nickname user similar to how you can block a profile. If you block a nickname as an admin or moderator, you will still be able to see the nickname’s posts or comments in the group. The blocked nickname will not be able to tag you or interact with your content. In some cases, they may still be able to see your content. The nickname you blocked will not be notified that you blocked them. The blocking only applies to that nickname and doesn’t block the main profile associated with the nickname.
  • Admins can review anonymous posts or nickname posts (if you have post approval turned on or require anonymous or nickname post approval) from the Pending posts queue.
  • If you don’t see the option to allow anonymous participation or nicknames in your group, it could be because anonymous participation or nicknames isn’t available in your group for now. If some members can’t post, comment or react anonymously or with a nickname, it could be because the feature(s) aren’t available to them or the group for now.
  • If someone participates anonymously or with a nickname, their profile name and photo will still be visible to the group’s admins and moderators, as well as to Facebook’s systems, in order to help keep groups safe and in compliance with our Community Standards.
  • Details someone includes in an anonymous or nickname post or comment could inadvertently reveal their identity.
  • In larger groups, the nicknames feature may be automatically enabled and available to members; it is designed to provide members with a way to participate with added privacy. Even if admins turn off anonymous participation in these groups, the nicknames feature will remain enabled.

Manage badges in your Facebook group

Manage my group badges

What are group badges?

Add expertise to my badge

Turn off my admin badge

Badges show people who you are or what you’ve accomplished in a group. If you have a badge and allow it to be displayed, it will appear on your group posts, comments and profile for the group.

Here are some of the badges you can get in groups:

  • Badge name: Admin; Who can get it: Group admins; How to get it: Accept an invitation to be an admin of the group; How long it’s displayed: Until an admin turns this badge off for the group Or Until an admin decides not to display the badge by their name
  • Badge name: Moderator; Who can get it: Group moderators; How to get it: Accept an invitation to be a moderator of the group; How long it’s displayed: Until an admin turns this badge off for the group Or Until a moderator decides not to display the badge by their name
  • Badge name: Group Expert Note: This badge isn’t available in all groups; Who can get it: Eligible group members, admins and moderators; How to get it: Accept an invitation to be a group expert for demonstrating knowledge on topics the group cares about; How long it’s displayed: Until an admin turns this badge off for the group Or Until a group expert decides not to display the badge by their name
  • Badge name: Rising contributor, top contributor or all-star contributor; Who can get it: Group members, admins and moderators; How to get it: Be among the most active participants in the group by receiving replies or reactions on your posts or comments, being an admin or moderator, and/or being a group expert; How long it’s displayed: Until an admin turns the Contributions feature off for the group Or Until a top, rising or all-star contributor decides not to display the badge by their name

Manage which badges appear next to your name

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click your profile photo to the left of “Write something…” to go to your member profile.
  3. On your member profile, click Edit Profile.
  4. Scroll down to Badges and click Edit.
  5. Choose which badges you’d like to appear on your group posts and comments, then click Done.

Add your expertise if an admin made you a group expert

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click your profile photo to the left of “Write something…” to go to your member profile.
  3. On your member profile, click Edit Profile.
  4. Click Add Expertise below Expertise.
    • To add your topic of expertise, click Add topic below Select your topic of expertise, then search for and select your topic.
    • To show your expertise on your badge, click Add to group expert badge.
    • To add additional credentials, click Add experience and follow the prompts.
    • To let admins of other groups discover your expertise, click the option to be invited to other groups as an expert.
  5. Click Save.

To remove yourself as a group expert, go to the member list and scroll down to Group Experts, then select your name and select Remove as group expert.

Note: Group admins can choose to turn badges on or off in their group.

Badges appear in the tab for your nickname

You can view your points on your group profile.

  • Badge points are awarded per group. Your points do not carry over from one group to another.
  • Points are tracked separately. The points you earn on your main profile do not transfer to or count toward your nickname profile, and vice versa.
  • Your main profile and nickname each display their own points total and badges based on activity under that identity.
  • You can view your points on each of your group profiles. Your points total is shown on the appropriate group profile page. Main profile points appear on the group profile for your main profile, and nickname points appear on the group profile for your nickname.

Adopting an admin badge while using a nickname

If you are the admin of a group, your group has nicknames turned on, and you have access to the feature, you can choose whether to display your admin or moderator badge while you use your nickname.

You may want to use your nickname without an admin or moderator badge if you want to act as a general member of a group, such as asking for or providing advice.

You may want to use a nickname with your admin or moderator badge if you are moderating content while you use a nickname and engaging in posts, comments or reactions.

Adopt an admin or moderator badge while using your nickname

  1. Confirm that you have adopted a nickname in this group.
  2. Go to your group-specific profile.
  3. Select the tab at the top that represents your nickname.
  4. Click Display badge shown below the Edit button, or select Manage shown in the badge section.
  5. Check the box next to the admin or moderator badge from the badge list.
  6. Select Save.
  7. Refresh your profile page to confirm that the admin or moderator badge appears in the badge section.

Turn off an admin or moderator badge for your nickname

  1. Click Manage shown in the badge section.
  2. Uncheck the box next to the admin or moderator badge from the badge list.
  3. Click Done.
  4. Refresh your profile page to confirm that the admin or moderator badge no longer appears in the badge section.

Manage membership for your Facebook group

Set who approves members

Set up membership questions

Approve or decline members

Automatically approve members

Public groups

In public groups, people can become members without admin approval, and visitors (people who aren’t members) can post and comment if admins allow.

You can choose to approve members and visitors as participants before they publish a post or comment for the first time. Once someone is approved as a participant, you can still require admin approval of their future posts.

Learn how to approve participants and manage posts in public groups and about membership preapprovals.

Private groups

In private groups, membership approval is required, unless limited membership is turned on. Learn more about limited membership in a private Facebook group.

This means admins or moderators will have to approve membership requests before someone can join the group. Admins can also allow anyone in the group to approve requests from their friends.

People can join certain private groups without admin approval as limited members if the group has limited membership turned on. Limited members can see all group content and react but won’t be able to post, comment, or chat until they’ve been approved by an admin to participate.

To make approving members easier, you can use Admin Assist to automatically approve or decline membership requests by setting up criteria such as automatically approving people who answered the membership questions or automatically declining people with new accounts. If you turn on limited membership in your private group, any Admin Assist rules you set up to automatically approve or decline membership requests will apply to participation requests from limited members instead.

If you’re an admin of a private hidden group, you can choose to allow people to invite new members to your group with a link. If you allow invitations with a link, you can choose who can invite with a link — anyone in the group, only admins, or admins and moderators — and you can disable active links.

Set who can approve member requests

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Group Settings in the left menu.
  3. Below Manage Membership, click Edit next to Who Can Approve Member Requests.
  4. Select who you want to be able to approve member requests:
    • Only admins and moderators
    • Anyone in the group: Members can approve requests from their friends. If your private group has limited membership turned on, this setting allows members to approve participation requests from their friends.
  5. Click Save.

Set up membership questions

You can set up membership questions to help you decide whether or not to approve a user as a member. If you turn on limited membership in your group, any membership questions you set up will become participation questions to help you decide whether or not to approve a limited member to participate in the group.

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Membership Questions below Badge requests in the left menu.
  3. Click Add Question to add your first question, or Create to add a new question.
  4. Next to Group Rules, click Toggle to ask members to agree to the Group Rules.

Approve or decline members

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Member Requests above Badge requests in the left menu.
  3. You can then:
    • Approve or Decline each request.
    • Approve All or Decline All.
  4. To leave feedback for someone you declined, click Options next to their request, then select Decline with feedback. When you send feedback, it will say that the feedback came from “an admin,” but it won’t disclose your name.

Automatically approve or decline membership requests with Admin Assist

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist in the left menu.
  3. Below Manage people, click Add next to Approve member request if and/or Decline member request if.
  4. Select criteria.
  5. Click Add to Admin Assist.

Admin Assist will only automatically approve a member request if all criteria are met. If a request meets both sets of criteria for approving and declining a request, the request will be approved.

Allow or not allow invitations with a link to your private hidden group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Group Settings in the left menu.
  3. Below Set Up Group, click next to Invite with link.
  4. Click Toggle next to Invite with link to allow or not allow invitations with a link.
  5. If you allow invitations with a link, select who can invite with a link: Only admins, Admins and moderators or Anyone in the group.
  6. Click Save.

Turn off an active link for invitations to your private hidden group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click + Invite at the top right.
  3. Select Invite with link.
  4. Select Turn off link, then Turn Off to confirm.

Manage spam in a Facebook group you admin

Manage potential spam folder

Set up Admin Assist

Set up participation questions

Keeping Facebook safe is a priority. This includes preventing and removing spam: unwanted posts, comments and membership/participation requests. If you come across spam on Facebook, we encourage you to report it to us.

Here are some tools to help you manage spam in a group you admin. All tools are available in the left menu in your group.

Potential spam folder

The potential spam folder contains posts and comments Facebook has identified as likely to be spam. They won’t appear in your group unless you publish them.

Check the potential spam folder

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Potential spam on the left.
  3. If a post or comment is spam or unwanted, click Decline. If a post isn’t spam and you want it posted in your group, click Publish. Help improve the accuracy of the potential spam folder

If you notice that the potential spam folder has posts/comments that aren’t spam, we suggest visiting the folder regularly and publishing posts/comments that aren’t spam. Your actions help improve our systems.

Admin Assist

Admin Assist automatically manages posts, comments and participation based on criteria that you set.

Select preset criteria for declining posts/comments that are likely to be spam

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist on the left.
  3. Below Manage Posts, click Add next to Decline incoming post if. Below Manage comments, click Add next to Decline comment if.
  4. Select Spam posts and/or Spam comments.
  5. Click Add to Admin Assist.

Participation/membership questions

Set up participation questions (in public groups) or membership questions (in private groups), then use Admin Assist to automatically approve requests by people who have answered the questions.

Automatically approve requests by people who have answered the questions

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist on the left.
  3. For public groups:- Below Manage requests, click Add next to Approve participant if, then select Participation questions. For private groups:- Below Manage people, click Add next to Approve member request if, then select Membership questions.
  4. Click Add to Admin Assist.

Participant/membership approval

For public groups, turn on participant approval to approve members and visitors before they post or comment for the first time. For private groups, turn on membership approval to require people to request to be members.

Post approval

Turn on post approval to review every post before it’s published.

Keyword alerts

Set up keyword alerts to be notified when posts or comments contain certain words or phrases.
