I can’t post anonymously

If you don’t see the option to post, comment, or react anonymously, it could be because:

  • The feature isn’t available to you for now.
  • The feature isn’t available in the group for now.
  • The group admins don’t allow the feature.

You can participate anonymously in a Facebook group if anonymous participation is available to your group, the group admins allow it, and it’s available to you. Anonymous participation includes the ability to post, comment, and react anonymously.

An anonymous post, comment or reaction will show that it was created by an Anonymous member (in private groups) or Anonymous participant (in public groups). It will include the Anonymous icon as your profile picture.

Note: If you participate anonymously, your name and profile photo will still be visible to admins, moderators and Facebook’s systems.

Post anonymously

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Write something…
  3. Click Toggle next to Post anonymously, then click Got it.
  4. Create your post, then click Submit.

To turn off anonymous posting, click or tap Toggle next to Post anonymously again to turn it off.

Comments you make on your anonymous post will also be anonymous. As with your anonymous post, the group admins, group moderators and Facebook’s systems will be able to see your name and profile photo.

What happens next

If the admins require post approval in the group or require approval of anonymous posts, then your anonymous post will be reviewed by admins or moderators. Otherwise, your post will be published immediately.

More information

  • Privacy
    • If you participate anonymously, your profile name and photo will still be visible to admins, moderators and Facebook’s systems, in order to help keep groups safe and in compliance with our Community Standards.
    • Details you include in your anonymous post or comment could reveal your identity.
    • Some post formats are disabled for anonymous posts to protect you from inadvertently exposing your identity.
  • Other limitations
    • You can’t customize the Anonymous icon or color that appears with your anonymous posts and comments. The color of the icon assigned to you is random. If more than one anonymous post has the same color icon, it doesn’t mean they were posted by the same person.
    • You can post, comment or react anonymously, but you can’t do other things anonymously like use Live Video, share content or send messages.

Participate with a nickname in a Facebook group

Post with a nickname

Customize my nickname

Change my nickname

Why can’t I use a nickname?

If you don’t see the option to customize or set a nickname, it could be because:

  • The feature isn’t available to you for now.
  • The feature isn’t available in the group for now.
  • The group admins don’t allow the feature.

You can participate with a nickname in a Facebook group if the nicknames feature is available to your group, the group admins allow it or it was automatically enabled for your group, and it’s available to you.

Nickname participation includes the ability to customize or set a nickname, and then post, comment, and react in the group using that nickname. Posting, commenting, and reacting with your nickname allows you to hide your main profile name and profile photo in connection with your post, comment, or reaction from other members. Remember that your main profile name and profile photo will still be visible to admins, moderators and Facebook’s systems.

A nickname may be assigned or suggested to you if you have not previously used a nickname in a group and choose to participate in that group with a nickname. You can use the assigned or suggested nickname, or you can update your nickname to one of your choosing. However, your nickname must comply with our Community Standards and cannot already be in use by another Facebook Groups member.

A profile picture for your nickname may also be assigned or suggested to you. You can use the assigned or suggested profile picture or select from the available profile pictures and color backgrounds for your nickname’s profile picture.

Post with a nickname

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Write something….
  3. If you have not yet set a nickname in that group, click Toggle next to Post anonymously, then click Got it.
  4. Click Customize a nickname and follow the prompts.
    • If you have already set a nickname in that group, click Toggle next to Post with your nickname.
  5. Create your post, then click Submit.

To turn off posting with your nickname, click Toggle next to Post as [your nickname].

You can also go back to using your main profile name or Anonymous member (private group) or Anonymous participant (public group) by using the comment bar:

  1. Next to the comment bar, click your nickname’s profile picture.
  2. Select whether you want to comment as your main profile or anonymously.
    • If you’re unable to change who you comment as on a specific post, it may be because in that group, anonymous participation isn’t available to you right now or because you’ve already interacted with that post using your nickname.

Comments you make on your nickname post will also be made with your nickname. As with your nickname post, the group admins, group moderators, and Facebook’s systems will be able to see your main profile name and profile photo in connection with comments you make with your nickname.

What happens next

If the admins require post approval in the group or require approval of anonymous or nickname posts, then your nickname post will be reviewed by admins or moderators. Otherwise, your post will be published immediately.

A nickname post, comment or reaction will show that it was created by your nickname, and it will include your selected profile photo and background color as your profile picture.

Customize nicknames

You can customize a nickname (example: Stargazer22) to use when posting, commenting and reacting anonymously in a group. Once you set a nickname, it will be your default way of participating in that group until you change it.

You have the option to use different nicknames in different groups. You will need to set your nickname in each group in which you want to use it.

Nicknames shouldn’t impersonate anyone or misrepresent your identity, and they must follow our Community Standards and Terms of Service. If the nickname you would like to use is not available because it does not meet our Community Standards or it has already been adopted by another user, Facebook will suggest other options for your nickname.

Participate with a nickname

  1. Open the Facebook app for iOS or Android.
  2. At the top of the group, tap Write something…
  3. Toggle on Post anonymously.
  4. Tap Customize a nickname.
  5. Enter a nickname. You will see a green check next to your nickname if it is available and passes our Community Standards.
  6. Tap Save.

Go back to participating as an Anonymous member (private group) or Anonymous participant (public group)

  1. Open the Facebook app for iOS or Android.
  2. At the top of the group, tap Post as [your nickname]…
  3. Tap Edit nickname.
  4. Select Post anonymously without a nickname.

Go back to participating with your main profile name

  1. Open the Facebook app for iOS or Android.
  2. At the top of the group, tap Post as [your nickname]…
  3. Toggle off Post anonymously.
  4. Tap OK, I understand.

Change who you comment or react as

  1. Open the Facebook app for iOS or Android.
  2. Go to a group post.
  3. Tap your profile picture next to Write a comment…
  4. Select who you want to participate as: your main profile, anonymous member or participant, or your nickname if you’ve set one.
    • If you have created a post with your nickname or already commented on a post using your nickname, you will not be able to change your voice on that specific post.

Report a nickname that doesn’t follow our Community Standards

  1. Tap a nickname from a group post, comment or reaction.
  2. Tap Report.
  3. Follow the prompts.

More information

  • Privacy
    • If you participate with a nickname, your main profile name and profile photo will still be visible to admins, moderators and Facebook’s systems, in order to help keep groups safe and in compliance with our Community Standards.
    • Details you include in your nickname post or comment could reveal your identity.
    • People may learn that the nicknames you customize are associated with your main profile based on what you say and do. Using the same nickname in multiple groups could make it easier for people to discover the nickname’s association with your main profile.
    • Some post formats are disabled for nickname posts to protect you from inadvertently exposing your identity.
  • You can only change your nickname once every 2 days. When you change your nickname:
    • Your previous nickname may become available for others to use.
    • Your nickname will update on your past posts, comments and reactions. This change may take time to take effect across your groups and devices. If you use different nicknames in different groups, changing your nickname in one group will only update your posts, comments and reactions in that group.
    • If you edit your nickname’s profile photo in one group, that profile photo will update in all groups where you use that nickname. You cannot use different profile photos with the same nickname in your various groups.
  • Other limitations
    • Two people can’t have the same nickname at the same time.
    • You can post, comment or react with your nickname, but you can’t do other things with your nickname like use Live Video, share content or send messages.
  • Note
    • Other group members (for private groups) or anyone (for public groups) can see your nickname post history in the group, as well as your comments and reactions within the group made with your nickname within the last 7 days. You can see what post, comment, and reaction history for a nickname, including your own, is shared with others by clicking on that nickname in your group.
    • You can block another nickname user from interacting with you.

Pause a Facebook group you admin

Pause my Facebook group

Resume my Facebook group

Change group resume date

If you’re an admin of a group, you can pause your group if you need a break from maintaining it or if you need time to catch up on tasks such as managing posts or membership. A message will be added to the top of the group explaining that all activity is paused. New posts, comments and reactions are paused for everyone, including admins.

If you’re a group admin and you want to permanently remove your group from Facebook, you can delete it. Learn more about the differences between pausing and deleting a group.

Pause a group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Options below the cover photo.
  3. Select Pause group.
  4. Select a reason for pausing the group, then click Continue. To confirm you want to pause your group, click Continue again.
  5. You will then have the option to write a group announcement about the pause, and schedule when the group will automatically resume.
  6. Click Pause Group at the bottom.

Change when a group will automatically resume

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Edit below the cover photo, then adjust the date and time and click Confirm.

Resume a group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Resume below the cover photo, then click Confirm.

When a group is paused, members can still:

  • Delete their existing posts or comments
  • Access their information
  • Leave the group

Keep in mind that Facebook can continue to enforce Community Standards when the group is paused.

Pin items to the top of your Facebook group

Pin a post

Pin group rules

Pin a group feature

Remove a pinned item

If you’re an admin or moderator of a Facebook group, you can pin items to the Featured section of your group to make them appear at the top. Posts, rules, and features can be pinned at the top of your group.

As you pin items, the newest item appears at the top of the list. You can change the order of any item.

Pinned items remain visible until you remove them. In public groups, anyone on or off Facebook can see the pinned items. In private groups, only group members can see them.

Learn how to pin items to your Facebook group below.

Pin a post

  1. Log into your Facebook account.
  2. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  3. Find the post you want to pin.
  4. Click Options next to the post you want to pin.
  5. Click Pin to Featured.

Pin the group rules

  1. Log into your Facebook account.
  2. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  3. Click Add next to Featured at the top of your group.
  4. Click Pin next to Rules.

Pin a group feature

  1. Log into your Facebook account.
  2. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  3. Click Group settings in the left menu.
  4. Scroll down to Added to group in the center and click Edit next to the feature you want to pin.
  5. Click the Toggle next to the Pin to the Featured section. (This option is only available for certain features.)

You can also remove pinned items.

Remove a pinned item

  1. Log into your Facebook account.
  2. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  3. Click Group settings in the left menu.
  4. Scroll down to Added to group in the center and click Edit next to the item you want to remove.
  5. Click the Toggle next to the Pin to the Featured section.

Preapprove members for a Facebook group you admin

Turn on preapproval

Upload a preapproval file

Remove preapproved groups

If you’re a group admin, you can save time by preapproving member requests from those who are already in your other groups or whose email is included in the file you upload.

Turn on membership preapproval

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Settings in the left menu.
  3. Click on Group Settings and scroll down to Manage memberships.
  4. Scroll down and click Edit next to Who Is Preapproved to Join.
  5. Click Choose Groups or Upload a File and follow the steps.
  6. Click Save.

You can remove groups or files from automatic membership approval by clicking Manage Groups or Manage File and then Remove.

Files must be smaller than 5 MB and accepted file types are .csv and .tsv. Only one file can be uploaded at a time with a maximum of 5,000 emails per file. Preapprovals from a file expire after 90 days.

Keep in mind that the emails in the file you upload must be associated with a Facebook account in order for the person to be preapproved.

Note: Preapproving people doesn’t invite them to join the group.

If someone who is listed as a preapproved member joins a private group with limited membership turned on, their request to participate will be automatically approved. Learn more about limited membership.

Learn more about turning on membership approval in your group. Learn how to use Admin Assist to automatically approve or decline membership based on criteria that you set.

Preapprove posts from some people in a Facebook group you admin

See preapproved members

Remove preapproval

Group admins and moderators can preapprove members of their group to post in the group without admin approval.

Preapprove a group member

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Tap Members or People.
  3. Tap Options next to the name of the member you’d like to preapprove and tap Preapprove posts.

See a list of preapproved group members or remove preapproval

Remove a post in a Facebook group you manage

Remove a post

Give feedback on removal

Note from admin

I can’t remove a post

Admins and moderators can remove posts from their group and give feedback about why the post was removed.

To remove a post from your group:

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Find the post you want to remove and click Options in the top right of the post.
  3. Click Remove post.
  4. Select the rule(s) that the post violated and add an optional note from the admin.
  5. Click Toggle next to Give a warning.
  6. Click Confirm. If you add a note from the admin, the author of the post will receive a notification that their post was removed. If they click the notification, they’ll be able to see the rules their post violated and the note from the admin for 14 days.

Keep in mind that if you include a note from the admin it will come from an anonymous admin, not a specific individual.

Remove an admin or moderator from your Facebook group

Remove an admin

Remove a moderator

Can’t remove group creator

Only admins can remove another admin or moderator.

Note: Group creators can’t be removed by another admin, but they can remove themselves as an admin or leave the group.

Remove someone as an admin or moderator

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Members or People below your group’s cover photo. If you don’t see Members or People, click More.
  3. Click Options next to the name of the person you want to remove as an admin or moderator.

More information

  • If you can’t remove someone as an admin, it might be because they’re the group creator. Group creators can’t be removed by another admin, but if they no longer want to be an admin they can:

Remove, ban or unban someone in a Facebook group you manage

Remove someone from group

Ban someone from group

Unban someone from group

Ban future accounts

Group admins and moderators can remove or ban someone from a group. Removed members will have to request to join the group again if they wish to rejoin. People who are banned won’t be able to find the group in search or see any of the content within the group, and they can’t be invited to the group again. They may still be able to see content previously sent in certain chats with Meta AI or other AIs while they were a member of the group.

Remove or ban someone

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Members or People below the cover photo.
  3. Find the person you want to remove or ban.
  4. Click Options next to their name and select Remove member or Ban from group.
    • Click to check the box next to Delete recent activity if you’d like to delete their last 7 days of posts, comments, reactions, polls and pending member invitations.
    • If you’re removing the member and you’d also like to ban them, click Ban [name].
    • To prevent someone you banned from joining again under a different account, select Ban [name’s] future accounts. Note that Facebook may not be able to detect all new accounts.
  5. Click Confirm.

If you already banned someone and then later decide to prevent them from joining again under a different account, go to your group’s Members or People section, unban them, then ban them again and select Ban [name’s] future accounts. Note that Facebook may not be able to detect all new accounts.

Unban someone

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Members or People below the cover photo.
  3. Click Unban next to the name of the person you’d like to unban.
  4. Click Unban to confirm.

Effect on additional profiles

If someone has additional profiles and you banned any of their profiles:

  • They can still participate in the group with any of their profiles that are already in the group.
  • They can’t see, join or participate in the group with any of their profiles that are not already in the group.

If a group member has additional profiles and you removed any of their profiles, this has no effect on any of their other profiles, whether or not those profiles are already in the group.

Note that up to two profiles from the same account can join/participate in the same group. Learn more about additional profiles in groups.

Report a Facebook group post or comment to the admins

Report post to admins

Report comment to admins

Admins know who reported

Report group to Facebook

If you believe a post or comment doesn’t follow the group rules or our Community Standards, you can report it to the admins.

Alternatively, you can report the post/comment to Facebook, or report the group to Facebook.

Note:

  • Reporting to the admins won’t send a report to Facebook. A group won’t be taken down just because something is reported to the admins.
  • If you report something to the admins, they will know it was you who reported it.
  • After you report something to the admins, you can also choose to take other steps such as blocking the author.

Report a post or comment to the admins

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Options in the top right of the post or comment you want to report.
  3. Click Report post to group admins for a post, or Report comment to group admins for a comment.
  4. Select a reason and fill out any other information if needed and click Next.
  5. You can choose to take other steps such as blocking or hiding the profile that created the post or comment. Then, click Done.

The admins will receive a notification that there’s content to review, and they may or may not take action.

Report a group post or comment to Facebook

Report a group post

Report a group comment

Report a group to Facebook

If you believe a post or comment doesn’t follow our Community Standards, you can report it to Facebook.

Alternatively, you can report the post/comment to the group admins, or report the group to Facebook.

Report a post or comment to Facebook

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Go to the post you want to report.

Report a group to Facebook

Report a group

What happens after I report?

Report an abusive group

If you think a group isn’t following our Community Standards, you can report it.

Report a group

  1. From your Feed, click Groups in the left menu or search for the name of the group you want to report.
  2. Click Options below the cover photo and select Report group.
  3. Select what’s wrong with the group, then click Done.

What happens when you report a group

After you report a group to Facebook, we review content in the group that might go against our Community Standards. We’ll send a message to your Support Inbox about whether or not the group was removed.

Please keep in mind that reporting something to Facebook doesn’t guarantee that it will be removed. You may see something you don’t like on Facebook that doesn’t violate our Terms of Service.

Review content in Flagged by Facebook for a group you admin

Review content in Flagged by Facebook

Options for flagged content

Set default for bullying content

Turn off Flagged by Facebook

This feature is only available in some groups.

Flagged by Facebook is a tool that alerts admins about potential violations of the Community Standards before they appear in your Group Quality. Content that is flagged and held will be hidden from the group while it waits for an admin to take action. If an admin doesn’t take any action within 7 days, the flagged content will be automatically deleted.

Options when reviewing content in Flagged by Facebook

As a group admin, you can choose one of the following options when reviewing content in Flagged by Facebook:

  • Agree and remove the content
  • Request that a Meta review team take another look. If the review team decides that the content doesn’t violate the Community Standards, the content will be automatically restored. If the team determines that the content does violate the Community Standards, they will take down the content and the violation will show up in your Group Quality.
  • Restore the content (only available in some groups for content flagged for bullying and harassment). An admin might use this option if their understanding is that the content was not intended as bullying and harassment (example: “I hear you, dog”).

If an admin:

  • Agrees and removes the content: The violation of the Community Standards will appear in your Group Quality. The violation appearing in your Group Quality does not necessarily increase the risk of your group getting taken down.
  • Requests that a Meta review team take another look and the review team determines that the content
    • violates the Community Standards: The violation will appear in your Group Quality.
    • doesn’t violate the Community Standards: The content will be restored and the flag won’t appear in your Group Quality.
  • Restores the content (only available in some groups for content flagged for bullying and harassment): The flag won’t appear in your Group Quality.

To review content in Flagged by Facebook:

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Flagged by Facebook in the left menu.
  3. Review each post and make your selections.

Set a default for all content flagged for bullying and harassment:

In some groups with access to Flagged by Facebook, admins also have the option to choose what happens by default to all content flagged for potential bullying and harassment:

  • Hold content and let admins decide: The content will be hidden from the group. Admins can then review it and decide whether to restore or remove it.
  • Keep content and alert admins: The content will stay in the group, but all admins can review the content.
  • Remove content: The content will be automatically removed from the group.

To set a default for all content flagged for bullying and harassment:

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Flagged by Facebook in the left menu.
  3. Click Settings gear in the top right.
  4. Click Options and select your preference.
  5. Click Save.

Note:

  • The tool flags potential violations by both members and admins/moderators.
  • Some types of violations might not be flagged.
  • Members will receive a notification when their content is flagged or removed. Members can see the flagged content by going to the group, clicking Options, selecting Your content, then selecting Flagged.
  • If someone sees content that was restored by the admins but they think it should have been removed, they can still report it. If the review team then determines that the content does violate the Community Standards, the violation will appear in your Group Quality. The violation appearing in your Group Quality does not necessarily increase the risk of your group getting taken down.
  • You can turn off Flagged by Facebook by going to the Flagged by Facebook tool, selecting Settings gear in the top right and toggling Send me flagged content. (In some groups, you may have to turn off Flagged by Facebook by selecting Remove content from the dropdown.) When Flagged by Facebook is turned off, admins can still see actions Facebook has taken to enforce the Community Standards in Group Quality.

Schedule a post or set up recurring posts in a Facebook group you manage

Admins and moderators can schedule group posts.

Admins can set up recurring group posts.

There are two options if you want a group post to publish at a specific time:

  • Scheduled posts: When creating posts, admins can choose to schedule them to publish at a later time. For example, an admin can use the Insights tool to see when the group is most active, and schedule an important announcement for that time. This option is only available for admins and moderators, and only once they’ve started typing a post.
  • Recurring posts: Admins can use Admin Assist to create a post that recurs daily, weekly or monthly. An admin may use this feature if they want to regularly engage members with a prompt or reminder. The admin who set up the original post will be the author. 24 hours before being published, it will appear in Scheduled posts, where the admin who set it up can view, edit or delete it. If other admins want to edit the post, they have to delete it from Admin Assist then re-add it. This option is only available for admins.

Schedule a post

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Write something… to start creating a post. You might need to click Discussion at the top of the group first.
  3. Write your post, then click Calendar next to Post.
  4. Select the date and time you want the post to publish.
  5. Click Schedule.

Note: This option is only available for admins and moderators, and only once they’ve started typing a post.

Edit, reschedule, cancel or publish a scheduled post

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Scheduled Posts in the Admin tools menu on the left. You might have to click Manage on the left first.
  3. Select Reschedule Post or Post Now, or click Options and select Edit post or Delete post.

Create a recurring post

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist in the left menu.
  3. Scroll down and click Add next to Publish a custom post.
  4. Select Start from scratch to create your own post, or select a suggested prompt.
  5. Edit the post, choose how frequently you’d like it to post and select the date and time for the first post.
  6. Click Add to Admin Assist.

Note: Some formatting options are available from facebook.com on a computer, but not the Facebook app.

Set up Admin Assist to automatically manage your Facebook group

Set up Admin Assist

Edit Admin Assist criteria

Delete Admin Assist criteria

Undo Admin Assist action

Admin Assist can help you automatically manage posts, comments, membership and more in your group based on criteria that you set.

Here are some examples of how you can use Admin Assist

  • Automatically approve membership or participant requests from people who answered the membership or participation questions.
  • Reduce spam by selecting preset criteria that automatically decline posts and comments that are likely to be spam.
  • Automatically manage posts that contain false information as determined by independent fact-checkers.
  • Manage conflict by automatically removing posts and messages that are reported a certain number of times, or turning off comments on posts that have been reported or may be contentious.
  • Automatically decline posts and comments that link to a specific site. You can also automatically notify the author why the post was declined and/or block them.
  • Set up recurring posts or automatically-created welcome posts that tag new members.
  • Automatically approve pending posts if they pass your specific criteria and our systems are very confident about approving them based on the content of the post, the author, your past decisions about similar posts and more.

Set up Admin Assist

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist in the left menu.
  3. Below Add or edit criteria, click Add next to each automatic action you want Admin Assist to take.
  4. Choose a preset to customize or create your own criteria and follow the prompts.
  5. To turn on or off automated moderation, where Admin Assist will automatically approve pending posts and/or participant requests for public groups if they pass your specific criteria and our systems are very confident about approving them: Click Settings at the top of Admin Assist, then click Toggle next to Pending posts and/or Participant requests (for public groups).

Edit criteria

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist in the left menu.
  3. Below Add or edit criteria, click Edit next to the criteria, then click Edit.
  4. Edit the criteria, then click Save criteria.

Delete criteria

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist in the left menu.
  3. Below Add or edit criteria, click Edit next to the criteria, then click Delete. Click Delete again to confirm.

Undo an action completed by Admin Assist

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Admin Assist in the left menu.
  3. Click Activity log in the upper right, then click Undo next to the action. Click Undo again to confirm.

Learn how to use Admin Assist to automatically

  • Manage posts and comments and people.
  • Manage posts that independent fact-checkers have determined contain false information.
  • Reduce spam by selecting preset criteria that automatically decline posts and comments that are likely to be spam.
  • Suspend someone if they’ve had multiple posts or comments removed.
  • Set up recurring posts or automatically-created welcome posts that tag new members.

Note

  • Admin Assist will automatically decline an incoming post if any criteria is met.
  • Admin Assist will only automatically approve a membership or participant request if all criteria are met.
  • If you’re a public group admin, learn how to use participant approval to review and approve people before they can post or comment for the first time.
  • If automated moderation is available and turned on in your group (see above):
    • Automated moderation works with other criteria you set in Admin Assist to automatically approve certain posts and/or participant requests for public groups.
    • Admin Assist will only make a decision for you when it’s very confident. Our systems look at the person’s history, signals about potential risk or spam, specific content, past moderation decisions and more. If Admin Assist isn’t confident enough, the request will still appear in your pending approvals queue.
    • You can review and undo any decisions you don’t agree with in the activity log, and Admin Assist will learn from your actions.
    • If you don’t see this feature, it could be because it’s not available in your group or because post approval and/or participant approval (for public groups) isn’t turned on.

Set up moderation alerts in a Facebook group you manage

Set up keyword alerts

Set up engagement alerts

Review moderation alerts

I can’t set up alerts

Only group admins and moderators can set up moderation alerts in their group.

When you set up moderation alerts in your Facebook group, you’ll be notified when posts or comments might need your attention. There are two kinds of moderation alerts:

  • Keyword alerts: Lets you know when members use certain words or phrases in your group.
  • Engagement alerts: Lets you know when posts or comments in your group are getting a certain number of comments, replies or reactions based on criteria you set.

Set up moderation alerts

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Moderation alerts in the left menu, then click Settings.
  3. Keyword alerts:
    • To add or edit a keyword: Click Create or Edit next to Keywords, write the keyword, then click Add then Back.
    • To delete a keyword: Click Remove next to the keyword you want to delete and then Back.
  4. Engagement alerts:
    • To add an engagement alert: Click Create next to Engagement, then select the content type, engagement type and amount, and then click Save.
    • To delete an engagement alert: Click Options then Delete alert, then Delete to confirm.
    • To edit an engagement alert: Click Options then Edit alert, then make your edits and click Update. Click Update again to confirm.

There’s no limit to the number of keyword alerts you can add.

Review moderation alerts

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Moderation alerts in the left menu.
  3. Click Ignore to disregard the alert, or click Remove to remove the content from your group.

Note: You’ll only receive engagement alerts if your criteria are met within a one-hour period. For example, if you set an engagement alert for posts that receive 100 comments, you will receive an alert if a post receives 100 comments over a 1-hour period. You won’t receive an alert if it takes more than an hour for a post to receive 100 comments.

Effect on additional profiles

If someone has additional profiles and you suspended any of their profiles:

  • They can still participate in the group with any of their profiles that are already in the group

Tag @everyone in a post or comment in a Facebook group

Tag @everyone in a group

Why can’t I tag everyone?

Turn off @everyone notifications

What does @everyone do?

The size of the group determines who can use the feature.

The batch mention @everyone can be used to tag all group members at once in a post or comment. For example, an admin might create a post and tag @everyone to inform the whole group of an important update. The size of the group determines who can use the feature:

  • Group size: Small; Who can tag @everyone in a group: Admins, moderators and members
  • Group size: Medium (not more than approximately 200,000 members); Who can tag @everyone in a group: Admins and moderators
  • Group size: Large (more than approximately 200,000 members); Who can tag @everyone in a group: No one

Tag @everyone in a group post or comment

  1. Start typing @everyone in the post/comment.
  2. Select @everyone from the dropdown suggestions.

Note

  • There are limits on how often someone can use @everyone in each group.
  • Members can turn off @everyone notifications.

Troubleshooting

Facebook has rules to prevent spam and make sure that batch mentions aren’t overused.

If you can’t use @everyone, it might be because:

  • Your group has more members than the feature supports (so it’s not available for admins, moderators or members).

  • You’re a member, and your group has more members than the feature supports for members (so it’s only available for admins and moderators).

  • You’ve reached the limit of how often you can use @everyone in that group. If someone isn’t notified when @everyone is used, it might be because:

  • They turned off notifications when @everyone is mentioned in a group.

  • They already received too many batch mention notifications in one day, or Facebook’s Notifications AI system decided not to send a notification.

  • They’re not a group member (if it’s a public group, they might be a participant but not a member).

  • They blocked the admin or moderator.

More information

  • Learn how to turn off @everyone notifications in a Facebook group you’re in.
  • Learn more about batch mentions on Facebook.

Voice call on Facebook

Note: In voice or video calls between only two people, your IP address will be shared with the other person’s device to establish a peer-to-peer connection. A peer-to-peer connection uses your IP address to connect directly with the person you’re calling to help improve the audio and video quality of your call. While this happens in the background, it may be possible for the other person to discover your IP address.

Something’s wrong with my microphone when I call someone on Facebook.

How do I make a video call?

How do I fix microphone issues?

You can call one person or make group calls on Messenger.

Start a voice call with one person or a group

Peer-to-peer connections

In audio or video calls between only two people, your IP address will be shared with the other person’s device to establish a peer-to-peer connection.

A peer-to-peer connection uses your IP address to connect directly with the person you’re calling to help improve the audio and video quality of your call. While this happens in the background, it may be possible for the other person to discover your IP address.

Troubleshoot microphone issues

Remember that you need to give Messenger permission to access your microphone before you can make a call.

Welcome new members to a Facebook group you manage

Set up new member intro

Set up welcome post

Automatically create welcome post

Group admins can welcome new members to their Facebook group with:

  • New member intro, which is a message from the admins that automatically appears to new members when they visit the group for the first time after joining. The intro can also include the group rules and/or a prompt encouraging new members to post.
  • Welcome post, which is a post that welcomes the new members and appears to everyone in the group. The prompt to create a welcome post will only be available if new members have joined in the past 7 days.

Set up new member intro

Admins can turn on, turn off or edit the new member intro at any time.

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Select Group settings on the left. You might have to click Manage first.
  3. Click More options next to New member intro.
    • To turn it on: Click Get started then write an intro message and choose whether to include the group rules. Click Publish.
    • To turn it off: Click next to Show intro message to turn it off. Alternatively, click Edit message then Delete intro message.
    • To edit: Click Edit message, make your changes, then click Update intro.

Set up welcome post

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Members (for private groups) or People (for public groups) at the top of the group. You might need to select More first.
  3. Click Write welcome post on the right.
  4. Customize the message and click Post.

The prompt to create a welcome post will only be available if new members have joined in the past 7 days.

Alternatively, use Admin Assist to automatically create a regular welcome post:

  1. Follow these instructions to go to Admin Assist.
  2. Scroll down and click Add next to Publish a welcome post.
  3. Follow the prompts.

The post will be created at the rate the admin chooses (example: weekly). 24 hours before it’s published, it will appear in Scheduled posts, where the admin who set it up can view, edit or delete it. If other admins want to edit the post, they have to delete it from Admin Assist then re-add it.

What happens when Facebook flags content in groups

What is auto-flagged content?

What are Community Standards?

When a group member posts something that might go against Facebook’s Community Standards, group admins may automatically be notified to review and manage the post. Posts that have been auto-flagged will not be shared to the group until a group admin has approved them. Group admins may also choose to delete the post and mute, remove or block the group member who created the post.

Keep in mind that any post that has been approved by a group admin may still be removed from Facebook if it is reported for going against our Community Standards.

What is preview mode?

I can’t join a group

When someone invites you to a group and that invitation is approved by a member, admin, or moderator, you’ll receive a notification that you’ve been invited to a group. You can preview the group and decide if you want to join.

While you’re in preview mode:

  • You can’t post or comment on other people’s posts in the group.
  • You can’t invite others to the group.
  • You can react to posts in the group.
  • Members of the group can see that you’re previewing the group in the members list, but those who aren’t members of the group can’t see you in the members list. You aren’t included in the total member count.
  • You can see the group’s members list and content.

After your invitation is approved by an admin or moderator, you can use preview mode for 28 days. If you interact with posts from a group that you’ve been invited to, preview mode will extend for an additional 28 days. If you don’t interact with group posts for 28 days, preview mode will expire.

You can leave a group at any time. Learn more about how to how to join a group, or invite new members to a group.

What it means that a Facebook group member is unavailable

What is an unavailable member?

Why is a member unavailable?

Remove unavailable member

As a group admin, you may see some group members listed in the Unavailable section of the member list. These accounts might be unavailable for several reasons. They may have blocked you, been blocked by you, been deactivated, or are pending account verification.

Admins can see all actions that unavailable members take within the group like posts and comments. Admins can also remove or ban unavailable members.

To view a list of unavailable names in a group you manage:

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Members at the top. If you don’t see Members, click More, then click Members.
  3. Scroll down to the Unavailable section. If you don’t see Unavailable, that means none of your group members are unavailable.

What it means that a group may contain flagged content

What is flagged content?

My content was flagged

How do admins review content?

Report restored content

This feature is only available in some groups.

In some eligible groups, admins have access to a tool that flags potential violations of our Community Standards. The admins can then do one of the following:

  • Agree and remove the content
  • Request that a Meta review team take another look. If the review team decides that the content doesn’t violate our Community Standards, the content will be automatically restored. If the team determines that the content does violate our Community Standards, they will take down the content and the violation will show up in the group’s Group Quality.
  • Restore the content (only available in some groups for content flagged for bullying and harassment). An admin might use this option if their understanding is that the content was not intended as bullying and harassment (example: “I hear you, dog”).

If your content was flagged and held for admin review:

  • You’ll receive a notification.
  • You can see the flagged content by going to your group, clicking Options , selecting Your content, then selecting Flagged.
  • You’ll receive another notification if the flagged content was then removed by an admin or the Meta review team.

Note:

  • If this tool is available to admins of a group you’re in, there will be a notice in the group’s About section saying that this group may contain flagged content.
  • If you see content that was restored by the group admins but you think it should have been removed, you can still report it.
  • Admins of some groups also have the option to choose what happens by default to all content flagged for bullying and harassment.
  • The tool flags potential violations by both members and admins/moderators.

Add two-factor authentication for your organization-managed Meta account

How do I set up two-factor authentication?

Add a backup method

My login code doesn’t work

You can’t turn on two-factor authentication if you already use single sign-on (SSO) to log into your managed Meta account.

If you turn on two-factor authentication for your managed Meta account, then you’ll be asked to confirm your identity when you try to log into your account from a new device. Using two-factor authentication reduces the risk of an attacker impersonating you and gaining access to your account.

Note: The instructions below are for people who are logging into a managed Meta account. This is an account that’s managed by an organization, such as where you work or go to school. If you’re trying to turn on two-factor authentication for your personal Meta account, follow these instructions.

Turn on two-factor authentication for your managed Meta account

  1. Go to L (l.facebook.com).
  2. Click [Image: Security and login] Password and security in the left menu.
  3. Click Two-factor authentication.
  4. Select either Authentication app (such as Google Authenticator or Duo Mobile) or Text message (SMS), then click Next.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions for your chosen option.

Add a backup method

You can add a backup two-factor authentication method (including a physical security key), in case there’s a problem with your primary method. To do this:

  1. Click [Image: Security and login] Password and security in the left menu of L (l.facebook.com).
  2. Click Two-factor authentication.
  3. Choose your option below Add a backup method.
    • If you add a physical security key, then you’ll need to have this key with you whenever you use this backup method.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions for your chosen option.

Backup codes (not available to all organizations)

After turning on two-factor authentication, you may see a list of backup codes that you can print or download. You can use these to log into your managed Meta account in case you lose access to your phone or other confirmation methods.

If backup codes are available to you, then you can access them and generate new ones in Two-factor authentication in Password and security.

You can only use a backup code once to log in. If you use up all your backup codes, then a new set will be created for you.

Note: Backup codes are not available to all organizations.

What to do if your two-factor authentication code doesn’t work

If your code doesn’t work when you try to log in, then click Try another way to view your options. These options will include any backup methods you’ve added.

Learn more about what to do if you can’t log into your managed account.

Confirming your age on Facebook

Download my information

We require people to be at least 13 years old to sign up for Facebook. In some regions, you may be required to confirm your age to continue using your account. You can confirm your age by providing your birthday, photo identification, and/or submitting a video selfie. If you need to confirm your age on Facebook, you’ll be asked for additional information to help us verify your age.

We partner with Yoti, a third party age verification service, to confirm people’s ages on Facebook. Yoti is verified by the Age Check Certification Scheme and is the leading age verification provider for several industries around the world including social media, gaming and age restricted e-commerce.

With Yoti, you can verify your age on Facebook by taking a video selfie or uploading your ID.

The information provided in each age verification option is used to confirm your age and won’t be visible on your profile, to friends or other people on Facebook.

You can review and can edit your birthday in your settings.

Create a passkey on Facebook

Create a passkey

Remove a passkey

How do passkeys work?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

It’s not recommended to create a passkey on a public or shared device.

To set up a passkey on your computer, you’ll need a computer that runs at least Windows 10, macOS Ventura, ChromeOS 109, or later, or a hardware security key that supports the FIDO2 protocol.

Supported browsers:

  • Chrome 109 or later
  • Safari 16 or later
  • Edge 109 or later
  • Firefox 122 or later

How passkeys work

Passkeys are a safe and easy alternative to passwords. When you create a passkey, you won’t need to enter your password to access your Facebook account or use Messenger.

To verify it’s you, you’ll use the method you use to unlock your device.

Passkeys are secure

Passkeys are more secure than passwords, because they’re uniquely generated for every account and are less vulnerable to phishing. Passkey information is stored on your device. Your biometric data, like a fingerprint or face scan, is never shared with Meta.

Create a passkey

The passkey you create will use your confirmed email address as its name, or your phone number if your email is not available. You can’t change your passkey name, and if your contact information changes, your passkey name will stay the same.

You may be prompted to create a passkey on your device when we need to confirm it’s you, like when you log into Facebook or Messenger.

Your passkey is verified using the same fingerprint, face scan, or device passcode that you use to unlock your device. Refer to your device information to learn more about setting up and managing your passkey.

If you remove a passkey, you’ll return to using alternative authentication methods, like passwords, where you had been using that passkey. Consult your device for information about how to delete your fingerprint, facial recognition, or screen lock data.

To remove a passkey:

Note: Removing a passkey is permanent.

  1. Tap Settings & Privacy.
  2. Tap Settings.
  3. Tap Accounts Center, then tap Password and security.
  4. Tap Passkey, then tap Remove next to the passkey you would like to remove. You’ll need to re-enter your password.

If you remove a passkey, you’ll return to using alternative authentication methods, like passwords, where you had been using that passkey.

Receive a one-time password

  1. Send a text message (SMS) to 32665 with the message otp. SMS messages may sometimes be delayed.

Your one-time password is temporary and can’t be used more than once. One-time passwords are not available if you have two-factor authentication turned on.

How Facebook uses the email or phone number you added for login alerts

Protect my Facebook profile

Receive login alerts by SMS

How Facebook uses my email

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

When you add a new email or mobile phone number for login alerts, we’ll use it to help you log into Facebook and keep your account safe.

If someone tries to log into your Facebook account from an unrecognized device or browser, we’ll send you an email alert. You can also choose to receive alerts by text message (SMS).

How we use the email or mobile phone number you added for login alerts

We may use the email or mobile phone number you add for login alerts to:

  • Protect you and others on Facebook.
    • Email addresses and phone numbers can help us detect if someone is using an email or phone number in a way that goes against our Community Standards. For example, if someone uses a phone number that may be yours to make a fake account, we might be able to prevent or catch fraud.
  • Help you access Facebook and use opt-in programs.
    • We use your email and phone number to help you log into Facebook.
    • In some countries, if you choose to use programs Meta offers with mobile network operators, we’ll use phone numbers to help you participate in these programs.
  • Count how many people use Facebook.
    • We use phone numbers to help correctly count how many people use Facebook and Meta Company Products.

We won’t use the email or phone number you added for login alerts for purposes such as suggesting friends or showing you ads.

Keep in mind, mobile phone numbers and emails added to other places on Facebook and Meta Company Products (for example, Marketplace and your Facebook profile) may be used for other purposes including suggesting friends or showing ads.

How Facebook uses your mobile phone number for two-factor authentication

Add phone number for 2FA

How 2FA keeps my account safe

Why can’t I reset password?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

When you add a new mobile phone number for two-factor authentication, we’ll use it to help you log into Facebook and help keep your account safe. If someone tries to log into your Facebook from an unrecognized device or browser, we’ll send you a text message alert and ask you for a verification code.

Keep in mind, mobile phone numbers added to other places on Facebook and Meta Company Products (example: Marketplace, your Facebook profile) may be used for other purposes including suggesting friends or providing ads.

For security reasons, you won’t be able to use the same mobile phone number that you use for two-factor authentication to help you reset your password. You’ll need to have a different mobile phone number or email address added to your account to reset your password if you ever need to.

How Facebook uses your selfie to confirm your identity

How long is my selfie stored?

Where is my selfie stored?

Why do you need my selfie?

When you send us your selfie, it will be stored securely. It won’t be visible on your profile, to friends or to other people on Facebook.

We’ll use your selfie to help confirm your identity. It may also be used to keep you and our community safe by helping improve our systems for detecting fake selfies, prevent abuse such as scams, phishing and fraud and to comply with legal obligations.

To help ensure that your selfie is genuine, we use both manual review and automated systems. We may also partner with trusted service providers to check your selfie is authentic. This helps detect and prevent risks, such as impersonation.

How long we store your selfie

How long we store your selfie depends on what you’re using it for. We’ll always let you know before you provide your selfie how long it can be stored. For example, if you’re uploading an selfie to get authorized to run ads, or for Meta Verified, we will store your selfie for up to 180 days. However, for ads about social issues, elections or politics or if we detect potential fraud or abuse, this may be extended to up to 1 year.

In some cases you can adjust how long we store your selfie in your identity confirmation settings.

How to enable Advanced Protection on Facebook

Turn on Advanced Protection

What is Advanced Protection?

Email about Advanced Protection

I can’t access Advanced Protection

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Beginning May 2024, Facebook Protect is changing to Advanced Protection. Select Instagram users can now use Advanced Protection to help improve account security. Learn more about Advanced Protection on Instagram.

What is Advanced Protection?

We know that certain people in the public eye can become a target for account compromise attempts on social media platforms, including Facebook. Accounts that face increased risk may need additional protection, that’s why we created Advanced Protection. Advanced Protection helps these high-target accounts adopt stronger security protections by simplifying security features like two-factor authentication. It also provides additional security protections for people’s accounts and Pages, including monitoring for potential hacking threats.

We’re currently rolling out Advanced Protection to more and more users around the world. People who are eligible for Advanced Protection will see prompts on Facebook to learn about the program and enroll. If you are not eligible for Advanced Protection but want to help improve your account security, you can learn how to turn on two-factor authentication. With two-factor authentication, you can add additional security protections to your account by logging in using a security key, login codes from a third-party authentication app, or by getting text message (SMS) codes sent to your mobile phone.

Turn on Advanced Protection

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Password and security.
  4. Click Advanced Protection.
  5. On the welcome screen, click Next.
  6. On the Advanced Protection benefits screen, click Next.
  7. We’ll scan your account for potential vulnerabilities and make suggestions on what to fix as you turn on Advanced Protection. Common suggestions of what to fix include choosing a stronger password or enabling two-factor authentication.
  8. Click Fix Now and follow the on-screen instructions to finish turning on Advanced Protection.

How do I know if an email I got about Advanced Protection is legitimate?

If you received an email about Advanced Protection, you can confirm if we’ve sent it by checking that it came from security@facebookmail.com. Facebook will never ask you for your password in an email or Facebook message, and our Advanced Protection email notifications do not include links or buttons to turn on Advanced Protection or to log into Facebook. Be aware of phishing attempts and do not click links or open attachments unless you can confirm the sender and know the content is safe. Learn more about how to keep your account secure and how to protect yourself against phishing attempts.

I received a notification that says I’m required to turn on Advanced Protection

Some accounts with the potential to reach lots of people may require stronger security. That’s why those accounts are required to turn on Advanced Protection.

I received a notification that said I’m required to turn on Advanced Protection, I never turned it on but now the notification is gone, what happened?

Some accounts with the potential to reach lots of people may require stronger security. That’s why those accounts are required to enable Advanced Protection. In some cases, an account may fall out of eligibility for this requirement. Those accounts would no longer be required to turn on Advanced Protection, and may stop seeing a notification. In this case, you may still be able to voluntarily turn on Advanced Protection.

I can’t access Advanced Protection

We’re slowly releasing Advanced Protection to more and more users. If you don’t see a way to turn on Advanced Protection but want to improve your account security, you can learn how to turn on two-factor authentication. With two-factor authentication, you can add additional security protections to your account by logging in using a security key, login codes from a third-party authentication app, or by getting text message (SMS) codes sent to your mobile phone.

How can I unenroll from Advanced Protection?

If your account or Facebook Page has a Meta Verified subscription, you may have been automatically enrolled into Advanced Protection. To unenroll from Advanced Protection, cancel your Meta Verified subscription from the App Store or Google Play Store if you purchased it on mobile.

How two-factor authentication works on Facebook

Set up two-factor authentication

Manage my security methods

I lost my recovery codes

I can’t log in with 2FA

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you’re having trouble logging into your Facebook account, review these tips first.

Two-factor authentication is a security feature that helps protect your Facebook account and password.

When two-factor authentication is turned on, you’ll be asked to enter a special login code or confirm your login attempt each time someone tries to access your Facebook from a browser or mobile device we don’t recognize.

You can also get alerts about unrecognized logins to your Facebook account.

Turn on or manage two-factor authentication

  1. Click on your profile picture in the top right, then click Settings and privacy.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Password and security.
  4. Click Two-factor authentication, then click on the account that you’d like to update.
  5. Choose the security method you want to add and follow the on-screen instructions.

When you turn on two-factor authentication, you’ll be asked to choose one of 3 security methods:

  • Tapping your security key on a compatible device.
  • Using login codes from a third party authentication app.
  • Using text message (SMS) codes from your mobile device.

You can get 10 recovery login codes to use when you’re unable to use your phone.

Learn how to set up Facebook login recovery codes.

Security tips for two-factor authentication

  • If you haven’t saved the browser or mobile device you’re using, you’ll be asked to do so when you turn on two-factor authentication. When you do this, you won’t have to enter a security code when you log in again. (Note: Don’t click Save this browser if you’re using a public computer that other people can access.)
  • We need to be able to remember your computer and browser information so we can recognize it the next time you log in. Some browser features block this. If you’ve turned on private browsing or set up your browser to clear your history every time it closes, you may need to enter a security code each time you log in.
  • For text message (SMS) two-factor authentication, you can either add a new mobile number or use a number that’s already been added to your account. Learn about how Facebook uses your mobile number for two-factor authentication.
  • Create a passkey for an easier and more secure way to log into your account.

Learn what to do if you have trouble logging in with two-factor authentication.

Protect your personal and business account from malicious software designed to steal your login information

My account was hacked

Scan my device for malware

What are signs of malware?

What to do after malware?

Visit our Newsroom to learn about how Meta works to counter business-targeted malware and how to protect your accounts.

Bad actors can use malicious software – or malware – to try to compromise online accounts across the internet. They often use deceptive tactics to trick people into clicking on malicious links or downloading malicious files and software.

Malware is typically designed to obtain sensitive information, like login and passwords to their various online accounts, and it can target a range of devices – from mobile phones to computers. Threat actors can even hide their malware by posing as web browser extensions or trendy apps available in official app stores.

Malicious hackers sometimes target people’s social media accounts in an attempt to later gain access to Business and Advertising accounts they might be connected to in order to run unauthorized ads as part of a scam or spam operation.

By knowing what suspicious signals to look out for, you can better identify these threats and keep your accounts and business secure.

Identifying Malware

Threat actors typically disguise malware within innocent-looking files, as well as mobile apps or browser extensions available in official app stores. They latch onto popular topics — from political news to the latest tech and business productivity tools — to hide malware and trick people into installing it.

If you observe unusual behavior on your device or online accounts, this might be a sign that you may have inadvertently downloaded malware. Here are some telltale signs to look for:

  • Suspicious activity on your online accounts that you did not authorize, including financial charges.
  • Your device runs significantly slower or frequently freezing.
  • New toolbars, icons, or tabs appear in your browser that you don’t recognize.
  • Scammy pop-ups appear in your browser.
  • Shorter device battery life.

What to do if you think you have been affected

If we believe your account has been affected by malware, we may send you a warning message to help you secure your account. While there is a chance that this is a false alarm, we want to alert you so that you can take precautionary steps to protect your account and any Business or Advertising accounts associated with it. Because malware is typically downloaded outside of our platforms, we may not always catch every single instance.

If you believe you’ve downloaded a malicious software, we recommend that you delete it from your device immediately and use the following instructions to secure your account:

Scan personal devices

We recommend scanning any and all devices you use to access Facebook. If you don’t remove potential malware, cyber attackers may continue to have access to your accounts and devices.

To help you scan and clean your personal devices, we suggest using independent antivirus/antimalware tools from third-party providers such as:

  • ESET Free Online Scanner
    • Windows - Free online scanner
  • ESET Smart Security Premium
    • Windows, Mac, and Android - Free 30-day trial
  • Bitdefender’s Total Security
    • Windows, Mac, iOS, and Android - Free 30-day trial

For all other devices, please scan using reputable and trusted antivirus products. New malicious applications are developed constantly, so it is important to keep this software up-to-date and scan your computer regularly. We recommend that you enable “automatic” scanning of files in your Antivirus software.

Scan corporate devices

If you believe your corporate device may be impacted, we suggest reaching out to your company’s IT department for support.

Review your web browsers

We recommend reviewing each of your browsers. If you don’t remove potential malware, cyber attackers may continue to have access to your accounts and devices.

You can remove most malware on your web browsers by following these steps:

  • Remove suspicious browser add-ons.
  • Review recent changes to your web browser settings.

Additional security tips and recommendations

  • Enable two-factor authentication to add an extra security layer to your account. Two-factor authentication is one of the most effective tools for combating these account compromise applications.
  • Reset your password. Never reuse your password across multiple websites.
  • Turn on log-in alerts so you’re notified if someone is trying to access your account.
  • Review your previous sessions to be sure you recognize which devices have access to your account.
  • Enable business notifications so you’re alerted of any changes to your Meta Business Manager account.
  • Use the Security Checkup Tool to help secure your account.

Recover a hacked Facebook Page you manage

My Page was hacked

Recover my Page

I can’t submit the form

Check what was accessed

Who this is for: This article is for you if you manage a Facebook Page and someone took control of it by hacking or scamming you or another admin.

Learn what to do if you’re looking for help with a hacked Facebook personal account, including accounts with pro mode turned on.

We take account access very seriously. If you can’t access a Facebook Page you manage or notice unexpected activity, it might be because you or another admin was hacked or scammed. For example:

  • A hacker might have stolen your password, logged into your personal account, added themselves to your Page, then removed your access to the Page.
  • A scammer might have tricked you into giving them control of your Page and removing your access. This might have happened in Business Manager or Meta Business Suite.

Submit this form to recover your Page

The best thing to do is submit this form to request Page recovery. We’ll take a look and update you by email. We aim to reply within a day, but some reviews may take longer.

Keep in mind:

  • If you have Meta Verified or access to other support, we still recommend submitting this form. It’s the fastest way to recover your Page.
  • We can only take action on your report if we can confirm that the Page was compromised.

After regaining access to your Page:

  • If we locked your account for security, open Facebook and follow the prompts to unlock your account.
  • Look through your Page and business portfolio and undo any changes you don’t recognize.
  • Turn on Advanced Protection or take other steps to keep your account secure.
  • Be aware of scams and phishing.

If you can’t submit the form

You can only submit the form if you’re logged in and recently lost access to a Page.

Here’s what to do if you can’t submit the form, depending on your issue:

  • If you don’t see the form: Try logging in first.
  • If you can’t log in: Visit Hacked (facebook.com) on a device you’ve used to log into Facebook before.
  • If the form doesn’t let you select a Page: This is because we don’t see that you’ve recently lost access to your Page. Try accessing your Page again.
  • If you’re helping someone else: Have them log in with their account then submit the form. If they can’t log in, have them visit Hacked (facebook.com) on their usual device.

Note: You may have also lost access to your Page if you’re not the authorized representative of the Page’s subject or content, or if your Page was reported and removed for going against the Community Standards.

What to do if your account was hacked

If your Facebook account was hacked, we recommend visiting Hacked (facebook.com). If you can, use a device you’ve used to log into Facebook before.

If you’re helping someone else, make sure they try these steps on a device they’ve used to log into Facebook before.

Signs that you may have been hacked

  • Your profile picture has been changed.
  • There are posts, comments, or messages that you didn’t write.
  • You’re having problems logging in or your two-factor authentication method (example: your authentication app) isn’t working.
  • You received a message or notification from Facebook telling you that someone is trying to log in or has already logged in, and it wasn’t you.
  • You received an email from Facebook telling you that an email address or mobile phone number was added or removed from your account, or that your password was changed, and it wasn’t you.
    • If the email associated with your Facebook account has changed, you can reverse this. When an email is changed, we send a message to the previous email account with a special link. You can click this link to reverse the email change and secure your account.
    • If you receive an email from Facebook, you can check to make sure it’s really from us.
    • Learn how to recover your Facebook account if you can’t access your email address or mobile phone number.
  • In the Where you’re logged in section of your Settings, you see a device or location you don’t recognize. If this happens, you can select the device and log it out.

Protect your account

Learn how to keep your account secure to prevent it from being hacked again.

About Marketplace messages

What are Marketplace messages?

How does AI use my messages?

Why am I not getting replies?

What is a meetup plan?

To help people have a good experience on Marketplace, Meta provides features to encourage safe, respectful, responsive Marketplace chats, which are designed to connect buyers and sellers to discuss commerce content. Information from Marketplace chats, including messages, may be automatically reviewed and used to improve safety, and to provide, improve and personalize your Marketplace experience, subject to applicable law. This only applies to Marketplace messages and will not impact your personal messages on Messenger. For example, Meta uses AI to power or assist you with various Marketplace messaging features. When you or others use these AI features for Marketplace messages or content in your chats, that content is shared with Meta AI in order for Meta AI to respond. This means people can share your Marketplace messages with Meta AI. You can learn more about personal messages and other types of messages on Messenger.

For example:

  • If a seller has not responded to multiple messages within a certain timeframe, buyers may receive a notification that the seller is unlikely to respond to them, and be shown options to see similar listings or message the seller anyway. The seller may be shown a reminder to update the listing.
  • When a seller is in advanced discussions about an item with a buyer, other interested buyers may receive a notification that the seller may be slow or unlikely to respond. They’ll be given options to browse similar listings or make an offer to the seller anyway.
  • AI can help sellers respond. For example, if a seller receives multiple messages from multiple buyers about the same listing, Meta AI can help the seller bulk reply to all buyers who have similar questions. When a seller initiates the “bulk reply” feature, Marketplace message content is shared with Meta AI in order for Meta AI to respond.
  • If a buyer or seller creates a meetup plan, we may utilize AI to recommend the time, date and location of the meetup using information from the message thread. When a user initiates the “create a meetup plan” feature, Marketplace message content is shared with Meta AI in order for Meta AI to suggest the time, date and location of the meetup.
  • If a buyer enlists AI’s help in a message thread, we may utilize AI to recommend questions that the buyer can ask the seller using information from the message thread. When a buyer initiates this feature, Marketplace message content is shared with Meta AI in order for Meta AI to respond.
  • To help keep Marketplace safe and better protect you from scams and suspicious activity, Meta may review content and related data in Marketplace messages, such as who is sending you messages or the location of the sender. Meta may notify you if something suspicious is detected, and in some cases, remove accounts immediately for scam activity.

To help determine when to show these features, Meta uses metadata (information about a message, such as the date and time it was sent) about messages sent between sellers and buyers on Marketplace. We may also use a limited detection of keywords in some Marketplace chats.

These features help remind Marketplace users to be responsive and respectful to others, inform buyers about listings they’re interested in, and remind sellers to update listings that may no longer be available, making the Marketplace experience more efficient for all users. You can learn more about information we may use in our Privacy Policy.

Note: Some of the experiences listed in the examples above are available in some jurisdictions and not others.

About access to prepaid shipping labels

Prepaid shipping labels are offered by Marketplace to select sellers. In some cases, we may remove a seller’s access to prepaid shipping labels, as per our Seller Agreement. This may happen when a seller has shipped a high volume of orders with prepaid shipping labels that incorrectly state the weight or size of an item sold.

This may occur when:

  • The weight of the shipped package was more than the weight entered when creating the listing. Be sure to enter the accurate weight of an item when creating a listing.
  • For USPS prepaid labels, the package dimensions are larger than USPS allows (greater than 12in x 12in x 12in in size (L x W x H)).

If you lose access to prepaid shipping labels on Marketplace, you can arrange for local pickup with buyers.

Starting January 1, 2022, we’ll ask you for your tax information, such as your Social Security Number (SSN) or Individual Tax Identification Number (ITIN), if you haven’t provided it to us already. This helps us meet our obligations to the IRS and ensures that you’ll be able to continue using your account and access features to accept payments for sales on Marketplace.

The following summarizes the tax information we’ll ask from you:

  • Last 4 digits of your SSN or full ITIN
  • Full 9 digits of your SSN or ITIN once your sales with checkout on Marketplace reach $499

We need to collect your tax information to comply with applicable laws and regulations. This information will be verified by our payment processor, PayPal. Your tax information won’t be visible or shared on Facebook.
