Where is my refund?

Items purchased with checkout on Facebook are subject to the seller’s return policy. To see the specific return policy for an item, check the Shipping & Returns section of the product page.

For orders with multiple items, you’ll need to request a return for each item separately.

How do I return an item I purchased from a shop on Facebook?

Note: Shops on Marketplace will no longer be available starting December 1, 2023.

To return an item you purchased from a shop on Facebook:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & Privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Scroll down and click Orders and payments.
  4. Below Activity, click your order.
  5. Click Return Order and follow the on-screen instructions.

Once a return is requested, we encourage the seller to review the request and respond via email in a timely manner. Sellers are responsible for handling returns on time, accepting or closing returns and issuing refunds, and appropriately following the returns policy stated in the product listing. If the seller agrees to accept your return, follow their return instructions.

Some sellers may automatically accept your return request. If your request is automatically accepted, the seller will send the return instructions to your email.

How do I return an item I purchased from an individual seller on Facebook?

To return an item purchased with checkout from an individual seller on Marketplace, you must contact the seller to see if they are willing to accept a return.

You can then send the seller a message with details of the issue and why you would like to return the item. If the seller doesn’t respond within 3 days, you can reach out to Facebook for support.

To contact the seller:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & Privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Scroll down and click Orders and payments.
  4. Below Activity, click your order.
  5. Click Contact seller for help and follow the on-screen instructions.

If the seller has accepted your request for a return, you’ll be sent a return shipping label to the email address you entered at checkout, or you may need to provide your own label depending on the seller. Once you have your return shipping label, you will need to print it, attach it to the package and drop the package off at the correct carrier within 3 business days.

Note: Returns and refunds for items purchased with local pickup on Marketplace are not available from Facebook.

About scams on Facebook Marketplace

Report a scam

What are payment scams?

What are phishing scams?

If you see something you think is a scam, you should stop communicating with the buyer or seller and report the suspected scam to Facebook. Learn more about how to avoid scams in the Scam Protection Center.

Scams on Marketplace can happen to both buyers and sellers. Some listings may also be scams. Scams come in different forms, so it’s important to know what scams are, and how to recognize them when buying and selling on Marketplace.

Communicating with a buyer or seller

When talking with a buyer or seller, you should avoid:

  • Communicating with buyers or sellers privately outside of Facebook and Messenger. This may look like:
    • Buyers or sellers requesting you contact them by a method outside of Facebook or Messenger – such as WhatsApp, phone, text or email – especially early in your conversation. Conversations that are routed off of Facebook or Messenger make detecting scams difficult to track.
    • Requests to contact other individuals (example: relatives of the seller) that are not the true owner of the Facebook account.
    • Users contacting you about a Marketplace listing outside of Marketplace
  • Messages or emails directly from the seller telling you that there was something wrong with your payment.
  • People that push you to move quickly to complete a sale, or pressure you to complete the sale immediately. This can be an attempt to get around any normal safe practices.

Payment scams

When dealing with payments, you should:

  • Use trusted payment services.
  • Ask to see valuable items in person before sending payment.
  • Be careful with fake emails that appear to be from payments apps like Zelle or Venmo asking you to take some type of action before you can accept payment. This may look like an email telling you to upgrade your account or pay a fee.
  • Always check your account to confirm payments.
  • Never pay for an item in advance. Avoid sellers who request payment before providing the item.

Common payment scams include:

  • Buyers sending you screenshots of payments—requesting that you send them the item(s) because they’ve already paid. You should never trust screenshots of payments as confirmation.
  • Buyers claiming they’ve accidentally overpaid you and requests that you refund them the overpayment.
  • Buyers offering to pay more than the asking price, and pretending to overpay for the item(s). Scammers may say the overpayment is for third-party movers to deliver the item(s), which can be a sign of a scam.
  • Buyers requesting refunds without actually paying. Avoid giving refunds before checking your account to confirm payment.
  • Payment requests asking you to pay with a gift card.

Phishing scams

A form of identity theft that gets you to volunteer personal information without you realizing what’s happening. These attacks come from people who want to use your information for their own dishonest benefit, such as hacking your Facebook, email or bank account.

This may look like messages or emails that ask you to provide:

  • Verification codes sent to your phone or email (example: two-factor authentication code, such as Google Voice Code).
  • Account information (example: email address and password).
  • Personal information or passwords. Someone sending you a link that requires you to log in with a username and password is likely a scam.

Other types of phishing include:

  • Link manipulation: These messages contain a link to a phony site that looks like the official business.
  • CEO fraud: These messages are sent to trick you into believing that the CEO or other executive is asking you to transfer money.
  • Smishing: Using SMS messages, attackers try to trick you into going to phony sites from your smartphones.
  • Off-platform link scams: Sellers may try to provide you with a link to another site to try and trick you into providing sensitive information, such as credit card or banking details and other personal identification information. Never share this type of information with another person under any circumstances.

Additional tips for buyers

  • Double-check deals that seem too good to be true. Be cautious of listings that are significantly underpriced compared to market value. Scammers may try to use underpriced items to lure buyers into a scam to purchase defective or fake items.
  • Do not send deposits for high value items (apartments, cars, etc.) without confirming that they’re real first. When possible, try to confirm the existence and ownership (example: a pink slip for a car) of the item(s) in person or over a video chat before sending payments.
  • Always verify the tracking numbers that you see on Marketplace on the shipping company’s website, and make sure that the delivery address and shipping information is correct.
  • Review the seller’s profile to learn more about the seller. On their profile, you can see ratings and reviews from other buyers, friends you may have in common, view their other listings, and review their Marketplace activity.
  • Eligible purchases made with checkout on Facebook are covered by Purchase Protection. Items exchanged in-person using cash or other person-to-person payment methods are not eligible.
  • When buying in person, before completing the transaction, be sure to inspect the items closely to make sure that they are real, in the expected condition and work properly.

Acceptable forms of identification for seller verification on Facebook Marketplace

What documents are accepted?

My ID was rejected

I changed my name

What is proof of address?

Some shipping features are not available to all eligible sellers.

We need to collect your tax information to comply with applicable laws and regulations. This information won’t be visible or shared on Facebook.

Proof of Identity

Documents must include information such as first and last name, date of birth, issuance and expiry date, as well as the document ID number. The name on this document must match the name you’ve registered on your Facebook Marketplace profile.

Acceptable Proof of Identity documents are:

  • Passport or passport card
  • Driver’s license (front and back)
  • State or Government Issue ID (front and back)

Unacceptable documents:

  • Military IDs
  • State medical cards
  • Student cards
  • Expired, partial or obscured documents

If you’ve recently changed your name and the information on your identity document doesn’t match the information on your account, you may have to provide additional documentation to show the name has changed.

Proof of Address

A proof of residence document that confirms where you live. This document must show both your full name and residential address. We can only confirm physical addresses, not PO Box addresses.

Acceptable Proof of Address documents are:

  • Utility bill (Dated within last 12 months)
  • Cell or landline phone bill (Dated within last 12 months)
  • Motor vehicle registration (Dated within last 12 months)
  • 401k/Brokerage Statement (Dated within last 12 months)
  • Copy of Grant Deed on Home or Lease Agreement for Home
  • Bank or credit card statement (Dated within last 12 months)
  • Identity card or driver’s license with physical address listed (must be current)

Unacceptable documents:

  • Envelopes
  • Military IDs
  • Invoices, receipts, all waybills
  • Expired, partial or obscured documents

Proof of SSN/ITIN

A document that confirms your 9-digit Social Security Number (SSN)/Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), assigned by the Internal Revenue Service or Social Security Administration.

Acceptable Proof of SSN/ITIN documents include:

  • Social Security Number card
  • Letter from IRS assigning SSN or ITIN
  • 1099 Form (Dated within last 12 months)
  • Employer-issued W2 (Dated within last 12 months)
  • Paystub with complete SSN (Dated within last 12 months)
  • 3rd party prepared tax documents (Dated within last 12 months, and signed by 3rd party preparer)

Unacceptable documents:

  • Envelopes
  • Self-completed applications
  • Self-prepared tax documents
  • Expired, partial or obscured documents

If you don’t have access to any of these documents, you can go to your local Social Security Office and request a letter which will confirm your Social Security Number.

Learn what you can do if you’re having trouble verifying your identify and why you need to verify your identity when you set up shipping on Facebook Marketplace.

What happens if I appeal?

Prevent Purchase Protection claims

Some shipping features are not available to all eligible sellers.

Sellers can either accept the decision from a Purchase Protection claim, or appeal the claim and decision that’s in the buyer’s favor. If you disagree with the decision and plan to appeal the claim, make sure you submit the appeal within 10 days from your first notification. The refund amount is the full price of the item, tax and shipping fees.

Note: Purchase Protection applies only to items purchased with checkout and shipping.

How do appeals for sellers work?

  1. When a Purchase Protection claim has been decided against you, you’ll receive a notification.
  2. Within 10 days of the first notification, you’ll need to accept or appeal the claim.
  3. After explaining why you’re appealing the claim, we’ll review the appeal and make a decision.

In reviewing your claim, Facebook may review order details, including tracking information and listing description, messages sent between you and the seller, and supporting documents.

Block someone on Facebook Marketplace

Block someone on Marketplace

Block a buyer or seller

Unblock someone on Marketplace

What happens when I block?

If you think someone has violated our Commerce Policies or Community Standards, please report them.

Before you block a profile

Keep in mind that when you block a profile that’s messaging you on Marketplace, you are blocking that profile on Facebook. When you block a profile on Facebook:

  • You can’t see each other’s listings on Marketplace.
  • You can’t send each other any new messages.
  • You and the profile you block can still see any messages sent before you blocked them.
  • Buyers and sellers will still be able to see ratings and reviews, even from profiles that they’ve blocked.

Block someone’s profile

Once you block a profile or Page, certain actions will be limited, such as interacting with each others’ timelines, posts, comments or messages. This doesn’t include apps, games or groups you both participate in. If you currently are connected with that profile or Page, blocking it will unfriend, unlike and unfollow it.

If you have additional Facebook profiles, you’ll need to manage blocking from each of your profiles separately.

You can learn more about how to unblock a profile or Page.

Block a profile or Page

You can block someone directly from their profile or Page:

  1. Go to the profile or Page you want to block.
  2. Click Options.
  3. Click Block, then confirm that you want to block them by clicking Confirm.

You can also block a profile or Page by going to your Blocking settings:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. In the menu, click Blocking under Audience and visibility.
  4. In the Block profiles and Pages section, click Edit.
  5. Click Add to blocked list.
  6. Type the name of the profile or Page you want to block.
  7. Click Block next to their name.
  8. Click Confirm.

Note: If you’re having trouble finding the profile you want to block, you can try using an email associated with the Facebook profile.

What happens when you block a profile or Page

When you block a profile or Page, that profile or Page won’t be able to:

  • See posts from the profile you blocked it from.
  • Tag the profile you blocked it from in posts, comments or photos.
  • Invite the profile you blocked it from to events or groups.
  • Start a conversation with the profile you blocked it from.
  • Add the profile that you blocked it from as a friend.

Other things to consider when you block a profile

  • If you don’t want to unfriend a profile but you want to see less of that profile’s posts on Facebook, you can take a break from that profile.
  • The profile you block from will not be able to do things such as:
    • Start a conversation with the profile you blocked.
    • Add the profile you blocked as a friend.
  • If you block someone’s profile from more than one of your profiles, the person you blocked may be able to figure out that you own all of those profiles.

Remember that blocking someone may not prevent all communications or interactions (example: in apps or groups). Learn more about what you can see when you block someone’s profile.

When you block someone who has more than one profile

  • Blocking one of their profiles only blocks that profile. It doesn’t block their other profiles. This means that you may still interact with their other profiles.
    • For example, you may start a conversation with those other profiles or add them as a friend.
  • When you block someone’s profile, this will limit some of the ways they can interact with you from their other profiles.

Remember these things

  • If you block a profile and then unblock it, you’ll need to send that profile a new friend request. If you block a Page and then unblock it, you’ll need to follow that Page again.
  • Profiles and Pages won’t be notified when you block them.

How do I block a profile from a Marketplace conversation?

Unblock a profile

When you unblock a profile or Page, that profile or Page will be able to see your posts on Facebook that you share with the public. An unblocked profile won’t automatically become your friend on Facebook, and you won’t automatically like or follow a Page you unblock. If you want to become friends with a profile you’ve unblocked, you’ll need to send a friend request to that profile. When you unblock a nickname in a Facebook group, you will be able to see their content in that group, and they’ll be able to tag you and interact with your content in the group.

Note: If you unblock a profile or Page, you won’t be able to block it again for a few days. This waiting requirement does not apply to blocking nicknames.

Unblock a profile or Page on Facebook

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. In the left column, below Audience and visibility, click Blocking.
  4. In the Block profiles and Pages section, click Edit.
  5. Click See your blocked list.
  6. Click Unblock next to the profile or Page you want to unblock.
  7. Click Confirm to finish unblocking the profile or Page.

What is Brand Rights Protection?

If your listing on Marketplace wasn’t approved, it may have gone against our Commerce Policies. Learn how to appeal a listing that wasn’t approved.

Brand Rights Protection is a tool that allows brands to identify and report content that misuses their intellectual property. It provides an interface for brands to identify trademark violations, counterfeit products and copyright infringement across many of our platforms. Learn more about Brand Rights Protection, including how to apply.

Another way we promote confidence for buyers and sellers is to inform people selling for business purposes that the law in certain countries (such as Germany, Austria and Switzerland) requires them to provide information about their identity, including their name, street address, email, registration number and/or VAT number. If you’re not sure if this requirement applies to you, you may wish to seek the advice of a qualified attorney with local expertise.

Keep in mind that Brand Rights Protection allows brands to search for certain types of content including ads, Marketplace listings, and more. For other content posted on Facebook, rights owners can protect their intellectual property by reporting infringement through our existing tools.

Buying and selling electronics on Facebook Marketplace

Tips for selling electronics

Tips for buying electronics

Avoid Marketplace scams

Here are some tips you may want to consider when you’re buying or selling electronics on Marketplace (example: phone, tablet, video game console).

Tips for selling electronics on Marketplace

  • Clear your personal information from the device to help protect your privacy. If you aren’t sure how to do this, ask the device manufacturer, or search online for help information about removing your personal data.
  • Write down the device’s serial number in case you need it later. If you aren’t sure how to find your device’s serial number, ask the device manufacturer or search online for help information about it. For mobile phones, you may want to find the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number.
  • Be clear about the condition of the item. Take and upload as many high-quality photos as you can. We also suggest including details about any issues or flaws, and if the item is new or used. You can always edit your listing to change the description or add photos.
  • List the actual price you’re asking for the item. Setting the price as $1 or another too-low price can be confusing or misleading for buyers, and goes against our Commerce Policies.
  • Get to know the person you’re selling to by visiting their Marketplace profile. You can see their profile picture, any ratings they’ve received from other buyers and sellers, and when their Facebook account was created.
  • After the sale is complete, mark the item as sold and rate the buyer to help other people who are considering buying or selling to them on Marketplace.

Meetup plan not working

When meeting a buyer and seller from Marketplace in person to complete a transaction, we recommend arranging your meeting in a public, well-lit area and letting a trusted friend or family member know where you’re headed.

You can create a meetup plan and share this plan with Facebook friends in Messenger. Whoever you choose to share your plan with will receive the location, time and date of when you’re planning to meet.

Create a meetup plan

  1. From your Messenger thread with the buyer or seller, tap More options.
  2. Tap Create meetup plan.
  3. Select the method and add the time of your meetup. You can also include the location or add notes.
  4. Tap Send plan to share the plan in your chat with the buyer or seller.

Share your meetup plan

  1. From your Messenger thread with the buyer or seller, tap Share plan on the meetup plan.
  2. Use the search bar or scroll down to find the person in your Facebook friends list you want to share the plan with.
  3. Tap Send next to their name. If you no longer want them to receive the plan, tap Undo.

You can also share your meetup plan by tapping More options at the top of the Messenger thread, then tapping Share plan.

Meetup plans are removed from the Messenger thread with your friend or family member after the scheduled meeting time.

Note: Creating and sharing a meetup plan is currently only available for local pickup transactions. You cannot create or share a meetup plan for an order made with checkout and shipping.

Customer data shared with sellers who use checkout on Facebook

What data do sellers receive?

What payment info is shared?

Is my credit card number safe?

For items purchased with checkout that require shipping, the seller may receive the following information that may be used for order fulfillment, advertising and analytics purposes:

  • Buyer’s first and last name
  • Email address
  • The delivery address entered at checkout
  • Purchase information, including the items that were purchased, the price of the items and any other details required to complete the order

Sellers only receive this information after the buyer places an order, and the seller accepts an order from a buyer.

About payment information

  • When using checkout, no one can see your whole credit card number or PayPal password on Facebook after you enter it, even with your Facebook password.
  • Only you can see your payment and transaction history. Your activity, such as payments or purchases, will not be shared with your friends or to your profile or Feed, unless you choose to share it.
  • We use encryption to protect your payments and keep your credentials secure. Learn more about how Facebook protects your payment information. You can also add or remove a payment method from your Facebook account.

Delete my Marketplace listing

I can’t delete my listing

What happens to my listing?

You can delete a listing on Marketplace if:

  • The listing is single-quantity, available and in stock.
  • The listing is multi-quantity and has never received an order.
  • The listing isn’t waiting to be accepted or declined.
  • A label hasn’t been generated for the listing.

You can’t delete a listing on Marketplace if:

  • An order for the listing is pending or waiting to be accepted or declined.
  • A label has been generated for the listing.
  • The listing has sold.

Delete your Facebook Marketplace listing

  1. From your Feed, click Marketplace.
  2. Click Selling in the left menu.
  3. Click Your listings.
  4. Click Options on the listing you want to delete.
  5. Click Delete, then click Delete again.

Note: If you’ve enabled the Checkout with shipping option, please keep in mind that listings with active orders can’t be edited or deleted. If the listing has an order that’s pending, waiting to be accepted or declined, or has been shipped or sold, it can’t be edited or deleted.

Facebook Marketplace tips for meeting in person

Stay safe on Marketplace

Share my meeting plan

Report suspicious activity

If you notice any signs of suspicious activity, immediately cancel the transaction and report the listing or person. Call local authorities if necessary.

To help promote your safety, we encourage you to review the following tips for meeting a buyer or seller in person, in addition to using your best judgment:

Share carefully

  • Be cautious when communicating with the other person.
  • Keep your home address private.

Plan accordingly

  • Share your meeting plan with a trusted friend or family member. You can tap Send plan in Messenger to send your meeting plan to someone in your Facebook Friends list so they know the location, time and date of when you’re planning to meet. Plans are removed from the Messenger thread with your friend or family member after the scheduled meeting time.
  • Do not change the meetup location once it’s agreed upon.
  • Bring a fully charged mobile phone with you.
  • Save local authorities’ phone number in your speed dial.
  • Notify the other person if you’re running late or on your way.
  • Carry minimal cash.
  • You can find a local law enforcement agency near you in the United States from the USACOPS directory

Meeting up

  • Follow local laws and directives.
  • If you’re meeting someone in person, we recommend arranging your meeting in a public, well-lit area.
  • Create and share your meeting plan with a trusted friend or family member through Messenger.
  • Use a live location sharing app or function on your mobile phone to share your location with a family member or friend during your scheduled meetup.

Consider delivery options for items

  • Some Marketplace items are eligible for shipping. This means that you can buy and sell items from all over the United States, not just near your location. The seller directly ships items to the buyer. Learn about the different ways to buy and sell.
  • If shipping isn’t available for an item, you can use a pick-up or drop-off service that works for you.

Read more tips for staying safe on Marketplace, or learn how to report someone on Marketplace.

How long do my Facebook Marketplace listings stay active?

Why was my listing deleted?

You can keep your listings on Facebook Marketplace for as long as you are actively selling the item. However, to help keep Marketplace relevant and up to date, listings that have been inactive for 2 years or more may be deleted.

If your listing is deleted due to inactivity, the listing details (such as the title, description, photos, and price) will be permanently removed from Facebook and cannot be recovered. You can download your Marketplace information at any time through the Download Your Information tool in your Facebook settings.

How to keep your listing active

If you want to keep a listing active for longer than 2 years, you can simply renew or edit the listing. Renewing your listing or editing any part of it will reset the 2-year timeframe.

To renew or edit your Facebook Marketplace listing:

  1. From your Feed, click Marketplace.
  2. Click Selling and then Your listings in the left menu.
  3. To renew a listing, find the listing and then click Renew.
  4. To edit a listing, click and then click Edit listing.
  5. Make your changes, then click Update.

Note: If your listing was boosted as an ad, the ad data may be retained separately according to our advertising policies, but the original Marketplace listing will still be deleted if it has been inactive for 2 years.

How are ratings calculated?

Buyer and seller ratings can only be provided from the Facebook app for iPhone or Android, not from facebook.com or Facebook Lite.

To share your feedback and help build a better community on Marketplace, you can rate buyers and sellers you’ve interacted with. Buyer ratings are ratings buyers receive from sellers. Seller ratings are ratings sellers receive from buyers.

Buyer ratings are only visible on the Facebook mobile app for iPhone or Android. They are not visible when you visit facebook.com on a computer or if you use the Facebook Lite app. Seller ratings are visible in the seller’s profile on all platforms, except on Facebook Lite, where the seller’s rating is visible on the product details page.

Note: We do not verify whether users have purchased the product or used the service they are reviewing or recommending on Marketplace.

About buyer and seller ratings

Your ratings may become public once you receive 5 or more eligible ratings. This may include both the seller and buyer ratings you receive. Anyone who can see your Marketplace profile will be able to see your ratings.

If you see a post on Facebook that suggests someone has an eating disorder

Report a post about eating disorder

How to support a friend?

What not to say to a friend?

Contact eating disorder support

We worked with the National Eating Disorders Association and Dr. Nancy Zucker, Associate Professor of Psychology and Neuroscience at Duke on the following answer.

If a friend posted something that suggests they may have an eating disorder and need help, we ask that you report the post to us so we can reach out to them and offer support. Please note that we’ll remove content that promotes or encourages eating disorders. You can visit our Community Standards to learn more.

You can also offer support. Here are some tips about what you should — and shouldn’t — do if you think your friend may be struggling with an eating disorder:

Do:

  • Check in with your friend about how they’re feeling. For example, you could say, “How have you been doing lately? I’m always happy to listen if there’s anything you need to talk about.”
  • Use “I” statements. For example, you could say, “I’m concerned because you didn’t eat breakfast and lunch.”
  • If your friend doesn’t want to share or says there’s no reason for you to be concerned, let them know that you care and will be happy to listen if they ever need to talk.
  • Spend time with your friend to show that you care about them (example: talk, watch a movie).
  • Set an example with your own life. Also, don’t make negative comments about your own or other people’s appearances.
  • If your friend says they’re not doing well, ask them if they’ve considered talking with a counselor, doctor, nutritionist or other health professional. For example, you could say, “I don’t know if this will help, but have you considered talking to a doctor about this?” You can also suggest that they take a free, anonymous online assessment to help them understand their risk of an eating disorder.

Don’t:

  • Use accusatory “you” statements, like “You’re not taking care of yourself.”
  • Place shame, blame or guilt on your friend about their appearance or actions.
  • Give simple solutions, like “If you’d stop dieting, everything would be fine!”
  • Expect to cure your friend.

For more information about eating disorders, contact the National Eating Disorders Association:

  • L (l.facebook.com)
  • 1-800-931-2237
  • info@myneda.org

Learn about Shop Pay

What is Shop Pay?

What data is shared?

What is the Shop app?

Shop Pay is now available as a payment method in Meta Pay when checking out from participating sellers on Facebook.

Shop Pay is a payment method offered by the commerce platform Shopify. People can save their email address, phone number, payment credentials and shipping address in Shop Pay for use in future transactions.

When you choose to check out with Shop Pay, your payment method and shipping info from Shop Pay will be used to complete your order.

Learn about payment methods available in Meta Pay.

What is Shopify?

Shopify is a commerce platform that provides tools for sellers to manage, market and grow their business. Many sellers use Shopify to power their shop on Facebook.

What is the Shop app?

Shopify also offers the Shop app, which allows people to manage and track orders made with Shop Pay. When you check out with Meta Pay using Shop Pay as a payment method, you can manage and track your orders in both the Shop app and in Meta Pay.

What data is shared with Shopify?

When you check out on Facebook using Shop Pay as a payment method, information about your purchase (including your order details and order tracking info) is shared with Shopify. Shopify may use your purchase info to improve its products and services according to its terms and policies, including to:

  • Provide you with services like order tracking and payment status updates
  • Recommend products, sellers and services in the Shop app

Meanings of item conditions on Facebook Marketplace

What does ‘Used (like new)’ mean?

What does ‘Refurbished’ mean?

What does ‘Used (fair)’ mean?

When you list an item for sale on Marketplace, you can choose the condition that best describes your item. If the condition is specified, buyers can see it on the listing.

  • Condition: New; Meaning: Brand new, never worn or used, undamaged item. Ideally in the original package (if original package isn’t a plastic bag or handmade item).
  • Condition: Used (like new); Meaning: Excellent condition, but has previously been worn or used. No signs of wear or defect.
  • Condition: Used (good); Meaning: Minor signs of wear. Item is operational and works as intended.
  • Condition: Used (fair); Meaning: Some signs of wear and tear or minor defects. Item is still usable as intended. Includes items from households with animals or smoking (example: potential hair, stains, or smell).
  • Condition: Refurbished; Meaning: Has gone through a refurbishing process. Refurbishing processes usually include inspecting the product, replacing any parts that don’t work, cleaning and repackaging.

I got scammed

If you see something you think is a scam, you should stop communicating with the buyer or seller and report the suspected scam to Facebook. Learn how to avoid scams on Facebook Marketplace.

Report a seller scam

  1. From your Feed, in the left menu, click Marketplace.
  2. In the left menu, click Buying.
  3. Click the listing of the seller you want to report as a scam.

Report a buyer scam

  1. From your Feed, in the left menu, click Marketplace.
  2. Click Selling.
  3. Click Seller dashboard.
  4. Click a listing the buyer purchased.
  5. Click the message between you and the buyer. If you can’t find the message, click See More.
  6. Click More options, then click Report.
  7. Click Scam, then follow the on-screen instructions to submit your report.

Report a listing scam

  1. From your Feed, in the left menu, click Marketplace.
  2. Click the listing that you want to report as a scam.
  3. Below the listing title, click Options.
  4. Click Report Listing, then click Scam.

I can’t sell in a group

Groups focused on buying, selling or promoting products are subject to our Commerce Policies and may have different features available for admins.

You must be an adult, based on the laws in your country, in order to buy, sell or see listings in a Facebook buy and sell group (example: at least 18 years old in the United States or at least 20 years old in Thailand). If you’re not an adult, you can still participate in the group, outside of listings.

You can only sell things in groups that have the buy and sell feature added. You must be an admin of the group to add the buy and sell group feature.

Sell something in a Facebook buy and sell group

  1. Go to facebook.com/groups and select your group.
  2. Click Sell Something.
  3. Click Item for Sale, Vehicle for Sale, Home for Sale or Rent or Sale event below Create new listing.
  4. Enter the details about the item you’re selling and click Next.
  5. Choose your audience. To help more buyers see your item, you can:
    • Post the item in other buy and sell groups you’re a member of. Click next to the name of a group to add or remove that option.
    • Create a Marketplace listing for the item. Click next to Marketplace to add or remove that option. Keep in mind that if you’re posting as a Page, you won’t see the option to create a listing on Marketplace.
  6. Click Post.

Manage your posts

Learn how to edit or delete your group posts, or mark your posts as sold. Keep in mind that you’ll need to edit or delete each post in different buy and sell groups separately, even if they’re for the same item. If you created a Marketplace listing for the item, you’ll also need to edit the Marketplace listing separately.

Note

  • Items like animals, drugs, weapons, counterfeits and other items that infringe intellectual property rights aren’t allowed in buy and sell groups or on Marketplace.
  • You must be an adult, based on the laws in your country, in order to buy, sell or see listings in a Facebook buy and sell group (example: at least 18 years old in the United States or at least 20 years old in Thailand). If you’re not an adult, you can still participate in the group, outside of listings.

Groups focused on buying, selling or promoting products are subject to our Commerce Policies and may have different features available for admins.

You must be an adult, based on the laws in your country, in order to buy, sell or see listings in a Facebook buy and sell group (example: at least 18 years old in the United States or at least 20 years old in Thailand). If you’re not an adult, you can still participate in the group, outside of listings.

Anyone can see listings posted in public buy and sell groups and Marketplace. They may also see listings posted in public buy and sell groups in their Feed.

Buy and sell group admins can’t help resolve shipping issues. If you are having trouble with an item that was shipped, contact your buyer or seller or Facebook Support.

Sell something with shipping in buy and sell groups

From the buy and sell group you want to list your item(s) in:

  1. Click Sell something at the top.
  2. Choose Item for sale.
  3. Upload all item photos, starting with the main photo, by clicking Add photos. You can upload up to 42 photos per listing.
  4. Enter the item information you want to include in the appropriate boxes, labeled:
    • Title
    • Price
    • Category (Required for shipping)
    • Condition
    • Description
  5. Click Next at the bottom of your screen.
  6. Click Location at the top of your screen to select your location.
  7. Click Delivery method to select your preferred delivery method.
  8. If the listing category you’ve selected is eligible for shipping, click Shipping & local pickup if you want to offer both shipping and local pickup options, or click Shipping only if you only want to offer shipping for your item.
  9. Click Set Up shipping at the bottom of your screen.
  10. Enter your:
    • Legal first name
    • Legal middle name (If applicable)
    • Legal last name
    • Zip Code
  11. Click Save.
  12. Confirm your legal name. You must enter your legal name to receive payments. The name you provide for payments is only visible to you. If the name displayed is incorrect, click Edit name to make any necessary changes.
  13. If the name displayed is correct, click Confirm.

To receive payments for your shipped orders, you need to add your:

  • Date of birth
  • Address
  • Bank information

You can complete this at any time before you ship your first order.

Tips for using Door Drop Off or Pick Up on Facebook Marketplace

How to use Door Drop Off?

How to use Pick Up?

Contactless Marketplace tips

Dropping off and picking up items helps you avoid interacting with people directly.

Plan carefully

  • Be sure to communicate timing, address and item placement details ahead of time. Consider sharing your meetup plan with a friend or family member or bringing a mobile phone with you. Learn more about buying and selling safely on Marketplace.
  • For local transaction listings, if the seller has chosen how they prefer to meetup (example: door pickup, door dropoff or public meetup), the preference(s) will be shown on the listing. If not, you can send the seller a message asking their preference.

Verify items

  • If you’re buying an item, make sure it’s what you want before paying for it. For high-value items (example: watches, luxury bags), you can request a certificate of authenticity or proof of purchase.

Clean and disinfect items

  • Clean and disinfect any item you intend to sell.
  • If you buy an item, make sure to clean it before bringing it into your home.

Use online payment methods

  • Consider using digital payments services to request money or pay for your items.
  • Buyers and sellers can offer person-to-person payment methods (example: PayPal).
  • If you choose to pay electronically using wire transfer or money order solutions, avoid payment links and log in directly through the payment method’s website.
  • Keep in mind that cashier and certified checks can be counterfeit. Transactions are between the buyer and seller only, and no third-party guarantee should be involved.

Protect your privacy

  • Don’t share your financial information (example: PayPal login and password, bank account info) with buyers or sellers.
  • If you’re selling electronics, make sure you’ve cleared any personal information from the device.

Compare prices before buying items

  • We encourage buyers to compare prices before buying an item.

Don’t buy or sell recalled items

  • In many places, it’s illegal to sell recalled items. If you’re unsure whether the item you’re buying or selling has been recalled, look on the website of the item’s manufacturer for this information.

Watch out for counterfeit items

  • It’s illegal to sell counterfeit items in most countries, and counterfeits aren’t allowed on Facebook. We recommend that you review any items you buy to make sure that they’re genuine. Learn more about counterfeit items.

Be cautious when buying or selling cars

  • Double-check deals that seem too good to be true. Scammers may try to use underpriced items to lure buyers into a scam. Before purchasing a car, you can check Kelley Blue Book or other trusted sites to have an idea of what you would expect to pay for a similar car.
  • You can also try getting a vehicle history report and arranging a car inspection before buying.
  • If you’re a seller, be careful about bouncing checks from buyers or paying for fake transportation or insurance costs for your vehicle. Learn more from the Federal Trade Commission (in the U.S.) or your local government agency about getting the vehicle’s history and steps for used car shopping.

Use a spreadsheet for multiple listings on Facebook Marketplace

Upload multiple listings

Spreadsheet template

My spreadsheet upload failed

What columns do I need?

When you sell something on Facebook Marketplace, you create a public listing that can be seen by anyone on Marketplace and in Feed, search and other places on or off Facebook. All listings on Marketplace and buy and sell groups must follow our Commerce Policies.

From your computer, you can use a spreadsheet or Comma Separated Values (CSV) file to upload multiple items to Marketplace at once, by using our template or uploading your own. This is a text file that contains information about the items you’re listing. You can also choose to add listings manually.

Programs like the ones listed below, can be used to create and edit spreadsheets.

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Google Sheets
  • iWork Numbers

Spreadsheet Help

What should I include in my spreadsheet?

Your spreadsheet should include:
  • Column Title: Title; Value Required: String; Column Description: This is the title of your listing.
  • Column Title: Price; Value Required: Number; Column Description: This is the price of the items in your listings. This will be rounded to the nearest whole number.
  • Column Title: Description; Value Required: String; Column Description: This is a description of the items in your listings.

Why did my spreadsheet fail to upload?

You can use a Comma Separated Values (CSV) file or spreadsheet to upload multiple items to Marketplace at once. We provide a template to make this easier for you.

Though we provide a template, it’s important to remember that you:

  • Should save your file as a CSV after editing. You can only upload CSV files to list multiple items at once. Uploading a file that is not a CSV, will stop you from uploading your file to Marketplace.
  • Should not remove or replace the headers in the CSV file. This will cause an error and stop you from uploading your file to Marketplace.

Note:

  • Providing as much information as possible in the CSV file makes the upload process easier.
  • We will try to predict the category of your listings based on the title and description you enter in the CSV file. If the predicted category is incorrect, from the listings screen, you can click on each row to make changes.

What influences the order of posts in your Facebook Feed

How is my Feed ordered?

Prioritize friends in Feed

Manage what I see in Feed

To help connect people to the posts that matter to them most, we use a process called ranking. Feed ranking creates a personalized and diverse stream of posts from the people, news sources, businesses and communities you’ve connected with on Facebook.

What influences ranking

Some things influence ranking more than others, and some of the most important factors include:

  • How you engage with posts you see on Facebook (for example, whether you like, comment or share them).
  • If the type of post is something you often interact with (example: photo, video, link).
  • The number of comments, likes, reactions and shares a post receives from the people and Pages that see it. Keep in mind that these posts are shared by the friends, groups or Pages you follow.
  • How recently something was posted.

Some things have a smaller influence over what you see. We may take into account signals such as how fast your internet connection is right now or what kind of phone you’re using (because this can affect how quickly things can load on your Feed). These are just some of the thousands of signals that may be considered for Feed ranking. Learn more about how personalized Feed ranking works.

Why some friends and Pages are prioritized

Certain friends and Pages are prioritized in your Feed based on your activity on Facebook or if you’ve added them to Favorites. Their posts are shown higher in your Feed. Certain factors that have more influence for who is prioritized include, for example:

  • Your past interactions on posts of friends or Pages, like reacting to or commenting on a photo or video.
  • Things you have in common, like mutual friends or groups you both belong to.

Many other factors also influence who is prioritized. The friends and Pages that are prioritized on Feed can change based on your activity on Facebook.

Only you can see who is prioritized in your Feed. You can control whose posts are prioritized even higher on your Feed by adding them to Favorites.

Manage what you see

You can control what you see from your Feed preferences or check your privacy settings. Some of the options for managing what you see in your Feed include:

  • Select a person or Page to add to Favorites.
  • Snooze a person, Page or group.
  • Hide or unfollow posts from people, Pages or groups.
  • Select Interested or Not interested on a post to temporarily increase or decrease its ranking score.

See what influences the order of posts you’re seeing in your Feed

  1. Go to the post.
  2. Click Options in the top right and select Why am I seeing this post?

What it means if your Facebook Marketplace access is at risk, limited or suspended

My Marketplace access is limited

My Marketplace access is suspended

Remove my Marketplace warning

Why can’t I access Marketplace?

Marketplace isn’t available to everyone right now.

We may limit or suspend your Marketplace access if you break our Commerce Policies. When you come close to having your access suspended, we’ll warn you that your access is at risk.

If your listing is rejected, you may have the option to:

  • Request a review. If we find that we made a mistake, we’ll restore your listing.
  • Remove your warning. If this is the first time you’ve broken a rule, and depending on the rule(s) you broke, you may be able to remove the warning that your access is at risk. However, your listing(s) that led to the warning won’t be restored.

Check your Marketplace status

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Click and select Profile status.
  3. Select Marketplace below Extra features.

Remove your warning

If this is the first time you’ve broken a rule, and depending on the rule(s) you broke, you may be able to remove the warning that your access is at risk.

  1. Open the Facebook app on a mobile device.
  2. Go to your profile.
  3. Tap and select Profile status.
  4. Select Marketplace below Extra features.
  5. Select Fix it now then Request review and follow the instructions.

You’ll be prompted to read about our policies and what they mean to avoid issues on your account later. You’ll also have a chance to share what you think happened (example: “I didn’t know about the rules”) to help us continue to improve our products and policies. However, your listing(s) that led to the warning won’t be restored.

What to do if you see a stolen item on Facebook Marketplace

Report a stolen item

Contact law enforcement

What to share with police?

Selling stolen items isn’t allowed on Marketplace and goes against our Commerce Policies.

If you see an item on Marketplace that you think was stolen, we recommend that you:

  1. Report the listing to us.
  2. Contact your local law enforcement to file a police report.

Report the listing

Learn how to report a listing on Marketplace. Make sure to select Appears to be stolen.

After you report the listing, we’ll send you an email with links to the listing and the seller’s Facebook profile. We’ll send the email to the email address associated with your Facebook account.

Contact local law enforcement

When you contact your local law enforcement to file a police report, you may want to share:

  • Screenshots of the listing and/or seller profile
  • Links to the listing and seller profile from the email we sent you
  • Any messages you received from the seller In California, you can also report items that you believe are stolen directly to the California Attorney General’s office.

Learn more about how Facebook works with local law enforcement.

What to do if your Facebook Marketplace listing is rejected

My listing was rejected

Request a review

Why was my listing rejected?

My Marketplace access is limited

We may reject your listing if we find that it doesn’t follow our Commerce Policies or Community Standards. For example, we might reject a listing for being a counterfeit item.

Your Marketplace access may be limited or suspended if you break our Commerce Policies. When you come close to having your access suspended, we’ll warn you that your access is at risk.

If your listing is rejected, you may have the option to:

  • Request a review. If we find that we made a mistake, we’ll restore your listing.
  • Remove your warning. If this is the first time you’ve broken a rule, and depending on the rule(s) you broke, you may be able to remove your warning if your access is at risk. However, your listing(s) that led to the warning won’t be restored.

You can also learn about Marketplace listing rules to avoid having your listings rejected and access suspended.

Request a review

To request a review:

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Click and select Profile status.
  3. Select Marketplace below Extra features.
  4. Click See what happened or See issue and select the listing.
  5. Click Request review.

If you don’t see an option to review, it may be because:

  • It’s been more than 180 days since your listing was rejected.
  • You already requested a review.
  • A review isn’t available for the rule you broke.

Find out why your listing was rejected

To find out why your listing was rejected:

  1. Go to your profile.
  2. Click and select Profile status.
  3. Select Marketplace below Extra features.
  4. Select Your listings.
  5. Click the listing(s) below Needs attention.
  6. Click See details.

We review listings when our systems detect a potential violation or when someone reports them. Listings that do not comply with our policies are rejected. If your listing is rejected but you see similar listings on Marketplace, you can request a review if you believe we made a mistake, or report a listing that you think violates the rules.

More information

Visit our Transparency Center to learn more about how Facebook uses technology and review teams to detect, review and take action on content.

The information in this article summarizes parts of the Commerce Policies for convenience. It is not intended to change the Commerce Policies.

Who can see your hidden listings on Facebook Marketplace

Who sees my hidden listings?

Hide listings from friends

My listings are still visible

Can’t hide listings in groups

Listings with Hide from friends turned on are still public. If you choose to hide a listing, it will be hidden from your friends on Facebook and Messenger in most cases but will still be visible to everyone off of Facebook and Messenger. All listings must follow our Commerce Policies.

Your listings can still be seen by

  • People who aren’t logged into Facebook or Messenger. For example, your friends may be able to see your listing while they are logged out of Facebook or Messenger. In addition, Marketplace listings may also appear in search results on other websites, such as Google.
  • Former friends (example: people that you’ve unfriended or have unfriended you).
  • Friends of your Facebook friends.

Your friends on Facebook or Messenger may also still see your listings if

Messenger

  • Someone shares the link to a listing that doesn’t have Hide from friends turned on, then you turn on Hide from friends after the listing is shared. In this case your friends may still be able to see a preview of your listing in Messenger.

Stories

  • You share a listing that doesn’t have Hide from friends turned on to Stories, then turn on Hide from friends after sharing the listing to your story. In this case your friends may still be able to see a preview of the listing until your story expires (up to 24 hours).

Groups

You can’t hide listings that you create in groups. You also can’t list any hidden Marketplace listings in these groups. If you list something in a group, then turn on Hide from friends on that listing, it will be removed from the group.

Renewed Listings

If you renew a listing, the Hide from friends settings from your original listing will apply. You can change this setting at any time.

Relisting Items

If you relist an item (example: after an item has sold), the Hide from friends setting will be turned off automatically. You can change this setting at any time.

Note: If you share the link to a listing with Hide from friends turned on in a post or comment, your Facebook friends won’t be able to see the listing. However, they’ll still be able to see the rest of your post or comment, such as any other text you post with the link to your listing.

Why your Facebook Marketplace order may have been canceled

Why was my order canceled?

Seller canceled my order

Order canceled, not shipped

I want to relist an item

There are few reasons why your order on Marketplace may be canceled:

  • Seller canceled the order: The seller accidentally cancelled the order or marked the item as sold. To get paid for items you’ve sold with shipping & checkout, you need to mark the order as shipped, not as sold. Learn how to enter the tracking information for your order and mark the order as shipped.

    If you didn’t mean to cancel the order, we suggest asking the buyer if they want to purchase the item again using the messages you already have open with them.

    To sell the item again, you’ll need to mark it as available. Learn how to mark an item as available.

  • Buyer requested to cancel the order: The seller cancelled the order per the buyer’s request. If the buyer didn’t mean to cancel, we suggest asking them if they want to purchase the item again using the messages you already have open with them. You can also relist the item on Marketplace and make it available to other buyers. To sell the item again, you’ll need to mark it as available. Learn how to mark an item as available.

  • Order was canceled due to not generating a shipping label and/or marking the item as shipped: When a sale is made, you have three days to either generate a prepaid shipping label or to mark the item as shipped. Our system will automatically cancel the order if it hasn’t been marked as shipped, regardless of any agreement made with the buyer.

    We suggest asking the buyer if they want to purchase the item again using the messages you already have open with them. You can also relist the item on Marketplace and make it available to other buyers. To sell the item again, you’ll need to mark it as available. Learn how to mark an item as available.

Memorialization and Deceased Accounts

About legacy contacts on Facebook

Add a legacy contact

What can my contact do?

What can’t my contact do?

Manage a memorialized profile

Choosing your legacy contact is currently only available for your main profile and doesn’t apply to additional Facebook profiles. You can choose to either appoint a legacy contact to look after your memorialized main profile or have your account permanently deleted from Facebook.

A legacy contact is someone you choose to look after your main profile if it’s memorialized after you’ve passed away. If you add a legacy contact, that person will be able to make decisions about your main profile once it is memorialized.

What your legacy contact can do

  • Write a pinned post for your profile (example: to share a final message on your behalf or provide information about a memorial service).
  • Update your profile picture and cover photo.
  • Request the removal of your account.
  • Download a copy of what you’ve shared on Facebook, if you have this feature turned on.

We may add more capabilities for legacy contacts in the future.

What your legacy contact can’t do

  • Log into your account.
  • Read your messages.
  • Remove any of your friends or make new friend requests.

Learn more about memorialization and how to add a legacy contact to your account.

If you’re a legacy contact, learn how to manage a memorialized profile.

Note: You must be 18 or older to select a legacy contact.

About Memorialized Accounts

Memorialize an account

What happens to their account?

How long does memorialization take?

Remove their account

Memorialized accounts are a place for friends and family to gather and share memories after a person has passed away. Memorialized accounts have the following key features:

  • The word Remembering will be shown next to the person’s name on their profile
  • Depending on the privacy settings of the account, friends can share memories on the memorialized Timeline
  • Content the person shared (ex: photos, posts) stays on Facebook and is visible to the audience it was shared with
  • Memorialized profiles don’t appear in public spaces such as in suggestions for People You May Know, ads or birthday reminders
  • No one can log into a memorialized account
  • Memorialized accounts that don’t have a legacy contact can’t be changed
  • Pages with a sole admin whose account was memorialized will be removed from Facebook if we receive a valid request

Learn how to memorialize or request the removal of a deceased person’s account.

Data legacy contacts can download from Facebook

What data can a legacy contact download?

What data can’t a legacy contact download?

What is a legacy contact?

In your legacy settings, you can allow a legacy contact to download an archive of information you’ve shared after your account is memorialized. In that download, a legacy contact will receive:

  • Photos and videos you uploaded.
  • Wall posts.
  • Profile and contact info.
  • Events.
  • Friends list.

Keep in mind that your legacy contact might download content that wasn’t originally visible to them.

A legacy contact will not receive:

  • Messages.
  • Ads you clicked.
  • Pokes.
  • Security and settings info.
  • Photos you automatically synced but didn’t post.

Facebook may provide access to this type of information in response to a valid will or other legal consent document expressing clear consent.

To remove a legacy contact without choosing a new one, you must select Delete After Death. Since this option deletes an account immediately and completely, we strongly suggest you share this preference with your loved ones. To un-select Delete after death, select a legacy contact.

Once Memorialization is initiated, you must always have one of the options selected. If you do not select either option, anyone within the proper documents can request to memorialize your account after you pass away.

Note: No changes can be made to memorialized accounts that do not have legacy contacts.

  • Delete a memorialized account at any time.

Legacy contacts can’t:

  • Read messages.

Memorialized accounts are a place for friends and family to gather and share memories after a person has passed away. Memorializing an account also helps keep it secure by preventing anyone from logging into it.

It’s our policy to memorialize an account for someone who has passed if a valid request is received. Learn more about what happens to a memorialized account.

Please keep in mind that we can’t provide login information for someone else’s account even under these circumstances. It’s always against Meta’s policies to log into another person’s account.

To request memorialization for a profile, please contact us.

Removing the account

Facebook friends with the correct documentation may request the removal of a loved one’s account from Facebook.

Abouts Jobs messages

Report a job scam

Avoid job scams

What are Jobs messages?

To help people have a good experience on Jobs, Meta provides features to encourage safe, respectful, responsive Jobs chats, which are designed to connect job seekers and job creators to discuss jobs content. Information from Jobs chats, including messages, may be automatically reviewed and used to improve safety, and to provide, improve and personalize your Jobs experience, subject to applicable law. This only applies to Jobs messages and will not impact your personal messages on Messenger. For example, Meta uses AI to power or assist you with various Jobs messaging features. When you or others use these AI features for Jobs messages or content in your chats, that content is shared with Meta AI in order for Meta AI to respond. This means people can share your Jobs messages with Meta AI. You can learn more about personal messages and other types of messages on Messenger.

For example

  • If a job creator has not responded to multiple messages within a certain timeframe, job seekers may receive a notification that the job creator is unlikely to respond to them, and be shown options to see similar job listings or message the job creator anyway. The job creator may be shown a reminder to update the job listing.
  • When a job creator is in advanced discussions about a job with a job seeker, other interested job seekers may receive a notification that the job creator may be slow or unlikely to respond. They’ll be given options to browse similar job listings or message to the job creator anyway.
  • AI can help job creators respond. For example, if a job creator receives multiple messages from multiple job seekers about the same job listing, Meta AI can help the job creator bulk reply to all job seekers who have similar questions. When a job creator initiates the “bulk reply” feature, Jobs message content is shared with Meta AI in order for Meta AI to respond.
  • If a job seeker or creator attempts to set up an interview or collect additional information off-platform, we may utilize AI to recommend time, date and location of suggestions using information from the message thread. When a user initiates the “create a meetup plan” feature, Jobs message content is shared with Meta AI in order for Meta AI to suggest the time, date and location of the meetup.
  • If a job seeker enlists AI’s help in a message thread, we may utilize AI to recommend questions that the job seeker can ask the job creator using information from the message thread. When a job seeker initiates this feature, Jobs message content is shared with Meta AI in order for Meta AI to respond.
  • To help keep Jobs safe and better protect you from scams and suspicious activity, Meta may review content and related data in Jobs messages, such as who is sending you messages or the location of the sender. Meta may notify you if something suspicious is detected, and in some cases, remove accounts immediately for scam activity.

To help determine when to show these features, Meta uses metadata (information about a message, such as the date and time it was sent) about messages sent between job creators and seekers on Jobs. We may also use a limited detection of keywords in some Jobs chats.

These features help remind Jobs users to be responsive and respectful to others, inform job seekers about job listings they’re interested in, and remind job creators to update listings that may no longer be available, making the Jobs experience more efficient for all users. You can learn more about information we may use in our Privacy Policy.

Note: Some of the experiences listed in the examples above are available in some jurisdictions and not others.

How active status works on Facebook and Messenger

Turn off active status

My active status is off

Troubleshoot active status

Green dot on Pages

Active status shows when you’re active, currently in the same chat or were recently active on Facebook or Messenger on this profile. Your active status shows to people you’re connected to on Facebook and Messenger, and to people you’ve sent friend requests to.

Learn how to turn your active status on or off. You can also block someone to stop sharing your active status with them.

When your active status is on

  • Your connections and people you’ve sent friend requests to across Facebook and Messenger who also have their active status on will see a green dot or timestamp next to your profile picture that shows when you were last active on the profiles you have active status turned on for. They’ll also be able to see if you’re currently in the same chat as them on this profile.

When your active status is off

  • You won’t see other people’s active status.
  • If you turn off active status for one app, you may still appear active on a different app that doesn’t have it off. For example, if you turn off active status for your Facebook app but not for your Messenger app, people may still be able to see your status on Messenger. If you don’t want to show your active status, turn it off wherever you’re using Messenger or Facebook.

Troubleshoot active status

Keep in mind there may be a delay between when someone becomes active or recently active and when they’re shown as active or recently active. If you are still having issues with active status, you can try these tips to troubleshoot your Facebook app:

  • Close then reopen your Facebook app.
  • Update your Facebook app.
  • Check your Internet connection.

If you cannot see someone else’s active status, it may be because:

  • That profile has turned off their active status.
  • That profile has blocked you.

Understanding the green dot for Facebook Pages

Facebook Pages that have been online recently, or have a record of being quick and responsive in their replies to messages on Facebook, Messenger, or WhatsApp will have a green dot.

This is different from the green dot you see for a person’s active status, which is why you may see a green dot on a Facebook Page even when your own active status is off.

How Meta processes messages in the European Economic Area

How Meta processes messages

Marketplace messages in EEA

Threads messages in EEA

What is Directive 2002/58/EC?

Meta previously informed users of changes to Meta’s messaging services in the EU, because of new laws applying to some of Meta’s messaging services.

In the European Economic Area, the Directive 2002/58/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 July 2002 concerning the processing of personal data and the protection of privacy in the electronic communications sector determines how providers of messaging services can process messages and related metadata.

Marketplace and Threads messaging are product features within Facebook Marketplace and Threads respectively, rather than standalone messaging services, and they are not subject to the Directive 2002/58/EC. Meta processes Marketplace and Threads messages, for example, to protect the integrity of its services and keep users safe. Meta may also use these messages to maintain and improve the automated measures it deploys to protect the safety, security and integrity of its services.

I was warned for sending spam or harassing messages on Facebook

Why was I warned?

What is considered spam?

What is harassing behavior?

I was warned by mistake

It’s against our Community Standards to send spam or engage in harassing behavior. If you received a warning that you were sending spam on Facebook, you may have:

  • Sent friend requests to people you don’t know in real life.
  • Posted or shared something too quickly or too often in a short amount of time.
  • Tagged or messaged people who aren’t your friends.
  • Sent someone a message or link that they marked as unwelcome.
  • Contacted people for commercial purposes without their consent. If you’d like to use Facebook for your business, you should create a Facebook Page.

Navigate messages on Facebook using a screenreader

How do I navigate messages?

How do I use heading structure?

How do I use ARIA landmarks?

Heading Structure

Facebook.com/messages includes the following headings to make navigation with a screen reader easier:

  • H2 Heading (1 of 2): A heading with the text Conversation List that marks the start of your list of conversations.
  • H2 Heading (2 of 2): A heading containing the names of the people in the current conversation or the title of the conversation if you’ve named it. It marks the start of the main content.
  • H3 Heading: A heading in the main content with the text Messages. It marks the start of the messages that are shown for the current conversation.
  • H4 Heading: Headings in the message region containing a date or timestamp. Each one marks the start of a block of messages in the current conversation that began at the specified date or time.
  • H5 Heading: Headings in the message region containing the name of a participant. Each one marks the start of a block of messages in the current conversation from the specified person.

ARIA Landmarks

Facebook.com/messages includes the following landmarks to make navigation with a screen reader easier:

  • Conversations Navigation: The left side of the page, which includes a list of all of your conversations. Activating a link to a conversation in this list will display it in the main content.
  • Main Navigation: The main content, which includes information, past messages and the message composer for the currently displayed conversation.

I can’t remove a message

You can permanently remove a message that you’ve sent for everyone in the chat, or just for yourself.

If you select Remove for You, other people in the chat will still see the messages in their chat screen.

If you select Unsend for Everyone, people included in the chat won’t be able to see the removed message. Keep in mind that people you sent a message to may have already seen your message and can still report the conversation.

  2. Open a conversation.
  3. Hover over or put your cursor on the message and click Options.
  4. Click Unsend.
  5. Select Unsend for everyone or Unsend for you.
  6. Click Remove.

If you think a removed message you’ve received goes against our Community Standards, you can report it. Learn how to give feedback on or report a conversation in Messenger.

You can set your Page’s messaging status to away for up to 12 hours. Learn how to create an away message for your Page that’s automatically sent to people who message your Page when your Page’s messaging status is set to away.

Note: Messages received when your Page is away aren’t included in your Page’s response rate or response time.

Learn how to automatically set your Page’s messaging status to away when your business is closed.

If you have Facebook or task access to a Page, you can set your Page’s messaging status to away.

Set your Page to away with Facebook access

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all Profiles, then select the Page you want to switch to.
  3. Click Messenger in the top right of Facebook.
  4. In the top right of your Inbox, click Available.
  5. From the dropdown menu, click Away. You can also choose to Edit away message and schedule.

Set your Page’s messaging status to away with task access

  1. From your Feed, click Pages in the left menu.
  2. Below the Page you want to manage, click Manage Page and then click Meta Business Suite.
  3. In the left menu click Inbox.
  4. In the top right of your inbox, click Available.
  5. From the dropdown menu, click Away. You can also choose to Edit away message and schedule.

Turn instant replies to Page messages on or off

Instant replies not sending

Edit instant reply message

Turn off instant replies

You must have Facebook or task access to a Page to turn Instant Replies on or off for a Page. You can log into Meta Business Suite to manage Page messages.

Instant replies are messages sent automatically as your Page’s first response to new messages. For example, you can use your instant reply message to let customers know that you’ll get back to them soon or to thank them for contacting your Page.

Note: Instant Replies aren’t sent when your Page’s messaging status is set to Away and aren’t included in your Page’s response rate or response time.

Turn on instant reply for your Page with Facebook access

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. At the top right of your Feed, click Messenger.
  4. At the top of your Inbox, click Automations.
  5. In the top right, click Create automation.
  6. In the left menu, click Greet people.
  7. Select Instant reply, then in the bottom right click Create automation.
  8. At the top, next to Instant reply, click Toggle to turn instant replies on.
  9. Select a Channel and enter your instant reply below Message.
  10. In the lower right, click Save changes.

Turn off instant reply with Facebook access

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. At the top right of your Feed, click Messenger.
  4. In the left menu below Meta Business Suite, click Inbox.
  5. At the top, click Automations.
  6. Scroll down to Your automations, then click Toggle next to an automated message to turn it on or off.

Unable to send messages on Facebook

I’m blocked from sending messages

Why can’t I reply?

Troubleshoot message errors

How to avoid message blocks?

This is about using messages on Facebook. For help with the Messenger app, visit the Messenger Help Center.

If you see an error message saying “You can’t reply to this conversation,” it might be because:

  • A message or something you shared goes against our Community Standards.
  • You recently sent an unusual number of messages, which may seem like spam to our security system.
  • Messages you sent were marked as unwelcome.
  • You blocked the person you’re messaging or they blocked you.

We understand you may not have known about our standards or meant to send unwelcome messages. If you’re blocked from sending messages, remember:

  • This block is temporary.
  • You can still connect with your confirmed friends through the Facebook app or www.facebook.com while you’re in this block by leaving comments on posts, posting on your profile or using other Facebook features.
  • If you can’t send messages, you may also be temporarily blocked from sending friend requests.

To avoid blocks like this in the future, you can:

  • Review our Community Standards to understand what kind of sharing is allowed on Facebook.
  • Only message people and businesses you already know.
  • Use the name you go by in everyday life to help the people you’re messaging recognize you.

Troubleshoot technical issues

If you see an error message saying “This message didn’t send” or “Unable to connect to Facebook,” it may be because of a technical issue. Try the following:

  • Check your internet connection. Test to see if other websites are working.
  • Update your Facebook app to the latest version.
  • Update your browser. We recommend using the latest version of one of these web browsers.
  • Close your Facebook app and restart your device.
  • Make sure the person you’re messaging hasn’t deactivated or deleted their account.
  • Make sure you haven’t blocked the person you’re messaging or they haven’t blocked you.
  • If you’re replying to a group chat, make sure the other members haven’t left the chat.

If you’ve completed the steps above and are still unable to send messages, report the problem to let us know more about the issue.
