Use text messages (SMS) for two-factor authentication on Facebook

Set up 2FA with SMS

I’m not getting SMS codes

Turn off SMS 2FA

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you’re having trouble logging into your Facebook account, review these tips first.

When you turn on two-factor authentication, you’re asked to choose either a security key, text message (SMS) codes or a third-party authentication app as your primary security method. If you choose to use text message (SMS), you’ll be sent a text message (SMS) with a special 6-digit security code each time someone tries logging into your Facebook account from a mobile device or browser we don’t recognize.

Note: Please make sure you are viewing your personal profile before starting the steps below.

Turn on text message (SMS) codes for your mobile device

  1. Click on your profile picture in the top right, then click Settings & privacy.
  2. Click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Password and security.
  4. Click Two-factor authentication, then click on the account you’d like to update.
  5. Click Text message (SMS), then click Next.
  6. Select a phone number already on your account, or add a new phone number, and click Next.

Note: Not everyone will be able to access this setting in Meta Account or Accounts Center at this time. If these steps don’t work for you, try this:

  1. Go to your Security and Login Settings.
  2. Scroll down to Use two-factor authentication and click Edit.
  3. Click Text message (SMS) when you’re asked to select a security method and follow the on-screen instructions.
  4. Once you’ve turned on text message (SMS) codes, you should also set up a second security feature, such as a security key, trusted contacts or recovery codes. This helps to protect you in case your mobile phone is lost, stolen or hacked.

Other Useful Resources

  • Text message (SMS) security codes used for two-factor authentication are always 6 digits long.
  • To set up text message (SMS) two-factor authentication, you can either use a mobile number that’s already been added to your account or add a new number. Learn more about how Facebook uses a mobile number added for two-factor authentication.
  • If you’re not receiving your text message (SMS) verification codes, you may have turned off text messages from Facebook. Learn how to turn text messages (SMS) back on.
  • If you want to turn off text message (SMS) codes and use a different security method for two-factor authentication instead, you’ll need to have have a third-party authentication app turned on or a security key added to your account to do this.
  • You can disable text message (SMS) verification codes by clicking or tapping Turn off next to the mobile phone number you want to stop using. If you don’t have a third-party authentication app turned on or a security key added to your account, turning off your mobile phone number will also turn off two-factor authentication.
  • You can turn back on text message (SMS) codes for a mobile phone by clicking or tapping Use two-factor authentication, then Text message. Click or tap on the mobile phone number you want to start using again and follow the on-screen instructions.
  • Learn more about managing two-factor authentication settings.
  • Learn about what you can do if you turned on two-factor authentication but are now having trouble logging in.

Note: Facebook doesn’t charge you for using text messages (SMS) for two-factor authentication. However, your mobile provider’s standard rates for sending and receiving messages still apply.

What happens when you block messages from someone’s profile while using Facebook

Block messages from someone

What happens when I block?

Unblock messages from someone

Messages on Facebook appear in Facebook Chat. They’re not comments on posts, or posts on a profile or page.

When you block messages and calls from someone’s profile, they can’t:

  • Chat with you on your Messenger app or Facebook Chat. You won’t receive messages or calls from the profile you’ve blocked.
  • Receive messages or calls from your Messenger or Facebook profile to their profile.

When you block messages and calls from someone’s profile, they can still:

  • See your profile on Facebook.
  • Leave comments on your posts, or post on your profile.
  • See your messages if you’re both in the same group conversation. If you and the profile you block are in a group conversation together, you’ll be notified before you enter the conversation.

What is branded content on Facebook and how do I know if someone is sharing a promotional message?

What is branded content?

How to identify branded content?

Branded content vs. ads

Branded content policy

Branded Content is marketing through the creation of content that is funded or produced by an advertiser. For example, an influential fashion blogger might be paid by a sponsor to create a video that endorses the sponsor’s new clothing line and share it on their Page, or a travel publisher might be paid by an airline to post a video featuring their airline that talks about tropical destinations.

Branded Content requires disclosure to people to notify them that the content is commercial in nature. Facebook provides tools to help our publishers, creators and advertisers with their disclosure obligations. Keep in mind, you are responsible for compliance with relevant laws and regulations, including by ensuring that you provide all necessary disclosures to people using Facebook or Instagram, such as any disclosures needed to indicate the commercial nature of content posted by you.

If a Page uses Facebook’s tools to disclose branded content, the post will be specially marked:

  • With [Page sponsor name] in the post if a sponsor’s Page is being featured in the branded content.
  • With Paid Partnership below the post title.
  • With at the top right, which if selected, provides details about the partnership.

Branded content on Facebook generally must follow Facebook’s relevant policies including our Branded Content Policy and Pages, Groups, and Events Policy.

Keep in mind, branded content is different from advertising on Facebook, where a Page pays Facebook to promote its own post to people. This content shows Sponsored below the Page name. A post with branded content can also be an ad, but not all branded content posts are ads.

If you’re a Page owner, you can learn more about branded content in the Business Help Center.

You got a suspicious email or message claiming it’s from Facebook

Report a fake email

Check if email is from Facebook

My account was phished

What is a phishing email?

Facebook will never ask you for your password in an email or send you a password as an attachment.

Scammers sometimes create fake emails that look like they’re from Facebook. These emails often look like:

  • Notifications about friend requests, messages, events, photos and videos.
  • False claims that you went against our Community Standards, and if you’re a business, that you aren’t in compliance with Meta Advertising Standards, the Commerce Policies, and other policies and terms.
  • Warnings that something will happen to your account if you don’t update it or take a certain action.
  • Claims or offers that sound too good to be true (such as winning a Facebook Lottery.)

Here are some ways to check if an email is really from Facebook.

If an email or Facebook message looks strange, don’t open it or any attachments. Instead, report it to phish@fb.com or through the report links that appear throughout Facebook. If you’re a business, go to Business Support Home to help verify if there are any issues with your business accounts. Learn more about Business Support Home.

Learn what to do if someone sends you a message that makes you uncomfortable and about what to do if you get contacted by someone who says they’re a Meta representative.

Meta AI and Avatars

About Admin AI on Forum

What can Admin AI do?

How Admin AI saves time?

Admin AI recommendations

Forum is currently available for some people in the US, so it may not be available to you yet.

Admin AI is like an assistant for managing your groups on Forum. You can ask Admin AI questions about your groups, brainstorm ideas together, and even have it do things for you.

What Admin AI can help you do

  • Get group insights: View engagement metrics, growth trends, popular topics, and top-performing posts.
  • Manage content moderation: Review pending posts and reported content, and approve or decline posts.
  • Handle membership requests: Review pending member requests, and approve or decline them.
  • Automate tasks using Admin Assist: Get recommendations on what group management tasks to automate using Admin Assist. Work together to set-up, update, or delete Admin Assist criteria.
  • Improve group settings: Get recommendations for your group description, rules, privacy settings, and group photo.
  • Create content: Get post ideas, draft posts, and create member spotlights based on what’s trending in your group.
  • Get answers to questions about groups: Learn how to use admin features, set up post approval, manage badges, and more.

Why use Admin AI

Managing a group can be time-consuming, especially as your community grows. Admin AI helps you:

  • Save time: Get a prioritized overview of what needs your attention, and quickly see what your group is talking about to inspire posts.
  • Make informed decisions: Get data-driven recommendations tailored to your group’s specific context and needs.
  • Improve group health: Receive proactive suggestions for moderation rules, engagement strategies, and settings adjustments.
  • Learn about admin tools: Discover new features and best practices.

Things to know about Admin AI

  • You’re still in control — Admin AI will only take actions, like approving content or updating group settings, if you tell it to or confirm it can.
  • Admin AI uses your conversation with it, group content and activity, and group information, like group name, description, existing group settings, review queues, and admin tools, to generate its responses and recommendations.
  • Anything Admin AI posts, changes, or does at your direction is recorded in the Admin Activity Log for the group, and you can review and undo most actions at any time.

Notes

  • Similar to other chats, interactions with AI are subject to our Community Standards and Terms of Service.
  • Meta’s AI Terms apply to the feature and its use.
  • An AI’s response may be inaccurate or inappropriate and should not be used to make important decisions.
  • Meta uses your interactions with AIs in public groups to improve AI at Meta.
  • Depending on your prompt, the content generated may go against our Community Standards or Terms of Service of Meta’s platforms. Sharing AI-generated content on our platforms that goes against these standards will be treated the same as sharing other content that goes against our standards. If you share generated content that goes against our standards, your content may be removed and your account may be restricted or disabled. Learn more about the Community Standards and Terms of Service on Facebook.

Learn more about AI at Meta.

About the Meta AI support assistant on Facebook

How to use Meta AI?

Where is Meta AI?

What can Meta AI do?

The Meta AI support assistant is only available on Facebook and Instagram.

The Meta AI support assistant is here to help you with a wide range of issues on Facebook — from simple tasks, like how to tag someone in a photo, to more complex processes, like changing your password.

How to chat with the Meta AI support assistant

You can find the Meta AI support assistant in a few different places on Facebook.

From Facebook

You may also see the Meta AI support assistant pop-up while using Facebook in situations where you might need some help, for example offering support if your listing gets denied on Facebook Marketplace.

From the Facebook Help Center

To use the Meta AI support assistant from the Help Center, you need to be logged into your Facebook account on this browser.

From any page in the Facebook Help Center, you can start a chat by:

  1. Selecting “Ask a question…”
  2. Typing your question, or selecting a question from the prepopulated options.
  3. Selecting Send.

You can also choose one of the prepopulated questions at the top of any article, and it’ll open up a new chat with the Meta AI support assistant.

What the Meta AI support assistant can do

The Meta AI support assistant can:

  • Troubleshoot problems: If you’re having trouble with features, settings, or updating your password, the AI assistant can provide step-by-step instructions to help.
  • Provide information: The AI assistant can answer questions about how to use different features and help you find relevant information from the Facebook Help Center.
  • Guide you through processes: It can walk you through steps like how to appeal content decisions, or help you secure your account if you believe it has been compromised.
  • Check your account status: It can assist with checking the status of your account, such as monetization eligibility or any violations.

The Meta AI support assistant can’t directly access and edit your personal account or perform actions on your behalf without your consent.

Important information about AI support

  • AI can make mistakes: Our AI assistant is constantly learning, but it might not always get things right. If you get an answer that’s inaccurate or doesn’t seem right, please let us know by tapping or clicking Thumbs down underneath the response.
  • Your chats with support AI make it better: Your conversations with the Meta AI support assistant will help make it better.
  • We collect some info to help you: To resolve your issue, the Meta AI support assistant has access to some general information about your account like your account status, recent activity, and device type. You can learn more about information used for AI at Meta in our Privacy Center.

Why verify my identity?

Why verify my payment method?

What is a temporary transaction?

Payments in Messenger are only available on your mobile device in the US at this time.

We may ask you to verify your identity or payment method to help keep your account secure, prevent unauthorized access to your financial information, or to comply with various federal and state laws.

When you send or receive money in Messenger, we may ask you:

  • To verify your payment method if unusual activity is detected.
  • To verify your identity after you reach a certain transaction amount.

Verifying your payment method

To verify your payment method, we’ll send a temporary transaction with a verification code to your default card. You’ll need to enter that code in Messenger before you can continue sending payments.

Learn how to find your verification code.

Verifying your identity

To verify your identity, we may ask you to provide one or more of the following:

  • Your legal name (first name and last name)
  • Your date of birth
  • Your ZIP or postal code
  • Your address of residence (not P.O. box)
  • The last 4 digits of your Social Security number
  • A photo ID
  • Answers to multiple-choice questions only you would know

Facebook Pay is now called Meta Pay

Where is Meta Pay available?

How do I use Meta Pay?

Is my data collected?

As part of Facebook company becoming Meta, Facebook Pay is now Meta Pay. If you’re an existing Facebook Pay user, there is no action required on your part. All of your existing Facebook Pay information will remain the same in Meta Pay, including account details, your payment method, and settings.

If you’re a new user, learn how to get started with Meta Pay.

Where is Meta Pay available?

Meta Pay is available across Meta technologies, including Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, WhatsApp, and anywhere you see the Meta Pay button when shopping online. Meta Pay will roll out globally over time, so you may still see Facebook Pay in some places when paying.

Why is Facebook Pay now called Meta Pay?

Facebook Pay is now called Meta Pay to align with Facebook’s company rebrand to Meta.

Does the name change to Meta Pay affect existing Facebook Pay users?

There is no change to the way existing Facebook Pay users use Meta Pay. Current Facebook Pay users can use Meta Pay immediately. All existing Facebook Pay information including account details, your payment method, and settings will stay the same.

How do I use Meta Pay to make purchases going forward?

Meta Pay works in the same way as Facebook Pay. To shop, donate, and send money across Meta technologies or to make purchases using the Meta Pay button, you’ll need to have Meta Pay linked with a payment method.

If you’ve already linked a payment method to Facebook Pay, there is no action needed on your part. Your current payment method linked in Facebook Pay will be available in Meta Pay.

Are my purchases protected with purchase protection when paying with Meta Pay?

Our Purchase Protection policy has not changed. Purchase Protection is available on eligible products bought with Meta Pay on Facebook and Instagram. Purchases made from third-party sites, other messaging services, local pickups, or sending money on Messenger with Meta Pay do not qualify for Purchase Protection.

Is Meta collecting new or additional data from Meta Pay users?

There are no changes to existing data collection or data use. Learn more about Meta’s data policy.

What payment information will be stored and protected with Meta Pay?

When you make payments with Meta Pay, we’ll collect information about your purchase such as your payment method, transaction date, billing, shipping, and contact details. Your payment card numbers are encrypted and securely stored.

Fees associated with Meta Pay

PayPal fees for donations?

Fees for businesses selling?

There are no fees from Meta when using Meta Pay.

PayPal may charge fees to their users for certain types of transactions, such as processing fees for donations. There may also be fees charged to businesses that are selling items on Facebook.

Find your verification code for payments on Messenger

I can’t find my verification code

My verification code expired

My code isn’t recognized

How do I submit a manual review?

Payments in Messenger are only available on your mobile device in the US at this time.

We may ask you to verify your payment method to help keep your account secure. To verify your payment method, we’ll send a temporary transaction with a verification code to your default card. You’ll need to enter your verification code on Messenger before you can continue sending payments.

Note: Verification codes expire after 24 hours. If your code expires, you can send a new code to verify your payment method.

Find your verification code

  1. A verification screen will appear when you’re sending money on Messenger.
  2. On the verification screen, tap Send code to receive a temporary transaction on your default card.
  3. Log into your card’s online account, then go to your recent transactions.
  4. Find the temporary transaction of $1.00 with your 4-character verification code. (Example: 13AF)
  5. Once you find your verification code, enter the code on Messenger.

If you have trouble with your verification code, we recommend trying these solutions:

  • Make sure you enter your verification code correctly.
  • Enter your verification code before it expires.
  • Make sure you check the correct financial account for your verification code.
  • Make sure you’re connected to a reliable Wi-Fi network.
  • Close your Messenger app and restart your device.
  • Try using a different payment method.

If your verification code isn’t recognized after three attempts, you can submit a request for a manual review. Note: You won’t be able to send payments on Messenger while your account is under review. If you need help with your verification code or manual review, please contact our support team.

How does Purchase Protection work with Meta Pay in Thailand

How does Purchase Protection work?

What purchases are covered?

How do I dispute an order?

How do I file a claim?

This article is about Purchase Protection in Thailand. You can learn more about Purchase Protection in the United States here.

Purchase Protection is a policy that allows buyers to purchase with peace of mind when shopping on Facebook and paying in Messenger with Meta Pay. It also helps sellers build credibility and trust.

How does Purchase Protection work with Meta Pay?

Purchase Protection guarantees that eligible transactions will be refunded if buyers have problems with their order. Many purchases made with Meta Pay are covered by our Purchase Protection policies. Purchase Protection is free for buyers and sellers and automatically covers eligible purchases.

With Purchase Protection, payments to sellers will be held by Facebook until buyers mark purchases as received, or for up to 7 days after the payment has been successfully made. During this time, a buyer can dispute an order with a seller in the following situations:

  • Item not received
  • Item damaged or significantly different than described

If a buyer and seller cannot come to an agreement on a dispute, the buyer can file a claim with Facebook after 24 hours. For further details on the different situations that are covered, please read the Purchase Protection policies.

Which purchases are covered by Purchase Protection?

Purchase Protection only covers items purchased on Facebook through Messenger, which requires using Meta Pay. This means that items purchased through other apps or services are not covered. Items covered by Purchase Protection are clearly labeled in both the product details and payment pages. If the buyer files a Purchase Protection claim and it is approved by Facebook, they will receive a refund for the full amount of the purchase.

Some purchases are not covered by Purchase Protection, such as multiple items combined into one single order or items priced over ฿9,300. You can find full details for what purchases are covered and excluded in our full policy.

Is my payment info secure?

We value the trust you place in us. We work hard to prevent unauthorized access to your information.

To protect your payment information:

  • We store your financial information on secured servers.
  • We take extra steps to protect this info from hackers.

While we may share your contact or other profile information according to our privacy policy, no banking or PayPal information is shared, except as necessary when making payments or complying with legal requirements.

Facebook may store your information to prevent you from having to re-enter it for future payouts. Additionally, if you request updates to your payment information, we may retain certain evidence (example: bank information) supporting these changes.

If you’re experiencing issues or have questions about specific payments, let us know. We’ll work with you to help resolve the issue.

How Purchase Protection works on Facebook

Request a refund

My item was damaged

What is not covered?

Many purchases made with checkout on Facebook are covered by our Purchase Protection Policies. Purchases made through third-party sites, local pickups, Messenger transactions, or through other messaging services don’t qualify for Purchase Protection.

Purchase Protection is free, and automatically covers eligible orders. Purchase Protection means that you can request a refund if:

  • You didn’t receive your order.
  • The product arrived damaged or different than described on the listing (example: the condition isn’t accurate).
  • The seller didn’t follow their stated refund policy.
  • The purchase was unauthorized.
  • The seller has been removed from Facebook.

In reviewing your claim, Facebook may review order details, including tracking information and listing description, messages sent between you and the seller, and supporting documents.

Goodwill refunds are at Facebook’s discretion. If Facebook approves your Purchase Protection claim, you’ll get a refund for the full purchase price of the product and any shipping costs. You can see full policy details in the Purchase Protection Policy.

ID requirements with Meta Pay

Meta Pay ID requirements

My ID was rejected

What IDs does Meta Pay accept?

My name is different on ID

Meta Pay is a regulated financial service. One regulatory requirement is that Facebook validates your identity at certain times. Just like other financial institutions, Meta Pay needs to make sure you are who you say you are.

Please make sure that the name and date of birth on your Facebook account matches the information found on your ID so that we can re-enable your account more quickly.

Learn more about the types of IDs accepted by Meta Pay.

IDS accepted by Meta Pay

What IDs does Meta Pay accept?

My ID was not accepted

What image formats are accepted?

Types of IDs accepted by Meta Pay

  • Driver’s licenses
  • State or National IDs
  • Passports
  • Green cards, residence permits or immigration registration cards
  • Tribal identification or status cards
  • Voter ID cards

Images of your ID

To be accepted, images of your ID must be in color, have all corners showing and clearly show the following information:

  • Photograph (where applicable)
  • Name
  • Date of birth
  • Issuer (e.g. country or state)
  • Expiration date

We accept JPEG and PNG file formats for images, but aren’t able to verify PDF images. Photos must be under 5MB and 8000 pixels (width or height).

You may need to include photos of both the front and back of your ID to make sure it shows all the above requirements. The document submitted cannot be expired or altered in any way.

Making a purchase

You can use the following accepted payment methods when making a purchase from Meta for a third-party app:

  • Visa or Mastercard Credit card or Debit card

To make purchases for a third-party app from a Facebook ad

  1. Tap Shop now on the Facebook ad post that shows the item(s) you’d like to purchase.
  2. Review the details of the item(s) you’d like to purchase and tap Buy.
  3. Enter your contact and payment information if you’re new to our checkout. If you already have Meta Pay set up, select the payment method you want to pay with if you haven’t already set a default method in Meta Pay. Learn how to add or remove a payment method with Meta Pay.
  4. Check the total purchase amount, including taxes and/or fees.
  5. When you’re ready, tap Pay [amount] to make your purchase and confirm the payment. You may be asked to enter your Checkout with Meta PIN or other validation method.
  6. Next, tap Check now to confirm that your app is updated. You will be redirected to the app store to update your app if it’s required.
  7. If you’re not connected to the third-party app with your Facebook account at the time of purchase, navigate back to the activation screen and tap Activate item. You’ll be redirected to the third-party app and will be able to use your purchase.
  8. If you’re connected to the third-party app with your Facebook account at the time of purchase, your item will be activated automatically and you can begin using your purchase in the third-party app.

If you are based in the US or Canada, you are purchasing the digital item from Meta Platforms Inc (1601 Willow Road, Menlo Park, California USA 94025) for use in the relevant third-party app.

Our Terms of Sale apply to these purchases, as well as Meta’s Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, Community Payments Terms, and Payments Privacy Policy.

Meta Pay not syncing

What is Meta Pay?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Your payment information that was previously saved on Facebook or Instagram is now available in Accounts Center. This includes any payment methods or shipping info that you may have saved.

Unless you opt to separate your payment information, your payment information will remain synced across your Facebook and Instagram accounts.

With your payment information synced across accounts in the same Accounts Center, you can view and manage your payment, shipping, and contact information in one place across apps with Meta Pay.

Note: If Shop Pay or PayPal is your only payment method saved for Meta Pay, your payment methods will not be synced across accounts.

Sync or manage your payment information in Accounts Center from Facebook.com

  1. Open facebook.com on your computer.
  2. Click on your Profile Picture, select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center.
  4. Below Account settings, click Meta Pay.
  5. Click Manage.
  6. To sync your payment information across accounts when they aren’t all synced, click Manage synced payment info at the bottom.
  7. To sync your payment information across accounts when no payment information is synced, click Sync payment info at the top.
  8. From the Meta Pay screen, click on the accounts with synced or separate payment information that you’d like to manage. Note: If your payment information is synced across all of your accounts, you do not need to click into one account.
  9. From here, you can update your saved payment methods, email address, shipping address, and phone number.

Separate your synced payment information in Accounts Center from Facebook.com

  1. Open facebook.com on your computer.
  2. Click on your Profile Picture, select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center.
  4. Below Account settings, click Meta Pay.
  5. Click Manage.
  6. Click Manage synced payment info.
  7. Deselect any accounts that you want to separate your payment information from.

Please note that when you separate previously synced payment information, that payment information (including payment methods, delivery address, name, email, and payment activity) will still be accessible on the Facebook and Instagram accounts that were previously synced.

While separated, further updates to your payment information on Instagram or Facebook will not sync between each other.

Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund

Meta requires that nonprofits in the United States using key fundraising tools are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

Meta partners exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund (PPGF) for our fundraising products in the US, UK, Canada and Australia. In these markets, when you want to donate or raise money for a nonprofit, you will be donating to PPGF, which will then distribute donations to the benefiting organization.

Meta’s platforms offer an opportunity for nonprofits to reach and engage with new and existing supporters. Our partner for charitable giving, PPGF, has a robust history of helping people support their selected nonprofits.

Where we partner with PayPal Giving Fund

Meta partners with PPGF for fundraising on Facebook and Instagram in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia and Canada.

How donations are handled

PPGF receives donations benefiting nonprofits and grants funds to nonprofits, subject to their policies. All donated funds may be used by the benefiting charity on an unrestricted basis, regardless of any designations made by the donor or fundraiser creator.

PPGF payout timelines

Funds distributed by PPGF are paid out according to PPGF’s timelines. For PPGF-enrolled nonprofits, PPGF distributes funds within 45 days. For nonprofits that are not enrolled with PPGF, PPGF distributes funds by check within 45 days in the US, and 90 days in Canada, the UK, and Australia.

Transaction reports

PPGF provides donation and fundraising activity reports to nonprofits that are enrolled with PPGF. The reports provided by PPGF will include several key fields, including Payout Date, Donation Date, Program Name, Currency Code, Net Amount of the Donation, PayPal Transaction ID, donor contact info, fundraiser contact info if they decide to share with your organization,and more.

Meta provides limited transaction and fundraising reports in Nonprofit Manager, however, Meta does not issue tax documentation. Learn more about understanding and accessing Meta’s transaction and fundraising reports.

Donation receipts

PPGF provides donors with an official donation receipt that can be used for tax purposes. Meta only provides a confirmation for donations, which donors can find below their Orders and payments.

Support with fundraising tools

You can use the following forms and help pages to get support with Meta’s fundraising tools:

  • If your nonprofit wants to report an issue or provide feedback, fill out this form.
  • If your nonprofit has questions about payments from Meta, use the Facebook Payout Support form.
  • If your nonprofit is having enrollment and payout issues with PPGF, visit the PayPal Giving Fund Help Center.
  • If you have questions about fundraising tools and donations you have sent to or received from PPGF, use the fill out this form.

Payment method verification with Meta Pay

Verify my payment method

My Meta Pay PIN isn’t working

I can’t find my verification code

My CVV code isn’t working

We may ask you to verify your payment method with Meta Pay to help keep your account secure, prevent unauthorized access to your financial information, or to comply with various federal and state laws.

Verifying your payment method

When you send or receive money in Meta Pay, we may ask you to verify your payment method with one or more of the following verification methods:

  • Meta Pay PIN
  • Payment method verification code
  • CVV security code
  • Confirmation code via phone or email

Confirming a payment method with your Meta Pay PIN

For this verification method, we’ll ask you to enter the 4-digit Meta Pay PIN you may have created when setting up Meta Pay. You’ll need to enter your PIN before you can continue making payments.

Learn more about setting up your PIN with Meta Pay.

Verifying your payment method with a verification code

For this verification method, we’ll create a temporary transaction with a payment method verification code on your default card’s transaction history. You’ll need to leave Meta Pay and visit your default card’s app or website to retrieve the verification code. You’ll then need to return to Meta Pay and enter the verification code to continue making payments.

Learn more about verifying your payment method by code and finding your verification code in Messenger.

Confirming a payment method with your CVV security code

CVV is a security feature in the form of 3 digits on the back of your card to the right of the signature strip or 4 digits on the front of your card. It can also be called CSC, CVV2, CVC, or CVC2.

For this verification method, we’ll ask you to enter the CVV security code found on your credit or debit card. You’ll need to enter this code before you can continue making payments.

Confirming a payment method via phone or email

To confirm your contact details, we’ll send a 6-digit confirmation code to your phone or email. You’ll need to enter your 6-digit security code before you can continue making payments.

Learn more about keeping your information secure when using Meta Pay.

Qualifications and enrollment process for PayPal Giving Fund

Enroll with PayPal Giving Fund

What information is needed?

How long does enrollment take?

I can’t enroll my nonprofit

Meta requires that nonprofits in the United States using key fundraising tools are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

As of October 31, 2023, we partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund for nonprofits in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

As of December 16, 2024, nonprofits in the United States that are enrolled to use Meta’s fundraising tools are required to be enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund. Enrollment is free and eligibility is based on policies in each country. Learn more about enrollment eligibility.

For enrolled nonprofits, PayPal Giving Fund will distribute donated funds within 45 days. Payouts are issued at the end of the month.

For unenrolled nonprofits, PayPal Giving Fund will distribute donated funds via check within 45 days in the US, and 90 days in Canada, the UK, and Australia.

Enroll with PayPal Giving Fund

Once enrollment verification is complete, your nonprofit will be eligible to receive donations with their PayPal account.

To enroll with PayPal Giving Fund:

  1. Create a PayPal business account. If you already have a PayPal business account, go straight to step 2 to confirm it belongs to a nonprofit.
  2. Confirm the PayPal account belongs to a nonprofit.
  3. Eligible nonprofits will receive an email verifying that their nonprofit status has been confirmed with PayPal and will automatically be enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

Nonprofits will need to have these details available to sign up:

Account holder details

  • Email address
  • Date of birth
  • Home address
  • Proof of identity (passport, drivers license, identity card)

Bank account information

  • Bank statement or voided check for a bank account linked to the charity’s PayPal account

Nonprofit details

  • Registered nonprofit name and EIN
  • Registered nonprofit address
  • Website URL
  • Anticipated monthly donations
  • Organization’s IRS Tax determination letter

Profile information

  • Mission statement
  • Call to action
  • Cause area
  • Logo

For nonprofits in California:

Nonprofits in California must complete the PayPal Giving Fund enrollment form after completing steps 1 and 2 above.

What common money scams should I look out for when sending or receiving money in Facebook messages?

What are common money scams?

How to avoid money scams?

Report a money scam

What is Meta Pay?

Payments in Facebook messages are only available in the US at this time.

In the rare case there is a money scam on Facebook, cyber criminals will either create fake accounts or hack into existing Facebook accounts of people you may know. The fake or compromised accounts will then try to trick you into giving them money by sending you personalized messages.

What are common types of money scams?

Here are common money scams you should look out for when sending or receiving money in Facebook messages:

  • Romance scams: Romance scammers typically send romantic messages to people they don’t know, often pretending to be divorced, widowed or in a bad marriage. To pay for things like flights or visas, they’ll engage in online relationships in hopes of receiving money. They may use photos they’ve found online of representatives from official institutions like the military or government agencies. Their goal is to gain your trust, so the conversations may continue for weeks before they ask for money.
  • Lottery scams: Lottery scams are often carried out from accounts impersonating someone you know, or fake profiles pretending to represent an organization. The messages will claim that you’re among the winners of a lottery and that you can receive your money for a small advance fee. The scammer may ask you to provide personal information, such as your physical address or bank details.
  • Donation scams: These scams are done by accounts impersonating famous religious figures or by accounts pretending to be representatives from various charities or orphanages. In the messages, the scammers will ask for donations.
  • Inheritance scams: The scammer will claim to be a lawyer or from another legal authority, pretending to represent the estate of a deceased person. The messages will state that you’re entitled to the inheritance. The scammer may ask you to provide personal information such as your physical address or bank details.
  • Loan scams: Loan scammers send messages and leave posts and comments on Pages and in Groups offering, or claiming to know someone offering, instant loans at a low interest rate for a small advance fee.
  • Marketplace scams: Although eligible items purchased on Marketplace from sellers and stores using checkout on Facebook are covered by Purchase Protection, local pickup items using person-to-person payment methods are not covered. Facebook does not offer refunds for any person-to-person transactions. Always be cautious when using person-to-person transactions to purchase Marketplace items, especially if an item needs to be shipped. Learn how to buy and sell responsibly on Facebook. You can also learn more about the difference between buying something with checkout and local pickup.

What online behaviors should I look out for?

To protect yourself from scammers, look out for the following:

  • People asking you for money who you don’t know in person
  • People asking you for advance fees to receive a loan, prize, or other winnings
  • People asking you to move your conversation off Facebook (example: a separate email address)
  • People claiming to be a friend or relative in an emergency
  • Poor spelling and grammatical errors

Learn how we’re working to help keep you safer on our technologies.

What Meta Pay does with your payment information

What payment info is collected?

How is my payment info used?

Is my payment info shared?

How do I update payment methods?

When you use our Products to buy things or make payments with Meta Pay, we collect information about the purchase, like the items you bought, transaction date, billing, shipping and contact details, and whether you completed the transaction, as outlined in our Privacy Policy.

Your payment method (example: credit card or bank account information) will be stored in a separate, secured network. The credit card and bank account numbers you provide will not be used to personalize your experience or inform the ads we show you.

Your payment information will be collected, stored, and used to facilitate your purchases and transactions, including for renewal of your subscription products, and other products and services that you purchase in the future. Before you make a purchase, you will have the opportunity to confirm the purchase. For subscription products, you will be automatically charged on the next renewal date. You can learn more about how to update your payment methods. If you do not want your payment method stored for renewal of a subscription, you can cancel your subscription up to 24 hours prior to the next renewal date.

The purchase information we collect when you purchase a product or service you’ve requested or authorized to personalize your experience across Meta Products can be used to deliver you more relevant content and ads, to provide customer support, and to promote safety and integrity (e.g., to investigate violations of our payments policies). Your payment card and bank account numbers will not be shared with anyone for marketing purposes without your consent. Learn more about how we use information in our Privacy Policy.

When you check out using Shop Pay as a payment method, your purchase info (including your contact info and order details and order tracking info) is shared with Shopify. Shopify may use your purchase info to improve its products and services, according to its terms and policies, including to:

  • Provide you with services like order tracking and payment status updates
  • Recommend products, sellers and services in its Shop app

Learn more about Shop Pay.

Note: If you are in the European Region and subscribe to use our Products without ads, we won’t use your autofill activity to improve ads or other parts of your experience.

About politicians and Facebook Pages

Why multiple Facebook Pages?

Follow a politician’s Page

See politician’s activities

Politicians may have a Facebook Page for their role as elected officials and a separate Page for their activities as a candidate for office. For example, a state legislator may have a Page to share information about campaign events and another Page to share information about community events and legislation they’re sponsoring.

You may be automatically added as a follower of an elected representative’s government Facebook Page if you started following their candidate Facebook Page soon after their election. Following the Facebook Page that represents a politician’s government office is a way to make sure that you see the most relevant information about that politician’s activities as an elected official.

About verified Pages and profiles on Facebook (How do I get verified?)

What is a verified badge?

How do I get verified?

Why was my badge removed?

What is Meta Verified?

Some verified accounts are owned by a notable person, brand, or entity, while others are subscribed to Meta Verified.

  • Verified badges mean an account has been verified based on their activity across our products and information or documents they provide.
  • Meta Verified is a paid subscription that comes with benefits like the verified badge, enhanced support, impersonation protection, and more.

If you already have an existing verified badge based on prior requirements, you can still subscribe to Meta Verified.

The verified badge means an account has been verified based on their activity across our products and information or documents they provide.

A Facebook Page or profile with a verified badge next to it now indicates that Facebook has confirmed that it is the authentic presence for that person or brand. Previously, the verified badge also required the person or brand to be notable and unique. You may still see users with a verified badge that represents our previous eligibility requirements.

The verified badge is a tool to help people find people and brands’ real Pages and profiles. If a Page or profile has the verified badge, we’ve confirmed that it represents who it says it does. If the badge isn’t there, it may not be the real Page or profile. Posts, stories and other content from verified Pages and profiles aren’t verified by Facebook. We don’t use the verified badge to endorse or recognize individuals, public figures or brands.

A verified Page or profile cannot transfer ownership or modify its purpose. Edits such as name, category and bio updates are reviewed before they’re posted. Ownership transfers and significant changes may be grounds for badge removal.

Learn more about how Pages or profiles are verified. If you already have a notable profile and an existing verified badge, you can still apply for a Meta Verified subscription. Learn more about Meta Verified subscriptions.

As we test and learn, there will be no immediate changes to accounts on Facebook that are already verified based on prior requirements.

Merge 2 Facebook Pages

Merge my Facebook Pages

I can’t merge my Pages

What happens after merging?

Unmerge my Facebook Pages

The ability to merge Pages may not currently be available to all users.

If you have Facebook access to 2 Facebook Pages, you may be able to merge them if:

  • They have the same name and represent the same thing. If you’d like your Pages to have the same name, you can request a name change for one of your Pages. After the change is approved and your Pages have the same name, you can request to merge them.
  • They have the same address if they have physical locations.
  • They’re under the same Business Manager account.
  • The Page you want to merge from isn’t the primary Page of a Business Manager account.

You can’t merge:

  • 2 Facebook Pages if they’re global Pages.
  • A verified Page into a Page that isn’t verified.

If you have Facebook access to a Page, you can switch into your Page and request to merge 2 Pages on Facebook. If you have task access to a Page, you can’t merge Facebook Pages.

If your Pages can be merged, your Page followers and check-ins from profiles will be combined. Groups linked to the Page you merge will be migrated to the Page you want to keep. The Page you want to keep will remain unchanged, except for the addition of people who follow the other Page.

Posts, photos, reviews, ratings and the username will be deleted from the Page you merge. The Page you don’t want to keep will be removed from Facebook, and you won’t be able to unmerge it.

Before you request a Page merge, make sure that any campaigns you’re running aren’t pointing to the Page that will be deleted.

Merging your Pages

To merge your Pages:

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page’s profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  4. Click Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  5. In the left menu, click Page setup.
  6. Next to Merge Pages, click View.
  7. Next to Merge multiple Pages, click Start request.

If you don’t see the option to merge Pages, it means that your Pages aren’t eligible to be merged.

Messaging audience controls for Pages

Turn on Page messaging

Turn off Page messaging

Message requests not working

We are gradually introducing this feature. It may not be available to you right now.

Messaging audience controls help you manage who can start new conversations with your Page and how these new conversations are received and organized.

Note: Chat threads generated from ads are not affected by messaging audience controls.

Messaging audience controls can be set for 3 distinct groups of senders:

  • Those you follow
  • Your followers
  • Those who don’t follow you

You can specify if these senders can start conversation with your Page as:

  • Chats: The sender will be able to immediately start a new chat with your Page. You will not be asked to accept, block or delete a message request.
  • Message Requests: The new chat will be received as a message request, which you can accept, block or delete.
  • Not allowed: The sender will be prevented from starting a new chat with your Page.

The Those you follow setting overrides your other messaging audience controls. For example, a Page you follow wants to send your Page a message. Your Pages you follow setting is set to chats in the Those you follow setting, but your messaging audience control settings for Pages you follow is set to message requests. In this case, you will receive their first message as a chat, because the Those you follow setting overrides your messaging audience controls.

Learn how to update your messaging audience controls on Facebook and Messenger.

Tag other Facebook Pages or profiles in your Page’s photos or posts

Tag other Pages in photos

Tag people in my Page photos

Remove a tag from a photo

You can tag other Pages in your Page’s photos if the Page has allowed others to tag it.

You can tag people in your Page’s photos if they’ve liked your Page and are at least 18 years old. The profile will be notified of the tag and can choose to:

  • Accept the tag. The profile will be tagged in the Page post or photo and may share it to their timeline (depending on the profile’s Timeline review settings).
  • Reject the tag. The profile will not be tagged in your Page’s post and the post will not be shared to the profile’s timeline.

Tag other people or Pages in your Page post or photo

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page profile photo in the top right, then click your Page name to go to it.
  4. Find the photo you want to tag and click it.
  5. Click Tag photo in the top right of the photo.
  6. Click the person or Page in the photo.
  7. Begin typing the profile’s or Page’s name, then select them from the list that appears.
  8. Click Done Tagging at the bottom.

Note: You’ll need Facebook access to a Page to tag other people or Pages in your Page’s photos.

Remove a tag from a photo

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Find the photo you want to tag and click it, then click Tag photo in the top right.
  4. Click on the tag, then click X on the tag to remove it.
  5. Click Done Tagging at the bottom.

Tag people or Pages in photos on Facebook

Tag a photo before posting

Tag a photo already posted

I can’t tag someone

How many people can I tag?

You can tag people or Pages in photos you share on Facebook. You can also tag photos others have shared, if their privacy settings allow it.

Tag a photo before you post it

  1. At the top of your Feed, click Photo/Video below What’s on your mind, [Name]?
  2. Select the photo you want to share.
  3. Hover over the photo and click Edit in the top left.
  4. Click Tag photo, then click a person in the photo and start typing their name.
  5. Select the full name of the person or Page you want to tag when it appears.
  6. When you’re finished tagging people, click Save, then click Go back.
  7. Select the audience for your post, then click Post.

Tag a photo that has already been posted

  1. Click the photo you want to tag.
  2. Click Tag in the top right of the photo.
  3. Click the person in the photo and start typing their name.
  4. Select the full name of the person or Page you want to tag when it appears.
  5. Click Done tagging.

Remember

  • You can tag up to 50 people or Pages in a photo.
  • When you tag someone in a photo, that person’s friends may also see, like or comment on the photo.
  • Your tag may need to be approved by the person you tagged or the person who posted the photo (if it is not yours), depending on their privacy settings for posts they’re tagged in or tag review.
  • You may not see the option to tag people in photos posted by others, depending on their audience settings.

Learn more about how tagging works.

What happens to my ID?

How long is my ID kept?

In an effort to increase accountability of Pages, Facebook is requiring people who manage high potential reach Pages to get authorized to publish as their Page. You’ll know if you need to get authorized if you receive a notification from Facebook.

As part of the authorizations process, some people who manage Pages may be required to submit a photo ID for review.

This information will be used to complete the publishing authorizations process only. Your information won’t be shared on your profile, or with other people who manage your Page. After we confirm your identity, we’ll delete this information from our systems. This normally happens within 30 days.

Learn more about what happens to your ID after you send it to Facebook. If you’d like more information about how we handle other personal data, please see the Privacy Policy.

Why Facebook asks for location from people who manage Pages

Why is Facebook asking my location?

Confirm my country location

Turn on Location Services

I can’t confirm my location

In an effort to increase accountability and transparency of Pages, Facebook is requiring people who manage a Page with the potential to reach a lot of people to get authorized to publish as their Page. Part of this process might include confirming your country or region.

If you receive a notification from Facebook, you must complete the publishing authorizations process to continue to publish posts as your Page.

How does Facebook determine your country or region?

Your primary country or region is determined by your information and activity on Facebook, including the stated location on your Facebook profile, device and connection information.

How do I confirm my country or region?

To confirm your primary country or region, you’ll be asked to:

  1. Enter your current city. Learn how to update your About section.
  2. Turn on Location Services on your mobile device. Learn how to turn on your Location Services. Once you’ve completed these steps, you’ll be able to continue posting as your Page until we’ve finished reviewing your information.

What happens if Facebook can’t confirm my country or region?

If we’re unable to confirm your primary country or region, you won’t be able to post as your Page.

To help us confirm your primary country or region:

  • Use the Facebook app on your mobile device with Location Services turned on. By using a phone or tablet, we will receive more accurate location information.
  • Avoid using a VPN or similar services.
  • Ensure the current city on your profile is updated.

You can revisit your authorization status at any point by going to Identity Confirmation in General Account Settings.

Why Facebook Pages get taken down or have limits placed on them

My Page was taken down

Appeal a Page decision

Why was my Page unpublished?

My Page has limits

Sometimes, Pages may be taken down or have limits placed on them if they don’t follow our Community Standards. For example, Pages that publish spam may be unpublished or deactivated, and the Like button may be disabled on Pages that deceptively obtain likes. Using multiple accounts or accounts with fake names can result in account deactivation.

If you believe your Page was taken down or received limits by mistake, submit an appeal by going to the Page and clicking Appeal at the top.

Accounts that do not follow Community Standards or Terms of Service may be suspended. If your Facebook account has been suspended, you’ll be informed in an email and when you access your account in an app or web browser. Information about whether an appeal is possible will also be provided if you think there has been a mistake. After logging in, follow the on-screen instructions to submit your appeal.

Common Reasons Your Page May Be Taken Down or Have Limits Placed On It

  • Not all admins of your Page have authentic profiles: Creating an additional profile to impersonate goes against our Community Standards. Make sure all admins of your Page represent themselves authentically with the profiles they create.
  • People who manage your Page have acted against our Community Standards: Facebook is a place where people connect with each other using their authentic identities. Profiles that don’t follow our Community Standards or go against our Terms of Service may be removed from Facebook. Make sure you only add admins that you know and trust to manage your Page. Regularly check to see all the Pages you manage and remove yourself from any Pages you no longer actively manage. You can also check all of the people who have access to your Page by going to your Page Settings, clicking Page setup, then clicking Page access.
  • Your Page has a misleading name: Facebook limits a Page’s ability to make a significant change to its name that might cause people to feel misled. If you need to change your Page’s name, make sure it accurately reflects your Page. Learn more about what’s allowed.
  • Your Page posts content that may mislead people who like or follow your Page: In line with our commitment to authenticity, we don’t allow people to artificially boost the popularity of content, or engage in behaviors that go against our Community Standards. This includes misleading people about their identity, and who or what the profile or page represents.
  • The content posted on your Page goes against our hateful conduct policies: Hateful conduct isn’t allowed on Facebook because it creates an environment of intimidation and exclusion, and in some cases may promote real-world violence. We define hateful conduct as a direct attack on people based on race, ethnicity, national origin, religious affiliation, sexual orientation, caste, sex, gender, gender identity and disease or disability. Learn more about our hateful conduct policy.
  • Your Page has severely or repeatedly violated our Ads Policies: Our Ads Policies provide guidance on what types of content is allowed in an ad. If you severely or repeatedly violate these policies, we may disable your ad account and take down your Page. If you believe this was a mistake, you can appeal the decision through the Policy Disabled Ad Account Help form or through Ads Manager. Learn more about our Ads Policies.
  • Your Page does not have an admin with full control: If your Page does not have at least one person with Facebook access with full control, it will be automatically deactivated and scheduled for deletion. If your Page has been deactivated because the last person with Facebook access with full control is no longer active, you can submit a Page admin dispute.

Choose who can see a post you’re tagged in on Facebook

Who can see my tagged posts?

Change who sees my tags

My friends can’t see tagged posts

What happens when I’m tagged?

When someone tags you in a post, it will be visible to:

  • The audience selected by the person who made the post.
  • The audience you indicate in your Profile and Tagging settings. You can choose to automatically add your friends, select specific friends or not add anyone to the audience of the post you’re tagged in.

Choose your audience for posts you’re tagged in

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. In the left menu, click Profile and tagging.
  4. Click When you’re tagged in a post, who do you want to add to the audience of the post if they can’t already see it?.
  5. Select an audience (example: Only Me).
  6. Click Done.

Keep in mind:

  • This setting defaults to Friends, which means when you’re tagged in a post, you and your friends can see the post, even if they weren’t in the original audience.
  • The post you’re tagged in may be shared with the original audience, as well as the friends you suggest. These people may see it in Feed, search and other places on Facebook.

You can also review photos and posts you’re tagged in before they appear in your profile using Review posts you’re tagged in before the post appears on your profile? in your Profile and tagging settings.

Create a 3D photo on Facebook

Create 3D photo on computer

Create 3D photo on mobile

3D photo not working

To create 3D photos on Facebook from a computer, you’ll need to create a depth map file. To share 3D photos without this, log into the Facebook app for iOS or Android.

You can share 3D photos from your Feed, a group or a Page. Keep in mind that you’ll need to be an admin or editor to post a 3D photo from a Page.

Computer

To post a 3D photo, save 2 files on your computer:

  • The image you’d like to use: Save in .png or .jpg format.

  • A depth map for the image: Make sure your map has “_depth” appended to the file name (example: myImage_depth.png) and has the same aspect ratio as the image you’re using.

  • Original photo: [Image: Example of original photo]; Hand-drawn depth map: [Image: Example of hand-drawn depth map]; Resulting 3D photo: [Image: Example of resulting 3D photo]

Create your 3D photo

  1. Click Photo/Video at the top of your Feed, a group or your Page.
  2. Select your two files (the image and the depth map), then drag and drop your files onto your post. When the files are added to your post, the 3D image will be created.
  3. Click Post. [Embedded video omitted]

Keep in mind

  • 3D photos can’t be edited. If you edit a photo using Facebook, your computer or a third-party app, you may not be able to convert it into a 3D photo.
  • If you’d like to share a 3D photo, you can’t add multiple photos to a post. Only one 3D photo can be shared at a time.
  • At this time, 3D photos can’t be added to an album.
  • If you’re posting a 3D photo from a Page, 3D photos can’t be boosted or used in ads at this time. If you’re having trouble posting a 3D photo, you can try these tips.

Edit the alternative text for a photo on Facebook

I can’t edit alt text

What is alt text?

Alternative text (alt text) is a text-based description added to an image that can benefit people who are blind and have low-vision. You can replace this text to provide a better description of a photo. Keep in mind that this description will only be read if someone is using a screen reader to access Facebook.

See and edit alt text for a photo before you post it

  1. Click Photo/Video at the top of your Feed.
  2. Select the photo you want to add.
  3. Hover over the photo and click Edit.
  4. Click Alternative text in the menu on the left.
  5. The automatically generated text will be shown on the left of your photo. Click Custom alt text to edit it.
  6. Write your alt text in the box. To change back to the automatically generated text, click Select next to the automatically generated text.
  7. To save your alt text, click Save in the bottom left.

Change the alt text of a photo after you’ve posted it

  1. Click the photo to open it.
  2. Click Options in the top right and select Change Alt Text.
  3. Click on Type alternative text or change the alt text in the text box. You can also click Clear to change your edited alt text back to the automatically generated text.
  4. Click Save.

How to handle threats to share nude or sexual images of you on Instagram

Report a threat

Block someone threatening me

Find support organizations

What if I am under 18?

Find support and take action if needed. We worked with the Cyber Civil Rights Initiative and ConnectSafely.org on this list of things you can do and organizations you can reach out to for support and advice.

Start here

If someone is threatening to share things you want to keep private, asking you to send them money or anything else, you have options:

  1. Document the post: You may need a record of the post if you decide to take further action. Learn how to take a screenshot.
  2. Report this to local law enforcement.
  3. Report this to Facebook. Sharing or threatening to share intimate images goes against our Community Standards. If someone is threatening to share things you want to keep private (example: messages, photos, videos), asking you to send money or asking you to do something else you’re uncomfortable with, please report this to us.
  4. Block this person. Depending on your privacy settings, people on Facebook can see a list of your Facebook friends. Once you block someone, they no longer have access to your friend list and won’t be able to start conversations with you or see things you post on your profile. Remember that if somebody asks you to share something you’re not comfortable with, you have the right to say no.

If you’re under 18

If you’re under 18, we recommend also talking with a parent or other adult you trust to help you think through what to do. You can also talk to a school counselor or administrator who you feel comfortable with.

What you can do next

  • Contact a crisis helpline or chat service. These can be found all over the US and in many other countries. This is a good option if you want to remain anonymous while deciding what to do. Crisis lines can also often refer you to a victim advocate or other legal adviser near you.
  • Talk with a victim advocate or social worker in your town or city. In the US, there are victim advocates in county offices, police stations, domestic violence prevention centers, rape crisis centers, sheriff’s offices and offices of state attorneys general. Victim advocates can help you gather evidence, figure out how to keep you safe and get a civil protection or anti-stalking order against the person threatening you. If you’re in the US, call the National Organization for Victim Assistance at 1-800-TRY-NOVA/800-879-6682 or go to L (l.facebook.com).
  • Contact a legal aid society or organization near you for free advice.
  • Ask a lawyer or other counselor for advice.

Where to find additional support

If you, or a friend, are being harassed or harmed online, these organizations should be able to provide support. Many of them offer resources and support specifically for situations when intimate images have been shared without consent. If you’re concerned about a friend, please encourage them to reach out directly to the organization as well.

If you or a friend are having thoughts about suicide or self-injury, please contact local emergency services or a suicide helpline instead.

How to handle threats to share private images or personal info on Facebook

Report a threat

Block someone threatening my child

What happens if I report?

We worked with ConnectSafely.org on the following answer.

If someone is threatening to share personal information about your child (asking for money or anything else), you have options. Here’s what you can do:

  • Report this to local law enforcement.
  • Report this person to us. Sharing or threatening to share intimate images goes against our Community Standards.
  • Ask your child to block this person. Depending on your privacy settings, people on Facebook can see a list of your Facebook friends. Once you block someone, they no longer have access to your friend list and won’t be able to start conversations with you or see things you post on your profile.

Advice For Parents

Even when they’re being threatened, young people are often reluctant to tell trusted adults about sensitive issues. Often they’re afraid or confused about what might happen next. They worry that by speaking up they could make their situation much worse — they could be judged, disciplined, made an example of or publicly criticized by adults.

There is nothing more effective than letting your children know — often and in different ways — that you are there for them no matter what and will respectfully help them work through the issue with each step you take together.

If your child is being threatened, you may need to gather more information about the situation. Get the whole story from your child’s perspective, and then talk to people you both trust to fill in gaps. A legal adviser or victim advocate can help you gather evidence that can be used in a legal case or to get a restraining order, if necessary.

I’m having trouble viewing 360 photos on Facebook.

I can’t view 360 photos

My 360 photos are broken

Update my graphic driver

If you’re having trouble viewing 360 photos, try these troubleshooting tips:

  • Quit and reopen your browser or try using a different browser (example: Chrome, Firefox, Safari).
  • Make sure that your graphic driver is on the latest version. Refer to your operating system’s (example: Apple, Microsoft) process to update the graphic driver.
  • Make sure hardware acceleration and WebGL is enabled in your browser settings.

If you’re still having trouble viewing 360 photos, learn how to report a problem.

If you see images of a child being physically abused or sexually exploited on Facebook

Report child abuse images

Contact law enforcement

Resources for abuse victims

Images and videos of children being physically abused or sexually exploited are against Facebook policies.

If you see images on Facebook of a child being physically abused or sexually exploited, we ask that you:

  1. Please contact your local law enforcement immediately. They may be able to identify and rescue the child.
  2. Report the photo or video to Facebook. You’ll be able to check the status of your report from the Support Inbox. If you don’t have a Facebook account or are blocked from seeing the content you want to report, you can ask a friend to help you.
  3. Notify the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children using the CyberTipline: Visit L (l.facebook.com) or call 1-800-843-5678.
  4. Don’t share, download, or comment on the content. It can be criminal to share, or send messages with, photos and videos of children being sexually abused and exploited. You won’t be asked to provide a copy of the content in any report.

Additional support resources

Seeing an image or video of a child who has been abused can be distressing. We understand that people may be affected in different ways when they view these types of images, and we want to be sure that there are resources available for further support. Facebook has worked with a number of safety experts around the world to identify these resources, including social services and tips for reaching out to professionals.

If you, or a child you know, have been the victim of child physical or sexual abuse, or if you’ve witnessed child physical or sexual abuse and are interested in resources or support services, we encourage you to consider the resources provided by these organizations:

  • The National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) assists in cases of missing or exploited children throughout the world.
  • The International Centre for Missing and Exploited Children (ICMEC) provides a list of international operational centers that work to assist in cases of missing or exploited children.
  • Child Helpline International is a global network of hotlines providing support and social services.
  • ECPAT is a global network of civil society organizations dedicated to fighting against the sexual exploitation of children.
  • UNICEF defends the rights of children across 190 countries.

We also offer resources if you need to report a missing person or runaway.

You can manage what you’ve been tagged in on Facebook, like posts, photos and videos, all in one place from your activity log.

  6. Click Remove.

The post or photo you’re tagged in will still be shared with the audience selected by the person who made the post. These people may see it in Feed, search and other places on Facebook.

For example, if you’re tagged in a photo that your friend shared with their Facebook friends, when you remove your tag from that photo, the photo will still be visible to your friend’s Facebook friends.

  • Report any content that you’re tagged in that goes against our Community Standards.
  • Ask the person who posted the content to take it down.

Policies and Legal

About federal regulations that may impact sellers on Marketplace

What is the INFORM Act?

How seller verification works

Who is eligible for verification?

Some shipping features are not available to all eligible sellers.

The Federal INFORM Act (or INFORM Consumers Act) requires commerce platforms like Facebook Marketplace to verify, collect and display certain contact and financial information for eligible sellers. To meet these regulatory requirements, we may ask you to provide additional information, such as phone number or address. These requirements are intended to promote the safety of people who use Facebook Marketplace.

How seller verification works

Once you’ve been prompted to provide your contact and financial information, your ability to sell may be on pause until we verify your information. It should take about 2 business days to review your submission.

After we’ve reviewed your submission, certain information you provided will be visible to buyers on your seller profile (see below), and you’ll be able to continue to sell your products on Marketplace as before.

Sellers eligible for verification

Eligible sellers are identified based on the number of transactions completed and the gross merchandise value (GMV) sold. Goods sold from eligible sellers must be new, and eligible high-volume sellers must have payments enabled on Facebook Marketplace.

How to provide your contact and financial information to Meta

If you’re required to provide certain contact or financial information about your business, we’ll send you an email and you’ll get a notification in Marketplace.

To provide this information to Meta:

  1. Open the email we sent you. You can also open the notification you received in Marketplace on your desktop computer (verification isn’t available on your mobile device).
  2. Follow the instructions to submit the required contact and personal information.
  3. When you’re done, click Submit.

Your contact and financial information

Information we’ll collect from you

  • Legal name.

  • Legal address.

  • Email address.

  • Phone number.

  • Tax ID (ITIN or SSN).

  • Customer support email.

  • Customer contact number.

  • Seller details, such as:

  • Your merchant type (manufacturer, importer or reseller)

  • Platform exclusivity (whether you sell solely on Facebook Marketplace or on other platforms as well)

Information visible to your buyers

The following information will be displayed on your profile on Marketplace. You can mark your address and phone number as private when you are prompted to provide this information.

  • Legal name.
  • Legal address (unless you’ve marked it as residential/private).
  • Phone number (unless you’ve marked it as private).
  • Customer service phone number (if available).
  • Customer service email address (if available).
  • Merchant type.

In some cases, you may be asked to provide personal documents to confirm this information. Learn more about acceptable forms of documentation.
