How to use activity log on Facebook to manage content

Hide content from profile

Delete content from Facebook

Move content to Archive

Move content to Trash

You can use your activity log to hide or delete specific content on Facebook or move some of your Facebook content to your Archive or Trash. Here are some options you can choose from:

  • Hide from profile. When you hide something you’ve shared on Facebook from your profile, it means people won’t be able to see it when they visit your profile. Keep in mind, things you hide from your profile may still be visible to the audience they’re shared with on other places on Facebook, such as in Feed and Search.
  • Delete. When you delete something from activity log, it will be deleted from Facebook and can’t be restored.
  • Move to Archive. When you move your content to your Archive, it’ll only be visible to you. If you choose to restore your content, it’ll be visible to the audience that was selected before it was moved to Archive.
  • Move to Trash. When you move content to your Trash, it’ll stay there until it is automatically deleted 30 days later. While it’s in your Trash, it’ll only be visible to you.
    • During the 30 days, you can restore your content to where you originally posted it on Facebook, move it to your Archive or you can select content to delete before the 30 days are over. When you restore your content, it’ll be visible to the audience that was selected before it was moved to Trash.
    • After 30 days, the content will be automatically deleted and can’t be restored.

Keep in mind, not all content in your activity log is able to be moved to Archive or Trash. If you choose Manage Activity in your activity log, you’ll only see the content that you’re able to move. Learn more about Manage Activity.

Hide, delete, archive or trash something you’ve shared using activity log

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy, then tap Activity Log.
  3. On the left, click the category you want to review.
  4. From here, you can filter by:
    • Date
    • Activity Type (For example, under Your Facebook activity, you can click Posts and then Your posts, photos and videos to see posts, photos and videos you’ve shared)
  5. When you find the content, click Options on the right side of the content. From here there may be different options, which can include:
    • Hide from profile
    • Delete
    • Move to archive
    • Move to trash

Depending on the type of content you’re reviewing, you may have different options. For example, you may also be able to Edit Privacy of the content, which lets you choose a different audience to share with. Or, for content that you’ve reacted to (example: if you’ve loved or liked a post), you’ll have the option to Remove Reaction or Unlike.

Third-party apps include any apps, websites and games that you log into with Facebook or connect to your Facebook account. Third-party apps can be active, removed or expired depending on the type of application and how often you use it.

See and edit your settings for apps, websites and games

Stop an app, website or game from accessing your information

Information that an app, website or game can access on Facebook

Some information about you is part of your public profile or is information you’ve made public. An app, website or game can access this public information at any time. Other information is not public and an app, website or game can access it only if you choose to share it with the app, website or game when you log in with your Facebook account.

To help third-party apps comply with applicable laws and regulations concerning teens, we may share information about your age category (example: whether you are under 18) with third-party app and game developers on our platform.

An app, website or game can be:

  • Active: If it appears that you have used a third-party app, website or game within the last 90 days, it may access any information on Facebook that you’ve shared with it at any time.
  • Expired: After 90 days of inactivity, an app’s access to non-public information expires. It may still have non-public information you previously shared with it while it was active. There are a couple of exceptions:
    • We only expire access to information you can make non-public on your Facebook account. Certain information that is always public on Facebook, like your name and profile picture, can still be accessed after 90 days of inactivity. This information is publicly accessible to everyone, and an app, website or game can access this information even if you’re not an active user.
    • Some apps and websites have permissions that are used to monitor or manage information on Facebook business products, like Pages, groups, ads and messages. Apps and websites with these permissions are called Business Integrations. We do not expire these permissions after 90 days of inactivity because they may need to access these products continuously (even if you haven’t logged into the app or website recently).
  • Removed: When you remove an app, website or game, or the app developer has made an app unavailable for you, it can only access public information on your Facebook account. Remember that:
    • The app, website or game may have stored information from when you were using it.
    • Removing the app, website or game only prevents it from continuing to access your non-public information through Facebook.

Keep in mind

  • If you start using an app, website or game again after 90 days of inactivity, it may become active again and can access the non-public information you previously chose to share with it.
  • An app, website or game may ask you for permission to continue accessing your non-public information after its access has expired. You can approve or deny its request directly or by updating your Facebook settings at any time.
  • We aren’t always able to tell when you haven’t used an app, website or game for 90 days, so we may sometimes stop an app, website or game from accessing your non-public information, even if you’ve used it in the past 90 days.

Visit the Instagram Help Center to learn more about how long apps and websites you’ve added have access to your information on Instagram.

Protect your account from mobile apps designed to steal your information

My account was hacked

Protect my Facebook account

What are malicious apps?

I received a warning message

Third-party app stores may offer mobile apps that appear legitimate but are actually maliciously designed to steal your login information. These account compromise mobile apps might be phishing for your Facebook or Instagram login credentials, or your login credentials for another app. By knowing what to look for when downloading a new mobile app, you can better identify these malicious apps and keep your accounts secure.

We’re always looking to detect and take action against these third-party malicious apps. If we believe you may have logged into Facebook using one of these mobile apps, we may send an alert to warn you so you can take steps to protect your account. If you think you’ve been impacted by malware, we encourage you to use the Security Checkup Tool to help secure your account.

You can use Security Checkup to review and add more security to your account. You’ll need to log into your Facebook account to start Security Checkup.

Start Security Checkup

What to do if you receive a message from Facebook that your account might be compromised

If we believe you’ve logged into Facebook from a malicious app, we may send you a warning message to help you secure your account. While there is a chance that this is a false alarm, we want to alert you so that you can take precautionary steps to protect your account. Because these apps are typically downloaded from the internet, off of our platforms, we may not always catch every single instance. If you believe you’ve downloaded a malicious app and have logged in with your Facebook credentials, we recommend that you delete the app from your device immediately and follow the following instructions to secure your account:

  • Reset your password. Never reuse your password across multiple websites.
  • Enable two-factor authentication, to add an extra security layer to your account.
  • Turn on log-in alerts so you’ll be notified if someone is trying to access your account. Be sure to review your previous sessions to make sure you recognize which devices have access to your account.
  • Visit the Security Checkup Tool to help secure your account.

What is activity log?

Activity log is a place where you can review and manage your Facebook activity. You can scroll through your content, or you can filter your content by category to review specific things like posts, posts you’re tagged in, photos and videos, friend requests and your events.

Note: Only you can see your activity log, but the posts and other content in your activity log may appear other places on Facebook, like on your timeline, in Search or in your friends’ Feeds.

What’s included in activity log?

You’ll find many categories of your Facebook activity in activity log, organized by the date you added it to Facebook (starting with the most recent activity). Keep in mind, this means when you add a life event to your profile, it will show up in your activity log on the day you added it, not the day of the event itself.

Categories of your information in activity log include:

  • Your Posts to review things like photos, videos, text and status updates you’ve shared on Facebook.
  • Activity You’re Tagged In to review things like posts, photos and comments you’ve been tagged in.
  • Interactions to review things like likes, reactions and comments.
  • Groups and Events to review things like your group activity and events you’ve created.
  • Profile information to review things like your phone number and email address.
  • Connections to review things like friends, Page likes and relationships.
  • Logged Actions and Other Activity to review things like your devices, logins and videos you’ve watched.

Note: This list isn’t comprehensive. You can access most of the content you post to Facebook by logging into your account. Also note the categories of data we receive, collect and save may change over time. Learn more about your Facebook data in our Privacy Policy.

You can use activity log to:

  • Find a specific activity you’re looking for.
  • Remove a search from your search history.
  • Hide or remove posts on Facebook.
  • View things you’ve hidden on your timeline.

Why we may ask for additional permission to use your info before you can continue to use Facebook

Why do you need my birthday?

What happens if I don’t agree?

Can I get my account back?

When you create a Facebook account, we ask you to agree to our Privacy Policy, which describes how we collect and use your info. However, laws in some regions require us to get additional permission from some users. If the birthday you provided for your Facebook account is in a specific age range, you may be asked to give us permission to process your info in order to keep your existing account, or to create a new account.

Once notified, you will have 180 days to choose whether to allow us to use your info and keep your account, or not. If you don’t make a choice within 180 days, or you choose not to allow us to collect and use your data, your account will be permanently disabled and scheduled for deletion.

Why you may be blocked from using features on Facebook

I am blocked from posting

Why was I blocked?

How to avoid future blocks?

My block is too long

We understand that you may have had good intentions or may have not known about our policies on acceptable behavior, and we also understand that this block can be frustrating. To help keep Facebook open and welcoming, we try to prevent people from unintentionally misusing Facebook, even if you felt that what you did was acceptable.

Why you may be blocked

  • Something you posted or shared seems suspicious or abusive to our security systems.
  • Messages or friend requests you sent were marked unwelcome.
  • You’ve done something that doesn’t follow our Community Standards.

Note: The length of a block depends on the severity of the violation and your history on Facebook.

How to avoid blocks in the future

  • Review our Community Standards to understand what kind of sharing is allowed on Facebook.
  • Only message people you already know.
  • Only send friend requests to people you know.

Profile

About additional Facebook profiles (Can people see my other profiles?)

Can people see my other profiles?

What info is public?

How do I update privacy?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

You are no longer able to create additional Facebook profiles. Existing additional profiles have not been affected.

People may learn the profiles you create are connected based on what you say or do. Your profile may be suggested as a friend to others, and some information on your profile will be public.

Because your profiles are under one Facebook account, we use information from all of your profiles to personalize your experience across Meta Products, including ads. You may also see friends, groups, and other recommendations based on activity from your other profiles. Learn more about the difference between your Facebook profile and account.

Things to keep in mind when you use additional Facebook profiles

  • The settings of your additional Facebook profiles are automatically set to default settings. Your notification and privacy settings from one profile don’t carry over to your other Facebook profiles. You can manage some settings separately for each profile, such as choosing who can see that profile’s posts or send friend requests to that profile. You can update privacy settings for your profiles at any time. Keep in mind: You can update things like ads or security in your Facebook account settings.
  • People may be able to tell which profiles are yours based on public information on Facebook like your name, profile picture and more. Example: If you use the same profile picture across your profiles, people may figure out that your profiles are connected.
  • People are more likely to discover your Facebook profiles are connected if you use them in similar ways such as:
    • Add a friend or send a friend request to the same friends
    • Add your profiles as friends
    • Join the same groups
    • Follow the same Pages
    • Interact with the same content like posts
  • When you block a profile on Facebook, that profile will no longer be able to do things such as tag your profile or see things you post on your profile. Blocking a profile also means your profile won’t show up in that person’s People You May Know suggestion. Blocking on one profile does not carry over to other profiles you may have.
  • People may tag or post things on your additional Facebook profiles that could make it possible for other people to figure out that your profiles are connected. You can control what appears on your profiles by adjusting each of your profile’s settings for tagging and reviewing posts.
  • People who are friends with your additional Facebook profiles may discover your main profile if you:
    • Allow people to find your main profile using your contact information. You can adjust your settings to control how people can find you on Facebook.
    • Add your Instagram account and main profile on Facebook to Accounts Center. For example, if you’ve linked your Instagram account to your main profile on Facebook and someone follows one of your additional Facebook profiles, that person may see your main profile as a People You May Know suggestion on Facebook.

Note: We share information with law enforcement and respond to legal requests as outlined in our Privacy Policy and Information for Law Enforcement Authorities. This may include information from your additional Facebook profiles.

About additional Facebook profiles (Switch between profiles)

Switch between profiles

Log in to another profile

Report an additional profile

What is a main profile?

You are no longer able to create additional Facebook profiles. Existing additional profiles have not been affected.

Additional profiles can represent different things about you like your interests or communities you belong to. Each profile will have its own friends list and Feed and each can follow different groups and Pages.

Additional Facebook profiles are different from your main profile, which is the profile you create when you sign up for a Facebook account. Your main profile is required and can only be deleted if you delete your Facebook account.

Log in to additional profiles

You’ll use your existing login information across all of your profiles. When you’re logged in to your account, you’ll land in your main profile first and can then switch to the profile you want to use. Learn more about the difference between your Facebook account and profiles.

Note: Only Facebook profiles created through your Facebook account are considered additional profiles. If you created a new Facebook account it is separate from your primary account.

Report additional profiles

You can report additional profiles that go against our Community Standards. Learn more about reporting profiles or content on Facebook.

About Facebook Page Status

See my Page Status

Recent violations on my Page

Review my Page Status

What are Community Standards?

Anyone who has Facebook access to your Page can visit Page Status to see:

  • Recent Community Standards violations.
  • Content shared by your Page that’s been rated by third-party fact-checkers.
  • Intellectual property rights violations.
  • Content shared by your Page that’s been identified as clickbait.
  • Violations for sharing too much content from other sources.
  • Events take-downs.
  • Content shared by your Page that isn’t eligible for suggestions.

This includes violations and content that may have occurred as a result of actions by other people who manage your Page.

See Page Status for your Page

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page profile picture in the top right.
  4. Click Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  5. In the left menu click Page setup, then click Page Status.

Review your Page Status

Below the Page Status section:

  • You can see the status of your Page along with details around how some violations may impact your distribution or risk of being unpublished.
  • Below the header, you can see a summary box that shows which type of violations are affecting your Page. You can click Learn More to read more about each violation type.

Below the Recent Violations section:

  • You can see individual violations by your Page.
  • For Community Standards violations, you can click See Details to learn more. You can then either accept the decision or request review depending on the type of violation.
  • For misleading content that was shared by your Page, intellectual property rights violations or events take-downs, you can click See Details to learn more.
  • For misleading, deceptive or fraudulent job post take-downs, you can click See Details to learn more.

For violations that may have occurred as a result of actions from other people who manage your Page, you can see the violation as well as who posted the content to your Page to help ensure better Page management. Learn more about how to add or remove someone with access to your Page.

Keep in mind that multiple violations may result in your Page being unpublished, having limits placed on it or other restrictions (example: no longer being able to create ads). Pages and websites that repeatedly share false news or violate our Community Standards may have their distribution reduced, their ability to monetize and advertise removed, their ability to register as a news Page removed, and suspension of access to fundraising tools.

Page Status doesn’t include all areas of Community Standards and Page policy violations. There may still be violations from your Page that Page Status doesn’t reflect yet, such as violations of our Page Policies.

Learn more about:

  • Community Standards
  • Fact-Checking on Facebook: What Publishers Should Know
  • Clickbait
  • Intellectual property

Community Standards Notification

When you go to a Page that has Community Standards violations, you may see the notification “This Page may share content that violates our Community Standards.” We show this message so you know that you may see posts on the Page that aren’t allowed on Facebook but that haven’t been removed for Community Standards violations yet.

If you see the notification, you can choose:

  • Review Page: Go to the Page and review the content to make sure that you’re ok with the content that is shared on the Page before you decide to like it.
  • Like Page: Like the Page without reviewing it.

You can also read our Community Standards to learn more about what is and isn’t allowed on Facebook.

About Facebook profile types

What is professional mode?

Difference between profile and Page?

Can I create additional profiles?

What is a Facebook Page?

Facebook offers different profile types for different purposes.

Your main profile is the profile you create when you sign up for a Facebook account. You must have a main profile to create a Page.

Professional mode for profiles

Professional mode is a setting you can turn on for your main profile on your Facebook account. You might turn on this setting if you are a creator who wants to use your existing social network to grow a public presence.

  • When professional mode is on, anyone can follow you and see your public posts.
  • You get access to professional tools, such as insights and monetization features.
  • Only you can manage your profile in professional mode, and your real name is still required.

Additional profiles

Note:You are no longer able to create additional Facebook profiles. Existing additional profiles have not been affected.

Additional Facebook profiles under your Facebook account represent different things about you like your interests or communities you belong to. Some features such as professional mode are not available on Additional Profiles at this time.

Page

A Page is a separate profile with access to professional tools. If you are a creator or have a business or organization you want to promote, creating a Page is a good way to build your brand, engage with audiences and use professional tools to grow a separate public presence.

  • Pages have public settings by default, so anyone can follow and see your posts.
  • More than one person can manage a Page.
  • Pages do not require a real name and are designed for public use.
  • You can have more than one Page.
  • Pages and professional mode both offer professional tools, but only Pages can have multiple managers and are separate from your main profile.

Avatar AutoGen Privacy Notice

How does AutoGen use my selfie?

What information does AutoGen collect?

Does AutoGen use facial recognition?

This notice applies to users (excluding IL/TX) utilizing autogen before June 22, 2023. This notice governs usage from June 22, 2023 onward.

The Avatar autogenerate feature (“AutoGen”) enables us (Meta Platforms, Inc., “we”, “us” or “our”) to quickly recommend avatars to you that more closely match your facial appearance using a video recording of yourself (“Selfie”) that you submit. This Avatar AutoGen Privacy Notice applies to our processing of your information in connection with generating recommended avatars via AutoGen. It does not apply to the processing of information used to power augmented reality features, such as filters, masks or other interactive digital experiences, that you may use with your final avatar after it is generated. The information processed in connection with those augmented reality features is subject to the Face and Hand Effects Privacy Notice. Depending on your location, you may need to turn on those augmented reality features before you are able to access them.

Information we use to provide the AutoGen feature

Our software analyzes your Selfie to estimate facial points, such as eye, nose, and mouth locations, and their contours. Our software also detects facial attributes like shape and color pigment from your Selfie. We use estimated facial points and predicted facial attributes to suggest avatars that resemble you. You can customize recommended avatars using the avatar editor before selecting your final avatar. None of this information is used to identify you.

Deleting your account also deletes your final avatar. You can delete your final avatar at any time by clicking the trashcan icon in Avatar Editor settings. Your final avatar will also be deleted if you delete your account.

Your Selfie, estimated facial points and predicted facial attributes will be used for recommending avatars inspired by you and, together with your recommended avatars, will be deleted within 14 days.

Other information we use

As stated in our Privacy Policy, we also collect other information in connection with your use of the avatar editing tools (for example, whether you used one of our recommended hairstyles or used our editing tools to choose another hairstyle for your final avatar). We use this other information to troubleshoot, diagnose and fix problems that you may have in using the feature, as described in our Privacy Policy. This information does not include your Selfie, estimated facial points, predicted facial attributes, recommended avatars, or final avatar. This other information will be disassociated from your account and will be deleted when we no longer need it to provide or improve the avatar service.

We do not share this information

We do not share any of the information described in this notice, including your Selfie or any of the other information processed to generate your recommended avatars, with third parties.

If you help manage a Page, you must have Facebook access in order to block profiles or Pages from your Page on Facebook. If you have task access to content, messages or community activity for the Page, you can block profiles or Pages from other tools.

When you block a profile or Page from your Page, that profile or Page can no longer:

  • See things you post on your Page.
  • Tag your Page.
  • Invite your Page to events or groups.
  • Start a conversation with your Page.
  • Find your Page by searching for it on Facebook.

If you block a profile or Page that follows your Page, it will also be removed as a follower.

Note: When you block a profile or Page, you only block it from your Page. This does not include apps, games or groups that your Page and the blocked profile or Page both participate in.

Block someone’s Facebook profile, Page, or nickname

Block a profile

Block a Page

Block a nickname in a group

What happens when I block?

Once you block a profile or Page, certain actions will be limited, such as interacting with each other’s timelines, posts, comments or messages. This doesn’t include apps, games or groups you both participate in. If you currently are connected with that profile or Page, blocking it will unfriend, unlike and unfollow it.

Once you block a nickname in a Facebook group, that nickname’s ability to interact with your group content will be limited.

If you have additional Facebook profiles, you’ll need to manage blocking from each of your profiles separately.

You can learn more about how to unblock a profile or Page.

Block a profile or Page

To block someone on Facebook:

  1. Go to their Profile or Page.
  2. Click Options (or More).
  3. Click Block, then confirm that you want to block them by clicking Confirm.

You can also block someone by going to Settings & Privacy > Settings > Blocking and typing their name.

Note: The Block option is no longer available directly from the post menu in Feed. You can still block someone from their profile or through your Settings.

You can also block a profile or Page by going to your Blocking settings:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. In the menu, click Blocking under Audience and visibility.
  4. In the Block profiles and Pages section, click Edit.
  5. Click Add to blocked list.
  6. Type the name of the profile or Page you want to block.
  7. Click Block next to their name.
  8. Click Confirm.

Note: If you’re having trouble finding the profile you want to block, you can try using an email associated with the Facebook profile.

Block a nickname in a Facebook group

  1. Find a post or comment from the nickname you want to block.
  2. Click on the nickname or the nickname’s profile photo.
  3. Next to the nickname on its group profile page, click Options.
  4. Click Block [Nickname], then confirm that you want to block them by clicking Block.
    • Note: Blocking a nickname in a group only blocks that nickname and doesn’t block the main profile associated with that nickname.

What happens when you block a profile or Page

When you block a profile or Page, that profile or Page won’t be able to:

  • See your posts.
  • Tag you in posts, comments, or photos.
  • Invite you to events or groups.
  • Start a conversation with you.
  • Add you as a friend.

What happens when I block a nickname in a group?

When you block a nickname in a group, that nickname won’t be able to:

  • Tag you in posts or comments in the group.
  • Interact with your content in the group.

In some cases, they may still be able to see your content. When you block a nickname in a group, you won’t see any posts or comments from the nickname in that group. You may still see content from that nickname in other groups.

Other things to consider when you block a profile

  • If you don’t want to unfriend a profile but you want to see less of that profile’s posts on Facebook, you can take a break from that profile.
  • The profile you blocked won’t be able to:
    • Start a conversation with you.
    • Add you as a friend.
  • If you block someone’s profile from more than one of your profiles, the person you blocked may be able to figure out that you own all of those profiles.

Remember that blocking someone may not prevent all communications or interactions (example: in apps or groups). Learn more about what you can see when you block someone’s profile.

When you block someone who has more than one profile

  • Blocking one of their profiles only blocks that profile. It doesn’t block their other profiles. This means that you may still interact with their other profiles.
    • For example, you may start a conversation with those other profiles or add them as a friend.
  • When you block someone’s profile, this will limit some of the ways they can interact with you from their other profiles.

When you block someone who has more than one nickname

Blocking one of their nicknames only blocks that nickname. It doesn’t block the main profile associated with the nickname or the other nicknames associated with that main profile. This means that you may still see content from these other nicknames or the main profile associated with them.

Remember these things

  • If you block a profile and then unblock it, you’ll need to send that profile a new friend request. If you block a Page and then unblock it, you’ll need to follow that Page again.
  • Profiles, Pages, and nicknames won’t be notified when you block them.

Content you can see from a blocked profile

I see content from blocked person

What does blocking do?

What happens after I block?

Blocking allows you to prevent many interactions with someone’s profile on Facebook, but you may still encounter content they’ve shared.

Here’s what you might see

  • Messages: Your message history with a profile you’ve blocked will stay in your inbox. If the blocked profile is ever included in a conversation with a group of friends, you may be able to see the messages. Remember, you can leave a conversation that you don’t want to be part of, or delete a conversation that you don’t like.
  • Mutual friend content: There’s a chance that you’ll see content about the blocked profile through mutual friends. For example, if the blocked profile tags a mutual friend in a photo, you might see this on your friend’s timeline.
  • Photos: You might see photos or tags of the blocked profile added by other people.
  • Groups: A profile you’ve blocked won’t be able to add you to a group, but you’ll be able to see groups that the blocked profile created or is a member of.
  • Events: A profile you’ve blocked won’t be able to invite you to an event, but you’ll be able to see events to which both you and the blocked profile are invited.
  • Games and apps: Since games and apps are run by outside developers, the Facebook block won’t apply to them. So you could see someone whose profile you blocked while you’re playing a game (example: in the game’s chat room).
  • Marketplace seller ratings and reviews: If you block a Marketplace seller that you’ve rated or submitted a review for, then the seller’s profile will still be able to see, report, and respond to your review.
    • Buyers: If you block a Marketplace seller that you’ve rated or submitted a review for, then the seller’s profile will still be able to see, report, and respond to your review.
    • Sellers: If you block a buyer on Marketplace, then you will still be able to see ratings and reviews left by that buyer’s profile. You will still be able to report and respond to those reviews.- Additional profiles: Blocking a profile won’t carry over to other profiles someone may create. You may still see and interact with their other profiles.

Control who Facebook can suggest your profile to based on your email address or phone number

Control who can suggest me

Adjust email suggestion settings

Adjust phone suggestion settings

People You May Know suggestions

Through your privacy settings, you can control who Facebook can suggest your profile to based on your email address or phone number using the setting labeled Who can Facebook suggest your profile to based on your phone number or email address.

You can choose to limit suggestions based on your email address or phone number to:

  • Possible Connections. People who have uploaded your phone number or email address and your Friends of Friends.
  • Friends of Friends. Your Friends of Friends on Facebook who have your phone number or email address.
  • Friends. Your Friends on Facebook who have your phone number or email address.
  • No one. Your profile won’t be suggested to anyone based on your phone number or email address.

Adjust who Facebook can suggest your profile to based on your phone number or email address

Adjust your settings

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Below Audience and Visibility click How people find and contact you. From here, you can adjust the relevant settings. There are separate settings for your email address and your phone number.
  • To update your email setting, click View to the right of People with your email address.
  • To update your phone number setting, click View to the right of People with your phone number.
  1. Select whether your email or phone number can be considered as a factor in suggesting you to different groups of people who have your phone number or email.

How these settings apply to People You May Know

People You May Know can help suggest you as a friend to people you may know on Facebook. There are many factors used to determine who to include in these friend suggestions. One reason we may suggest you to someone else is if the other person’s contacts that they have uploaded to Facebook or Messenger include your phone number or email address. Learn more about how Facebook may use your information to show suggestions in People You May Know.

Note: Your phone number or email address is not shared in People You May Know as part of the suggestion.

Keep in mind:

  • By default, your setting is set to Possible Connections. This means that your profile might appear as a friend suggestion in People You May Know to people who have uploaded your phone number or email address to Facebook.
  • Even if you restrict these settings, People You May Know may suggest your profile based on information other than your email address or phone number. Learn more about what information is used to show suggestions in People You May Know.
  • If someone searches for your email address or mobile phone number using Facebook’s search feature, the search results won’t show your profile. But if someone searches using your email address and it includes your full name, your profile may be shown in search results.
  • We’ll also check this privacy setting before we confirm your profile to your friends of friends or friends when they’re adding you to their business account, or if they help you recover your password, and we won’t provide that confirmation if your setting is restricted to exclude them.
  • You control who can see your mobile phone number or email address on your profile separately. If you choose to share your phone number or email address on your profile with an audience, everyone in that group can see it. Learn how to adjust who you share your email address or mobile phone number with.

When you log into a game with Facebook, you can share your profile’s player name and avatar with the game instead of your profile name and profile picture. The difference between your Facebook account and profile

What is a Facebook account?

What is a main profile?

What are additional profiles?

Delete my Facebook account

Your Facebook account

You have to create a Facebook account in order to use Facebook. Your account is where you’ll:

  • Enter information about yourself like the name you go by in everyday life, email, mobile phone number, date of birth and gender. You may be asked to confirm that this name is the name you’re known by. Learn more about names on Facebook.
  • Create a password to log into your account and access your main profile.

Your main profile

Your main profile is the profile you create when you sign up for a Facebook account. Your main profile is required and can only be deleted if you delete your Facebook account. Your main profile must be active in order to create and use additional Facebook profiles.

This profile represents you on Facebook and is a place where you can share information about yourself (example: your interests, photos, videos, current city and hometown). It’s also where you’ll:

  • Use the name you go by in everyday life.
  • Use Messenger as your main profile or create a Messenger Kids account for your child.
  • Upload your mobile contacts.
  • Manage certain settings like how people can find and contact you using your contact information.
  • Access Pages that you manage as an admin.
  • Manage your account settings such as:
    • Account information: Your contact information, language preferences, payment information and other general information about your account.
    • Security: Login information, apps and websites connected to your account.
    • Ads: Ad preferences to control how data influences the ads you see.- Delete or deactivate your Facebook account. Deleting or deactivating your account will also delete or deactive all profiles managed by that account. Learn more about deactivating or deleting your account.

Your additional Facebook profiles

Additional Facebook profiles can represent different things about you like your interests or communities you belong to. You can delete or deactivate your additional Facebook profiles individually.

Each profile has a unique @username that will appear on the profile. Each profile also has its own friends list and Feed and can follow different groups and Pages.

Because your profiles are under one Facebook account, we use information from all of your profiles to personalize your experience across Meta Products, including ads. You may also see friends, groups, and other recommendations based on activity from your other profiles.

Account settings apply to all your profiles, and you can access these settings through your main profile. Profile settings, including privacy and who you block, apply to each profile individually. When you create an additional Facebook profile, its profile settings are automatically set to default settings. Profile settings include things like:

  • Privacy: Adjust who can see things like the profile’s posts.
  • Profile and tagging: Control what appears on the profile by adjusting settings for tagging and reviewing posts.
  • Blocking: Manage who you block for each profile. Learn more about blocking profiles on Facebook.
  • Messaging: You can use Messenger as your additional Facebook profile. If you delete or deactivate an additional Facebook profile, you’ll lose access to Messenger for that profile.

Your notifications and profile settings from one profile don’t carry over to your other Facebook profiles. You can manage some settings separately for each profile, such as choosing who can see that profile’s posts or send friend requests to that profile. You can update privacy settings for your profiles at any time.

People may learn that the profiles you create are connected based on what you do or say. Your profiles may be suggested as a friend to others, and some information on your profile is public. Learn about things to keep in mind when you use additional Facebook profiles.

This feature is not yet available to everyone.

Your Facebook profile has additional fields where you can add information about yourself and the things you’re interested in. The sections of your profile that you can add or edit include:

  • Intro: A bio or brief description of yourself.
  • Personal details: Personal details including relationship status, family members, location, gender, and birthday.
  • Work: Your past and current work experiences.
  • Education: Your high school and/or college.
  • Hobbies: Hobbies you’re interested in.
  • Interests: Things you’re interested in, including TV shows, movies, games, music and sports.
  • Travel: Places you’ve visited or want to go visit.
  • Links: Links to any personal sites or things you like
  • Contact info: Ways people can get in touch with you, including social media links, phone number and email address.

You can also choose to share any new profile updates to your feed with the Share to Feed option.

When you tap the Friends with things in common tab on your profile, you’ll see a list of friends who have added the same interests or details to their profiles as you have. You’ll also see which specific interests or details you share with each friend. If you tap on an interest you’ll get a full list of friends who share that interest. This allows you to connect with more people who have similar interests.

Learn how to select your audience on Facebook.

Note: Some information on Facebook is always public. Learn more about public information on Facebook.

Guidelines for creating a custom username or screen name on Facebook

Create a custom username

Username already taken

Username requirements

I can’t create a username

When you create a custom username on Facebook or Messenger, keep in mind:

  • You can only have one username for your Page or profile, and you can’t have a username that is already being used.
  • Usernames can only contain alphanumeric characters (A–Z, 0–9) and periods (“.”). They can’t contain generic terms or domain extensions (e.g., .com, .net), including country extensions (e.g., .ie, .de, .ca).
  • Usernames must be at least 5 characters long.
  • Periods (“.”) and capitalization can’t be used to differentiate usernames. For example, johnsmith55, John.Smith55 and john.smith.55 are all considered the same username.
  • Usernames shouldn’t impersonate someone else.
  • Your username must adhere to the Facebook Terms.

Usernames for Pages

Keep in mind that you must be an admin to create or change the username for a Page.

You may not be able to immediately create a username for a new Page if you’ve recently created several new Pages. A Page’s username can also be removed because of inactivity.

Guidelines for Facebook Page names

Change my Page name

Page name not approved

Page name rules

Page name capitalization

Page names must accurately reflect the Page and follow our naming guidelines. Keep in mind that only authorized representatives can manage a Page for a brand, place, organization or public figure.

Page name best practices

Keep Page names simple, specific and grammatically correct to accurately reflect the purpose of your Page. For example, Hungry Bear Coffee, Allstar Locksmith or Caring Hearts Daycare.

Page names can’t include

  • Terms or phrases that may be abusive or violate someone’s rights.
  • The word “official” if the Page isn’t the official Page of a brand, place, organization or public figure.
  • Improper capitalization (example: tHe best CaFE). Page names must use grammatically correct capitalization and may not include all capital letters, except for acronyms.
  • Symbols (example: ® ) or unnecessary punctuation.
  • Descriptions or slogans (example: The Best Cafe - We serve the best coffee in town). People who manage Pages can add this information to a Page’s About section.
  • Any variation of the names “Facebook” (referring to the product), “Meta” (referring to the company) or any of the Meta Company Products.

Page names can’t consist only of

  • A single, general word (example: Pizza). Pages must be managed by official representatives of the topics they’re about, so avoid any Page names that are too broad.
  • General geographic locations (example: New York). However, you can create a Page name for an organization that represents a geographic location. For example, “New York City – Mayor’s Office” and “Queen Elizabeth II of Great Britain” are acceptable Page names. You may also use a Page name that’s different from the name of the organization as long as the name accurately reflects what the Page is about (example: “Tourism Ireland” can have a Page named “Discover Ireland”).

Learn how to submit a request to change your Page’s name.

Hide or delete a comment from a post on your Facebook profile

Hide a comment

Delete a comment

Unhide a comment

If you manage a Facebook Page, learn how to hide or delete comments for your Page.

When you hide a comment from a post on your profile:

  • The comment will still be visible to the person who wrote it and their friends. This can help prevent more unwanted comments.
  • The comment will be hidden for everyone else that you chose to share it with (example: Friends or Public).
  • Replies to the comment will also be hidden. If you want to hide specific replies to a comment, you can select and hide each reply separately. If you only hide replies to a comment, the original comment will still be visible to everyone else that you chose to share it with.

Hide comments

To hide a comment and its replies from a post on your profile:

  1. From your profile, go to the post that has a comment you want to hide.
  2. Next to the comment you want to hide, hover over Options, then click Hide comment.

To unhide a comment and its replies from a post on your profile:

  1. Go to the post that has a comment you want to unhide.
  2. Go to the comment you want to unhide, then follow one of these options:
    • Below the comment, click Unhide.
    • Hover over Options, then click Unhide comment.

After you hide a comment, you can also report the comment if it doesn’t follow our Community Standards.

Delete Comments

When you delete a comment from a post on your profile, the comment will be removed from the post.

To delete a comment from a post on your profile:

  1. Go to the post that has a comment you want to delete.
  2. Click Options to the right of the comment you want to delete.
  3. Select Delete.

You can block the profile or Page that made the comment by going directly to the profile or Page.

How Avatar AutoGen Works (Illinois, Texas)

What is Avatar AutoGen?

How Avatar AutoGen works and how Meta processes your AutoGen data

Delete my estimated facial points

Delete my Selfie

What is AutoGen?

How long is my Selfie stored?

Note: This notice applies to users (excluding IL/TX) utilizing autogen from June 22, 2023 onward. User usage prior to June 22, 2023 is governed by this notice.

The Avatar autogenerate feature (“AutoGen”), where available, enables us (Meta Platforms, Inc., “we”, “us” or “our”) to quickly recommend avatars to you that more closely match your facial appearance using a video recording of yourself (“Selfie”) that you submit. This Avatar AutoGen Privacy Notice applies to our processing of your information in connection with generating recommended avatars via AutoGen. This Avatar AutoGen Privacy Notice also does not apply to the processing of information used to power augmented reality features, such as filters, masks or other interactive digital experiences, that you may use with your final avatar after it is generated. The information processed in connection with those augmented reality features is subject to the Face and Hand Effects Privacy Notice. Depending on your location, you may need to turn on those augmented reality features before you are able to access them.

Information we use to provide the AutoGen feature

In order to recommend avatars inspired by your appearance, our software analyzes your Selfie to estimate the location of parts of your face, like your eyes, nose and mouth, and specific points on the contours of those parts of your face (collectively, “estimated facial points”). Our software also analyzes your Selfie to detect the approximate size, shape and color pigment of certain features, and estimated skin tone (collectively, “predicted facial attributes”). We then use the estimated facial points and predicted facial attributes together to suggest avatars that look more like you (“recommended avatars”). If you choose to, you can use the avatar editor to customize the recommended avatars, such as by adjusting the estimated skin tone, before selecting your final avatar. None of this information is used to identify you. You may be able to choose from a selection of standard body shape options for your avatar. To select which standard body shape options are presented to you, we may consider certain selections you may have made in your profile information, such as gender. Regardless of the options presented to you, you can use the avatar editor to further customize your recommended avatar, including by selecting from any available body shape option, before finalizing your avatar.

We will store your final avatar so that you can use it for interactive digital experiences across our services. Once your final avatar has been created, you can delete it at any time by clicking the trashcan icon in your Avatar Editor settings. Your final avatar will also be deleted if you delete your account. Once you delete your final avatar (or account), we no longer store this data.

After you select your final avatar, we will delete your estimated facial points within 14 days, and use your recommended avatars, predicted facial attributes and any customizations you make to understand how well Autogen worked for you and how we can further improve it. Your recommended avatars and predicted facial attributes will be disassociated from your account immediately and deleted within 90 days.

How we store your Selfie and how you can opt out or delete the Selfie

You can opt out of Selfie storage when you create your avatar. If you opt out, your Selfie will be deleted within 14 days and will not be used for product improvement.

If you do not opt out of Selfie storage, we will store your Selfie for up to 2 years from the time of capture. We will use your Selfie to evaluate how well the AutoGen feature works and to improve and train our systems, including machine learning models and algorithms.

You can access and delete your Selfie at any time by navigating to your “Personal Information” in Activity log and once deleted, this information will not be stored.

How can I navigate my profile and timeline using a screenreader on Facebook?

Navigate profile with screenreader

Navigate timeline with screenreader

What are ARIA landmarks?

Profile Heading Structure

Your profile has headings so you can navigate its different sections using screen readers:

  • Home is an h1 heading. This will take you out of the profile to your Feed.
  • Your name is an h2 heading. The information in your About section comes next, followed by your posts.
  • Friend requests, messages and notifications are h3 headings. These headings appear when you click one of the icons.
  • The chat sidebar is an h4 heading.
  • Posts on your timeline have h5 headings.
  • Ads have h6 headings.

Timeline ARIA Landmarks

ARIA document landmarks are used to represent important parts of timeline. Besides the main, banner, search and content info landmarks, different navigational landmarks are marked on timeline with appropriate labels. Stories on your timeline are marked as complementary landmarks to enable easy navigation with screen readers.

Note: If you’re navigating with a screen reader using headings, you’ll likely hear similar headings repeated because of what appears on the screen. If you continue reading below the heading, you’ll hear the updates from different posts.

How Facebook uses the email or mobile phone number on your profile

How Facebook uses my data?

Why does Facebook want my email?

How to add email to Facebook?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

How we use your email address or mobile phone number

We may use your email address or mobile phone number for purposes like:

  • Helping you log in. If you forget your password, you’ll need an updated phone number or email address to reset it. If you forget or lose access to the email address or phone number associated with your account, you can use one to look up the other.
  • Sending you email, WhatsApp and SMS notifications for updates about activity on your account, promotions and account safety. These notifications can help keep your account safe through features like two-factor authentication and alerts about unrecognized logins.
  • Providing and improving ads for you and others. We use your contact information alongside information we get from your activity to help us improve our ads services for everyone within the Facebook community.
  • Some of our security checkpoints can be difficult to pass using assistive technology. If you add a mobile number or email address to your Facebook account, you’ll have another way to verify your account if you need to pass any of these checkpoints. Keep in mind that these checkpoints may require internet access.

By entering your phone number, you authorize your mobile network provider to share data from your account and device to Facebook or its service providers for phone number verification and fraud prevention purposes. Learn more about the data we collect and how we use it in our Privacy Policy.

We never sell personal information, including your email address and phone number, to anyone. Keep in mind that you can control who can see your contact information and who we can suggest your profile to based on your phone number or email address. Learn more about how Facebook uses your phone number and email address in our Privacy Policy.

You may see an email or phone number suggested for you when we ask you to add your contact information. Emails or phone numbers shown in this way will only be added to your account if you choose to add them.

How we suggest email addresses or phone numbers

We may suggest an email address or phone number for you based on information we receive from sources such as:

  • Contact information provided by others on Facebook.
  • An email address or phone number that you entered previously but didn’t confirm.
  • Your mobile phone or tablet.

Reasons for confirming your mobile phone number

We may ask you to confirm your mobile phone number because:

  • You previously added the phone number we’re asking you to confirm.
  • Time has passed since you last added or updated your phone number.
  • We’ve received information from your device that helps us suggest the number connected to that device.
  • You haven’t added one yet, and we want to show you how.

More information

  • Add or remove a mobile phone number.
  • Add or remove an email address.
  • Adjust how you get notifications.
  • Recover your Facebook account if you can’t access your account email address or mobile phone number.

How usernames and user IDs are used on Facebook profiles

Create a username

Find my user ID

What is a username?

What is a user ID?

Usernames and user IDs are part of your public profile, which can help your friends find you on Facebook. A username is the web address for your profile or Page (example: Facebook.com/yourname).

Username

Your username is used across both Facebook and Messenger, and is often a variation of your name, like jane.doe33 or janedoe3. You can create your own username or choose a suggested username.

Some of the things you can do with usernames:

  • Create a custom link (for example, www.facebook.com/janedoe3) to your profile that you can share with your friends or post on external websites.
  • Access information about someone through Facebook. For example, if your username is janedoe3, your friends can go to “facebook.com/janedoe3” to see your profile and any public information.
  • Search for someone you want to start a chat with on Messenger.

You can control what information you share publicly. Learn how to adjust what people can see in your profile.

User ID

Your User ID is a string of numbers that doesn’t personally identify you but does connect to your Facebook profile and specific chats on Messenger. You have a User ID automatically, whether or not you choose to create a username. Learn how to find your user ID.

User IDs can:

  • Allow someone with the ID to see your Facebook profile, including any public information. Learn how to adjust what people can see in your profile.
  • Help other applications personalize your experience by connecting with your Facebook account. When you allow apps to connect with your Facebook account, they can use your user ID to see public information, like your public profile and your friend list.
  • When you run into issues with an app or game, your User ID can help the developer better investigate the problem to understand and address your specific concerns.

How your profile, settings, and content are shared between Forum and Facebook

Manage Forum settings

Sync Forum and Facebook

Forum dark mode

Forum push notifications

Forum is currently available for some people in the US, so it may not be available to you yet.

Forum, a Facebook app, brings all your Facebook Groups and group conversations into one place. Your profile, some settings, and your group content are also shared between Forum and Facebook.

Your profile on Forum

You log into Forum with your Facebook account. You don’t need a new, separate account.

When you join and log in, this information is shared:

  • Facebook profile: Forum uses your Facebook profile, including your profile name and picture.
  • Group membership and creation: If you join, leave, or create a group in one app, it updates in the other.
  • Identity: If you use a nickname or post anonymously in a Facebook group, it works the same way on Forum.

Your profile on Forum shows your activity and content across groups on both apps.

Your content

Posts, comments, and reactions are synced between Forum and Facebook Groups. This means:

  • Content posted in one place appears on both Forum and Facebook Groups.
  • Comments and reactions show up on both.
  • Changing a reaction or editing a post or comment changes it in both places.
  • Deleting a post in one app deletes it from both.
  • Posts you save on either app are shown on your profile on Forum.
  • If a post or comment is taken down in one app, it is taken down in the other.

Note: As with Facebook, Meta’s Terms of Service apply to your use of Forum, and you must follow Meta’s Community Standards. Information relating to your use of Forum will be processed in accordance with Meta’s Privacy Policy.

Your settings

Some settings apply to both Facebook and Forum, and are managed on Facebook or in Accounts Center. Other settings apply only to Forum and are managed on Forum.

Settings managed on Accounts Center

Facebook account settings, like username and password, apply to both Forum and Facebook, and can be managed on Accounts Center.

Settings managed on Facebook

These settings apply to both Facebook and Forum and can be managed on Facebook:

  • Blocking (you can see your blocked list in Forum, but you manage it on Facebook).
  • Content preferences (like political content)
  • Language and region
  • Tagging and mentions.
  • Notification settings for tagging or comments
  • Notifications settings per group
    • Note: Push notifications can also be managed on Forum.

Settings managed on Forum

You can find settings on Forum by tapping Menu, and then tapping Settings.

These settings only apply to Forum:

  • Dark mode
  • Media autoplay.
  • Device permissions.

These settings apply to both Facebook and Forum and can be managed on Forum:

  • Notification settings per group.

Keep your Facebook profile secure

Protect my password

Set up two-factor authentication

My account was hacked

I can’t create a passkey

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

We have seen evidence of malicious actors sending Business Manager partner requests that include phishing links. As we investigate this issue, we encourage you to exercise caution as these notifications come from a legitimate Meta domain (facebookmail.com). If you don’t know the person or business mentioned in the partner request, do not click on any links.

Here are a few things you can do to keep your account secure.

Protect your password

  • Avoid reusing the same password across multiple websites or apps. Don’t use your Facebook password anywhere else online, and never share it with other people.
  • Your password should be hard to guess, so don’t include your name or common words. Use unique, strong passwords or passphrases, for all of your accounts.
  • Learn more about creating a strong password.

Create a passkey

  • Passkeys are a safe and convenient alternative to passwords.
  • Passkeys are more secure than passwords, because they’re uniquely generated for every account and are less vulnerable to phishing.
  • Learn more about creating a passkey on Facebook.

Set up two-factor authentication and other security options

  • With two-factor authentication, you’ll be asked to enter a special login code each time someone tries to access your account from a browser or mobile device we don’t recognize.
  • If you’re logged into Facebook on a computer, you can use Security Checkup to review your security settings or to set up two factor authentication.
  • You can also get alerts about unrecognized logins.

Never share your login information

  • Scammers may create fake websites that look like Facebook and ask you to log in with your email and password.
  • Always check the website’s URL before you enter your login information. When in doubt, type www.facebook.com into your browser to get to Facebook.
  • Don’t forward emails from Meta to other people, since they may have sensitive information about your account.
  • Learn more about how to protect yourself from phishing.

Don’t accept friend requests from people you don’t know

  • Scammers may create fake accounts to friend people on Facebook.
  • Becoming friends with scammers on Facebook might allow them to spam your timeline, tag you in posts and send you malicious messages.

Never click suspicious links, even if they appear to come from a friend or a company you know

  • This includes links on Facebook (example: on posts), in emails or texts.
  • Keep in mind that Meta will never ask you for your password in an email.
  • If you suspect that a link on Facebook is suspicious, report it.

Watch out for malicious software

  • Malicious software can cause damage to a computer, server or computer network.
  • Learn the signs of an infected computer or device and how to remove malicious software.
  • Keep your web browser up to date and remove suspicious applications or browser add-ons.

Log out of Facebook when you use a computer you share with other people

  • If you forgot to log out on a device, you can log out remotely.

Learn what categories of information are available to export from your Facebook profile

Export my Facebook information

What information can I export?

Export data from other profiles

What are data logs?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you have additional Facebook profiles, you can export a copy of your Facebook information for each of your profiles using the Export your Information tool.

Please note, some information collected from your additional profiles, including ads information, can only be accessed by exporting your Facebook information for your main profile, which is the first profile you create when you sign up for Facebook.

We store different categories of information for different time periods, so you may not find all information from the time you joined Facebook. You won’t find information or content that you deleted because we delete that content from our servers.

Remember, you can access most of the content you post to a certain profile on Facebook by logging into your account and switching to that profile.

Keep in mind: The categories of information we receive, collect, and save may change over time. Learn more about your Facebook information in our Privacy Policy.

Depending on the information category you are interested in, we offer you a variety of tools to view, manage, and export your information.

Within the Your information and permissions section of your Accounts Center, you can export a copy of your Facebook information to a device or to an external service.

There are different types of information you can export to a device versus an external service.

Types of information you can export to a device

  • Your Facebook activity: Information and activity from different areas of Facebook, such as posts you’ve created, photos you’re tagged in, groups you belong to and more.
  • Personal Information: Information that you’ve provided when you set up your Facebook accounts and profiles.
  • Connections: Who and how you’ve connected with people on Facebook, including things like your friends and followers.
  • Logged Information: Information that Facebook logs about your activity, including things like your search history.
  • Security and Login Information: Technical information and logged activity related to your account.
  • Apps and Websites off of Facebook: Apps you own and activity we receive from apps and websites off of Facebook.
  • Preferences: Actions you’ve taken to customize your experience on Facebook.
  • Ad information: Your interactions with ads and advertisers on Facebook.
  • Data logs: Data logs are additional details we collect and store that can be associated with you. Learn more about exporting data logs.

When you export your information to an external service, you can export a copy of the original media you shared on Facebook like photos and videos.

Note: Your export won’t include information that someone else shared, like another person’s photos that you’re tagged in.

Learn more about managing your information and permissions in Accounts Center.

Additional Resources

These tools and resources are available in the Your activity section in your Facebook settings or in Your information and permissions in Accounts Center to help you view, manage and export your information.

  • Export your information: Export a copy of your Facebook information to a device or to an external service.
  • Activity Log: Within your profile, your activity log is a history of that profile’s activity on Facebook. Review and manage things you share, from posts you’ve commented on or liked to apps you have used or anything you’ve searched for. Learn more about your Activity Log.
  • External accounts: Manage your activity information sent from specific ad partners. When you connect external accounts from certain businesses to Meta technologies, we use your activity information sent from these businesses to show you ads.

Note: The categories of information we receive, collect, and save may change over time. Learn more about your Facebook information in our Privacy Policy.

Manage the About section of your Facebook profile

Who can see my About section?

Hide sections on my profile

Add info to my About section

Your About section of your profile helps you share what you care about with others, such as movies or books you’ve added, stories from apps and games you use and things you’ve followed. Learn how to update the About section of your profile.

If someone is in the audience of things you’ve added or the audience of stories shared by apps and games, they can see that stuff. From Facebook on a computer, you can edit the privacy of each section or you can choose to hide a section entirely.

Adding information to your profile’s About section

You can follow a Page for music, books, TV shows, movies, apps and games, or video games to add it to the About section of your profile. To remove something you’ve followed from your About section, you can unfollow the Page.

Some apps can add things to your About sections based on your in-app activity (example: some music streaming apps).

Show or hide sections of the About section of your profile

  1. From your Feed, click [your name] at the top of the left menu.
  2. Click More below your cover photo, and select Manage sections.
  3. Click the sections you want to add or remove.
  4. Click Save.

You can also hide a section by clicking at the top right of the section and selecting Hide section.

When you hide a section, the things you’ve followed are still visible to the audience they’re shared with elsewhere on Facebook, such as in Feed and search.

Learn more about editing or removing basic info on your profile.

Choose an audience for the things you’ve followed

  1. From your Feed, click [your name] at the top of the left menu.
  2. Click About below your cover photo and scroll to the Following section. If you don’t see Following, follow the above instructions to add it.
  3. Click at the top right of the section and select Edit privacy. Use the audience selector to choose who can see the different categories of things you’ve followed (example: movies). Remember, the people and Pages you follow can see that you’re following them.

If you’re sharing stories from an app or game, you can adjust the audience of future stories.

Keep in mind that when you share something on your timeline, the audience you choose can also see it in other places on Facebook, such as in Feed and search.

Manage top fan and rising fan badges for your Facebook Page or profile

Turn on fan badges

Set custom badge name

Remove a fan badge

We are gradually enabling Pages to set a custom top fan badge name, but this feature may not be available to all creators yet. Any information in this article about the top fan badge also applies to a custom top fan badge name. Please refer to the “Set a custom badge” section below to learn how to set up your new top fan badge name.

Top fan and rising fan badges are only available for:

  • Profiles with at least 10,000 followers
  • Pages and profiles with pro mode and at least 100 followers

People can become eligible for a top fan or rising fan badge on your Facebook Page or profile, including a pro mode profile, by being one of your most active engagers. They can be one of your most active engagers by reacting to, commenting on or sharing your content.

People who qualify for and then accept top fan or rising fan badges will have a badge next to their name when they comment with your Page or profile’s content. If someone is your friend on Facebook, they can’t become a top fan or rising fan of your Page or profile.

Turn top fan or rising fan badges on or off

Top fan and rising fan badges for your Page or profile are turned off by default. To turn them on or off:

For a Page or profile:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook, then click your name to go to your profile.
  2. Click Options below your profile name.
  3. Select Manage fan badges.
  4. Click Toggle to turn this setting on or off.

For a profile using pro mode:

  1. Click Menu at the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Professional Dashboard, then select Fan engagement tools.
  3. Toggle Top fan and/or Rising fan to turn the badges on or off.

Remove a badge from a top fan or rising fan

You can only remove a badge with the Facebook app for Android, iPhone or iPad.

  1. From the Facebook app, tap Menu.
  2. Go to the post on your Page or profile that has a comment from the top fan or rising fan that you want to remove.
  3. Next to their name, tap the top fan or rising fan badge.
  4. Tap Remove top fan badge or Remove rising fan badge.

Set a custom top fan badge name for your Page

If you’ve received a notification about setting up a custom badge, you’re eligible to set yours up now. You can also follow the instructions below to check your eligibility. We are gradually rolling out this feature, and it may not be available to all creators yet. Custom top fan badge names are currently only available for Pages.

If you select a custom name for your top fan badge, your top fans will receive a notification to accept this new badge, and they must accept it for the new badge name to display for them.

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page’s profile picture in the top right to go to your Page.
  4. Go to your badge settings.

It may take a few days for your custom badge name to reach all of your fans. You can only change your custom badge name once a month. You can also revert to the default top fan badge name at any time. If you do not set a custom badge name, there will be no change from the default top fan badge name.

View a list of your Page or profile’s top fan and rising fans and choose which badges you want to display

  1. From the Facebook app, tap Menu.
  2. Go to a comment from a top fan or rising fan and tap the badge next to their name.
  3. Select See All Top Fans or See All Rising Fans.
  4. Go to the profile whose badge you want to remove, then tap Options.
  5. Tap Remove top fan badge or Remove rising fan badge.

Names allowed on Facebook

What names are allowed?

I can’t change my name

What names are not allowed?

Can I use a nickname?

Facebook is a community where everyone uses the name they use in everyday life. This makes it so that you always know who you’re connecting with.

Not allowed in names

  • Symbols, numbers, unusual capitalization, repeating characters or punctuation.
  • Characters from multiple languages.
  • Titles of any kind (example: professional, religious).
  • Words or phrases instead of a name.
  • Offensive or suggestive words of any kind.

If your name follows our standards and you’re still having trouble changing it, find out why.

Keep in mind

  • The name on your profile should be the name that your friends call you in everyday life. This name should also appear on an ID or document from our ID list.
  • Nicknames can be used as a first or middle name if they’re a variation of your authentic name (example: Bob instead of Robert).
  • You can also list another name on your account (example: maiden name, nickname, professional name).
  • Profiles are for individual use only. You can create a Page for a business, organization or idea.
  • Pretending to be anything or anyone isn’t allowed.
