Permanently delete your Facebook profile

What happens if I delete?

Can I get my account back?

What happens to my photos?

How long does deletion take?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you want to take a break from Facebook instead of deleting your profile, you can learn how to temporarily deactivate your profile.

If you have additional Facebook profiles, you can also delete or deactivate all profiles under your main profile. Learn how to delete or deactivate additional profiles.

Before deleting your account, you may want to Export your information (like your photos and posts) from Facebook, and a copy of your Meta Quest information if you use your Facebook account to log into Meta Quest. After your account has been deleted, you won’t be able to retrieve anything you’ve added.

What happens if you permanently delete your Facebook profile

  • You won’t be able to reactivate your profile.
  • Your photos, posts, videos, and everything else you’ve added will be permanently deleted. You won’t be able to retrieve anything you’ve added.
  • You’ll no longer be able to use Facebook Messenger.
  • You won’t be able to use Facebook Login for other apps you may have signed up for with Facebook, like Spotify or Pinterest. You may need to contact the apps and websites to recover those accounts.
  • Some information, like messages you sent to friends, may still be visible to them after you delete your profile. Copies of messages you have sent are stored in your friends’ inboxes.
  • If you use Facebook to log into Meta Quest, deleting your Facebook profile will also delete your Meta Quest information. This includes your app purchases and your achievements. You will no longer be able to return any apps and will lose any existing store credits.
  • Pages that only you control will also be deleted. If you don’t want your Page to be deleted, you can give someone else full control of your Page. You’ll then be able to delete your account without deleting the Page.

What if you don’t want all your content deleted, but you want to take a break from Facebook

You can take a break from Facebook and temporarily deactivate your profile. When you temporarily deactivate your profile:

  • People won’t be able to see or go to your Facebook profile.
  • Your photos, posts and videos won’t be deleted.
  • You can still use Facebook Messenger. Your profile picture will still be visible in your conversations and people will still be able to search for you by name to send you a message. You will continue to appear to friends on Facebook in places where they can message you.
  • You will not be able to use Facebook to access Meta Quest Products or your Meta Quest information.
  • Pages that only you control will also be deactivated. If your Page is deactivated, people can’t see your Page or find your Page if they search for it. If you don’t want your Page to be deactivated, you can give someone else full control of your Page. You’ll then be able to deactivate your profile without deactivating the Page.
  • You can choose to come back whenever you want.

Delete your Facebook

If you see Manage account at the bottom of Accounts Center:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings and privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center at the top left of your screen.
  4. Click Manage accounts.
  5. Click Manage next to the account type you want to delete.
  6. Click Deactivation or deletion.
  7. Click Continue then follow the instructions to confirm.

If you see Accounts at the bottom of Accounts Center:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings and privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center at the top left of your screen.
  4. Click Personal details.
  5. Click Account ownership and control.
  6. Click Deactivation or deletion.
  7. Click profile you want to delete, then click Continue.
  8. Follow the instructions on the screen to delete your profile.

Canceling your Facebook account deletion

If it’s been less than 30 days since you initiated the deletion, you can cancel your account deletion. After 30 days, your account and all your information will be permanently deleted, and you won’t be able to retrieve your information.

It may take up to 90 days from the beginning of the deletion process to delete all the things you’ve posted. While we’re deleting this information, it’s not accessible to other people using Facebook.

Copies of your information may remain after the 90 days in backup storage that we use to recover in the event of a disaster, software error, or other data loss event. We may also keep your information for things like legal issues, terms violations, or harm prevention efforts. Learn more about our Privacy Policy.

To cancel your account deletion:

  1. Log into your Facebook account within 30 days of deleting your account.
  2. Click Cancel deletion.

Note: The number of days that you can cancel an account deletion varies by region.

Profile Transparency section on Pro Mode

Where is transparency section?

What info is shown?

What is primary country location?

Hide my primary location

Pro mode is a state of your main profile that offers access to professional tools like monetization and content insights.

In an effort to increase accountability and transparency, Facebook is showing more information about profiles and profile owners in the Profile Transparency section on pro mode profiles.

Where can I find the Profile Transparency section on a profile?

To access this information as a profile visitor:

  1. Go to a profile by clicking its name in your Feed or searching for it.
  2. Click on Profile in Intro section.

This information is also visible when viewing a profile in the Ad Library.

What information is shown in the Profile Transparency section?

The information in the Profile Transparency section comes from Facebook and includes:

  • The date the profile was created.
  • The primary country locations of the profile owner.
  • Whether the profile is running ads.

What is primary country location?

Meta determines the primary country location of a profile owner by a person’s information and activity across Meta technologies. This includes the stated location on their Facebook profile, and device and connection information.

Sometimes Facebook can’t share the exact country location of a profile owner because the account may be too new, or we haven’t determined their location yet.

However, we will not show a primary country location for any disabled accounts or for system users. You can learn more about System Users in the Business Help Center.

Note: If your location is inaccurate, turning on Location Services may help Facebook determine your location. Facebook uses Location Services to help you check in, find local events and get better ads.

What if I don’t want this information on my profile?

The Profile Transparency section itself cannot be removed or hidden. You can remove or request to remove some information.

You can submit a request for Facebook to hide your primary country location because of special circumstances including risks to personal safety. If your primary country location is hidden, people visiting your profile will see Location hidden by profile owner below Profile Info.

See if your Facebook profile or Page is available for people under 18

My profile is unavailable

My Page is unavailable

Request a review

Facebook and Messenger 13+ default settings aim to show teens content that is similar to what they would see in content rated ages 13+ and limit their ability to message or interact with profiles and Pages that primarily share content inappropriate for teens. If you’re a creator, you may want to check if your profile or Page has been hidden for people under 18.

If your content, profile or Page is about topics that may not follow our age-appropriate guidelines, your profile or Page may not be available for people under 18. This means that without their parent’s or guardian’s permission to change out of the Ages 13+ content setting, people under 18 may not be able to:

  • See your profile picture, bio, profile, stories, posts or reels
  • Follow or friend you
  • Message you or receive messages from you. You both may be able to see message history
  • Access or join your Broadcast channel

To review your profile status:

  1. From your profile, tap in the upper right hand corner.
  2. In the menu select Profile status.
  3. If you see a message under Profile and account issues that says Age-inappropriate content and Your profile is unavailable to people under 18 then your content and profile are not available for people under 18.

To review your Page status:

  1. From your Page, tap in the upper right hand corner.
  2. In the menu select Page status.
  3. If you see a message under Page and account issues that says Your Page is unavailable to people under 18, then your content and page are not available for people under 18.

If you’d like your account to be accessible for people under 18, you can tap See Options to delete the content that does not meet our age-appropriate guidelines

We’ll review the updates you made and if your content and profile or Page align with our age-appropriate guidelines, we’ll update your status. Note that this could take up to 7 days to complete.

If you think your content doesn’t violate our guidelines, you may be able to request a review of your profile or Page without deleting your content . To do this, follow the steps above or tap on the Your page is unavailable to people under 18 notification or navigate to Page/Profile. Tap Request review at the bottom of the next page and follow the instructions.

Take a break from someone’s profile in Facebook

See less of someone

Limit who sees my posts

Edit who sees past posts

Take a break from a profile on Facebook who you want to see less.

You can take a break from someone’s profile on Facebook when you change your relationship status to single, divorced or leave it blank. You can also take a break from a profile you’re friends with on Facebook.

When you take a break, you’ll be able to:

  • See less of someone’s profile: Limit where you see someone’s profile on Facebook. If you choose to see them less, their posts and posts they’re tagged in won’t appear in your Feed and you won’t be prompted to message them or tag them in photos. To see their posts again, you can follow them.

  • Limit a profile’s ability to see your posts and posts you’re tagged in: Hide your posts from the profile you want to take a break from. They’ll be added to your Restricted List and will only see posts you tag them in or share publicly.

  • Edit who can see past posts: Limit who can see posts including photos, status updates, videos and more. You can limit posts you’re tagged in or that you’ve tagged someone else in by changing your privacy settings.

    These posts can only be seen by the profiles that are tagged in them. These posts won’t appear on your timeline anymore but will still appear on other profiles’ timelines and search results unless the profile who originally posted removes the content.

    You’ll also be removed as a contributor from any shared albums with the profile you want to take a break from.

If you’re looking for other ways to take a break from someone, you can change your profile picture or archive your message thread with their profile.

Keep in mind that you can always block or unfriend someone’s profile on Facebook.

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Facebook settings may not look the same for everyone. If you have additional Facebook profiles and delete or deactivate your Facebook account, you also delete or deactivate all profiles under your account. Learn how to delete or deactivate individual profiles.

Deactivate your Facebook profile

If you see Manage accounts at the bottom of Accounts Center:

If you see Accounts at the bottom of Accounts Center:

When your account is deactivated

  • No one else can see your profile.
  • Some information, like messages you sent to friends, may still be visible.
  • Your friends may still see your name in their friends list. This is only visible to your friends, and only from their friends list.
  • Group admins may still be able to see your posts and comments, along with your name.

Keep in mind that if you choose to keep Messenger active or are logged into Messenger when you deactivate your Facebook account, then Messenger will remain active. Learn how to deactivate Messenger.

When your Facebook account is deactivated, but you still have Messenger

  • You can still chat with friends on Messenger.
  • Your Facebook profile picture will still be visible in your conversations on Messenger.
  • Using Messenger will not reactivate that Facebook account, but your Facebook friends will still be able to message you.
  • Other people can search for you to send you a message.
  • Parental Supervision is not available.

Reactivating your account

If you’d like to come back to Facebook after you’ve deactivated your account, you can reactivate your account at any time by logging back into Facebook or by using your Facebook account to log in somewhere else. Remember, you’ll need to have access to the email or mobile number you use to log in to complete the reactivation.

Learn how to permanently delete your account.

If you don’t want your Page to be deactivated, you can give someone else full control of your Page. You’ll then be able to deactivate your account without deactivating the Page.

Turn pro mode on or off for your Facebook profile

Turn on pro mode

What changes with pro mode?

What happens if I turn off pro mode?

Pro mode gives you access to professional tools and insights that can help you build your professional presence from your Facebook profile. If you’re eligible, you can access monetization products to generate income from your content.

When you turn on pro mode, these tools are added to your existing Facebook profile experience. You don’t create a new profile. You can build your professional presence and maintain your personal friends and family experience from one place on Facebook.

You can turn pro mode on or off at any time. Learn more about pro mode.

When you turn on pro mode

Things that stay the same:

  • Your current friends and profile content won’t change.

Changes when you turn on pro mode:

  • You’ll be able to view content and audience insights to track your progress.
  • You’ll gain access to enhanced safety features such as Moderation Assist.
  • Your content will become eligible for discovery opportunities on Facebook.
  • Your Who can follow me preference will be set to Public, allowing fans to connect with you and see more of your content. You can change this in your settings.
  • If you’re eligible, you’ll be able to access monetization products that help you generate income from your content.

Turn on pro mode

  1. Click your profile photo in the top right corner of Facebook, then click your name.
  2. Click Options below your cover photo.
  3. Click Turn on pro mode.
  4. Click Turn on.

When you turn off pro mode

Some things stay the same:

  • Your current friends and profile content won’t change.
  • Your Who can follow me preference will change to Friends.
  • You will lose any followers who are not your friends. You can allow public followers again by turning on pro mode.

Some things change:

  • Your existing content or audience insights won’t be available.
  • You’ll lose access to enhanced safety features such as Moderation Assist.
  • You’ll no longer be eligible for discovery opportunities on Facebook.
  • If you’re eligible for monetization, you’ll receive pending payouts or bonuses, but future bonuses and payouts will be paused.
  • If you have content protection turned on, you lose the ability to protect your original content. Protection for all of your content will be removed, including any protected content that currently has an ownership issue.

Turn off pro mode

  1. Click your profile photo in the top right corner of Facebook, then click your name.
  2. Click Options below your cover photo.
  3. Click Turn off pro mode.
  4. Click Continue, then click Turn off.

Unblock a Facebook profile, Page, or nickname

Unblock a profile

Unblock a Page

Unblock a nickname

I can’t unblock someone

When you unblock a profile or Page, that profile or Page will be able to see your posts on Facebook that you share with the public. An unblocked profile won’t automatically become your friend on Facebook, and you won’t automatically like or follow a Page you unblock. If you want to become friends with a profile you’ve unblocked, you’ll need to send a friend request to that profile. When you unblock a nickname in a Facebook group, you will be able to see their content in that group, and they’ll be able to tag you and interact with your content in the group.

Note: If you unblock a profile or Page, you won’t be able to block it again for a few days. This waiting requirement does not apply to blocking nicknames.

What happens to your Facebook profile if you pass away

Memorialize my profile

What happens to my profile?

Add a legacy contact

Delete my profile after death

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Choosing your legacy contact is currently only available for your main profile and doesn’t apply to additional Facebook profiles. You can choose to either appoint a legacy contact to look after your memorialized main profile or have your account permanently deleted from Facebook.

If you don’t choose to have your account permanently deleted, only your main profile will be memorialized if we become aware of your passing.

Memorialized profiles

Memorialized profiles are a place for friends and family to gather and share memories after a person has passed away. Memorialized profiles have the following key features:

  • The word Remembering will be shown next to the person’s name on their profile.
  • Depending on the privacy settings of the profile, friends can share memories on the memorialized timeline.
  • Content the person shared (example: photos, posts) stays on Facebook and is visible on Facebook to the audience it was shared with.
  • Memorialized profiles don’t appear in suggestions for People You May Know, ads or birthday reminders.
  • No one can log into the account of a memorialized profile.
  • Memorialized profiles that don’t have a legacy contact can’t be changed.
  • Pages with a sole admin whose profile was memorialized will be removed from Facebook if we receive a valid memorialization request.
  • Groups with a sole admin whose profile was memorialized will be paused if we receive a valid memorialization request.

Legacy contacts

A legacy contact is someone you choose to look after your profile if it’s memorialized. We strongly suggest setting a legacy contact so your profile can be managed once it’s memorialized. You can change your legacy contact to someone else at any time.

A legacy contact can accept friend requests on behalf of a memorialized profile, change the profile picture, change the cover photo and even have it deleted whenever they choose.

They can also download a copy of what you’ve shared on Facebook, if you have this feature turned on.

To remove a legacy contact without choosing a new one, select Delete after death. This deletes an account immediately and completely after we receive proof of death, so we strongly suggest you share this preference with your loved ones.

Once Memorialization is initiated, you must always have one of the options selected. If you do not select either option, anyone within the proper documents can request to memorialize your account after you pass away.

Note:

  • No changes can be made to memorialized accounts that do not have legacy contacts.
  • You can’t select a legacy contact if you are a minor. The age at which you are no longer considered a minor varies by region.

Learn more about what legacy contacts can do and how to add a legacy contact to your account.

Deleting your account when you pass away

You can choose to have your account permanently deleted should you pass away. This means that when someone lets us know that you’ve passed away, all of your messages, photos, posts, comments, reactions and info will be immediately and permanently removed from Facebook. Your main profile and any additional Facebook profiles will also be deleted.

We strongly suggest you share this preference with your loved ones.

To un-select Delete after death, you must select a legacy contact.

Note: If you are a minor and choose the Delete after death option, you will not be able to change this setting until you are no longer considered a minor.

Manage your memorialization preference in Accounts Center

  1. From your main profile, click your profile photo in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts Center, then click Profiles and personal details.
  4. Click Account ownership and control, then click Memorialization and select your account.
  5. Click Memorialize account or Delete after death. If you choose to memorialize your account, you’ll need to select a legacy contact to manage your account.
  6. Click Next to confirm.

Note: Not everyone will be able to access this setting in Meta Account or Accounts Center at this time.

Request that your account be deleted

  1. From your main profile, click your profile photo in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Select Settings & Privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Click Accounts center, then click Personal details.
  4. Click Account ownership and control, then click Memorialization and select your profile.
  5. Click Delete after death, then click Next to confirm.

For friends and family

If you’d like to create another place for people on Facebook to share memories of your loved one, we suggest creating a group.

Learn how to request the memorialization of an account or how to request the removal of a deceased person’s account from Facebook.

Allow another Facebook Page to crosspost your Page’s videos

Set up crossposting

Crossposting videos not working

Crossposting violations

I can’t crosspost videos

Crossposting is a way to use videos across multiple Pages. Before you crosspost videos, you’ll need to establish a crossposting relationship with another Page.

Keep in mind:

  • Buying and selling cross posts is a violation of our Partner Monetization Policies.
  • Crossposting should not be used to gain likes or followers for Pages with no clear relationship.
  • Posts that don’t follow our Partner Monetization Policies may be demonetized, and you won’t be able to run ads with the post.
  • You should only give an admin or editor role to individuals you know and trust.
  • Crossposting partners with your Page should be listed as Affiliated Pages in Business Manager. Pages with a high number of views from crossposts are required to have Business Manager associations with their crossposting partners in order to monetize crossposts.

If you have Facebook access to a Page, you can switch into the Page on Facebook and follow the instructions below to request a crossposting relationship with another Page. If you already have Facebook access to the other Page, you don’t need to establish a crossposting relationship and can go directly to Creator Studio to crosspost videos.

Request a crossposting relationship with another Page on Facebook

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click your Page photo in the top right.
  4. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  5. In the left menu, click Media.
  6. In the Crossposting section, type the Page’s name or Facebook URL you want to add next to Add Page, then select the Page you want to add.
  7. For Live Videos, select whether you’d like to:
    • Allow the other Page to crosspost their live video to your Page without further approval.
    • Require the other Page’s crossposted live videos to be approved by someone with Facebook access or task access to your Page before being crossposted to your Page.
  8. Click Next.
  9. Follow the instructions on the screen, then click Done.

The other Page must confirm the crossposting relationship by adding your Page to its crossposting settings. To help the Page confirm the relationship, you can copy and send the confirmation link to someone that manages the Page.

After a crossposting relationship has been established, people with Facebook access or task access to a Page must go to Creator Studio to crosspost videos and manage crossposting.

Change the remix settings on a reel you shared to Facebook

Enable remixing on my reel

Change remix settings later

Change default remix setting

Disable original audio use

When you share a reel on Facebook, you can enable or disable remixing of that reel. Only reels that you share as public can be remixed.

Someone can create a reel based on yours if you allow remixing, and you’ll be credited as the original creator.

The owner of a remix can download your reel as part of their remix.

You can only enable or disable remixing on Facebook when you create your reel. If you want to change your remix setting later, you can do so from the Facebook app for iPhone and Android, or from Meta Business Suite.

Using Facebook to change the remix settings on a reel you shared to Facebook isn’t available to everyone yet. If you’re unable to change your remix settings, use the Facebook app for iPhone and Android.

Allow remixing for a reel you’re creating

  1. Create a Facebook reel.
  2. Toggle Enable remixing.

Change your remix settings on the Facebook app for iPhone and Android

  1. From your Feed, tap Menu.
  2. Tap your name to go to your profile.
  3. Tap Reels, above Details.
  4. Tap the reel you’d like to change.
  5. Tap Options in the bottom right.
  6. Tap Enable Remixing or Disable Remixing.

Change how others can use your original audio and remix your future public reels

You can change how other people are able to use your original audio and remix your future public reels. Please note that any changes to these settings will only apply to new reels you share on Facebook, and will not apply to any reels you’ve previously shared.

To change your settings:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & privacy, and then click Settings.
  3. Under Audience and visibility, click Reels.
  4. Click Allow others to use your original audio and remix your future public reels?.
  5. Select one of the settings:
    • Remixing and original audio use: Allow remixing and use of original audio.
    • Original audio use only: Allow use of original audio only. Remixing is not allowed.
    • Don’t allow: Don’t allow remixing or use of original audio.

You can also go to the settings for an individual reel and change its remix settings.

To change the settings for an individual reel:

  1. From your Feed, click your profile picture and name in the left panel of Facebook.
  2. On your profile timeline, scroll to the reel you want to modify the original audio and remix settings for.
  3. Click on the reel to display the video player screen.
  4. Click select Remixing and use of original audio.
  5. Select one of the settings:
  • Remixing and original audio use: Allow remixing and use of original audio.
  • Original audio use only: Allow use of original audio only. Remixing is not allowed.
  • Don’t allow: Don’t allow remixing or use of original audio.

If you have a Facebook Page for your business, you can also update the original audio and remix settings for your reels in Meta Business Suite by going to Content and then Posts & reels.

Keep in mind (Remix)

  • Before you select a default remix setting, remixing is enabled by default for all public reels. You can disable and re-enable remixing for each reel at anytime. You can choose a default remix setting on the Facebook app for iPhone and Android.
  • If you delete your reel, all remixes of it will be deleted.
  • If you delete your Facebook account, all remixes of your reels will be deleted.
  • Remixes will be deleted if you change the audience of your reel to an audience other than Public for longer than 24 hours.
  • If you disable remixing of your reel, any existing remixes of it will not be deleted. New remixes can’t be created.
  • If you lock your profile, any public reels you published will be set to Friends only. Remixes of those reels will be deleted.
  • If you unlock your profile, any reels that were public when you locked it will be set back to public. Reels that you enabled remixing on will be able to be remixed.
  • If a remix of your reel is not set to public, you may not be able to view it. You may not be notified when another person remixes your reel.
  • If you block someone on Facebook who’s remixed your reels, their remixes will be removed. If you unblock them, their remixes will be restored.

Keep in mind (Original Audio)

  • You can change the audience of your reel at any time, which will affect how your original audio is used. If you set your reel to any audience besides Public, any reels that use your original audio will be muted.
  • If you change a reel’s audience to Public and the original audio from your reel was previously used in someone else’s reel, that reel will be unmuted.
  • If someone creates a reel using your original audio and they download their reel, the downloaded version will be muted.
  • If you change a reel’s audience to Public, and you didn’t add music or someone else’s audio, other people can use your reel’s original audio in their reels.
  • If you delete a reel with your original audio, any reels using the same audio will be muted.
  • If you lock your profile, any public reels will be set to Friends Only. Any reels that use your original audio will be muted and your original audio attribution will be removed.
  • If you unlock your profile, any reels that were public when you locked it will be set back to public. Any reels that use your original audio will be unmuted and your original audio attribution will be added.

Available audiences

Why won’t my reel upload?

Update (September 2025): Facebook has unified all video uploads under the Reels format. All videos posted to Facebook will be shared as reels, regardless of length or orientation. This unifies the video experience for creators and viewers. Learn more about this change.

Privacy and sharing

All videos you post on Facebook (except Stories and Live) are now Reels and follow your selected privacy settings. If your account or a specific reel is set to private (or non-public), only your chosen audience (such as your friends or followers) can view your content. People who do not follow you will not be able to see your Reels, use original audio from your content, or share your Reels with others who are not in your audience.

  • Original audio from your private or non-public Reels cannot be reused by others.
  • Your Reels cannot be shared with people outside your selected audience.
  • If you change a Reel from public to private, any content that reused your original audio will be muted for users who are not in your audience.

Reels on Facebook are now unified videos—any length, any aspect ratio, and can combine multiple clips. You can share your reels publicly or with your friends on Facebook. Advanced editing (effects, music, multi-clip) is available on mobile.

Upload a video as a reel

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook, then click your name to go to your profile.
  2. Click Reels, then click Create reel.
  3. Click Add video, then select a video on your computer. Click Next.
  4. (Optional) Trim your video, add a description, hashtags, or select a cover image.
  5. Click Next.
  6. Click Describe your reel… to add a description or any hashtags. Hashtags help other people find your reel when searching. Descriptions are optional.
  7. Select the audience for your reel by clicking on your currently selected audience. Click the audience you’d like to use, then click Done. If your profile is locked, you can’t select a public audience. Audience options may include:
    • Public: Anyone, including people off of Facebook, can see your reel.
    • Friends: Only your friends can see your reel.
    • Friends except: Your friends, except for the friends you choose, can see your reel.
  8. Switch remixing on or off. If remixing is enabled and your reel is public, others can use your original audio or clips in their own reels.
  9. Once you’ve selected your options, click Publish to share your reel.

Use mobile app for advanced editing

To create a reel with effects, music, or to use multiple clips in a single reel, use the Facebook app for iPhone and Android.

Crosspost another Facebook Page’s video

Crosspost a video

Crosspost a Live video

Change video captions

I can’t crosspost a video

You can crosspost another Facebook Page’s videos in Meta Business Suite. You can visit Meta Business Suite on a computer or download the Meta Business Suite app for iOS or Android.

Crosspost another Facebook Page’s video

  1. Log into Facebook, then click your profile photo in the top right.
  2. Click See all profiles, then select the Page you want to switch into.
  3. Click Professional Dashboard in the left menu.
  4. Click Content in the left menu.
  5. Click to select the videos you’d like to crosspost.

Crosspost another Page’s non-live video

For non-live video, you can only crosspost another Page’s video if:

  • You’ve established a crossposting relationship with the Page. (Remember that if you already have Facebook access on the Page, you don’t need to establish a crossposting relationship.)
  • The Page has allowed you to crosspost the video.

The Page that owns the video can see posts you’ve used the video in and their insights. If the Page removes your crossposting permissions, posts with the video may be unpublished or removed from your Page.

Captions that are added when a video is first uploaded will be carried over to any crossposts. Captions added through “Edit Video” will not appear in any crossposts. You can also change captions on a crossposted video by uploading a new SubRip (.SRT) file.

Crosspost another Page’s Live video

Only live videos created via the Live API are eligible for live crossposting, and live video from a mobile device can’t be crossposted.

Even if you choose to manually post another Page’s live videos but you’re a shared admin or editor of both Pages, the crossposted live video will automatically be posted to your Page.

Note: Each live crosspost is treated as a separate broadcast on each Page. Comments and reactions from the other Page’s live video won’t appear in your Page’s crossposted video, and viewers can’t see where the original live video is coming from.

Metadata and Targeting

If you want a description, title or targeting setting for a crossposted live video on your Page that is different from the original live video before it is shown to the public, make sure you’ve chosen to manually post the other Page’s live videos and that both Pages don’t share an admin or editor.

If a crossposted live video has targeting different from the original live video, select manual crossposting to ensure that people with access don’t have to change targeting settings in real-time and followers of Pages don’t receive a live video notification for a broadcast that they likely can’t see.

Go live on Facebook using streaming software

Set up live stream

Choose streaming software

My stream key is compromised

Download streaming software to broadcast your computer screen or use broadcasting equipment for live streaming on Facebook.

Account requirements

Your account must meet these requirements before you can go live on Facebook:

  • Your account must be at least 60 days old.
  • Your Page or professional mode profile must have at least 100 followers.
  • To go live from a Page, you need to have Facebook access or task access to create content.

Choose and download streaming software

Use streaming software (also called encoding software) to broadcast your computer screen or use broadcasting equipment for live streaming. Choose software that fits your needs. Popular options include:

  • Open Broadcaster Software
  • Streamlabs OBS

View a full list of streaming software partners.

Set up your live stream

  1. Go to facebook.com/live/create.

  2. In the left menu, click Choose where to post and select where your live video will appear.

  3. Click Go live.

  4. In the Select a video source section, choose Streaming software.

  5. (Optional) In Advanced Settings, turn on the Persistent stream key option if you want to reuse this stream key in the future.

  6. Copy the Server URL and Stream key (or persistent stream key) shown by Facebook.

  7. Configure your streaming software:

  8. Locate the stream/encoder settings in your streaming software.

  9. Set the type to Custom Streaming Server or RTMP Server.

  10. Paste the Server URL and Stream key you copied from Facebook.

  11. Enable a secure connection (RTMPS) if your software supports it.

  12. Start streaming from your software, a live preview will appear on Facebook.

  13. Add details: Write a description and title for your stream in the Add post details section.

  14. Click Go Live Now to start, or use the scheduling option (Later) to set a specific broadcast date and time.

Audience interaction

  • Viewers can react and leave comments during your live stream.
  • You can reply in chat or respond during your stream.
  • If you stream to your timeline, you can choose your audience privacy settings.
  • After your stream ends, the video will remain as a post on Facebook where it was shared.

Stream key security

  • Never share your Stream Key or Persistent Stream Key. Anyone with these details can stream to your post.
  • Standard stream keys cannot be reused unless you use the persistent stream key feature.
  • You may only have one live video at a time with a persistent stream key.

Add your live stream to your website

To embed your Facebook live stream on a website:

  1. Choose the Page for your live stream.
  2. In Settings, go to Stream.
  3. Switch on Embed Live Video.
  4. Click Get Embed Code and copy the code for use on your website.

Video format guidelines

  • Follow Facebook’s video format guidelines for live streaming.
  • Verify your encoding software’s documentation for more on custom RTMP and supported formats.

Additional streaming options

You can also live stream through the Facebook Live API or via publishing tools.

All broadcasts must comply with Facebook’s live streaming policies.

How video selfie age verification works on Facebook

Take a video selfie

How age verification works

My video selfie failed

How long does verification take?

If you are under 18 and trying to change your age on Facebook to over 18 or access a Facebook feature or product intended for adults, you will be asked to give us additional information to help verify your age.

There are a few different ways you can verify your age:

  1. Take a video selfie
  2. Upload your ID

How your age is verified

If you choose to take a video selfie, we partner with vendors who use technology to estimate your age. After you’ve taken a video selfie, we’ll share an image from that selfie with the vendor. Our vendors’ technology only estimates age. It can’t identify specific people.

Once your age has been estimated and shared with us, we will delete the image within 30 days. We don’t share any other information about you with the vendor.

How to take the selfie

If you choose to take a video selfie to verify your age, you’ll see instructions on your screen for how to take the selfie. If you haven’t used the camera on Facebook before, we’ll ask you for permission to use the camera so you can take the selfie.

When you take the selfie, make sure your whole face is visible and that you have enough light for the camera. Avoid wearing anything that blocks your face, like a mask or hat. You’ll be asked to move your face in different directions, such as to the right and left and up and down.

Once you have taken the selfie, you’ll see a screen to submit your selfie. Once you have submitted your selfie, you can keep using Facebook or exit the app.

It can take up to 20 minutes to verify your age. You will get a notification with the outcome of the verification.

Your watch history

Your watch history is never visible to others on Facebook. However, if you take a specific action related to a reel, live video, or a Page (example: liking a reel), that action may be visible to people on Facebook.

Your activity

When you watch reels or videos, the following actions may be seen by others depending on your privacy settings:

  • Liking or following a Page: When you like or follow a Page, your friends may see your name when they come across that Page (example: “[Name] and 4 other friends like this”).
  • Liking a reel or live video: When you like a reel or video, your name may be visible when your friends come across that specific content (example: “[Name] also liked this”).
  • Commenting on a Page, reel, or live video: Any comments you make can be seen by anyone on Facebook.
  • Sharing an episode, series, reel, or live video: You can choose to share content to your timeline or in a direct message to a person or group. When you do this, it will be visible to your selected audience.

Learn more about watching reels and videos on Facebook.

I’m having problems live streaming to Facebook

My live stream isn’t working

Check my stream key

My internet connection is bad

Disable ad blocking software

If you’re attempting to live stream to Facebook and having problems:

  • Make sure you use the Google Chrome web browser to go live from your computer.
  • Keep in mind that it may take 10 seconds for the video stream to appear in the preview area after you’ve started your live stream.
  • Check that the server URL and/or stream key were copied correctly.
  • Make sure that you have a reliable internet connection.
  • Disable ad blocking software or browser plugins that could prevent the video player from loading.
  • Check your firewall settings and make sure that RTMP is allowed.
  • Make sure that the server URL and key aren’t older than 7 days. If they’re older than 7 days, create a new URL and key.

Audio not playing long enough

If you’re having trouble adding audio to your reel, or with audio in a reel you’ve created, try these troubleshooting steps.

My audio is muted on a published reel

If your published reel has been muted, there may be an issue with music rights. When the music rights change on Facebook for a song you’ve added to your reel, your reel won’t be recommended to other people. Other people can still find your reel on your profile or page. When your reel is viewed, it will be muted. Learn more on the Meta Business Help Center.

Reels that have been muted will be labeled with .

If your reel has been muted, you can replace the music in your reel using the Facebook app for iPhone and Android. You can’t replace the music on a reel that isn’t muted.

Learn how to replace the music on your muted reel.

Note: Licensed music rights are based on the location of the reel’s viewer. If your reel is muted in your country, it may still be unmuted for people in a different country. If someone is in a different country from you and rights have changed in that country, your reel may not be recommended to them and it may be muted. You won’t be notified in either of these cases.

Learn about and manage suggested products on Facebook Reels

Hide suggested products

Why am I seeing this?

Report a product

To help you discover new things on Facebook, you may see suggested product content that’s relevant to you and are influenced by things such as your activity across Meta Products on Reels. You may see some suggested products in Reels that are similar to the items featured in the Reel.

What influences suggested product content

Many factors influence which suggested product content you see, and some factors have more influence than others. Some of the most important factors include:

  • Location: You may see suggested content based on where you are and what people near you are interacting with on Facebook.
  • Ads: Your interactions with ads, including ads you view or engage with.
  • Products: You may see suggested content based on products or categories you’ve shown interest in.
  • Your activity on Meta Products: For example, your posts, likes or comments across Instagram, Facebook and Threads as well as activity by others with similar interests.

Facebook’s standards for suggested content

Our goal is to make recommendations that are relevant to each person who sees them. Through our Recommendations Guidelines, we work to avoid making recommendations that could be low-quality, objectionable, or particularly sensitive. We also avoid making recommendations that may be inappropriate for younger users. Products we recommend for you in suggested content are not ads. They are shown to help you discover products that may be relevant to you based on your interests and activity across Meta technologies.

Manage what you see

You have control over which content is suggested for you in the Facebook app for Android or iOS.

To manage suggested product content:

  1. On the Facebook app, go to the suggested product content that you want to manage, then tap Options.
  2. Select how you want to manage this content:
    • Select Show more to see similar products.
    • Select Show less to see less of a suggested product.
    • Select Hide product to see less content like this.
    • Select Report product if there is a problem with the product.

Select Why am I seeing this product? to learn more about why you may be seeing a product.

Why can’t I see reels insights?

Update (September 2025): All videos on Facebook are now Reels. All videos posted to Facebook will be shared as reels, regardless of length or orientation. This unifies the video experience for creators and viewers. Learn more about this change.

Insights are presented as reels insights, which exclude live videos and Stories. This provides a unified view of your reels performance, simplifying analysis and optimization of your content strategy.

Insight availability

The availability of insights depends on the type of account you have and the number of followers you have.

Requirements for personal profiles

To view insights for your reels on a personal Facebook profile:

  1. Enable pro mode. This grants access to more detailed content performance data.
  2. Ensure your profile has a minimum of 1000 followers.

Access insights on your personal profile

  1. Navigate to your Facebook profile.
  2. Scroll down to the reel you wish to analyze.
  3. Click See insights. You will be directed to the Insights page, displaying metrics such as:

    • Reach
    • Average watch time

Access insights for your Page’s reels in Meta Business Suite

Insights for your Page’s reels can be found in Meta Business Suite, accessible via computer or the mobile app (iOS and Android).

To view insights for your Page’s reels:

  1. Log in to Facebook and click your profile picture in the top right corner.
  2. Select “See all profiles” and then choose the desired Page.
  3. Click “Professional dashboard” in the left-hand menu.
  4. Click “Meta Business Suite” in the left-hand menu.
  5. Select “Insights” from the left-hand menu.
  6. Use the filters to analyze reel performance based on length.

To access performance data for a specific reel on your Page:

  1. Go to Facebook and click your profile picture, located in the top right corner.
  2. Select “See all profiles” and choose the relevant Page.
  3. In the left-hand menu, click “Professional dashboard”.
  4. From the left-hand menu, click “Meta Business Suite”.
  5. Choose “Insights” from the left-hand menu.
  6. Select Content.
  7. Click the Posts and Stories dropdown menu and choose either Posts, Stories, or both.
  8. Click the Media type dropdown menu and select Reels.
  9. Select a specific reel to view its detailed insights.
  10. Utilize the available filters to analyze reel performance based on factors like length.

Note: Historical views will be available for a limited time to help you compare earnings and performance before and after Reels and video formats were unified.

Set your default audience for reels on Facebook

Set my default audience

Who can see my reels?

Change reel audience

What is a custom audience?

Update (September 2025): All videos on Facebook are now Reels. Your default audience setting applies to all future reels, including those shared from Instagram. Audience and privacy controls are unified for a simpler experience. Learn more about this change.

You control who can see your reels on Facebook by selecting an audience for the reel. Setting a default audience will set the audience for your future reels, including reels you share from your Instagram account.

You can change the audience for a specific reel at any time, including when you create it. Your future reels will still use your default choice.

Set a default audience for your reels

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & privacy.
  3. Click Settings.
  4. Click Reels under Audience and visibility.
  5. Next to Who can see your reels? click your current default audience.
  6. Click your new selection, then click Save.

Available default audiences for your reels

  • Public: Anyone, including people off of Facebook, can see your reel.
  • Friends: Only your friends on Facebook can see your reel.
  • Friends except…; Your friends on Facebook, except for the friends you choose, can see your reel.
  • Only me: Only you can see the reel.
  • Specific friends: Only the friends you choose can see the reel.
  • Custom: You can create a custom audience based on your preference.

Note: If you share a reel from your Instagram account to your Facebook account, and you haven’t selected a default audience for reels on Facebook, your default audience on Facebook is automatically set to Friends for a private Instagram account or Public for a public Instagram account. This will be your default audience for reels on Facebook until you change it on Facebook.

Consider audience differences between Instagram and Facebook

Keep in mind that your followers on Instagram may not be the same as your friends on Facebook, so if you share a reel from Instagram to Facebook, you may be sharing your reel with different people.

Settings recommended to use when adding an edited video to Facebook

What video settings should I use?

What aspect ratio should I use?

What frame rate should I use?

What audio settings should I use?

If you’re exporting your video from editing software and want to add it to Facebook, we recommend using these custom settings:

  • H.264 video with AAC audio in MOV or MP4 format.
  • An aspect ratio no larger than 4000px wide and divisible by 16px.
  • A frame rate at, or below, 30fps.
  • Stereo audio with a sample rate of 44,100Hz.
  • Videos should not contain edit lists or special boxes in file containers.

What happened to the Videos tab?

Update (September 2025): All videos posted to Facebook are now shared as Reels, with no length or orientation restrictions. The Videos tab is now the Reels tab. You can stream any Reel (video) to your TV using the Facebook app or website Learn more.

You can stream Facebook Reels from your Feed or the Reels tab to a TV using your computer.

To watch Facebook Reels on your TV:

  1. Make sure your TV is linked to a streaming device (Chromecast, Apple TV, Samsung TV, Amazon Fire TV, Android TV) or has built-in streaming features. Both your TV and computer must be on the same Wi-Fi network.
  2. Access Facebook on your computer and locate the Reel you want to stream.
  3. Click the Reel to view it in full screen.
  4. In the video player’s top-right corner, click Options then tap Cast video.
  5. From the list of available devices, choose the TV where you want to play the Reel.

Note: Not all smart TVs support streaming Reels from a computer.

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Can I cast long videos as Reels? Yes, Reels can be any length and can be cast to your TV.
  • What happened to the Videos tab? The Videos tab is now called the Reels tab. All new videos are Reels.
  • Why can’t I find my device? Make sure your TV and device are on the same Wi-Fi network and support casting.
  • Can I cast from iPhone to Chromecast? No, Chromecast is not supported on iOS devices.

Troubleshooting

  • If your TV/device does not appear, check that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network.
  • Update your Facebook app to the latest version.
  • Restart your TV and casting device if issues persist.

For more help, see About Facebook Reels and Troubleshooting casting issues.

Time limit and guidelines for live streaming on Facebook

What is the time limit?

Extend my stream time

Recommended video settings

My stream ended early

The time limit for a live video session on Facebook is 8 hours.

Facebook Live lets you broadcast video content in real time to audiences across computers and mobile devices. To maintain stream quality and platform reliability, Facebook enforces time limits and recommends specific technical settings for live video broadcasts.

Time limits for Facebook Live

  • Maximum duration per stream: 8 hours
  • This time limit applies to:
    • Streams from computers
    • Streams via external software or API
    • Mobile device streams

Extended streaming for premium partners and gaming streams

Select premium partners, gaming creators, and media organizations may be approved for longer streams, typically up to 12 hours. These extensions aren’t automatic and are decided by Meta internal teams. If your event may require more than 8 hours of uninterrupted streaming, reach out to your account manager for evaluation.

Note: Facebook will automatically end streams that reach their assigned duration limit (typically 8 or 12 hours). There is no grace period once the limit is reached.

Best practices

If your live event is expected to exceed the current stream time limit:

  • Plan scheduled breaks to end and immediately restart the broadcast.
  • Notify your viewers in advance about planned restarts to minimize audience disruption.

Technical recommendations

Recommended video settings

  • Resolution: 1080p (1920 x 1080)
  • Frame rate: 30 fps
  • Bitrate range: 3,000–6,000 Kbps
  • Keyframe interval: 2 seconds
  • Video codec: H.264, Level 4.1

Recommended audio settings

  • Sample rate: 44.1 kHz
  • Channel layout: Stereo
  • Bitrate: 128 Kbps

Applying these settings helps ensure high reliability and avoids throttling or quality drops, especially for professional creators and premium partners.

Streaming workflow

  • Schedule streams in advance to build audience anticipation.
  • Preview your stream before going live to test settings.
  • Manage stream keys and refresh if older than 7 days.
  • Restart your stream for long events exceeding the time limit.

Storage and replay options

  • Replay window: Live videos are automatically available for replay for up to 30 days after broadcast.
  • Download and archival: Creators may download the full live video file at any time within the 30-day window for external backup, publishing on other platforms, or archiving.
  • Convert live to Reels:Use Facebook’s highlight tools to turn key moments or segments from live streams into Reels for ongoing engagement.

Note: Live video content that is not saved, downloaded, or converted to Reels will be automatically deleted 30 days after the live session ends. Ensure you retrieve any content you want to retain before this deadline.

Learn more about the full range of supported live streaming specifications. You can also learn more about live streaming on Facebook.

What are reels on Facebook

Create a reel

Differences with Instagram Reels

View reel likes

View reel plays

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

Update (September 2025): All videos on Facebook are now Reels. All videos posted to Facebook will be shared as reels, regardless of length or orientation. This unifies the video experience for creators and viewers. Learn more about this change.

Reels on Facebook is a video format complete with music, audio, AR effects, and other options. You can also view public reels from Instagram, if the creator chooses to recommend it on Facebook. Reels are recommended based on what may be relevant to you and may appear in places like your Feed and in Video.

Learn more about Reels and how to create a reel.

Differences between reels on Facebook and Instagram

  • Instagram names: Reels from Instagram have the creator’s Instagram username instead of their Facebook name (if they have a Facebook account). You’ll also see Instagram icon next to their username.
  • Comments: You can view comments on reels created on both Facebook and Instagram. Leaving comments is different depending on where the reel was created.
    • Facebook Reels: If you’re watching a reel created on Facebook, you can leave comments and reply or react to comments.
    • Instagram Reels: If you’re watching a reel created on Instagram, you can leave a comment and reply or like comments if you have added your Instagram account to Accounts Center. Your comment, reply or like will be posted with your Instagram profile.
  • Likes: You can see how many people have liked a reel. You can also see who on Facebook has liked a reel, but if it’s a reel created on Instagram, you can’t see who on Instagram liked it. You can only see who liked the reel on Instagram in the Instagram app or on Instagram.com.
    • To see a list of who on Facebook liked the video, use the Facebook app for iPhone and Android.
  • Views: The number of times your reel was played. A view is 1 ms of playtime.

Note: Videos published before 3/14/2024 define a view as 3 seconds of playtime. Reels use 1 ms regardless of when they were published. Learn more about how to view the number of times a reel or video has been played.

  • Creator Page: When you’re watching a reel created on Facebook, you can see other reels they’ve created by tapping on their name. If you’re watching a reel created on Instagram, you will be directed to their profile on Instagram instead.

Important information

  • When commenting on an Instagram reel with your Instagram account, your comment will be visible on both Facebook and Instagram.
  • You can change the Instagram profile you’re using to comment on Instagram reels by visiting the Accounts Center.
  • You can find comments you’ve left on Instagram reels in Your Activity on Instagram. They won’t appear on your Facebook Activity Log.
  • Comments left on Instagram reels can only be deleted on Instagram. If you delete the comment on Instagram, it’ll be removed from both Instagram and Facebook. Learn more about how to delete comments on Instagram.

What help is available if you’ve shared a nude or sexual photo or video of yourself and you’re under 18

If you or someone you know is in immediate danger, contact local authorities for help.

It’s possible that during your relationship or when talking with your friends and followers you may have shared nude photos or videos of yourself. Maybe you felt excited to share these and it seemed like a good idea at the time, or maybe you felt uncomfortable or felt pressured to do so.

Get support

You have a right to feel safe. If someone asks you to do things that make you feel uncomfortable or says or does things that make you feel bad, it is not your fault. If you’ve shared a photo or video with someone and you are worried, there are ways you can get help.

Here are some things you can do:

  • Contact your local law enforcement if you are in danger and need immediate help.
  • You can report any nudes or sexually explicit content that was shared. You can also report anyone who has made you feel uncomfortable or pressured you to do this.
  • You don’t have to deal with this alone. Find someone you can talk to about this, like a close friend, teacher, counselor, or trusted adult.
  • Increase your privacy settings to protect yourself by controlling who can see what you share or who can find you.
  • Contact a helpline if you are being harassed or harmed online. There are many organizations that provide support specifically for situations when images have been shared without consent.
  • You can contact a suicide helpline if you are upset and need to talk with someone or are struggling with your mental health or thinking about harming yourself.

We want to make sure Facebook is a safe environment. Learn what steps to take if you see images of children or teens being sexually abused or exploited. Learn more about where to get help if you’re a victim of human trafficking.

Risks to sharing

In addition to being against our rules, there are risks to sharing this type of media with others, even if you trust them.

Even if it seemed like a good idea at the time, sharing this content can lead to negative situations:

  • The person you sent the photo to could send it to someone else or share it somewhere online. Even if you trust them now, it is possible that the relationship could change later on.
  • Once this type of content is shared, it can be hard to control what happens to it.
  • Some people have bad intentions and may want to use the content against you.
  • Family members, friends or strangers who you didn’t send the photo to might end up seeing the photo.
  • Your feelings or thoughts about sharing the photo might change as well.
  • The content goes against our Community Standards and will be removed. You could also lose access to your Facebook account.
  • You may not have known this, but sharing this type of content of someone under 18 is also against the law in many countries and could put you, your partner or anyone else who has looked at the content at risk.
    • Remember, help is available, and you can contact a helpline in your region

Why a live video you’re watching on Facebook may be having broadcast problems

My live video keeps pausing

My live video stopped

My network connection is weak

If a live video pauses, unexpectedly stops or experiences a broadcast issue, it’s likely because:

  • The broadcaster’s network connection is weak.
  • The broadcast has been paused.
  • Your network connection is weak.

If your network connection is weak, try going to an area with a better network connection.

If you’re unable to start a live video, your browser or device hardware may not support live video. Try updating your device’s browser or try watching the live video with a different device.

You see videos playing silently when you scroll through your Feed. How this works with your mobile data plan

Change autoplay settings

Stop videos from playing

Autoplay uses too much data

I can’t change autoplay settings

Autoplay videos begin automatically as you scroll. Videos use more data than other posts on Facebook, and may affect your mobile data plan.

You can change your video autoplay settings at any time. Learn how to stop videos from playing automatically in your Feed.

Autoplay settings on the Facebook app for iOS or Android

When you change your settings on a mobile device, you can select from the following options:

  • On Mobile Data and Wi-Fi: Videos will autoplay using a mobile data connection. The data used depends on the amount of time you spend watching a video. If you scroll past an autoplay video in Feed, your phone will use less data than if you stop to watch it for a longer period of time.
  • On Wi-Fi Only: Videos will autoplay only when your phone or tablet is connected to Wi-Fi. If you’re using Facebook on a mobile data connection, you’ll have to click on a video to play it. If you click and play a video while using a mobile data connection, it will use mobile data.
  • Never Autoplay Videos: You’ll always have to click on a video to play it. If you click and play a video while using a mobile data connection, it will use mobile data.

Note: You may need to click a video to play it, even if your autoplay settings are On Mobile Data and Wi-Fi. This could happen if the mobile connection is slow or if you’ve used a large amount of mobile data recently.

Add a security key to your Facebook account

Add a security key

Use a security key

My security key isn’t working

What is a security key?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

In order to add a security key to your account, you’ll first need to purchase your own third party Universal 2nd Factor (U2F) or FIDO2 security key.

Some types of keys can be used by inserting them into a USB or lightning port. Other types of keys can be used by holding them near your computer or mobile device. Before purchasing, make sure that your security key is compatible with the browser and the device that you use to log into your account. After you add a key to your account, you can then use that key to log in.

Learn more about security keys and how they work.

To add a security key on your desktop, you’ll need to be using the latest version of Chrome, Opera, Firefox, Edge, or Safari. You’ll need to have a Bluetooth, USB, or NFC security key. You’ll need to ensure that your computer is compatible with your security key.

Add a security key

  1. Go to your Security and login settings.
  2. Click Accounts Center, then click Password and security.
  3. Click Two-factor authentication and select your account. You may be asked to re-enter your Facebook password at this point.
  4. Click Use security key.
  5. Insert your security key and then click Register security key.
  6. Follow the on-screen instructions. If you do not see the Register Security Key option, you may need to update your browser.

Once you’ve successfully added a security key to your account, you can start using it when you log in. Learn more about how to log in with your security key.

I’m having trouble registering my security key to my account

If you’re having trouble registering your security key to your account, try the following:

  • If you have a USB or lightning security key, make sure it’s plugged in correctly.
  • If your security key is touch activated, make sure to tap the sensor or button on your key when you want to activate it.
  • Move NFC keys slowly over your device near the sensor. The location of the NFC sensor depends on your device.
  • Charge Bluetooth keys regularly.
  • Check the manufacturer’s instructions for your security key for additional help.
  • Try updating your browser or mobile app and make sure your key is compatible with the device and browser you’re logging in from.

Other Useful Resources

  • Learn about what to do if you lose your key or if your device or browser does not support security keys.
  • Learn how to log in with your security key after you’ve added it to your account.
  • Your security key can be used with other websites while also being used for your Facebook account.
  • If you’re running Linux, you’ll need to follow this additional step to use your security key.

Avoiding scams on Facebook

How to avoid scams?

Report a scam

Common scams on Facebook

If you see something on Facebook that you think is a scam, don’t respond. Please report it to us.

You can report a scam at any time. Visit the Scam Protection Center to learn how to recognize common scams and keep your account safe.

Your experience on Facebook should be safe and secure. We remove content that purposefully deceives, willfully misrepresents, or otherwise defrauds or exploits people for money or property.

The following tips and tools will help you to stay safe online and help keep your accounts protected.

About scams

Scammers target people to trick them into giving away money or sensitive information. Think of emails that offer a quick-and-easy investment scheme or an urgent text message from someone claiming to be a friend in need, or a phishing email claiming to come from Meta to alert you of issues with your account and asking you to immediately click on a link to learn more.

They may create fake accounts pretending to be someone they are not or compromising existing social media accounts to try to deceive or defraud you or your friends out of money, personal information, or access to your account(s).

Note: If you get a suspicious email or message claiming to be from Facebook, don’t click any links or attachments. You can view recent emails sent from Facebook in your Facebook Settings.

How to protect your account

Scammers who try to trick people into sharing personal information, passwords, or credit card numbers typically do so via fraudulent emails, messages, or websites that might appear legitimate, such as a bank, email provider, or social media platform. More on common scams below.

To start, here are three simple rules to help you protect yourself when you encounter a scam:

  1. Slow down: Scammers often try to create a sense of urgency or threaten you with losing your account or other action. Take time to ask questions and think it through.
  2. Spot check: Scammers often mention a problem to encourage you to act. Do your research to double check the details before clicking links or downloading files. Does what they’re telling you make sense?
  3. Don’t send: Scammers often pretend to be from a familiar organization, they may use an employee photo they stole from the internet to convince you. No reputable organization will demand payment on the spot.

On social media, look out for the following signs when considering whether to accept a friend request or respond to a message:

  • People who you don’t know or famous people asking for money.
  • Asking you for advance fees to receive a loan, prize or other winnings.
  • People claiming to be a friend or relative in an emergency.
  • People asking you to move your conversation off Facebook.
  • People claiming to want a romantic connection with you quickly and then asking for money.
  • Messages or posts with poor spelling and grammar errors.
  • A message asking for your urgent response because something is wrong with your online account.
  • A message that simply asks you to log in with your social media, email or bank account to read an important message about the services you use online.
  • Accounts that have no friends, profile photo, or real-looking activity on Facebook.

Tips to keep your account secure

  • Don’t click suspicious links: If you get a suspicious email or text or social media message claiming to be from Facebook, don’t click any links or attachments. First, check in your Facebook settings whether it came from Facebook.
  • Do not download files or software coming from people you don’t know: Use caution when installing browser extensions and 3rd party apps, particularly when they offer functionality that sounds too good to be true or require you to log in with your social media credentials before even using them.
  • Don’t answer and report messages that ask for your:
    • Password
    • Social security number
    • Financial information like credit card numbers
  • Strengthen your online security:
    • Enable two-factor authentication to add an extra security layer to your accounts across the internet. Two-factor authentication is one of the most effective tools for combating account compromise attempts.
    • Never reuse your password across multiple websites.
    • Use trusted antivirus software. It is important to keep this software up to date and scan your devices for malware regularly.
    • Turn on login alerts so you’ll be notified if someone is trying to access your account. Be sure to review your previous sessions to make sure you recognize which devices have access to your account.
    • Visit the Security Checkup Tool to help secure your account.
    • For businesses: enable Business notifications so you’ll be alerted of any changes happening within your Meta Business Manager Account. More here.

If you think someone has access to your account or you’re unable to log in, please visit this page to take steps to regain access to your account.

Learn more in the Scam Protection Center.

Common scams

  • Investment scams: Scammers may promise unrealistic monetary benefits like offering to convert a small amount of money into a larger sum (example: $100 = $1000) and solicit money from you. Typically, scammers disappear with the payment. Some types of false investment scams to watch out for include “cash flipping” scams, Ponzi schemes or “get rich quick” schemes.
  • Romance scams: Scammers may send romantic messages to people they don’t know, often pretending to be divorced, widowed or in a bad marriage claiming they are seeking a relationship. They may claim they need money or your information to purchase a flight or apply for a visa. Because their goal is to first gain your trust, they may engage in conversations for weeks or months before they ask for money.
  • Job scams: Scammers may use misleading or fake job postings to try and get your personal information or your money. Avoid job postings that sound too good to be true or that ask you to pay anything upfront before your application is considered. When clicking on a link from a job posting, watch out for websites that seem unrelated to the original job posting or that ask for sensitive information (example: government ID) but don’t use secure (https) browsing. For more tips, read our guidelines when looking for jobs on Facebook.
  • Lottery scams: Scammers may use accounts or Pages impersonating someone you know or a legitimate organization (such as a government agency) to claim that you’re among the only winners of a lottery which you can receive for a small advance fee. The scammer may ask you to provide personal information, such as your physical address or bank details to “verify your identity” before receiving your prize.
  • Loan scams: Scammers may send messages and share posts offering instant loans at a low interest rate for a small advance fee. Once an initial payment is made they may ask for more money to provide a larger loan or simply end the conversation and disappear with the payment.
  • Donation scams: Scammers may use online accounts pretending to represent charities or orphanages or religious figures. They would then ask for donations.
  • Inheritance scams: The scammers may claim to be a lawyer or representative of the state reaching out to you about the estate of a deceased person. They may claim that you’re entitled to the inheritance and ask you to provide personal information such as your physical address or bank details to receive such inheritance.
  • Commerce scams: Scammers may claim to be selling goods and services online, often at a price that’s too good to be true, and they may try to convince you that you can get a better price if you move the conversation to other communications channels, like email or chat apps. Once you pay them, they would stop responding and the goods never arrive. They may try to create a sense of urgency to get people to act quickly to place an order and request payment through crypto currency.
    • Note: Although eligible items purchased via onsite checkout on Facebook or Instagram are covered by Meta’s Purchase Protection Policies, Meta does not offer refunds for any person-to-person or offsite transactions. Here are some shopping safety tips for using person-to-person transactions to purchase items via Facebook Marketplace, especially if an item needs to be shipped. You can also learn more about the difference between buying something with checkout and local pickup.
  • Paid subscription services: Scammers may offer to purchase lifetime access to coveted subscription services for a one-time payment and then never deliver the product.

Does the number of times something gets reported determine whether or not that content is removed?

Why wasn’t content removed?

What are Community Standards?

How do I block someone?

We take something down from Facebook if it goes against our Community Standards, which are designed to encourage expression and create a safe environment. The number of times something is reported doesn’t determine whether or not it’s removed from Facebook. We use the same guidelines each time we review whether a profile goes against our Community Standards.

If you reported someone’s profile and we found that it doesn’t go against our Community Standards, there are some other things you can do to control your experience on Facebook. If someone repeatedly posts things you don’t want to see, you can use these tools to see less from them:

  • Unfollow them: Unfollowing a person or Page prevents you from seeing their posts or updates in your News Feed.
  • Block them: When you block someone, they won’t be able to start a conversation with you, tag you or see things you post to your profile. If you block someone you’re friends with, we’ll unfriend you as well.
  • Take a break from them: You can take a break from someone by changing when you see them on Facebook or preventing them from seeing your posts.
