Content settings for Teen Accounts on Facebook and Messenger

Change my content setting

What is Ages 13+?

What is More content?

What content is inappropriate?

This Content setting and additional protections for the Ages 13+ option are currently being rolled out on an individual basis, which means parents and guardians may have a teen who has the Content setting or additional protections before their other teens do.

People ages 18 and older will be placed into the Default option for Sensitive content control.

Teens who tell us they are 13-17 years old are automatically placed into Teen Accounts. You can use your Teen Account content setting on Facebook and Messenger to manage the content you may see, as well as the profiles and Pages you may message and interact with. On Facebook, the setting you choose impacts the content you may see from profiles, Pages, Groups, Events and suggested content on surfaces like Feed, Reels and more. On Messenger, this setting impacts your ability to message or interact with profiles and Pages that primarily share content that may be inappropriate for teens. These and additional protections continue to be rolled out gradually across Facebook and Messenger.

If you’re a teen 13-17 years old, you’ll be defaulted into the Ages 13+ content setting. This means we work to hide more content that may be inappropriate for people under 18. For example, we’ll increase the strength of and expand the filters we use to hide certain content from teens. Your ability to message or interact with content from profiles and Pages that primarily share content that may be inappropriate for teens will also be limited, unless your content setting is More content.

Note: This setting doesn’t apply to all filtering that we do. For example, you won’t be able to see content that is hidden for all Teen Accounts on Facebook and Messenger. In addition, our AI experiences also apply protections for all Teen Accounts that are not affected by this setting.

There are currently two options for your content setting:

  • Ages 13+: You’ll typically see content, such as posts, reels and stories, that’s similar to what you would see in content rated for ages 13+. Your ability to message or interact with profiles and Pages that primarily share content inappropriate for teens will be limited. In addition, your ability to discover, join, manage or access Groups or Events that primarily contain content inappropriate for teens will be limited.
  • More content: We won’t apply the content filters and restrictions that are part of the Ages 13+ option and you may see content, such as posts, reels and stories, that’s similar to what you would see in content rated for ages 18+. You’ll need permission from your parent or guardian to choose More content.

To request permission to update this setting to More content:

  1. From your profile, tap the Tap Menu in the top left of Facebook. in the top left corner.
  2. Tap Teen safety settings, then tap What you see.
  3. Tap Content setting.
  4. To request to change your setting to More content, tap More content, then tap Confirm on the following screen, then tap Send request or Add parent.

Our Community Standards define what is and isn’t allowed on Facebook and Messenger. These guidelines help us keep Facebook and Messenger authentic and safe places. If we’re made aware of content and we find that it goes against our Community Standards, we take action. The Teen Account content setting impacts how strongly and expansively we work to filter content that may go against our age-appropriate guidelines.

The following types of content are examples of what may be inappropriate for people under 18:

  • Suicide, Self-Injury, and Eating Disorders: We hide certain suicide and self-injury related content that we find, to help protect teens from potentially distressing or sensitive material. For example:
  • A post where someone is describing their own personal experiences with suicide, self-injury or eating disorders, except in the context of recovery.
  • A photo or video showing people in a hospital engaging in euthanasia or assisted suicide.
  • A Story where someone is discussing extreme weight loss behavior.
    • Restricted Goods and Services: We hide content that we find from teens that could influence them to engage in activities that are potentially harmful. For example:
      • A post offering to sell tobacco, nicotine products, alcohol, or firearms when shared by a legitimate brick-and-mortar business.
      • A Story encouraging people to take psychedelic drugs (also known as entheogens) or cannabis products.
      • Images with recipes for alcoholic drinks.
      • A post selling weight loss products or services.
    • Threatening and Graphic Content: We hide most graphic and disturbing imagery that we find from teens, even if we’d allow it behind a warning screen for adults. For example:
      • A photo of a severely burned person, which we’d cover with a warning screen for adults.
      • A photo or video of shootings, brutality, or deadly car crashes.
    • Nudity, Sexual Activity, and Sexually Explicit Language: We hide additional content that we find from teens that don’t contain explicit nudity or sexual activity but could be considered sexually suggestive. For example:
      • A post with near nudity such as nudity covered by digital overlay.
    • A photo zoomed in on someone’s buttocks.
      • A Story with sexually suggestive language describing sexual encounters, including the use of sexual metaphors

Learn more about how we help teens see age-appropriate content.

Extra supervision features available under regional law on Facebook

Set up extra supervision

What features are available?

I can’t set up supervision

Remove extra supervision

These features are only available in some regions and may not be available in your area. This article covers supervision of your teen’s Facebook profile.

Parents and guardians of teens under 18 can set up supervision on Facebook to help teens balance their time and provide support. The supervision features we provide everyone are optional—parents or teens can invite each other to set them up and can remove them at any time.

To set up supervision you must be 18 or older, both you and your teen must agree to participate in supervision and the teen you are supervising must be 13-17 years old, depending on where they live.

In some regions, laws give parents the right to set up extra supervision features. Parents can request to set up these features if their teen lives in one of these regions and meets the age requirements outlined in the law. Only parents can remove these features until a teen turns 18 (or the relevant age in their region), at which point they’ll automatically be removed.

Setting up extra supervision features

If your teen lives in one of the regions listed below and they meet the age requirements outlined in the law, you can set up extra supervision features on Facebook by clicking the link under the relevant region. You can choose the app (Facebook and Messenger, Instagram or Meta Horizon) you’d like to use to supervise your teen.

You may be asked to verify your identity before you can invite your teen to set up extra supervision features. To do this, we’ll ask you to upload a valid government ID, or two forms of non-government IDs. Confirming your identity may take up to 48 hours. Your ID will be stored securely and deleted within 30 days after we’ve finished confirming your identity. It won’t be used for anything else, including ads. We might use trusted service providers to help review your information.

Once we’ve confirmed your identity, you can invite your teen to set up extra supervision features. They’ll be asked to confirm that you’re their parent or guardian before features are set up. If your teen doesn’t confirm that you’re their parent or guardian, or they don’t respond within 7 days, you can invite them again. If your teen remains unresponsive or doesn’t confirm, you can set up supervision features by providing us with more information like their birth certificate.

Using another Meta app to supervise on Facebook

You can use some other Meta apps (Facebook, Messenger, Instagram, Threads or Meta Horizon) to supervise your teen’s Facebook profile. When setting up, you’ll choose which app you’d like to receive notifications on. You can still use the other apps to manage supervision.

If you want to set up extra supervision for your teen’s profile on another Meta app, go to that app’s Help Center article for instructions:

  • Instagram
  • Threads
  • Messenger
  • Meta Horizon

Managing or removing supervision

Parents can manage supervision features, including removing supervision at any time. If you’ve added extra supervision features available under regional law, all features will be removed when you remove supervision. Extra supervision features provided in your region will automatically be removed when your teen turns 18 (or the relevant age in your region).

If your teen moves out of that region, we’ll remove extra supervision features. You’ll still be able to supervise your teen by seeing insights into their activity, setting time limits, responding to requests to change their Teen Account settings and more. We’ll notify you of any changes if this happens.

Teen Accounts limit who can contact teens on Messenger. Learn more about Teen Accounts on Messenger.

Facebook is introducing a new experience built for teens, including teen creators with pro mode. This is designed to be the Facebook you know and love plus new protections around who can contact you, who can see your content, and the content you see.

These protections include limiting who can see some of your future content to Friends.

If you’re a teen, you’ll need to enable public posts in order to be eligible for pro mode. If you’re 13-15, you’ll need to get your parent or guardian’s permission to enable public posting (so you can be eligible for pro mode).

To turn on public posting:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. Click Settings & Privacy, then click Settings.
  3. Under Audience and visibility, click Posts.
  4. Click Who can see your future posts?, then select Public.

For teens aged 13-15 with pro mode, you can only change your content audience for future posts, stories or reels to public or change certain settings to be less protective with a parent’s permission. For teens aged 16-17, you can change these settings to be less protective without a parent’s permission.

If you’re a teen creator, some of your Teen Account settings may affect your ability to use some creator features. Your Teen Account settings may also restrict you from receiving messages from accounts you’re not connected to, which means you may not receive DMs from some brands or businesses, unless you message them first.

If you’re under 16, you need your parent or guardian’s permission to update your safety settings. If you’re 16-17, you can change most of these settings yourself. Learn how to manage your Teen Account settings.

How do privacy controls change when a minor becomes an adult on Facebook?

What changes when I turn 18?

My privacy settings changed

Who can message me now?

How do I change my settings?

When you turn 18, we’ll notify you that you no longer have a Teen Account and that some of your settings will be defaulted to less protective options. For example:

  • Anyone can message you.
  • You can now have a public search listing and use the tag suggest feature.
  • You can change your audience settings to be public. Keep in mind that stuff you share to Public can be seen by anyone, on or off of Facebook.
  • Daily limit and sleep mode will be turned off.
  • Sensitive content preferences will be changed to default.
  • If you had supervision, supervision will be removed unless you chose to keep it.

You can always modify your settings to be more or less protective in Settings & privacy.

For more information on controlling your information and staying safe on Facebook, visit The Family Safety Center.

How Facebook decides which ads to show teens

How are ads shown to teens?

How are ads shown to adults?

What are ad preferences?

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

We want to make sure everyone who uses Facebook sees ads that are appropriate and useful to them. All ads on our platforms must follow our Community Standards and Advertising Standards.

We have additional policies in place for ads shown to teens (people under 18 years old globally and under 20 in Thailand). For example, our Advertising Standards prohibit ads about restricted topics, like alcohol, financial products and weight loss products and services, to be shown to people under 18 (and older in certain countries).

Additionally, we limit the options advertisers can use to show ads to teens. For example, we don’t allow advertisers to select interests, behaviors, gender or activity on other apps and websites when choosing to show their ads to teens. Advertisers can decide to include teens in their audience based only on age and location.

In contrast, advertisers have more options for showing ads to adults who use our products. For example, an advertiser could choose to show their ads to people with certain interests or based on information that they, or other partners, share with us. This could include the products someone is interested in, interactions they have had with our AI products, websites they visited or Pages they interacted with on Facebook. Since advertisers have more options when reaching adults, these audiences will have additional Ad preferences to manage their personalized ads experience.

For all account holders, no matter what your age, your use of Facebook is governed by our Terms of Service.

How Teen Accounts work on Facebook

Adjust Teen Account settings

What are Teen Account protections?

What can parents see?

Teen Accounts are currently only available in some locations. Teen Accounts are being rolled out on an individual basis, which means parents and guardians may have a teen who has a Teen Account before their other teens do.

Teen Accounts limit who can contact teens on Messenger. Learn more about Teen Accounts on Messenger.

Teen Accounts are Facebook accounts for teens 13-17 that are automatically set to protective Teen Account settings. These settings aim to help keep you safe on Facebook by limiting unwanted contact and helping you manage your time on Facebook.

Built-in protections for teens 13-17

  • Protection from unwanted contact: We limit who can see and interact with your future content. On Facebook, you can still share content with people you’re friends with. On Messenger, only friends and other connections can chat with you.
  • Content that’s right for you: On Facebook, we’ll filter out more sensitive and potentially offensive content so you see the content that’s the most age-appropriate. Note: If you’re a teen under 18, we’ll try to hide more content that may be inappropriate for people under 18.
  • Managing your time: To help you avoid distractions, we’ll remind you to close Facebook from 10 PM to 7 AM and after you’ve spent one hour each day.

Adjusting your Teen Account settings

Ages 13-15

You can make your settings even more protective on your own, but you need a parent or guardian’s approval to make them less protective. They can approve your requests. Learn how to manage your Teen Account settings.

Ages 16-17

You can adjust your Teen Account settings anytime to make sure they’re right for you, unless you have supervision set up with a parent or guardian.

Supervision is optional

  • Adding supervision is your choice: You can add or remove supervision anytime, and it will be removed automatically when you turn 18.
  • What your parent would see: Your parent can help manage your Teen Account settings and the time you spend on each app. They can see your friends, people you’ve blocked, and other insights.
  • What your parent won’t be able to do: Your parent won’t see your chats or search history. They’ll only see your content if you let them.

Note: Teen Accounts and Teen Account settings may not affect teens’ participation in groups and pages. If teens use groups or pages to view or share content, they may be subject to the audience models for groups and pages.

Setting up supervision requires confirmation from a parent or guardian. If a teen sends an invite for supervision, and the parent accepts, supervision is confirmed. Keep in mind, only one parent can be supervising a teen’s account.

Sending invites

For parents

Send an invite to supervise your teen’s account

Parents and guardians can send invites for supervision. Parents who want to supervise more than one teen can send the same invite to each teen they want to supervise.

Keep in mind, invites expire 7 days from the time they are first created. If the invite has expired, create a new invite with the steps below.

Set up supervision in Family Center

  1. Visit Family Center.
  2. Click Continue.
  3. Select the accounts you want to supervise. You can also share a link if you can’t find your teen’s account.
  4. Click Send invite.
Resending or canceling invites

Invites expire after 7 days. You can resend or cancel an invite if it has been less than 7 days since you first created the invite. If it’s been more than 7 days, create a new invite with the steps above.

Accepting or declining invites

Parents can accept or decline a supervision invite. If a parent sends their teen an invite, supervision will start after the invite is accepted. If a teen sends their parent an invite, supervision will start after the parent accepts the invite.

To accept or decline an invite or request, open the link that was sent to you by your teen, then follow the instructions on screen to accept or decline. They will get a notification that you accepted or declined supervision.

If a request is declined, and the teen is under 16, they won’t be able to make any updates to their teen safety settings until they turn 16.

For teens

Teens can send requests to their parents for supervision. Keep in mind, requests expire 7 days from the time they are first created. If a request has expired, follow the steps below to create a new request.

Send a supervision request to your parent in Family Center
  1. Go to your settings on Facebook.
  2. Go to your Teen Account settings, then click or tap Parent or Guardian.
  3. From here, you can find your parent’s account and send a request. You can also send a link.
Resending or canceling requests

Invites expire after 7 days. You can resend or cancel a request if it has been less than 7 days since you first created the request. If it’s been more than 7 days, create a new request with the steps above.

Accepting or declining supervision invites

Teens can accept or decline a supervision invite. If a parent sends their teen an invite, supervision will start after the invite is accepted. If a teen sends their parent a request, supervision will start after the parent accepts the invite.

To accept or decline an invite, open the link that was sent to you by your parent, then follow the instructions on screen to accept or decline.

If your request is declined, and you’re under 16, you won’t be able to make any updates to their teen safety settings until you turn 16.

Note:

  • A parent can supervise more than one teen’s account, but they can only send one active invite link at a time. For security purposes, we may limit the number of accounts that a parent account can supervise at any given time. Teens can also change who supervises their account.
  • A parent can’t supervise a teen’s account if either of them has blocked each other. Learn how to unblock someone.
  • If supervision is set up and you block your parent or teen, supervision will automatically be removed and your parent or teen will be notified.
  • Parents and teens can get notifications about supervision activity. If a parent or teen has turned on push notifications, they may get push notifications. Parents can choose which account will be shown on Family Center and receive notifications in their Family Center settings.

Supervision on Facebook

Set up supervision

What can parents see?

What can teens see?

Remove supervision

Teen Accounts are currently only available in some locations. Teen Accounts are being rolled out on an individual basis, which means parents and guardians may have a teen who has a Teen Account before their other teens do.

Supervision is a set of tools and insights that parents and guardians can use to help support their teens (ages 13-17, or 14-17 in some regions) on Facebook.

Supervision is optional, and both the parent and the teen must agree to participate. It can be removed at any time by either person. The other person will be notified if it is removed.

With Teen Accounts, supervision also enables parents and guardians to view their Teen Account settings and approve or deny their requests to make certain settings less protective. Parents and guardians can also set time limits and make other Teen Account settings even more protective.

When supervision is set up, a parent can:

  • See how much time their teen has spent on Facebook each day for the last week, and their average daily time spent for the week.
  • Set up sleep mode to limit their teen’s use of Facebook during select days and hours.
  • Set up daily limit to limit how long their teen uses Facebook in a day. Parents can choose whether their teen sees a reminder to close the app, or is blocked from using Facebook.
  • See their teen’s Facebook friends.
  • Manage and approve some of their teen’s privacy settings and sensitive content preferences.
  • See the people and Pages their teen has blocked.
  • View and adjust their teen’s audience settings, including:
    • Who can see their future posts, stories or reels
    • Who can see their friends list
    • Who can see the people, Pages and lists they follow
    • Who can see posts they’re tagged in on their profile
    • Who can comment on their public posts
    • Whether anyone can remix their future public reels
    • Whether they must review posts they’re tagged in before the post appears on their profile.
  • View and adjust some of their teen’s profile details settings, including who can see their phone number, email address and other info like their birthday.

Parents will be notified via push notification, if enabled, if their teen changes any of these settings.

Teens will be notified via push notification, if enabled, if their parent changes any of their Teen Account settings.

With supervision set up, a teen can:

  • See a preview of what the parent sees while supervising.
  • Choose to notify their parent after reporting something on Facebook.

Teens 13-15 need to request parent or guardian approval to change their Teen Account settings to be less protective. Parents will be notified in their notifications tab and, if enabled, via push notification, if their teen requests to make changes to any of these settings.

Eligibility and privacy for parents

Eligibility and privacy for teens

Connecting with a supervised user

When you interact with a supervised account, their parent or guardian can see some of your activity and information. This can include information, like your username, profile picture and if the supervised user blocked you. The supervised user can let their parent or guardian know if they reported you.

It’s important that your supervisor is your parent or guardian, because they will be given controls and insights into your activity to help keep you safe. You can remove supervision at any time.

Learn how to set up supervision.

Note: Supervision features require the latest version of the Facebook app for iPhone and Android. The teen must update the Facebook app. The parent must either update the Facebook app, or visit www.Facebook.com using a desktop or mobile browser. If some features of supervision aren’t working appropriately, update the Facebook app.

Supporting your child’s Teen Account on Facebook

Set daily limit for teen

Set sleep mode for teen

Supervise my teen’s account

My teen can’t change settings

Teen Accounts and some of its protections are currently being rolled out on an individual basis, which means parents and guardians may have a teen who has a Teen Account or additional protections before their other teens do.

Teen Accounts limit who can contact teens on Messenger. Learn more about Teen Accounts on Messenger.

Teens automatically get defaulted into protective Teen Account settings with their Teen Accounts. There are several ways to manage these settings, depending on the age of the teen who has the account.

Supervised accounts

If supervision has been set up for your child’s Teen Account, you’ll be able to change their safety settings to be even more protective, give them permission to make their settings less protective, or approve any requests for your teen to make their safety settings less protective. You’ll also be able to set limits for the amount of time they can spend on Facebook and make other settings even more protective.

For parents and guardians of teens 13-15:

Before you can help your teen change the teen safety settings, or make certain settings even more protective, they’ll need to add you as their parent or guardian so you can supervise their account. Learn how to set up supervision on Facebook and Messenger.

View their Teen Account settings

You can manage your Teen Account settings in Family Center, where you can approve or deny their requests to change them. Your teen will need to request your approval to change certain settings to be less protective. These settings include their teen’s audience settings, content settings and time management tools. You will be notified in your notifications tab and, if enabled, via push notification, if your teen requests to make these settings less protective.

Time management settings you can manage for your teen:

Daily limit

You can limit the amount of time your teen can spend before they see a reminder to either close Facebook or are blocked from using Facebook entirely. By default, we remind teens to close Facebook after they spend 1 hour over the course of a day.

To set a daily limit for your teen’s account:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. In Settings & privacy, click Family Center. From here, you can see the accounts you supervise.
  3. Click on a Teen Account you supervise, then click Manage next to Their time spent.
  4. Click on the amount of time below Daily limit, then select the amount of time you would like instead, and then click Save.

You can also choose whether your teen sees a reminder or is blocked from using Facebook when they reach their daily limit. To choose what should happen when your teen reaches their daily limit:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. In Settings & privacy, click Family Center. From here, you can see the accounts you supervise.
  3. Click on a Teen Account you supervise, then click Manage next to Their time spent.
  4. Below Daily limit, you can choose “Remind teen to close Facebook” if you want your teen to see a reminder to close Facebook, but still be able to use it. Choose “Block teen from Facebook” if you don’t want your teen to be able to use Facebook after reaching their daily limit. Your teen can request additional time for that day.

Sleep mode

You can mute your teen’s notifications and remind them to close Facebook during certain times of day and on certain days of the week with the sleep mode setting. You can also choose to block them from using Facebook during the days and times you choose. By default, we remind teens to close Facebook from 10 PM - 7AM every day. To adjust sleep mode for your teen’s account:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. In Settings & privacy, click Family center. From here, you can see the accounts you supervise.
  3. Click on a Teen Account you supervise, then click Manage next to Their time spent.
  4. Click the preset time period below Sleep mode.
  5. From here, you can click next to Sleep mode to turn sleep mode on or off for the teen’s account.
  6. If sleep mode is turned on, you can then select the times and days you’d like your teen’s account to be in sleep mode.
  7. Click Save.

You can also choose whether your teen sees a reminder or is blocked from using Facebook during sleep mode. To choose what should happen during sleep mode:

  1. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  2. In Settings & privacy, click Family center. From here, you can see the accounts you supervise.
  3. Click on a Teen Account you supervise, then click Manage next to Their time spent.
  4. Below Sleep mode, you can choose “Remind teen to close Facebook” if you want your teen to see a reminder to close Facebook, but still be able to use it. Choose “Block teen from Facebook” if you don’t want your teen to be able to use Facebook during sleep mode.

For parents and guardians of teens 16-17:

Teens 16-17 can manage most of their own Teen Account settings if they don’t have supervision set up. You can invite your teen to let you supervise their account, or they can invite you to supervise their account, which means you’ll approve or deny their teen safety setting changes and help them balance their time on Facebook. You can also make some of their settings even more protective. Supervision on Facebook is automatically removed when a teen turns 18, unless they choose to keep it.

Note: Work with your teen to ensure they have their accurate age listed. They can view and edit their birthday in their settings if it’s not correct. Learn more about editing or adding a birthday on Facebook.

I can’t set time limits

Limit how much time your teen spends on Facebook

Teen Accounts are currently only available in some locations. Teen Accounts are being rolled out on an individual basis, which means parents and guardians may have a teen who has a Teen Account before their other teens do.

To supervise the amount of time your teen spends on Facebook, you and your teen must have already set up supervision.

If supervision is set up, you can visit Family Center to view how much time your teen has spent on the Facebook app in the last 7 days. You can also limit how much time your teen spends on Facebook and schedule breaks from the app.

Note: Supervision features require the latest version of the Facebook app for iPhone and Android. Your teen must update their Facebook app. The parent must either update the Facebook app or visit facebook.com on a desktop or mobile browser. If some features of supervision aren’t working, update your Facebook app.

View your teen’s time spent on Facebook

To view the time your teen spent on the Facebook app in the last 7 days:

  1. Go to familycenter.meta.com/dashboard and log into your account.
  2. Below Accounts, click on your teen’s account.

Below Time on Facebook, you can see your teen’s average daily time spent on Facebook for the last 7 days. You can also see how much time they spent on Facebook for each day by clicking on the bar graph. If the Facebook app is used on multiple devices, you’ll see the total time spent using it.

Limit the amount of time your teen can spend on Facebook each day:

Teen Accounts automatically have daily limit turned on and set to 1 hour. After a teen reaches their daily limit, the teen will see a reminder to close Facebook. You can adjust your teen’s daily limit if you supervise their account.

To manage daily limit for your teen:

  1. Go to familycenter.meta.com/dashboard and click on your teen’s account.
  2. Click Manage time limits.
  3. To turn on a daily time limit, click Toggle next to on.
  4. Click Edit to select specific days and periods of time per day to limit your teens time spent on Facebook.
  5. Click Set to confirm.

Turn on sleep mode for your teen

Teen Accounts automatically have sleep mode turned on from 10PM to 7AM every day. During sleep mode, Facebook notifications are muted and the teen will see a reminder to close Facebook. You can adjust sleep mode settings for your teen if you supervise their account.

To manage sleep mode for your teen:

  1. Go to Family Center and click on your teen’s account.
  2. Next to Their time spent, click Manage.
  3. Below Sleep mode, click [chevron icon] next to the current selection.
  4. Click Toggle to turn sleep mode on or off.
  5. Below Choose times, click into each selector to select a start and end time.
  6. Below Choose days, select each day of the week to add or remove them.
  7. Click Save to confirm.

On the Time management screen, you can also choose to Remind teen to close Facebook or Block teen from Facebook during sleep mode hours.

  • Make sure the VAT number that you provided follows the correct format (European Union).
  • Verify that you’re using the correct VAT number (European Union).

I can’t add or pay with a new credit card with Meta Pay

I can’t add my card

My payment information is wrong

My card was declined

If you’re unable to add or pay with a new credit card using Meta Pay, try the following troubleshooting steps:

Verify payment information

  • Double-check that your credit card number, expiration date, and CVV (security code) are entered correctly.
  • Ensure your billing address matches the one on file with your card issuer.

Card issuer issues

  • Make sure your card is active, not expired, and has sufficient funds.
  • Some banks require additional verification (such as 3D Secure). Complete any prompts from your bank.

Browser and device troubleshooting

  • Try adding your card using a different browser or device.
  • Clear your browser cache and cookies, or update your app/browser to the latest version.

Card type and regional restrictions

  • Prepaid cards, certain international cards, or unsupported card types may not work with Meta Pay.
  • Payment methods may vary by region.

Account status

  • Ensure your Meta account is in good standing and not restricted from making payments.

Advertising payments

  • To add a new payment method for advertising, go to Ads Manager.

Additional support

  • If you’ve tried all the steps above and still can’t add or pay with your card, please contact us.

If you’re having trouble creating an account with your mobile phone number:

  • If you see a message that your mobile number isn’t recognized, make sure you typed your mobile phone number correctly. Enter the country code (example: 91 for India) before the number.
  • If you see a message that an account already exists with your mobile number, you may need to wait a few days to try adding it to your account.
  • Try creating an account with an email instead of a mobile number.
  • If you try to sign up for a new Facebook account with the same, or similar, phone number and password as an account you’ve already created, you will be logged into your existing account.

If you already have a Facebook account with your mobile number but forgot your password:

  • You can reset your password and log into your account.
  • If you don’t have access to that mobile number, you can try these steps to log back into your account.

Note: If you don’t have a mobile phone number, you can create an account with your email instead. Make sure you are logged out of any existing accounts before trying to create an account.

If you see This message didn’t send or Unable to connect to Facebook when you try to send a message, you can try the following:

I can’t upload photos on Facebook

I can’t upload photos

Check my photo format

Update my browser

If you’re having trouble uploading or posting photos on Facebook, here are some things you can try.

Make sure you have the latest version of Adobe Flash

  • To get the latest version of Adobe Flash:
    1. Remove outdated versions of Adobe Flash that might be on your computer.
    2. Download the latest version of Adobe Flash.
    3. Quit all web browsers before you begin installing.
  • Most of the time, this will fix any issues with sharing photos to Facebook.

Manage any adblocking software

  • If you’re using adblocking software, turn it off or make sure that Facebook is included as an exception.

Check your photo format

  • Try uploading the original photo instead of an edited version. Editing photos (example: with iPhoto or Photoshop) before uploading them may cause the upload to fail.
  • We recommend uploading JPEG, BMP, PNG, GIF or TIFF files. If you’re uploading a PNG file, it’s best to keep the file size below 1 MB. PNG files larger than 1 MB may appear pixelated.
  • Check the size of the photo. We recommend uploading photos under 15 MB.

Update your browser

  • Make sure you’re using the latest version of your browser.

Check your Facebook Support Inbox

  • If you’re still having trouble, go to your Support Inbox. If you’ve been warned for posting abusive content, you may be temporarily blocked from uploading photos.

Let us know if you’re still having issues adding photos

  • If you’re still experiencing a problem after trying these suggestions, learn how to report a problem.

I can’t find the information I’m looking for in my Facebook activity log.

You can use the filters in your activity log to find specific things on Facebook, such as your posts, your photos and videos, things you’ve been tagged in and things you’ve hidden from your timeline. Learn more about how to use your activity log.

If you still can’t find the information you’re looking for in your activity log, it could be because:

  • It doesn’t exist for the category or dates that you’re reviewing.
    • For example, you won’t see any activity about events in 2005 because Facebook Events didn’t exist yet.
  • It isn’t accessible through activity log. You can also find your information using:
    • Export your information: where you can export your information to a device or external service. Learn more about exporting your information.
    • Access your information: where you can go to your Facebook Settings and Privacy Center.
    • Review the categories of data available to you in your Facebook settings.
  • The information was deleted from Facebook.
    • You won’t find information or content that you deleted because we delete that content from Facebook.
    • We may no longer be storing the data. For more information on how long we store data, visit our Privacy Policy.

I’m having an issue with something I purchased on Facebook Marketplace

Contact the seller

Order hasn’t shipped

Item is damaged

Item doesn’t match description

If you have an issue with an order on Facebook Marketplace, please contact the seller for help. If the seller doesn’t reply or resolve your issue within 2 business days, you can contact Facebook support.

Contact the seller if you experience any of these issues:

  • Your order hasn’t been shipped: If the seller hasn’t shipped your order within a few days of your purchase, we recommend contacting them to check on the order status.
  • Your order didn’t arrive: We recommend waiting 2 days after the estimated delivery date in your order history. On the third business day, contact the seller.
  • The item is damaged or unusable: Contact the seller to ask if they’d like you to return the damaged or unusable (example: locked phone) item. If the seller wants you to send the order back, you’ll need to coordinate with them on who will cover the return shipping costs.
  • The item doesn’t match the description: If the item you received is different from the description on the product page, please contact the seller to try resolving the issue.

If you’re not able to resolve the issue directly with the seller and purchased the item using checkout on Marketplace, please contact our team.

First, make sure that you’ve turned on Facebook texts. If you’re receiving texts (SMS) but are having trouble sending them, try these troubleshooting tips:

  • Check that you’re sending your texts (SMS) to the correct number.
  • Make sure that your phone doesn’t include a signature at the end of your texts. This can interfere with Facebook mobile correspondence.
  • Check that outgoing texts are still included in your service plan.
  • Try contacting your mobile carrier for help, especially if you receive any error messages when you try to send your text.

Issue a refund for something you sold with shipping on Facebook Marketplace

Refund an item

Refund after payout

Contest an issue

Some shipping features are not available to all eligible sellers.

All items sold with shipping and checkout are final sale, but you may still choose to issue a refund for a buyer.

Learn about the policies and best practices for selling with shipping and checkout.

Issue a refund

You can issue a refund before you’ve been paid out for an order. If you’ve already been paid out, you can’t issue a refund yourself.

  1. From your Feed, click Marketplace in the left menu. If you don’t see Marketplace, click See more.
  2. Click Your payouts.
  3. Select the order you want to refund.
  4. Scroll down and select Refund buyer.
  5. Select Full refund or Partial refund.

Learn how payments for shipping and checkout work and the best practices for sellers who offer shipping and checkout.

How refunds work

If you issue a refund:

  • We’ll notify the buyer of the refund amount and send the refund to their original payment method.
  • The buyer will receive either the full or partial amount that they paid (item price, shipping cost, tax).
  • If a refund is issued after payout, the refund amount may be deducted from your current balance. If your balance is less than the refund amount, we may deduct the remaining amount from any future sales. Some sellers may be required to keep a payment method on file. If your payout balance doesn’t cover the full amount owed, the remaining balance will be charged to your payment method on file. Learn more in our Seller Terms.

If you’ve already been paid out for an order and need help, go to Shipping orders, select the order, then scroll down and select Contact support.

For example, if an item arrives damaged after payout, the buyer can request help through their order, and we can issue a refund if the buyer can provide proof.

Keep in mind that you can cancel orders sold with shipping and checkout on Marketplace as long as the order isn’t marked as shipped. Neither you nor the buyer will be charged.

Note: This article is about items sold by individual sellers with shipping and checkout. Learn about the different ways to buy and sell on Marketplace.

Issues with donation payouts from PayPal Giving Fund

Why haven’t I received funds?

Update my charity address

My charity is no longer eligible

Meta requires that nonprofits in the United States using key fundraising tools are enrolled with PayPal Giving Fund.

As of October 31, 2023, we partner exclusively with PayPal Giving Fund for nonprofits in Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the United States. All donations are irrevocable gifts to PPGF and can only be refunded in certain circumstances as outlined by PayPal Giving Fund’s Donation Refund Policy or when required by law.

You can learn more about Meta’s partnership with PayPal Giving Fund.

Nonprofits may not receive donated funds from PayPal Giving Fund for several reasons.

  • PayPal Giving Fund hasn’t distributed the funds yet. Enrolled nonprofits receive donations into their account at the end of the month. This includes donations received between the 16th of the previous month up to the 15th of the current month. Unenrolled nonprofits receive a check within 45 days in the US, and 90 days in Canada, the UK, and Australia from the date of donation. The check is sent to the nonprofit’s address on file with the IRS.
  • Outdated address or no address on file. For unenrolled nonprofits, PayPal Giving Fund will send a check to the address listed with the IRS. If this address is outdated, you can update it with the IRS directly. If you enroll with PPGF, you’ll receive payouts more quickly into your PayPal account.
  • Your nonprofit is no longer eligible. Your nonprofit may no longer be eligible if it has lost its charitable status with the IRS or if your nonprofit has breached the terms of PayPal’s Nonprofit Certification Policy.

You can manage how other profiles and Pages tag and mention a Page on Facebook.

I can’t create an account

Existing account with my email

There are a few reasons you may be having trouble creating a Facebook account with your email address. If you follow these steps and are still having trouble, remember that you can try creating your Facebook account with a mobile phone number instead of an email.

If you see a message that there’s an existing Facebook account associated with your email, but you forgot your password, you can request a new password. Learn more about resetting your password.

If you’re having issues logging in, then you can learn what to do if you can’t login to your account.

There’s an existing Facebook account associated with your email

You can’t create a new Facebook account with an email address already tied to an existing account. Make sure you entered your email address correctly.

If you share an email address with someone and they have a Facebook account tied to that email, you can create an email account for free with Yahoo! or Gmail.

Email entered incorrectly

If you see a message that your email is invalid, make sure you entered your email correctly.

Confirmation email errors

If you see an error when you click the link from the confirmation email, try logging in with the email you created the account with.

If you can’t log in, copy the link from your confirmation email and paste it into your browser. Learn what to do if you didn’t get the confirmation email.

Note: It’s against our Community Standards to maintain more than one personal account. If you try to sign up for a new Facebook account with the same, or similar, email and password as an account you’ve already created, you will be logged into your existing account.

Reasons why you can’t change your name on Facebook

I can’t change my name

What names are allowed?

My name was rejected

I changed my name recently

We’re gradually updating people to Meta Accounts. You may see either Accounts Center or Meta Account settings as the place to manage your account settings.

If you change your name, you can’t change it again for 60 days. Don’t add any unusual capitalization, punctuation, characters or random words.

Facebook is a community where people use the name they use in everyday life. Always knowing who you’re connecting with helps keep you and the rest of our community safe from impersonation, scams and phishing.

If you don’t want someone to see your name or profile, you can block them.

What isn’t allowed

  • Symbols, numbers, unusual capitalization, repeating characters or punctuation.
  • Characters from multiple languages.
  • Titles of any kind (example: professional, religious).
  • Words or phrases instead of a name.
  • Offensive or suggestive words of any kind.

You can also review what names are allowed on Facebook.

Steps to change your name

Change your name on Facebook using a computer:

  1. Review our name standards.
  2. Click your profile picture in the top right of Facebook.
  3. Select Settings & privacy, then click Settings.
  4. Click Accounts Center.
  5. Click Profiles, then click your account.
  6. Click Name.
  7. Enter your name and click Review change.
  8. Click Save changes.

If you’re having trouble changing your name, please let us know. You can only change your name every 60 days.

Keep in mind

  • Your name must follow our name policy.
  • You can’t change your name too frequently.
  • You may need to confirm your name on Facebook if asked.
  • Your name on Facebook should match the name that appears on an ID.

Recover your Facebook account if you can’t access your account email address or mobile phone number

My account was hacked

Recover my account

No access to my email

I can’t find my account

This article is for people who are having problems logging into Facebook because they no longer have access to the email address or mobile phone number on their account. If you can access your account email or phone, learn how to reset your password.

If you suspect your account was hacked, visit Hacked (facebook.com) on a device you’ve used to log into Facebook before.

First, try this link

You may be able to recover your account by visiting facebook.com/hacked, even if you’re not sure whether your account was compromised.

If that didn’t work, try these steps

If you don’t have access to the email address or mobile phone number associated with your Facebook account — maybe because you were hacked and your password was changed, or you lost or forgot them — try these steps to recover your account:

  • Try using a different mobile phone number or email address, which you might have forgotten are associated with your account.
  • Double check that you’ve entered your mobile phone number or email correctly at login. If you’re entering a mobile phone number, try including the country code. For example, +1 is the United States country code.
  • Try contacting your email provider to see if they can help you recover access to your email account.

If that worked, follow the steps to reset your password.

Find your account on a familiar device

Important: This next part is most helpful if you can use a device you’ve used to log into Facebook before. This might be your own phone or computer, or it could be an old phone or a family member’s laptop. If you can get access to that device, try these steps:

  1. On a device you’ve used to log in before, type this into your usual browser: facebook.com/login/identify
  2. Enter an email address or a mobile phone number. It can be the one you usually use to log in, or any other that you think could be registered to the account.
  3. If that doesn’t work, try entering your account name or username. If you don’t know your username, you could ask a friend to go to your profile and send you the username found in the URL:

Get more help finding your Facebook account.

Steps to follow after finding your account

  1. Select No longer have access to these? If you can’t see this, you might see Forgot account? or Recover instead.
  2. Follow the prompts. You may be asked to provide new contact information. The contact information you provide must not have been used for your Facebook account before.
  3. Follow the prompts to confirm that the account you’re trying to recover belongs to you.
  4. Once you have successfully passed all the security checks, follow the instructions to reset your password. Try to choose something that is easy for you to remember, but hard for other people to guess.

Suspect your account was hacked?

If you suspect your account was hacked, visit facebook.com/hacked on a device you’ve used to log into Facebook before.

Things that can’t be listed for sale on Facebook Marketplace

My listing was rejected

My Marketplace access is limited

Report a listing

Products listed on Facebook Marketplace must comply with Meta’s Commerce Policies and the Facebook Community Standards. Buyers and sellers are also responsible for complying with all applicable laws and regulations.

Examples:

  • Counterfeits: Anything that violates intellectual property rights (examples: counterfeits, knockoffs, replicas of branded goods, pirated copies of a movie) isn’t allowed on Marketplace.
  • Unauthorized or pirated copies of copyrighted works: This includes videos, movies, TV shows and broadcasts, video games, CDs or other musical works, books, etc.
  • Services: Offering services (example: house cleaning) is only allowed on Jobs on Marketplace.
  • Animals: Selling animals or animal products isn’t allowed on Marketplace. This includes posting about animals for adoption, except by approved pet adoption matching services.
  • Healthcare products: Medical and healthcare-related products aren’t allowed on Marketplace (example: thermometers, first-aid kits).
  • Recalled products: If you’re unsure whether the item you’re buying or selling has been recalled, look on the website of the item’s manufacturer or relevant government entity. For example, the US Consumer Product Safety Commission or the EU Rapid Alert System for Dangerous Non-food Products.

Learn what options you might have if:

  • Your Marketplace listing was rejected.
  • Your Marketplace access is at risk, limited or suspended.

Learn how to report a listing on Marketplace.

Note: The information above summarizes parts of the Commerce Policies for convenience, but you should consult the policies themselves for comprehensive and up-to-date information.

Troubleshoot login with two-factor authentication on Facebook

Use a recovery code

Approve login from another device

Confirm my identity

I can’t get security codes

This article is for Facebook users who have turned on two-factor authentication and are now unable to log in because they can’t receive or enter a security code. Two-factor authentication is an extra security step that requires you to enter a code — in addition to your password — each time you log in to Facebook from an unrecognized device or browser.

If you can’t receive your two-factor authentication code by text message (SMS) or through an authentication app (such as Google Authenticator or Duo Mobile), there are several ways to regain access to your Facebook account. Try the tips below in order.

Tips for logging in to Facebook without your two-factor authentication code

  • Wait for the SMS code to arrive. Text message codes can sometimes be delayed by your mobile carrier. Check your phone again after a few minutes. Make sure you have cellular signal and that your phone’s message inbox is not full.
  • Approve the login from another device. If you are already logged in to Facebook from a different browser, phone, or tablet, check your Facebook notifications on that device. You may see a prompt to approve the new login attempt without needing a code.
  • Use a recovery code. Recovery codes are one-time backup codes that you can generate from your Facebook Security and Login Settings. If you previously saved or printed your recovery codes, enter one of them in place of the two-factor authentication code to log in. Each recovery code can only be used once.

How to update your two-factor authentication methods after logging in to Facebook

Once you have successfully logged back in to your Facebook account, update your authentication methods so you don’t get locked out again. You can:

  • Add a new mobile phone number to receive two-factor authentication codes by text message.
  • Set up a different authentication app, such as Google Authenticator or Duo Mobile, to generate codes on a new device.
  • Add a security key — a physical USB or NFC device that you tap or insert to verify your identity instead of entering a code.
  • Turn off two-factor authentication entirely from your Security and Login Settings if you no longer want the extra security step. (Note: Meta recommends keeping two-factor authentication turned on to protect your account.)

How to confirm your identity and regain access to your Facebook account

If none of the tips above work and you still can’t log in, you can ask Facebook to confirm your identity so you can regain access. The steps differ slightly depending on your device:

  1. Attempt to log in to Facebook and continue until you reach the screen asking for your two-factor authentication code.
  2. Look for a help link on that screen:
    • On a computer: Click Need another way to authenticate?, then click Other Options, then click Get more help.
    • On Android or mobile web: Tap Having trouble?
    • On iPhone or iPad: Tap Need help?
  3. You will be asked to confirm your identity. This may involve uploading a photo of a government-issued ID (such as a driver’s license or passport), answering security questions about your account, or confirming your identity through trusted contacts you previously designated. The specific options depend on what you set up on your account.
  4. After you submit your identity confirmation, Facebook will review your request. You will receive instructions on how to regain access, typically within 1–2 business days, via the email address or phone number associated with your account.

Tip: If you don’t have access to your phone at all, look for an option that says I don’t have my phone on the authentication screen, then tap or click Contact Us to reach Facebook support directly.

Note: The identity confirmation process is not available on Facebook Lite. If you use Facebook Lite, open the full Facebook app for Android or visit Facebook in a web browser to complete the identity confirmation steps above.

  • How to add a security key to your Facebook account

Troubleshoot something that’s not working on Facebook

Facebook not loading

App not working

Report a bug

If something isn’t working correctly on Facebook, like content not appearing or a selection not loading, here are some ways to troubleshoot:

Computer

  • Refresh the page.
  • Close the page and reopen.
  • Clear your cache by going to your browser settings.
  • Try again with a different browser (example: if you’re on Chrome, try Firefox).
  • Restart your computer.

iPhone or iPad

  • Update the app. If you’re having trouble downloading the app, check your internet connectivity. For best results, connect to Wi-Fi before downloading.
  • Make sure you’re connected to a reliable data or Wi-Fi network.
  • Close the app and reopen.
  • Restart your device.

Android

  • Update the Facebook or Facebook Lite app. If you’re having trouble downloading the app, check your internet connectivity. For best results, connect to Wi-Fi before downloading.
  • Make sure you’re connected to a reliable data or Wi-Fi network.
  • Close the app and reopen.
  • Restart your device.

Mobile browser

  • Refresh the page.
  • Close the page and reopen.
    • iPhone/iPad instructions
    • Android instructions
  • Clear your cache.
  • Try again with a different browser (example: if you’re on Chrome, try Firefox).
  • Restart your device.

Something might not be loading properly because of settings you or someone else set up. Try searching the Help Center for the issue you’re experiencing. You might also be experiencing an issue if a feature isn’t available to everyone yet, or if you’ve been blocked from doing something, like posting, commenting or sharing.

If you’re still experiencing an issue after trying these suggestions, it could be a bug or broken feature. You can report the bug by:

  • iPhone or Android: Shaking your phone, then following the on-screen instructions.
  • Computer or iPad: Going to Help & Support and selecting Report a Problem.
  • Mobile browser: Tapping Report a Problem. Learn more about how to report a bug.
